Every tiny piece on that board felt more valuable than all the ivory Chess sets in her father’s study, or the handcrafted boxwood and ebony set she’d gotten from him in her college years.

“I see you’re in the middle of a game. Can one even play on a board that small?”

“What?” Other Lena looked up, irritated that she’d been pulled from her own thoughts.

Lex sighed condescendingly, a smug smile around his lips.

“The chess game, Lena,” he said patiently. “You’re playing against yourself? On a thing like that?”

“It’s got all it needs.”

“I suppose,” Lex said. “I could get you a better set if you’d like? Perhaps one from the House of Staunton? I believe you always loved playing with their pieces, did you not?”

“The luxury of chess boards and pieces is overrated, Lex,” Other Lena cut him off. “A true master can play on any board, anytime, anywhere.”

Lex smiled dimly at that. He raised the box in his hands again.

“Sweets from Daniel’s – do you know that place? They have the best chocolate creations. Or so I’ve been told.”

Though Other Lena didn’t respond, Lex didn’t seem to lose his confidence, instead walking around her cell to the hatch on the sidewall. She heard it creak open, the cream box sliding inside. She could feel his eyes on her through the small open window leading into her space. She hated it. Hated him for intruding in her life, her space. But she didn’t turn around to face him. She just let the waves of disgust roll over her, her face a mask of trained, feigned indifference. Finally, finally, the hatch creaked to a close, and Lex’s expensive shoes walked back into her sight.

She repressed a sigh and looked back up at him, unimpressed. Lex pointedly stared from her to the hatch, but she didn’t move. Eventually, he relented and smiled.

“Care if I join your game?”

“I’d rather not.”

“Come on,” Lex said jovially, hands in his pockets. “We used to play together all the time. We had fun, didn’t we?”

He might have. She definitely didn’t. A lot more depended on her winning these stupid games under her mother’s watchful eyes than Lex. If he lost, he walked away scot-free, his reputation intact. If she lost, it was another sign of her being the inferior sibling. The lesser child. Never the genius. The pressure could’ve made her buckle if it hadn’t made her so angry with all of them. If it hadn’t made her hate them all so much.

“Please?” Lex asked. “Just one game?”

She could refuse. Make him ask again. Annoy him until his annoyance went from just irritating to downright dangerous. Could make him sneer at her until he made her life very, very uncomfortable in her already compromised position. So Other Lena played it differently. 

“Fine,” she said. “But I’m not starting afresh. I’m playing as White.

“Very well,” Lex said, taking his hands out of his pockets and crossing them behind his back as he studied the board. “Interesting positions.”

Other Lena could feel her nails digging into the palm of her hand.

“Just make your move.”

“Queen to C-6.”

Other Lena moved the magnet shaped like a tiny black queen to the corresponding tile on the board.

“The agents stationed at your door tell me you’ve been getting a lot of visits from Supergirl. From what I hear, she never shows up empty-handed.”

“Pawn to B-4,” Other Lena said, moving her own piece. “Your move.”

Lex bent over a little and squinted at the board.

“It sure isn’t easy seeing this game,” he frowned. “This would be much simpler on a bigger board.”

Other Lena wanted to roll her eyes and mentally patted herself on the back for biting down some of the remarks she had in mind.

“Won’t you sit down, Lex?” she said – a tad exhausted – instead. “I’m sure you’ll have an easier time observing the game.”

“And risk staining my suit?” Lex said. “In this dirty hallway? Lena,” he said in that same condescending, blood-curdling way of his, “this is a Berluti suit. I absolutely couldn’t. Between you and me, I highly doubt the personnel in this place has ever even contemplated giving the halls a mopping. I’m not even positive they have a vacuum cleaner in the building.”

“Then stop complaining and make your move.”

“Hm,” Lex seemed to be looking more at her than at the board, but Other Lena stubbornly refused to look at him. “Queen to E-8. You remember the Berluti suits, right Lena? I remember coming home from a work trip one time wearing one, and you were just fawning over it. I then called them and specifically ordered them to tailor one to your size and body. Do you remember that, Lena?” 

His voice was soft like honey like he was actually feeling sentimental. It made Lena want to gag.   

“You were so proud. You were over the moon,” he laughed a little. “You must’ve thanked me a thousand times that day. You wore it the first day of your internship at Lex-Corp, do you remember? You looked beautiful. And damn powerful too. I knew right then and there that you’d make an excellent asset to the company. And I haven’t been proven wrong since.”

Other Lena clenched her jaw. She was not impressed by Lex’s trip to memory lane and had no desire to join him there.

“Queen to F-5,” she said. 

“King to H-8,” Lex countered, not even sparing the board a single glance. “You do remember that, don’t you? I mean, the other dimension was practically a parallel to this world up until the accident, right?”

Other Lena could feel her nail drawing blood.

“Queen to F-6,” she said, taking his Horse off the board. “Interesting way to refer to your attempt to murder me.”

“Ah, you forget,” Lex said, “the stress was on the attempt. I never meant to cause you harm, dear Lena. I merely wanted to remind you who you were answering to. If I remember correctly, you were making some dubious business decisions. I couldn’t just stand by and watch. Pawn to F-6.”

Other Lena moved her own Queen off the board and placed it next to her other fallen pieces next to the board.

“Rook to F-6.” She took Lex’s pawn off the board and placed it on the floor with a little too much force. “So it was all purely accidental, hm? I only got hurt because of a flaw in your plan?”

“Lena,” Lex said. “At the time of the accident, both Supers were in National City.”

Other Lena clenched her jaw.

“I always knew they were. So I knew they’d save you. I expected you to be afraid, a little shaken, sure, but I never dreamed they would be so heartless as to just let you die. They were the ones who failed you, Lena. Not me. I was always predictable in my actions. I could have never estimated how cruel they could be, and how indifferent they were to the lives of anyone associated with me.”

Other Lena hated him for making it sound so simple. How he could twist his words and soften the tone of his voice until his hatred was replaced by compassion that Other Lena could almost understand and lean into. Like he was not to blame. Like he was innocent. Like everybody else was twisted. 

“It’s your move,” Other Lena whispered, trying not to let the hatred and disgust strangle the words out of her throat.

Lex sighed and shook his head. He slowly paced in front of her cell, checking her face and the board from time to time.

“Queen to H-5,” he said. Other Lena moved the piece. “Lena, I don’t mean to upset you. I’ve just become aware of just how often Supergirl is visiting you, and I’m worried she’s trying to infiltrate your mind. I’m worried she’s trying to win you over with gifts to make you forget all the terrible things she’s done to you. I’m worried she’s manipulating you into forgetting all the disgusting things she’s done to you. What she’s turned you into.”

He nodded at her chest, and while Other Lena knew it couldn’t be, she almost felt the Kryptonite core inside of her pulse with rage.

“And you aren’t?” she bit back, the cream box still visible in the corner of her eye.

“I’m your brother,” Lex said, almost sounding believably hurt. “I care for you. I worry about your well-being in this godforsaken cell! I want you to have nice things around you, to remind you that you are still a Luthor. Your name still matters in this world, and you deserve all the luxury that comes with that name.”

“Rook to F-8. That name,” she spat, “has brought me nothing but misery over the years! I want nothing to do with it. If I could start over in life, dirt-poor but with a different fucking last name, I’d do it in a heartbeat.”

Lex sighed, disappointed.

“Always so dramatic,” he mumbled to himself. “You truly can’t help it, can you?”

“You think that you can waltz right in here with your memories and your treats like I’m the same ten-year-old who took your every word for gospel! You were the one who attacked me, and you were the one who let my spine break into crumbs!” Other Lena’s face felt hot with rage, but she refused to back down. “You don’t get to hide behind some other scapegoat when you were the one who pulled the fucking trigger! I have more reason to hate her than anyone else on this planet, but don’t for a second think that I don’t feel the exact same way about you! If Supergirl is to blame, then you belong right there on trial with her!”

The fight had knocked the air right out of her lungs. She could feel her chest heaving, a snarl, a remnant of the discussion, still glued on her face. Other Lena felt the blood boiling under her skin, and she just knew her face was ablaze with anger.

Lex, for his part, looked only mildly surprised. His face was frozen, not a trace of worry or anger on his face, but Other Lena could tell from his silence that he did not quite know what to say, and that was a sign that she’d shocked him. Lex Luthor was never without rebuttal, never without a counterargument. He knew how to fight and fight dirty. He knew how to throw everything you’ve ever felt right back in your face until you could do nothing but break under the pressure. 

But this time, he was silent. He observed her with his face tilted just the slightest bit, eyes narrowed at the sight of her. As if she was an enigma, a puzzle he had yet to solve. Lex watched as Other Lena’s body still sizzled from the storm of feeling she had just reckoned with, and didn’t mock her. Didn’t attempt to gaslight her, to make her feel ridiculous for her outburst. Instead, Lex nodded, and bowed his head just a little bit. When he looked back up, his face was just as neutral as before.

“King to G-7.”

The casual comment knocked Other Lena off course.

“What?” she asked slowly – confused. 

“My King,” Lex said calmly, hands connected by his fingertips. “I’d like you to move it from H-8 to G-7. Please.”

As if in a trance, Other Lena’s hand hovered over the board and found the right piece, moving it to Lex’s desired tile. It was like the rage had been taken over by strange rationality, a weird peace-in-war situation where even if the world were burning down around them, they would still be right there, continuing to play chess in a sick contingent ritual.

Other Lena didn’t understand it, and part of her wanted to throw the game in his face and break every bone in his smug face. But then she remembered it was Kara’s game, the board she’d kept and touched and cherished as a child, played with in car rides with her sister… and she felt her anger ebb away instantly. Draining away. Her shoulders sagged, and she could only stare at the board with hollow eyes again.

“I know you are justified in your anger, Lena,” Lex said calmly – almost gently. “But please play your next move.”

Other Lena stared at the board. She could almost feel the pieces change and dance before her eyes, strategies only in the back of her mind, but moving her hands absentmindedly.

“Pawn to E-8,” she whispered. “Exchanging it for my Queen.”

She took her Queen back – someone had used a black sharpie to draw a tiny smiley on the top part of the piece and it made Other Lena want to protect the piece with all her heart. Like a child, choosing a piece, not because of its intrinsic value to the game, but for its beauty, her own emotional attachment to a plastic object. She put her Queen back in the game.

“Excellent move,” Lex complimented her. She didn’t react to it. “Rook to – wait.” Lex paused. “Why is my Rook a magnet?”

A small smile passed over Other Lena’s lips.

“Because they lost the original on a trip to San Francisco.”

When she made the mistake of looking up, Lex was staring right at her, brain going a mile a minute trying to fathom what was going through her head at that time. Other Lena refused to let up.

“Where did you want me to move it?”

“E-2,” Lex said slowly, never breaking their stare. “Move it to E-2.”

Other Lena did. She moved her own King to F-1. She glanced at the board, vaguely contemplating her new move, her mind jumping back to Kara again. Again and again. She was all too aware it was turning into an obsession, thinking of her.

“You’re humanizing her,” Lex said, his voice jarring the peaceful quiet Other Lena had grown accustomed to, ripping her from the trance that only involved her, the chess game, and Kara.

“What?”

“Supergirl,” Lex said, his lips twisting around her name like it physically pained him to enunciate it. “You’re humanizing her. You’re turning her into a person.”

Other Lena scoffed, though she could feel her nerves twisting around her heart, playing on the concerns that had been on her mind since the first time Kara had brought her a book, a sign she cared despite everything that had happened following Other Lena’s trip to Supergirl’s world.

“Would that be so bad?” she said, feigning interest, moving her King to F-1.

“You know better than that!” Lex snapped, and if Other Lena hadn’t gone through all the shit in the world to get to where she was today, she would’ve recoiled at his thundering voice echoing through the empty hallway.

“Do I?” she asked, despite her better judgment. She couldn’t help it. She loved seeing him finally off-balance. She loved to make him stumble.

“She is not your friend!” Lex snapped. “She is the one who made you into what you are today, and forgetting that would be making a mockery of the entire situation! She refused to lift a finger! She watched you crash! She watched you burn! She didn’t give a damn about what happened to you because you. Are. A Luthor! Are you really so desperate – so starved – for attention, that you would sink so low as to swoon over the woman who is probably still gloating about that incident today? Do you not think that she is out there talking to her friends right this second about how pathetic and how dependent you are? You are a naïve child if you think that she is on your side! She is an alien! The only side she’s on is her own. It’s better you get that through your skull now, before she stabs you in the back again!”

As his voice cut out, so did the last traces of sanity that he could always hide behind. The mask that hid the rage boiling underneath the surface, the rage that burned everyone close to him. His eyes were wide, the bloody-vein-riddled white of his eyes sickly and terrifying at the same time. His rage had made him work up a sweat, turning his once immaculate suit into a prison for his heaving, trembling body. 

And Other Lena realized something.

She was disgusted by him. Every single part of him. His entire presence made her stomach turn and she had to force herself not to crawl back as far away from him as possible. He could hide his hideous self behind suits and gentle, knowing smiles – but Other Lena knew better. She could see him for what he really was. A monster. A disgusting amalgam of brilliance and madness – and hatred. All of that mixed into one horrible man, who would torture his own sister just to watch another Super fall. He hadn’t given a damn about her life, couldn’t have cared less if she’d died in that helicopter; as always, he only cared about his mission to destroy the aliens he feared. And Other Lena hated him. She hated him more than she could ever find the words to express. 

He was staring at her expectantly, waiting for her to scream back at him, to get him to win. She wouldn’t let him. She let him simmer in the silence that followed his outburst, let his face contract at her refusal to engage. She could feel the waves of anger directed at her wash over her, created just to elicit a reaction – any reaction. She wouldn’t let him win.

“You,” she finally whispered, after the tension in the hall had grown so wild it made the goosebumps stand up on her arms underneath the blue jumpsuit she’d been handed by the D.E.O., “are losing.”

Now it was his turn to be knocked off-balance again. The rage made way for confusion, his eyes puzzled, almost young in their inability to comprehend the situation.

“What? What do you mean?”

“The game,” Other Lena smiled cockily. “You’re losing.”

He blinked at her for a few seconds before the rage came back with a vengeance. 

“You have some nerve – ”

“You should really check the board, Lex. It’s not looking too good.”

His eyes frantically scanned the board, checking her last move and eyeing his own pieces again, his mind strategizing as if he was actually planning a war. 

“Queen to H-3!” he demanded.

“King to E-2,” Other Lena countered, easily removing the white Pawn Lex had won, and the Rook-Magnet she’d won from him in turn.

His face was seething, the vein on his forehead bulging dangerously.

“You know, Lex,” she said, while Lex obsessively analyzed the board, “I’m not letting Supergirl off the hook. Not ever.” Lex looked up, the veins having definitely burst in his eyes, a pink sheen near his pupils. “She did what she did and she will pay for it. I will make sure of that. But you… I’ve already killed you once. I enjoyed every second of it. My only regret is that it went by so quickly. I will enjoy hurting you all over again.”

“Queen to G-2,” Lex said through gritted teeth.

“You’re not finding your way out of this one, Lex,” Other Lena sing-songed. “I will get out of here eventually.”

“Queen to G-2!” Lex spat.

Other Lena sighed, but moved his piece. She moved her own rook down to F-2 to serve as a barrier between her King and his Queen. 

“Queen to E-4!” Lex demanded.

“Just admit that you lost, Lex.”

“Queen to E-4!”

“This is the part where you surrender,” Other Lena said, unable to suppress a proud little smirk. “This is the part where you give up. King to D-2.”

Lex seemed to want to hum dismissively, but it turned into an angry sneer instead, one that brought Other Lena immense satisfaction.

“You would think so, wouldn’t you? I don’t surrender. I haven’t lost yet.”

“The situation is hopeless, Lex. You’ve all but lost.”

“I haven’t. I just haven’t gone over all the scenarios yet.”

His eyes scanned the board at a sickening speed, taking in every piece and every occupied tile.

“You’re down a Rook and a Bishop, Lex,” Other Lena smiled. “You’ve lost. I win.”

Both of them caught every dubious meaning in that phrase, but neither one of them seemed willing to admit it. Lex’s head whipped up to stare at her, but she merely raised an eyebrow in response.

“You think you’re too smart for me,” Lex realized softly. “You think you can win against me.”

“Well,” Other Lena said, “I clearly just did.”

Lex shook his head imperceptibly, scrutinizing her every move.

“No,” he said. “You haven’t. You just think that you have.”

Other Lena couldn’t help but scowl.

“You,” she said lowly, “are a coward. Any better man would’ve admitted defeat by now! You’re too proud to admit that I outlasted you! That you can’t predict my moves as well as you think you can, and that you don’t know me as well as you think you do!” She shook her head and stared at him in disgust. “You are nothing. A piece of shit with a delusion of grandeur and too much money and power to just be an asshole about it. You just have to make everyone around you as miserable as you can.” She shook her head. “I can’t believe I ever thought you were worth even a second of my time. You’re pathetic. You are nothing. Less than nothing. You can’t dictate my life anymore, Lex. You wouldn’t know how to.”

Lex looked up, and Other Lena realized he was standing too close to her glass window. He looked so imposing she could almost believe he could step right through the glass into her cell. The thought sent a shiver down her spine.

“You’ve lost the game, Lex,” Other Lena whispered. “You’ve lost.”

“Oh Lena,” Lex tilted his head. “There are much more important battles to win.”

“And what does that mean?”

“It means,” Lex said, standing up and straightening his tie, “that I am not finished. You will hear from me again soon.”

“I wouldn’t take that risk if I were you,” Other Lena said with a joyless smirk. “That might just be the little push I need to actively try and get out of this cell and kill you.”

Lex chuckled, folding his hands in front of his jacket.

“You always were a feisty one,” he said. “Let no one deny that.”

Other Lena, for her part, had lost all ability to see the jokes in their conversation.

“Get out, Lex,” she said. “I’m not here to be your fucking entertainment.”

Lex held up his hands and chuckled.

“Whatever you want, dear sister. I told you,” he smiled, “I live to make you happy.”

“Go to hell.”

“As you wish.”

Lex’s laugh was still reverberating through the hallway as he walked away, but Other Lena could feel it linger long after the door had fallen shut behind him. Rage and disgust swirled inside her until she could do nothing but clench her jaw and finally scream. She quickly blocked her mouth with her fist, panting as she forced her body to take control of the rage, force it down until it couldn’t hurt her anymore.

Stray hairs that had escaped her loose ponytail danced before her eyes. Other Lena watched as they moved with every erratic breath she took. She could feel her muscles straining, her eyes hurting from staying open for too long. But Other Lena couldn’t blink. She couldn’t move. She could do nothing but allow her body to process the rage coursing through her like a wild river. She willed it to run its course, willed herself not to throw her books against the wall in that fit of anger. The Kryptonite core inside of her burned, and she could scream out in pain if it weren’t such a familiar ache. It was slowly poisoning the muscles around it, scorching the flesh that had molded alongside the unnatural edges. She willed that thing inside her to calm down too. She couldn’t afford to be overpowered by that poisonous, alien bomb inside of her. She couldn’t afford to be in so much pain that she could barely move and get out of bed. Not now. She had bigger plans now.

She was not her brother. She wouldn’t break and destroy in her angry fits like a child. She would control her anger. She would bide her time. And then, when he least expected it, she would use all that control against him, and strike.

 

 

For the first time in a long, long while, Kara needed to take a minute to compose herself right outside the door leading to Other Lena’s hallway. She needed a minute to get her heartbeat under control. To feel her shaky warm breaths pass over her lips until they came out at least slightly steadier, and slightly more rhythmical than before. 

She closed her eyes and rested her forehead against the cold, metal door. Her eyelashes fluttered across her cheeks, a hint of sensation in Kara’s temporarily dark world. Empty, aside from the soft humming in her head. If it weren’t for her racing heart, Kara wondered if she could fall asleep like that; the stress and the fear finally driving her comatose, standing on her feet in an empty part of the D.E.O. How embarrassing that would be.

Kara wasn’t ready.

She wasn’t ready to face Other Lena and to tell her she could be on her way soon. She wasn’t ready to pretend like everything was fine and to play board games and discuss books like the world wasn’t absolutely blowing up in both their faces at the moment. 

She wasn’t ready to end this. Whatever it was they had built between them. A tentative peace? A begrudging understanding that neither of them could blame the other for everything? A thin line between understanding and compassion? Kara didn’t know. She did know, however, that’s she wasn’t finished exploring whatever it was between them, and having to tell Other Lena that it would have to be cut short…

Kara wasn’t ready. 

But she hadn’t seen Other Lena in two days, not since dropping off the books at Alex’s lab. She had been too afraid she’d take one look at Other Lena’s blue-ish green eyes and would start blubbering with tears. She couldn’t have that. She was sure it would take away the ounce of respect she had so difficultly managed to obtain in the time she’d spent with Other Lena. She couldn’t risk it all like that. It wasn’t worth it. 

So Kara refrained from freaking out, pushed down the urge to turn around, and run back to Alex’s lab, just to beg her to hold off on making any drastic decisions on Other Lena’s future. To beg her not to develop those plans any further. Beg her to let Kara – the one who had so adamantly protested Other Lena’s mistreatment in this world – keep Other Lena with her, in that horrid cell, just for a while longer.

Kara was sickened by her own thoughts. 

Selfish, she thought. She was being selfish. Other Lena deserved to have a fighting chance to work for her own future. To better her own life. To find a way out of the misery that Kara had inadvertently caused. She wouldn’t find that escape stuck in a cell in another world. She wouldn’t find anything here. 

Kara could feel the urge to just slide down the door, sit down and cry bubble up inside her, but she shot it down. This wasn’t her time to get emotional. This was her time with Other Lena. Her time to discuss what leaving really meant. For both of them. 

It was her time to enjoy Other Lena’s wittiness, her competitive streak, and the delightfully smug expressions that always came with it. Her endless carefree musings on books, stories, and scientific theories that Kara could just listen to for hours on end, never growing bored at all. Her rough yet warm voice. Her unexpectedness. 

She didn’t want to waste it.

Kara took a deep breath and pushed her hair behind her ears. She straightened her shoulders and tried not to let the panic tug at her heart. She tried to focus on Other Lena. Just her. She could do it. She pushed through.

 

 

“Hey!” Kara said cheerily, walking through the hallway to Other Lena’s cell. “The TV! It’s here! You got it!”

The medium-sized screen was attached to the wall in front of Lena’s cell, the sound humming softly through the hallway. A middle-aged woman with bright red lipstick and a frilly apron was making some sort of elaborate dish, with fruit and vegetables scattered in different bowls throughout a warm, inconceivably clean kitchen. Judging from the number of cut-up vegetables and condiments, the show had been on for some time, serving as background noise for Other Lena, who was once again holding a book in her hands. 

“And you,” Other Lena raised her chin trying to get a better look at the soft pink box in Kara’s hands, “got us donuts.”

She closed the book in her hands and stood up, eagerly moving towards the front glass wall of her cell. Kara laughed and raised the box, opening the lid to showcase four perfectly glazed donuts, each one shining in a burst of different colors that had undoubtedly called to Kara from their display in the shop.

“Uhu!” Kara said proudly. “Two jellies, two plain. The best of the best.”

“You’re gonna make me fat,” Other Lena said, walking to the other end of her cell as Kara rounded the corner. She easily took the donut Kara handed her through the hatch. “You realize they don’t let me out for any real exercise, right?”

There was a smile on her face, though, and the sparkle of joy in her eyes at the sugary treat already sticking to her fingers was enough for Kara to smile and shake her head.

“I’m sure a donut or two won’t change much.”

Other Lena let out a quiet moan, her eyes closed after taking her first bite of the donut. It made Kara blush just the slightest bit.

“No,” Other Lena shrugged, holding her hand underneath the donut to catch any loose crumbs, a brief glimpse of her other self shining through, “but the scones from Thursday might. Or those homemade muffins you made the other day? If not those, then probably the pizza from last Friday.”

She shot Kara a pointed glare and Kara laughed.

“Okay, okay,” she held up her hands. “No more donuts.”

“Don’t you dare,” Other Lena said seriously and Kara chuckled.

“Sorry I dropped by so late,” Kara said, walking back around to the front of Other Lena’s cell. “Busy days lately.” Which wasn’t a total lie.

“That’s okay,” Other Lena said, “you’re definitely an improvement from my previous company.”

Kara pulled a face.

“Do I need to ask?”

“God no. Talk to me about anything else, please.”

Kara laughed and nodded. “Okay so,” she pointed at the TV, “cooking shows? Really?”

Other Lena shrugged. “They take my mind off things.”

“Fair enough.”

“And I feel like I could use this downtime to learn how to braze a duck breast in cranberry sauce to perfection.” 

“You can do that?”

“I will when I get to the end of this program. And I figure out how to actually use my oven from back home.”

“Sounds exciting.”

“My life here generally is.”

Her lips wobbled into a small smile, unable to keep the dry conversation going, and Kara laughed with her.

“To be honest,” Other Lena said after she’d sat down and had gestured for Kara to sit down on the floor, “it’s just nice to hear something else, you know. Besides my own voice?” She shrugged. “It gets so quiet in here sometimes, it almost feels like I’m in a universe all of my own. Just me and my crazy science ramblings,” she teased with a self-deprecating hint of a smile. “Talking to myself gets old fast.”

She joked, but Kara could only shoot a wry smile back. It didn’t seem all that funny, not when Kara remembered all the bottles on Lena’s liquor shelf one night, that Lena had joked “finally made her brain go quiet for once.” So Kara smiled politely and moved on.

“So,” Kara asked. She went to sit cross-legged on the floor, folding her dusty-pink coat over her arm and smoothing down the fabric on her lap. “Have you seen anything interesting yet then?”

“Mm,” Other Lena hummed dismissively, “not really. Although the news comes on from time to time. You seem to feature prominently every time.”

Kara tried her hardest not to blush.

“They do love to film everything Supergirl does, even if it’s just me flying around the same building they’ve seen on film a dozen times before. It’s silly.”

Other Lena hummed non-committedly and Kara didn’t know what to say to that anymore. Luckily, Other Lena only needed a few seconds to analyze Kara’s discomfort and switched to a different subject.

“No books today?” she asked with a raised eyebrow. When Kara shook her head sheepishly, she sighed over-dramatically. “Wow, you are really slacking. Only four donuts and no books? I’m hurt, Supergirl. It’s almost like I’m not a priority anymore.”

“Oh my God,” Kara rolled her eyes and put her donut down so fast that the powdered sugar stained her jeans. “I literally just came by with books. I know you’re a quick read but you can’t possibly have read all of them already! Especially with that new, fancy TV to keep you occupied!”

Other Lena giggled at Kara’s fake-outrage, covering her mouth with her hand.

“Also, I can see the chessboard, Lena. I know for a fact you’ve been playing yourself, which means you’ve probably spent hours on that game! Do not insult my book-finding skills!”

“Okay, okay,” Other Lena laughed. “You’ve defended your own honor, Supergirl. You’ve caught me; I haven’t finished all the books from last time.”

“Well I should hope so. Took me ages to gather that little collection. I really tried this time.”

Other Lena hummed. “I’ve noticed. Stephen King, John Green, Annabel Pitcher… It’s almost as if you’re going for an entire genre switch here.”

Kara laughed and adjusted her glasses.

“Yes, well, I didn’t want to overwhelm you with all the philosophy books again.”

“Overwhelm me, huh?” Other Lena teased. “Oh I’m sorry, were my philosophy ruminations too much for you? If you can’t keep up, you can just let me know next time, I’m willing to dumb it down a little if needed,” Other Lena smirked.

Kara threw her a look and Other Lena laughed again, the dimples in her cheeks accentuating the pure glimmer of happiness and pride in her eyes, and just like it always did in those rare instances Kara got to witness that spark, it took her breath away. Her heart hammered a little faster, and Kara forced herself to bend her head, shaking it slightly while Other Lena thoroughly enjoyed her reaction.

“Very funny,” Kara muttered. “Hilarious.”

“I did think so, yes,” Other Lena beamed, and Kara rolled her eyes. “Though in all seriousness, thank you.” She tilted her head and her eyes softly held Kara’s own. “I really enjoyed the new set of books.”

Kara smiled shyly. “I’m glad. Have you read many of them yet?”

“Oh,” Other Lena leaned back. “A couple. I read Carrie after lunch yesterday. I finished My Sister Lives on the Mantlepiece the day I got it. And I just finished Never Let Me Go today.”

“Did you enjoy it?”

“Enjoy might be a strong word,” Other Lena said, “but yes. It was beautiful.”

Her shoulders relaxed the slightest bit when she said that, like they always did when she was given the opportunity to gush and share all the new details she’d discovered in new books and articles. The freedom she got to express all her thoughts and ideas without interruption, to an audience captivated by every word she wanted to say.

“I didn’t think I’d like it as much as I did. It was… painful. It’s been a while since you’ve given me such a tragic story to read.”

Kara shot her an apologetic smile, but Other Lena didn’t seem to notice it, her eyes far away.

“I don’t even particularly enjoy reading from the points of view of children, and I’m not even sure if the subject is so original… I mean, how often has the burden of humanity and the loss of childhood been portrayed in literature and art right?”

Kara hummed in affirmation.

“But I don’t know,” Other Lena whispered. “The post-apocalyptic setting just allowed the reader to think about some uncomfortable truths of life. It… I don’t know. It was just so heart-breaking. I liked it. I guess that’s all I can really say. I liked it. It will stay with me for some time, I think.” 

She blinked and stared at Kara again, as if she’d forgotten she was there again.

“Have you read it?”

“No,” Kara said honestly. “I watched the movie, though. I had a friend in college who made me go with her. I don’t think I’ve ever cried that much in a movie theatre ever!”

Other Lena chuckled softly.

“But then I saw it on a flea market literally on my way over here to drop off the books I’d collected for you. It was a spur of a moment decision. I’m glad I picked it out, though. If you liked it.”

Other Lena hummed thoughtfully. 

“So you were actually here to bring the books by my cell?” she asked.

“Oh. Yes, I was.”

“I see. But you didn’t come by my cell. Agent Daxen came by instead.”

“I’m sorry! I didn’t think you would notice.”

“That Agent Daxen was bringing me my books instead of you?” Other Lena said with a teasing, little smile. “It wasn’t hard, Supergirl. He’s much less talkative than you, and he’s not nearly as colorful.” She shrugged. “I put two and two together.”

Kara let out a breathy laugh.

“No,” she whispered. “I just didn’t think you’d mind, is what I meant to say.”

“Well I don’t,” Other Lena said, and Kara couldn’t hide that the swift honesty with which Other Lena had spoken, hurt. “I just wondered why.”

Kara shook her head.

“Something just came up.”

Other Lena stilled when Kara said that. Then she leaned in, eyes focusing on Kara’s face, narrowing just the slightest bit in concentration. Like she was looking for something. It made Kara instantly feel guilty, though she rationally knew she had nothing – at that specific moment – to feel guilty about. She shrunk just the slightest bit on the floor, while Other Lena’s eyes scanned her face for any twitching muscles or nervous fluttering eyes that would give her away.

“Work?”

“No,” Kara said. “Or, well, not my work work. Not my actual job. It’s – yeah, not related to my work.”

“Ah,” Other Lena said. “So it’s related to your other work. The work that involves a bright, red cape?”

“Not entirely?” Kara rubbed her temple awkwardly. “It wasn’t really about me. I was just briefed on some… stuff.”

“Stuff,” Other Lena echoed.

Kara looked down, fiddling with her fingers. It caught Other Lena’s eye, and she waited.

“That… stuff,” Other Lena said slowly. “It wouldn’t happen to involve me now, would it, Supergirl?”

Kara swallowed, and when she nervously tried to look up through her lashes, Other Lena’s piercing eyes were still on her.

“No?”

Other Lena let out a husky laugh.

“How have you managed to live a double life for so long, being quite literally the worst liar I have ever met in my life?”

“I am not a bad liar!” Kara said indignantly. “I can fool people!”

“Uhu.”

“I can! I’ve kept my identity a secret for years now, and I’ve been largely successful too! Only a handful of people have ever discovered my secret on their own. That’s because I,” Kara leaned in, “am a good liar.”

“You could be,” Other Lena said slowly, a vague, contemplating look in her eyes, “or maybe everyone’s found out already, and they just feel so bad for you, they’re keeping you in the dark. What do you think?”

Kara gaped at her. “That’s a terrible hypothesis!” she exclaimed.

“Mm, I don’t know, a ponytail and some glasses seem like a terrible disguise that would fail absolutely no one.”

“It fooled you!”

“Did it though? Or was Other Me just part of the ruse?”

“What – that’s, no! Absolutely not! I can’t even tell you how wrong you are!” Kara spluttered, to which Other Lena’s serious expression shattered, and she started laughing. “You – I’m a good liar! I am – stop laughing! People wouldn’t… no one’s figured it out, you’re just being insufferable again. And – and I would know if people knew! You’re – you’re just making fun of me.”

Other Lena giggled in that childlike way of hers again, and while Kara tried to keep an indignant scowl on her face, she failed horribly, and her lips started trembling into a conceding smile. She shook her head while Other Lena enjoyed herself far too much for her liking, but it made something flutter in Kara’s chest, so she wouldn’t dare break it up.

“So what was today about?” Other Lena asked once her laughter had subsided, only a smile left on her lips.

“That was sneaky,” Kara whispered.

“And you’re avoiding the question.”

Kara sighed and hung her head, to which Other Lena giggled. 

“You don’t let up, do you?”

“Well, if I did, I don’t think I would be sitting in this cell right now.”

“Ugh,” Kara closed her eyes and brushed her hair down her head with both hands. “I suppose.”

“So,” Other Lena sat back against the wall, “care to tell me what the stuff was?”

Kara sighed again, but Other Lena didn’t give up. She continued looking at Kara, patiently waiting for her to explain.

“Tell me,” Other Lena implored softly. This time it felt more compelling, more demanding than before. Kara knew that Other Lena was not used to being denied something, and she was cautious about outright refusing her anything. She felt like she owed Other Lena all the information she had. The least she could do after everything.

“My sister,” Kara said after a beat, “she and Lena are working on getting you out of here. They have been for a long time, right?”

“Right,” Other Lena said. “Without success.”

Kara hesitated.

“Supergirl?”

Kara glanced at her, and Other Lena’s face became a blank slate.

A beat of silence passed before Other Lena spoke up again.

“They found a way out?”

“Well not exactly,” Kara said quickly. “From what I hear, whatever they’ve got planned requires more energy and more know-how than they currently have, not to mention the advanced technology they have to find and – 

“But they’ve found a way,” Other Lena stopped her. “They have an idea?”

Kara hesitated for just a second, but there was no use denying it. Her shoulders sagged. 

“Yes,” she finally said. “They have a way out.”

It went quiet. Kara could hear both of their evened-out breaths and their staccato heartbeats – Other Lena’s just a tad bit quicker than her own – echoing in the room. The solid thump of their blood being pushed around. The legs of the bug in the corner of the hallway touching down on the wall. The humming of the lights above her.

“You seem disappointed.”

Kara almost laughed, but she felt too tired to try, so she just sighed instead. “I do, don’t I?”

“How come?”

No question on how, no question on what Lena and Alex had come up with.

“I just didn’t think it would happen,” Kara said honestly. “Or, some part of me always knew it would, but I had just never seen it as happening so soon. I thought we’d have more time.”

“More time for what?” Other Lena asked.

Kara frowned and raised her head to look her in the eye. There was a hunger in Other Lena’s gaze. A desperate need for something that Kara had to give her. A truth or a reason that she could use and process and analyze.

“I don’t know,” Kara whispered. “This? Just us… talking?”

A second passed, and a warning flashed in Other Lena’s eyes at the sincerity in Kara’s. But Kara didn’t care anymore. Visibly so. She could feel her heart shatter at the mere sight of Other Lena. She didn’t, she couldn’t just let go. 

“Supergirl – ”

“I don’t know,” Kara laughed awkwardly. “I just liked talking to you.”

“I would hardly say we’ve had the most meaningful of conversations,” Other Lena said.

It hurt.

Kara swallowed it down.

“Well I thought they were.”

Other Lena sighed and Kara tried hard not to show just how much it affected her.

So?” she asked hoarsely. “Did all of our conversations have to be meaningful? Maybe I didn’t mind our conversations not being deep contemplative dialogues about ethics and life or whatever.”

“Or whatever,” Other Lena echoed.

“Fine!” Kara snapped. “If you think they were meaningless, then they were. Maybe it wasn’t the conversations that I cared about. It was spending time with you – that was meaningful to me. That’s what I’m going to miss. Is that so stupid?”

“Yes.”

Kara felt like she’d been slapped in the face.

“What?”

“Supergirl,” the Other Lena sighed, closing her eyes briefly, sounding more like a mother reprimanding her child than a woman talking to her nemesis – Kara should know, she’d encountered the latter too frequently over the years. “Don’t. We have been over this so many times.”

“I know,” Kara said, surprised by her almost petulant tears pricking her eyes, so she cast them down. “I know.”

“You cannot keep putting yourself through this. You knew from the start that this – these visits, these sweets,” Other Lena shook her head. “You know – I told you – it wouldn’t make a difference. I told you. And you agreed.”

“I know,” Kara echoed, unable to find any other words to defend herself with, the desperation tugging at her syllables. “I know.”

“If that is what you wanted to get out of this, a… a misguided friendship? Then you were mistaken to believe I could be so easily persuaded. What happened between us in my world,” Other Lena said lowly, “was too deep and too harsh to be resolved by an offering of books and presents. By any visits.”

Her hands gestured around the space, filled to the brink with everything Kara. Kara’s life, her money, her thoughts, and gifts for Other Lena, all gathered in the tiny cell Other Lena had been calling home for over a month now.

“If that was what all of this was about, then please,” Other Lena said seriously. “Take your books. Take your gifts. I don’t want anything if it’ll lead you to believe that we have something that would even resemble a relationship, Supergirl.”

Kara swallowed the lump in her throat. It felt like a jagged rock lodged in her throat, burying itself deeper with every word coming out of Other Lena’s mouth. 

Other Lena sighed deeply when she saw the hurt on Kara’s face. She bent her head down, balling her fist by her side.

“God damnit, Supergirl,” she whispered. “Why – why are we even having this conversation, hm? You knew – you knew – what the answer would be. You knew. And yet you chose to have this conversation anyway.”

She sounded so accusatory like Kara had personally insulted her, bringing up the inevitable. Like she was physically hurt by having that conversation again. She couldn’t look at Kara anymore, shaking her head over and over, very much not in control anymore. There was something fragile about Other Lena like this. Like she couldn’t handle the conversation but had no way out. It was driving her into a corner, making her desperate for any way out. 

But Kara felt angry. She felt a deep sense of injustice at Other Lena just capping off the conversation with that same, old, murderous crap that didn’t mean anything anymore.

“I don’t care,” she said.

“Well you should!” Other Lena snapped. “You have got to stop living in this blind, childish fantasy that I wouldn’t hurt you if given the chance. Like I wouldn’t kill you the second I got out of cell and – ”

“Oh my God, can you just stop?” Kara shouted. Other Lena looked shocked, but Kara relented. “It must be so easy to spout your bullshit sitting behind a door that you know you won’t be able to get out from behind any time soon.”

“I can get out of here,” Other Lena hissed, leaning in closer. “I don’t need your help.”

“Then prove it! Come on,” Kara said, throwing her hands up. “Get out of that cell right now and kill me. Do it!”

“Don’t.”

“You say you hate me,” Kara said angrily, “you claim you could hurt me, and torture me, and make me regret everything I’ve ever done since landing here all those years ago. But you and I both know you’re just talk.”

Other Lena clenched her jaw.

“You know it is!” Kara could feel a hysterical burst of laughter bubble up inside of her, but she shut it down, if only because she knew it would lead to hysterical crying too. “It’s so easy to tell me to fuck off, to tell me you hate me, to tell me you’ll destroy me when you know that you can’t. It’s easy to break me down when you know you won’t have to prove that you’re even capable of doing it.”

“I did it twice before,” Other Lena hissed.

“You did,” Kara said soberly. “And you failed twice too. And that was before you got to know me.”

“And what would that have to do with this?”

“Oh for God’s sake!” Kara buried her head in her hands for just a second before she whipped her head back up. “Fine, Lena. Fine. You have the potential to kill me, I’ll give you that. But you know what? You fucking suck at it. You have some dark in you. You have managed to hurt me just fine before. But you’re not evil. You’re not heartless. If you think that after everything we’ve been through, all the talks and all the late evenings and shared dinners, you’d still be able to hurt me like you did before… then you’re just fooling yourself,” Kara said honestly. “You know you are.”

Other Lena’s face was unreadable. She was sitting still, glaring at Kara with calculative green eyes, her face hard as if it could have been carved from marble. Kara didn’t care.

“I’m tired,” Kara said honestly, “of you trying to convince yourself you’re this all-powerful, evil being. You’re not. You’re just Lena. And I think that you’re happy you’re still stuck in there.”

Other Lena glared at her.

“I do!” Kara said. “I think that despite all of your insults and all of your threats, you’ve enjoyed our time together too. Because I think you loved not being in control of a chaotic world for once. I think you enjoyed not being ‘the Luthor’ that everyone fears. I think you loved being able to just read books and listen to music – ”

“While I’m stuck in a cell!”

“While you’re free from everything that has managed to keep you so isolated all this time!” Kara hit back. 

The frustration dripped from her words, but seeing as Other Lena was too stunned to actively fight back and do more than glare at her, Kara couldn’t let that stop her. She had to keep going.

“Lena,” she tried, softer, “you’ve been stuck in a cycle of pain for so long now, and you’ve never been able to escape from it. Not until now. I know I hurt you, and I know you have every right to hate me, but you can’t tell me a part of you isn’t relieved to finally be away from that mess! You’re clinging to the image of the old you because that’s the only thing that you think could stay the same in this different world where you have so little control,” Kara whispered. “But you’re not the same. You can’t tell me you haven’t changed. That you haven’t felt better, being away. You – you hold on to these threats, to these death-threats, like they can remain a stagnant truth in this world, but the truth is, they’re not real anymore. Not really. You can’t tell me you hate me as much as you did before – you can’t tell me,” Kara raised her voice when Other Lena made a protesting noise, “that I’ve not grown on you, at least a little bit. You can’t tell me our time together was fucking meaningless, because it would be a cold, cruel thing to say. It would be a lie,” she whispered softly, earnestly, “and we both know it.”

It went quiet for a bit. Kara felt her entire body rippling from the tension and the energy it had taken to finally say what she had felt for so long, but had only been able to express, both to herself and to Other Lena, just then for the very first time. It was exhausting. She felt like her spirit had been ripped from her body and had done all the talking, like she had seen herself from outside her body, yelling at Other Lena with a passion she didn’t know she had. 

She watched Other Lena sitting tensed up on her bed, with white knuckles and burning eyes, glaring daggers at Kara. She seemed beside herself with anger, her nails digging into the mattress like they couldn’t wait to sink into Kara’s skin instead, but there was something else there. Something beyond the anger. Fear, Kara thought, and doubt. Doubt that everything she had built on coming to this planet, had all faded in importance. Like it didn’t matter anymore, like it had lost all value in comparison to the reading, the listening she could do so far away from home. Like it was all a ruse to come to this universe, and she had just found out that her entire trip revolved around a stupid, unattainable, and above all, utterly meaningless goal that wouldn’t change shit in her real world. In her life.

And if Kara had interpreted that lost, scared look in her eyes correctly, she guessed that Other Lena seemed to have finally realized how empty her goals were, and how little she cared to fulfill them. And how deep Other Lena must be caught in the web of her own misery, to be utterly unable to admit it.

And just when Other Lena was right on the verge of hitting back, a soft, uncomfortable scraping of someone’s throat took both of them right out of their zone. They both turned their heads around with a start, and there she was.

“I’m sorry,” Lena said awkwardly. “Is this a bad time?”
