Lena’s hand felt cold in hers, but the way her fingers lifted her own with a touch so gentle, so careful; Kara felt warmer and more cared for than ever before. Once she was fully upright, she let out a quiet groan, her muscles aching as she stretched.

“Okay?” Lena asked.

Kara nodded. She let go of Lena's hands and let her hands rub down the pants of her suit instead as if she could make some imaginary fold disappear. Anything to avoid Lena’s eyes.

“I, ehm.” Kara paused, not really knowing what to say. Lena waited patiently. “I should go?”

It came out so hesitant, like Lena was the one who had to guide her towards the right decision.

Lena smiled kindly, some tiny wrinkles pulling at her eyes, betraying just how tired she was too.

“I think that would be best.”

Kara wanted to turn, but her eyes found its way back to Other Lena’s sleeping form. And even though she could feel Lena’s questioning eyes on her, Kara felt something inside her stir, something she knew Lena wouldn’t like too much. But Other Lena was still there, sleeping quietly on the floor. On the floor, because she had wanted to be as close to Kara as possible. As close as she could be to comfort her. She was huddled up in a position that would have her body ache for days, just because Kara had broken down in front of her. And now Kara would repay her by leaving, with not even a note to explain why.

The thought of Other Lena having to wake up groggy the next morning, blinking against the fluorescent light, only to discover she was all alone, to realize that she’d been left, vulnerable, sleeping on the floor – it rubbed Kara the wrong way. She couldn’t leave her like that. She couldn’t leave her to wake up alone in her cell with no explanation again.

“Other Lena,” she whispered tiredly. “I can’t… I can’t just go. I can’t just leave. She’s, she was listening to me. She… I can’t just leave.”

She shot Lena a pleading look, willing her to understand with just the few words that Kara could find at that moment. Kara could see a dozen different, undistinguishable, conflicting feelings pass over Lena’s face, but eventually, at least something seemed to click in Lena’s mind. She forced a smile and took a step back as if she could physically allow Kara to wake Other Lena up by gently shaking her shoulder too.

She couldn’t, of course, but the thought of nudging Other Lena awake like that, no glass barriers between them, was something that made Kara feel unexpectedly dizzy for just a second.

She hesitated, but Lena’s face was as kindly impassive as she could probably manage, leaving Kara to make her own decisions, whatever they would be. Kara swallowed the nerves that were buzzing in her throat, clenching and unclenching her nervous fingers that seemed awfully uncontrollable by her sides. She took a step closer to the glass wall separating her and Other Lena and crouched down just the slightest bit. She came so close to seeing Other Lena again, her pale skin so close Kara could almost feel it against her fingers as she rested her knuckles on the glass beside Other Lena’s ear, her fingernail close enough to almost feel Other Lena’s dark hair brush up against it.

“Lena,” she whispered. Her own breath fogged up the space right where Other Lena’s was fading. “Lena.”

A frown passed over Other Lena’s brow, her lips pulling together in an almost childlike pout that made Kara’s heart jump in a way she didn’t know it could. Other Lena’s hands twitched in her lap, her nose scrunching up like her own name had personally offended her.

Kara couldn’t suppress the smile that Other Lena’s adorable sleeping face so easily pulled from her. It made the world around her disappear. Kara bit her lip and instinctively leaned in closer to the window.

“Lena,” she whispered again, and she was surprised at how effortlessly warm and soft her voice came out despite the hints of sleepiness still in her voice. It reminded her of waking Alex up on a Sunday morning with breakfast muffins she’d snuck in from the kitchen. The way sunrays would brighten up the room and would illuminate the sleepy smile on both of their faces. That’s what it reminded her of.

This time, Other Lena did stir. Her shoulders drew closer, her eyebrows scrunched up one more time, and then her breathing changed, and Kara could hear Other Lena’s heartbeat speed up just the slightest bit. Her body had broken out of its sleepy rhythm, and Other Lena was awake.

She blinked against the cold light coming from the ceiling and frowned, pouting as her muscles went tout. Her eyes drifted over to Kara. Kara was ready for any jumpiness, but Other Lena didn’t startle at the sight of her. Instead, her eyes fell on Kara and settled there, before a slow smile spread over her face.

“You stayed,” Other Lena murmured, sleep tugging at her words.

The sound pierced through Kara’s abysmally few, last defenses and she could only offer a weak smile.

“I guess so.”

Other Lena smiled back, and for just one split second, Kara was ready to give up the whole world and crawl through that glass just to stay with Other Lena for just a moment longer.

But the moment didn’t last. Other Lena’s eyes drifted over Kara’s shoulder and landed on Lena, and Kara could see the exact second in which Other Lena’s smile dimmed and annoyance set in instead.

“Lena,” she said unenthusiastically. “You’re here.”

“I just came by to bring Kara home. After everything that’s happened today, she shouldn’t spend the night on the floor in a cell.”

“Right, that’s just reserved for interdimensional people left stranded in your universe,” Other Lena muttered, though there was no bite in her voice. She sounded more petulant than threatening. Like Lena’s words had reminded her that there were bigger things to worry about and she shouldn’t care to waste energy on getting back at her counterpart.

She looked at Kara again, sitting up the slightest bit, but allowing her forehead to stay close to the glass. Close to Kara. Other Lena moved her hair behind her ear, but a couple of hairs stubbornly refused to come with and dangled in front of her eyes. She made no effort to move them, and Kara reached out her hand before she quite realized what she was doing, and how impossible it was, thinking she was close enough to touch.

Other Lena followed the trajectory of Kara’s hesitant hand that now lingered uselessly in the air between them, and a small, gentle, knowing smile graced her features again. When Kara’s knuckles came to rest on the glass between them again, she chuckled quietly, her eyes wrinkling up in quiet amusement. Other Lena brought her hand up as well, covering Kara’s fist with the impression of the palm of her hand on her side of the glass wall between them. Kara could trace every single line in Other Lena’s hand with her eyes, and she did so with an endless fascination that surprised her. She was captivated by the tiny scar under her index finger. By the delicate lines of her fingerprints pressed against the window. The freckle at the base of her wrist. Kara looked back up, and Other Lena was still smiling, almost as amused by Kara’s long reflective stare as Kara had been looking at Other Lena when she was asleep. Like it was just the two of them on the planet.

A quiet but clearly agitated shuffling behind Kara reminded her that they weren’t. She sighed soundlessly and cast her eyes down. She could feel how Other Lena had noticed the moment between them had been disrupted – as quietly and kindly as a moment could be disrupted, it had gone and passed all the same.

When Kara looked back up, she expected Other Lena to look at Lena, perhaps with some remnants of annoyance and frustration, the way she usually looked when Lena interrupted the two of them. But instead, Other Lena’s attention remained focused solely on her. She looked more serious now. The smile that had softened her face before had been replaced with a more serious expression, a hint of quietly contained worry in her words that followed.

“Are you going to be alright?” Other Lena asked. She didn’t sound patronizing, or overly worried like Alex usually did. She sounded more mature, like she was enquiring about something entirely trivial, and nothing of the evening they’d had had passed.

Kara could tell by the sharp – slightly louder – intake of breath Lena took, that even she was surprised by the sincere concern in Other Lena’s voice.

Kara mustered a weak smile.

“Yeah,” she whispered. “I’ll be fine. Thank you.”

And she meant it. While she knew the overwhelming grief and pain would come back in hundredfold over the next couple of days, amplified only by the horrendous media coverage that would follow, she did honestly feel much, much better than she had before. There was a peacefulness in the hollow of her chest that hadn’t been there before. It had replaced the crawling, itching, terrible ache that had nestled in her chest like a disease – and now Kara felt calm. Tired, like the day had only just left its impression on her shoulders, but lighter. Forgiven, even if it was just for the night.

“Thank you,” she whispered then as if it had only just occurred to her. Her lashes fluttered as she tried to find her words. “Thank you for… tonight. For – ”

She struggled, hesitant to use any meaningful verb like it might set Other Lena off and break the spell that had been their evening together.

“Listening?” Other Lena suggested with a small smile.

“Listening” did not even remotely cover the magnitude of all that Other Lena had done for Kara that night, but she was also quite sure that it would take her a lifetime to find a word that could, so she simply blushed and nodded instead, looking down at her fidgeting hands.

“Yes,” she whispered softly. “That. Thank you.”

Other Lena smiled with such a delicate softness that it made Kara’s cheeks warm up. She felt infinitely more vulnerable under that smile and didn’t know how she would ever get over seeing it directed so easily at her. She didn’t know how she could ever go back to not seeing it again.

“Kara?”

Lena’s hesitant voice was enough to shake Kara out of her reverie and she looked over her shoulder with big, almost contrite eyes.

Lena looked terribly awkward, clutching her small purse under her shoulder. She looked like a fairytale princess plucked from her own story, standing there so lost in her beautiful gown, so hilariously unfit for the ugly, grey hallway she was in. She’d put a light jacket over her shoulders, but was still shivering from the cold wind coming from the vents, and Kara felt a pang of guilt knowing Lena had waited there so patiently for Kara to wrap up whatever the hell she was doing with Other Lena, while Kara had virtually ignored her. She knew it was time to leave then.

Kara shot Other Lena an apologetic look, but there was a quiet understanding in those green-blue eyes, and Kara knew she didn’t have to word the things she was thinking about. She knew.

Kara wanted to open her mouth and maybe prolong the inevitable for just a couple more minutes, but Other Lena didn’t let her.

“Lena’s right,” she said softly. “You should go home. Rest.”

Kara wanted to protest but found that she was just too empty to even try. Plus, she could barely win an argument with Lena on a good day, let alone an argument against two Lenas. Kara decided she would let this one slide just once.

She nodded, slowly standing up from her crouched position, her hand drifting away from the glass like it was mourning the loss of contact. Other Lena’s hand remained, guarding the fading print of Kara’s knuckles on the glass like it was the only thing that still mattered. Her eyes followed Kara’s upward movement and she shot Kara an encouraging smile before she turned to her counterpart, and her expression chilled considerably.

“You’re going to make sure she gets home, right?” Other Lena asked.

“Excuse me, I do have superpowers, you know? I can get home all by myself.”

But neither Lena was listening to her.

“Of course,” Lena said politely, hands folded in front of her lap. “I’ll be dropping her off at her place myself.”

Other Lena nodded, though she didn’t look pleased. Almost as if she figured she could’ve done a better job at getting Kara home safe herself. But at least they were finally in agreement about something, Kara thought. Even if that something was kind of ridiculous and vaguely patronizing in Kara’s eyes. But Kara much preferred this over the alternative. She’d had quite enough of people yelling around her – and more specifically at her. If quiet, begrudging agreements about her inability to care for herself were the best-case scenarios in the shared communication between the two Lenas, then Kara would gladly take it.

“Kara?” Lena asked, voice so much warmer now that her green eyes were on Kara. “Whenever you’re ready.”

Kara nodded. She turned and shot Other Lena a final, hesitant smile, and felt relieved when it was returned. She muttered a shy goodbye before she walked through the hallway, Lena following her closely after exchanging a final, distrusting look with her doppelgänger.

Their ride back was silent. Lena’s driver drove them through the lamp-lit streets of National City in a car that drove so quietly, Kara could almost pretend they were flying. Lena was sitting in the back with her, just a few inches from Kara, but didn’t try and initiate a conversation, which Kara felt very grateful for. Because no matter how happy she was to be sitting in close vicinity to Lena again, she didn’t think she had it in her to have one full conversation without bursting into tears, and she did not need that.

So Kara enjoyed the quick and easy maneuvers of the car, watching as each streetlight cast shadows over the car’s leather seats, showing off Lena’s dress true, deep-purple color in flashes before it mingled in with the dark of the night again. Kara let her head rest against the window with a short bump, and she could feel Lena’s eyes on her in a second.

“You okay?” Lena asked.

Kara turned her head, still resting against the window, and shot Lena a tired, but reassuring smile.

“All good,” she whispered.

Lena smiled back.

“Okay.”

They were home before Kara had even realized it. She was so tired, she felt like she had missed most of the ride home drifting in and out of her own thoughts tethering just on the edge of dreams. Lena got out with her and walked her to her door. Kara was so exhausted and so glad to be home, she didn’t even think twice about pulling Lena in for a quick hug to thank her for the drive home. A short, spontaneous, absentminded hug, like the ones she had given out so many times before. As a thank you. As a goodbye. They were uncommon now, but Kara’s tiredness had allowed her to forget all about that. Instead, her body acted on instinct, and she muttered a tired ‘thanks, Lena,’ in Lena’s ear while she wrapped her arms loosely around Lena’s shoulders.

Lena froze for only a split second – not long enough for Kara to notice anything when she was that tired, but just noticeable enough for it to stay in her brain, and come back the next day to haunt her for sure. But then, almost as if she had missed it just as much as Kara had, Lena’s body preferred acting on instinct too. Her hand came to rest on Kara’s side, while the other landed on the small of Kara’s back, holding her close as Kara rested her tired head on Lena’s shoulder for just a short moment.

“Thanks, Lena,” she muttered.

“Any time.”

Lena’s voice was hoarse, but Kara was too tired to make anything of it. Instead, she pulled Lena a little closer, hearing Lena’s quiet, sharp intake of breath as Lena’s fingers dug into her jacket a little deeper. The sheer fabric of Lena’s dress was surprisingly soft under Kara’s fingers, and Kara didn’t want to let go anymore. She was tempted to ask Lena to just come inside with her and stay, just so she could stay close to Lena, and touch her for as long as possible. She didn’t quite know where that thought had come from and why it had nestled so deeply into her brain and had turned into a dull longing in her chest. She just knew that when the time came to break off the hug, she found that letting go of Lena was just as hard as leaving Other Lena's cell. She realized she was terribly bad at letting go of any form of Lena altogether.

“Right,” Lena took a step back, wobbling slightly on her high stilettos in an uncharacteristic display of instability.

“Right,” she echoed again, eyes glazing over Kara for a bit, cheeks flushing red in the cold evening air.

Kara smiled softly, looking down.

“Goodnight, Lena,” she whispered, shooting her a tiny smile. “Thanks for coming to get me.”

The doubt dissipated from Lena’s face like snow in front of the sun. It was replaced with genuine, warm reassurance.

“Of course,” Lena whispered. “I’m… thank you for letting me help.”

With that, the both of them didn’t quite know where to look anymore, their matching shy expressions causing both of them to avert their eyes. Kara felt the jitters in the air and felt a rush of gratitude and love for Lena burst up inside of her.

She took a quick step towards Lena, and pressed a quick, gentle, blink-or-you’ll-miss-it kiss on Lena’s cheek before she stepped back, whispered a quiet goodnight with pink cheeks and a hesitant smile, and slipped through the door of her apartment complex.

It took Lena one full minute and two polite – but slightly concerned – nudges from her driver before she could finally get her mind back in order and her thoughts back on track, and could slip back into the car to be driven home. Once the car had resumed its course back to her apartment, Lena gingerly brought her fingers to the side of her cheek where Kara’s lips had been just moments before. She could still feel it tingling.

And in the back of her car, unbothered by the fact that her driver was throwing her curious glances from behind the wheel, Lena let out a wondrous giggle. Her knuckles didn’t leave the spot on her cheek for the rest of the car ride home.

 

 

Lena walked through the D.E.O.’s hallway in the direction of the cells with the distinctive click-clacking of her heels alarming the agents on call of her presence. Her seemingly confident strides ensured that every one of them moved out the way as she advanced, her killer eyes and impeccable business suits giving none of her doubts and fears away. She looked scary as shit and she knew it. Her new assistant had looked almost ready to drop her files and quit on the spot when Lena had walked into the office that morning, and it had made her feel so good. A remnant of her Luthor genes, she was sure, she’d figured with a smirk that morning, but she would allow it if it gave her this freedom. The freedom to mask the storm of feelings brewing inside. To hide the nerves that – if they were easily readable on her face – would’ve cost her so many business deals, and would’ve made her deal with quite a lot more frequent unpleasant encounters.

As it were that day, Lena was unstoppable. She was Lena Luthor, co-owner of the D.E.O. by means of her equally powerful brother, and she could go wherever she fucking wanted. And today, that place would be the previously deemed inaccessible cells of the D.E.O. building she owned. And while she was sure many agents – Director Danvers included – would be sorely displeased to find that she’d gone down there, she also noted with great satisfaction that none of them would even dare voice that disgruntlement. They all knew that if she wanted to go there, she would. And the way she strode forward to the halls of the D.E.O., she was damn sure they were all made aware of it too.

But that didn’t take away from the fact that her heart was beating a mile a minute. She could feel its anxious thump-thump echoing in her ears, and she hoped to God that the heat she felt on her face hadn’t yet translated into the overwhelming, pink blush she’d been fighting with since middle school. She hoped that no one could see how very anxious she did feel.

Kara could always tell, the annoying voice in her head reminded her. Kara could always tell when Lena didn’t feel as confident as she looked. In boardroom meetings and at big CatCo speeches, surrounded by distrustful employees and skeptical shareholders alike, Kara had always been the only one who could see through her. Who could ask her after what she needed. How she felt. What she could do for her. Who would bring her a coffee with a wobbly, little heart drawn around her name on the Styrofoam cup. Who would try her hardest to hype her up from her spot in the crowd.

Lena tried to shake the thought away, advancing forward on the black tiles like she knew exactly where to go and what business she had to take care of. Like this was just one tiny item on an endless agenda that Lena would handle in the span of a day. Like Kara Danvers wasn’t filling up her brain with those ever-cloudy blue eyes and giant red sigil on her chest, that she seemed to grow to dread putting on a little more with each passing day.

Lena sometimes wondered who was more upset about Kara being Supergirl; her or Kara. The way the red cape was always angrily pushed aside when Supergirl walked into the D.E.O., never satisfied with the work she’d done as her super alter ego, always searching for the next mission she could fly off to. Lena noticed it all from a safe distance, face hidden behind her L-Pad as Supergirl flew in and out of the D.E.O., always with a worried crease in her brow and her shoulders drawn so tight that Lena often wondered when Kara actually relaxed anymore these days.

It broke her stride only the slightest bit when she was reminded of the rare times Kara did actually look relaxed these days. She’d seen it. She’d been there to witness it, but always, always, from a distance.

When she was in a D.E.O. meeting room with her brother, watching from the windows looking down on the D.E.O.’s main hall from the second floor up whenever she got bored. Her eyes would glide from the screen at the front displaying figure after figure, one graph after another until they all turned meaningless – a vague murmur of numbers crunched and calculated in the back of Lena’s mind without requiring any real energy from her whatsoever. When that happened, the action on the ground seemed so much more interesting.

Brainy, hurrying out of the room carrying a burning metallic invention of any sort while Alex rushed behind him, furiously yelling things that Lena couldn’t hear from up there. Nia would flutter helplessly behind them, while the other agents couldn’t get away from the two of them fast enough, probably afraid Alex’s fury would be transmittable. The scene had pulled a small smile from Lena, just seeing how small Brainy would try and make himself while Alex gestured wildly at the space around them as if that would deter him from trying the exact same thing again with a new invention the next day. As if Alex hadn’t yelled at him about the same thing a hundred times before, and wouldn’t again a hundred times more.

But the thing that would always catch her attention the most was Kara. Supergirl always flew around with a dark, serious expression on her face, waiting to fight the next possible danger, arms crossed over her chest, inspecting a new hologram with a different alien’s head on it each day. She rarely smiled and never took longer than she needed to before rushing out to face the new day.

But when Kara walked around the D.E.O., the difference was palpable. Lena would sit up straighter, trying to catch a better look at Kara. She would only rarely be at the D.E.O. in her regular “Kara” fit. Trousers, or a cute sundress. Always paired with those damn glasses. But the handful of times Lena had seen her, she’d always emerged from the basement. From the cells. She would be skipping across the dark tiles of the D.E.O., ponytail swinging merrily behind her as she fluttered around the D.E.O. like a butterfly, greeting each new flabbergasted agent with a broad smile and twinkling eyes. Lena could never blame them when they stopped in their tracks and kept following her with their eyes long after she’d passed them. Who wouldn’t? Lena herself was glued to her silhouette like an obscene voyeur, watching her live her life from a distance. And Lena would know, she could just tell from the lack of tension in Kara’s shoulders, the easy smile on her face, and the empty tote bag swinging from her shoulder, that she’d visited the Other Her again. And Lena would swallow the hurt and jealousy that bubbled up inside of her when the realization that she was the one who could make Kara smile. She was the one who could make Kara forget about everything else going on in the world. That was all her.

And Lena would remember a time when she was the one who could make that smile light up on Kara’s face whenever she walked into CatCo unexpectedly, surprising Kara with coffee or donuts. When Kara would open the door and yell out the excited “Lena!” even though the game nights had been set for weeks, and it was truly no surprise at all that she’d shown up. She remembered when Kara would demand that Lena sit next to her, so mesmerized by her presence that she got jealous whenever anybody else offered to be her partner at game night. She remembered the dinner dates, the movie showings, the art gallery trips, and the hundreds of galas Kara had dutifully accompanied her to, even when those snobs had turned their noses up when Kara had kindly mentioned she was a CatCo reporter. Kara had always been happy to be with her. To be in her vicinity. Even when Lena couldn’t for the life of her figure out why. Kara couldn’t care less about her money, had no interest in a career at L-Corp, and had declined most of the benefits associated with Lena’s status, save for the occasional free coffee at the coffee cart near L-Corp. Kara was so beautifully, effortlessly, and unconditionally kind to her, with Lena’s friendship being the one thing she longed for – and something Lena would until recently so willingly give to her.

And so now, when Lena would stare down from the boardroom so close, yet so high up, away from Kara and her friends, stuck with her brother like it was a metaphor for the rest of her life, Lena missed her. And Lena was jealous.

But the few scraps of Kara’s presence she’d been given these last few weeks… Lena held onto those. Those were the key towards… something. She didn’t dare name it yet, because whenever a word like “reconciliation” popped into her head, her hopes of lunches and movie nights amplified exponentially, and she had to stop her heart from leaping out of her chest with longing. Lena had to wait. She had to see what would happen before she risked losing it all again. And she didn’t think that having Kara Danvers break her heart for a second time would be something she could ever recover from again.

Lena tried to shake the thought away. To start afresh. She wasn’t here for Kara right now. She was there because of her, but that was beside the point. She had a job to do. A bridge to cross.

Lena walked down the stairs and turned right. She slipped through the door guarded by the two agents that led to the long hallway with the one occupied cell. Lena clenched her jaw as a warmth spread through her limbs, the hairs on her arms standing up.

“What’s the point,” her Other Half said slowly as Lena passed the final, empty cell before hers, “of being kept in total isolation when I can’t even get a moment of respite around here?”

She was sitting on her bed, propped up against a pillow leaning against the wall separating her from the other cell. Her book was leaning on her knees, her sock-covered feet rubbing against each other on the blanket to get warm. She didn’t look up when Lena came to stand in front of her, awkwardly wringing her hands.

“Hello to you too,” Lena said cordially. It was too stiff, and she cringed at her own words the moment they’d left her mouth.

The corner of Other Lena’s mouth pulled up into a short, ironic, little smile before her face smoothed over again. She turned the page of her book.

“Slow day at work?”

“I – not particularly, I’m not sure…”

“It’s gotta be if you’re visiting me twice in as many days,” Other Lena noted calmly, eyes moving from the left page to the right one.

“I didn’t come here to visit you,” Lena said, almost as if she wanted to go against what her Other half was saying, no matter what it was. It made her feel petulant and powerless, something she absolutely hated. “Yesterday, I mean. I wasn’t here to visit you yesterday. I was here to pick up Kara.”

“Yes, Lena,” the Other Her threw her a look, “I’d picked up on that.”

“Oh.”

Her Other Half went back to reading her book, and Lena didn’t know what to do anymore. She awkwardly watched as the woman thumbed another page, eyes languidly sliding down the page as if Lena wasn’t even in the room.

She stood before the cell, awkwardly fiddling with her hands. Her thumbnail scratched along the side of a nail on the other hand, and she inwardly flinched when she could feel her nail polish getting stripped away by her own hand. Typical. Nothing gave nerves away like chipped nail polish, her mother would always say. Lena got annoyed just thinking about it. To avoid further damage to the fresh, steely grey coat on her nails, she instead let her hand fall down to the strap on her purse, holding on until the leather strap was digging deep into her palm.

Other Lena turned a page, arching her neck a little to get a better look at the new page. She was squinting just the slightest bit as she read, and Lena realized that she needed her reading glasses. She was almost tempted to fish them out of her own purse and hand them over before she thought better of it.

“So why are you here?” Other Lena asked slowly, voice so bored Lena almost wondered whether she’d only asked out of politeness instead of genuine interest.

“Oh, ehm…” She had an entire speech prepared. This shouldn’t be as hard as it was. “I, er, I actually came by for Kara.”

That got her attention. Other Lena’s head immediately turned. She sat up straighter, put her book down, and narrowed her eyes just slightly. Lena instinctively stood up straighter too, like she had to physically demonstrate that she was the one who still held all the power. In this case, holding the power meant having all the ways to contact Kara, and to still be in Kara’s favor. Her position was tricky and vaguely unreliable these days, but she could still see Kara whenever she wanted, and that meant she held an advantage on the Other Lena. 

“Well,” Lena said, “not for Kara, more, erm, because of her?” That didn’t clear anything up. “I… I came by to thank you for, ehm, what you did. Yesterday,” she shook her head. “Last night.”

“Jesus, try not to choke on that explanation,” Other Lena said, but the apprehension and pause in her eyes dulled the harshness of her words considerably. “What do you mean?”

Lena clenched her teeth and looked down to steady herself before she could find the power she needed to do what she had never wanted to do before. To thank her Other Half.

“What you did for her. Yesterday,” she paused. “When you… were there for her. I wanted to thank you for that.”

“I didn’t do it for you,” Other Lena bit.

“Yes, I’m well aware of that, thank you.”

They both looked away when their equally sharp tones managed to make the entire atmosphere around them feel positively venomous. Lena sighed inwardly and clenched her fists. It frustrated her to no end how completely impossible it felt to talk to her exact copy. But maybe even more so that Kara seemed to do it so effortlessly, and with such perfect ease. It could make Lena want to tear her own hair out just thinking about it.

Surprisingly, it was Other Lena who broke first. She sighed, and rolled her eyes with great flair, but was still remarkably soft and curious when she opened her mouth again.

“I wasn’t just going to let her torture herself over something she had no control over,” Other Lena said. She feigned annoyance, but Lena could clearly see a blush on the apples of her cheeks, like she was embarrassed about having been caught caring for someone else. Like it made her less – made her more vulnerable in Lena’s eyes.

“It doesn’t matter,” Other Lena mumbled. “How is she doing anyway?”

Lena shook her head.

“I wouldn’t know. I haven’t spoken to her yet. Haven’t had the chance, really.”

Other Lena paused briefly before looking up.

“You haven’t had the chance yet?” she echoed.

Lena grew uncomfortable.

“Well yeah. It’s a workday. Kara’s got her own life, her own… friends,” Lena said slowly. “I just… haven’t found the time to call yet.”

“But you found time to visit me?” Other Lena asked skeptically. “The choices you make.”

“Well, forgive me for popping by to see if you were alright – ”

“Oh, don’t act all self-righteous with me, it doesn’t work. What’s with you making these terrible choices of company?” Other Lena asked. “Working with Lex, and now staying with me instead of with Supergirl?”

“Kara is – ”

“Busy,” Other Lena cut her off. “You said.” She paused. “She always found time to see me.”

Lena shot her a look. “Is that supposed to make me jealous?”

Other Lena shrugged. “Not particularly. I’m just saying, she has time. If you really wanted to find time to ask her how she was doing, you know that you could. She has a flexible office and you are your own boss.” She hesitated and smiled sweetly at Lena. “Unless you have to report directly to Lex when it comes to asking permission to leave work and take breaks?”

“Funny,” Lena said dryly.

Other Lena laughed quietly to herself.

“Truly,” she said, shaking her head. “If I had the chance to choose between spending time with you or spending time with her, I know what I’d pick. Which makes me think that I know what you’d pick too, which once again brings us back to the question,” she shook her head. “Why the hell are you here when you could be out spending your time doing better things?”

Like talking to Kara.

“I’m here for you.”

Other Lena tilted her head.

“You did something I hadn’t expected. You helped Kara when no one else could. I came here to thank you for it. That’s all.”

“So is this like a new approach to prisoner reform?” she asked, unimpressed. “I do something good, I get a reward? I try to kill Supergirl and no more treats for me?”

“If only it were that simple,” Lena said dryly. “Consider this a kindness on my part. A thank you.”

“And what kind of thank you is that?”

She dug into her bag and fished out a thick stack of papers. Other Lena grew curious, stretching her neck to get a better look.

“What we like best,” Lena said softly. “Information.”

“Information on what?”

“On everything that happened in my life since meeting Supergirl. Everything I learned about our family, about L-Corp – LuthorCorp.”

Lena sighed and looked down at the coffee-colored binder containing all the information she’d stacked away for years, adding to it like a growing, festering pile of darkness, kept in the corner of her room like an infectious enemy she held close enough to slowly and surely poison her to death.

“It’s years of information that you were denied due to your… circumstances,” Lena tried carefully.

“That’s a nice way of putting it,” Other Lena whispered, but the bite she had intended got lost in the focused, almost demanding way she was staring at the binder.

“I thought… I thought that giving you what you’ve been asking for might… I don’t know.” She shook her head. “I don’t know what it could do. It’s probably horrible for the space-time continuum to give you this but…”

“But you wanted to thank me so you’re ready to throw logic and reason out the window?” Other Lena guessed, one eyebrow raised so dramatically Lena almost wanted to laugh.

“Right,” she said softly instead. “I figured that if talking worked for you and Kara.”

“Just barely,” Other Lena interrupted her. “Don’t mistake one act of – I wouldn’t even call it kindness – for forgiveness.”

“I’m not,” Lena said easily, to which Other Lena’s eyes narrowed in suspicion. “I’m really not. I have very little faith in any of this ending well. But if there is a chance for things to go better than expected, then I have to take it. And you’ve… you’ve done something I can’t thank you enough for.”

“How so?” Other Lena said, throwing her legs over the edge of the bed, palms flat on her mattress, book completely forgotten. “If she hadn’t come to me, she would’ve gone crying to someone else, I didn’t do anything that anyone else wouldn’t have said instead.”

“But she needed to hear things from you,” Lena said – and the truth hurt so well when she said it out loud. “She needed you to tell her all the things she wouldn’t hear from all of us. I know she did. And honestly,” Lena took a step forward, eyes sliding from the binder in her hands to her mirror-self eyeing her suspiciously from her bed. “I believe that if you hadn’t been available, and if she hadn’t been able to talk to you… I think she would’ve done something incredibly stupid.”

“More stupid than coming to chat with her own enemy then?” Other Lena bit, but she leaned in closer in anticipation like it would get her Lena’s explanation quicker.

“Yes,” Lena said softly.

“Like what?”

There was a tension in Other Lena’s voice. Like she was trying to command Lena to tell her everything she knew as fast as she could but knew that deep down, she didn’t have the power to do so. That she was bound to rely on Lena’s goodwill to know more, and it was killing her to wait.

“Like picking a fight with someone stronger than her for one,” Lena said, crossing her arms. “Or finding an impossible battle she can partake in.”

“She wouldn’t have to look far, just you know,” she gestured at the dark screen of the television, “going off the news.”

Lena frowned.

“Just pointing out that your National City’s crime rates are considerably higher than ours,” Other Lena murmured.

“Yes, well, when you literally obliterate anyone who disagrees with your tyrannical dictatorship, I’m sure people have more important things to worry about than stealing cars,” Lena shot back.

“Touchy,” Other Lena muttered. “But fine,” she held up her hands when Lena started to look just a little too annoyed, probably looking closer to changing her mind and leaving than to stay out of moral obligation. “I see your point.”

The quiet admission made both of them fall quiet. Neither Lena knew where to look. While Lena busied herself studying the edge of her binder with careful consideration and pink cheeks, Other Lena seemed to randomly move her book to different places on her bed like it would somehow make a difference. The awkwardness made Lena tense up so badly that she could almost feel her shoulders painfully draw in, and she did not look forward to the sleepless nights filled with muscle-aches that the meeting with Other Lena alone would bring her later that week.

“So,” Other Lena scraped her throat, awkwardly rubbing her hands together on her lap. She looked more insecure than Lena had ever known her to be, yet her fight-ready eyes seemed to want to portray a confidence that Lena knew she was definitely lacking at that moment. It was oddly charming to watch her own psychology at work right before her eyes. If she hadn’t felt so dissociated from the Other Her, she might’ve even sat down to appreciate it more. But Lena couldn’t help but want to keep her distance. She wasn’t Kara. She couldn’t let that woman in the way that Kara could.

“So,” Lena said.

“What kind of information did you bring me?”

Lena brought the binder up, and Other Lena nodded. They both walked to the side of Other Lena’s cell, and Lena slid the binder through the hatch and onto the waiting hands of her Other Self. It was brief and appropriately distanced. No touching and no eye contact were required for the exchange, and they both got back to their respective places so quickly that it almost seemed like nobody had even moved at all.

Other Lena opened the binder and started flipping through the pages. A deep frown settled between her eyebrows and stayed there for the remainder of her study session. The documents and texts Lena had included were filled to the brink with business jargon and extensive secondary and tertiary sources like business accounts and contracts, but Other Lena seemed to have no difficulty scanning and skimming through them while – judging from her frosty expression alone – soaking up all the necessary facts to make up her mind about her family’s recent dealings.

“There’s all kinds of stuff in there, really,” Lena said, a little redundantly. “LuthorCorp’s dealings, some of our most recent projects, some articles on the family…”

She trailed off when Other Lena didn’t even look up or acknowledge her with a single nod of her head. She kept reading and Lena took a deep breath, throwing a longing stare at the door at the end of the hall, feeling unsure as to whether or not she had done her duty already. Was she supposed to stay longer? Did she have to? Did anyone even appreciate that?

“Some joint venture ideas,” Lena murmured, more to herself than to anyone else at that point. “All kinds of stuff.”

“There’s a lot in here about mother,” Other Lena said, not looking up.

“Right!” Lena jumped a little at the sudden acknowledgment. “Everything I’ve found out from her I jotted down. Like, ehm, oh, our boyfriend Taylor in middle school?”

Other Lena hummed.

“She paid him an obscene amount of money to hang out with us,” Lena said, almost triumphant at the notion that she could finally share something juicy – something her Other Self didn’t know.

Other Lena scoffed and turned a page.

“Figures,” she muttered.

“There’s loads more stuff about her in there,” Lena said, taking a hesitant step forward, finger hovering in the air like she could pinpoint a single page from her spot before the cell. “Family secrets she told me over the years, secret deals I uncovered between her and some shady – ”

“Yes, I don’t care about that,” Other Lena said, turning over an entire stack of papers with a loud plop until she got to another chapter. It startled Lena a little, and she almost flinched just thinking about the years of careful research and passive-aggressive dinners she had had to attend to gain all that information, so carelessly dropped aside by her Other Half. Other Lena looked up at her expectantly and Lena had to blink her distress away for a good couple of seconds before she could focus on her Other Half again.

“What?” she asked, more polite and less strained than she could ever have hoped for given the circumstances.

“Mother. I don’t need to know the things she shared with you. I killed her.” She said it so easily, like it was the most trivial thing to mention at a dinnertime conversation. “I have no use of her anymore.”

“Yes, well I haven’t. Then again,” she muttered in quiet acquiescence, “I’ve come close a couple of times over the years.”

That actually pulled a chuckle out of Other Lena, and the sound was so sudden and discerning in the space previously filled with nothing more than turning pages and awkward silences that it seemed to stun both of them equally. They both looked away, but Lena couldn’t help but feel a proud little smile tugging at the corners of her mouth.

Other Lena flipped through the binder some more, and the smile was quickly replaced by that same frown as before. Lena felt her heart sink at the sight in disappointment.

“What is it?” Lena asked, anxiously fidgeting with the lower button of her vest. “What are you thinking?”

Other Lena sighed and shook her head.

“Look,” she said, looking up at Lena with a surprisingly genuine expression, “I appreciate this. I really do. But all of this,” she gestured at the binder in her arms, “it’s just more shit about Lex and the business. Everything I’ve been fighting against my whole life. Everything I’ve tried so hard to escape.”

Lena swallowed and looked down.

The freedom her Other Self had to be free of her family – regardless of the horrendous things she had done to obtain that freedom – seemed so impossible to her, she felt a deep, constrictive longing – jealousy – when she looked at the Other Lena. And she though that dream was depressingly impossible for her, she did understand that if she were ever to obtain that freedom, she would hide as far away from the remnants of her family’s past as possible. She might move to a tiny little hut in the middle of a forest and pretend she had never lived at all. So when she saw that unwillingness to discuss the Luthors in Other Lena’s eyes, Lena felt a bit of weight lift off her shoulders in a surprising, quiet understanding of her Other Half.

“That’s fair,” she said softly. “I understand.”

“Thought you might,” Other Lena murmured, but Lena could see that the frown had lifted, even if she couldn’t look Lena in the eye anymore.

“Is there anything else I can share with you then?” Lena asked hesitantly. “There must be something I can tell you that you’d like to know? Something to repay – to thank you for what you did?”

Other Lena was quiet for a beat. Then she looked up.

“Kara,” she said.

Lena wasn’t even surprised to hear that name come out of her Other Self’s mouth. Not one bit.

After her first meeting with Kara, years ago, Lena had craved bits and pieces of knowledge about Kara’s life with every cell of her body. She’d hung on Kara’s lips, absorbing every morsel of information like it would be vital to her own survival. It was obsessive and downright maddening, but it was the only thing that satisfied her until she got the clear confirmation that Kara wanted her in her life just as bad as she did. The knowledge that she would get to see Kara again and live in her life, experience her highs and lows, and hear her memories through endless stories during endless nights out and parties was the only thing that could keep her satisfied. The only thing that could quell the urge to call Kara up and ask her more. More life stories, more memories, more stories about heartbreak and Cat Grant’s unbelievable, mind-boggling wishes at the office, more interview stories, more stories from College, more stories about Alex and how they’d fight and make up, more stories about how they dealt with heartbreak, more stories about late nights in bars and crazy things they’d had to hide from Eliza growing up – the only thing that kept her from asking was knowing that she would get to find out herself by living that life in Kara’s vicinity. It was the most precious gift she’d ever received. And it was the one thing she pitied her Other Half most for; that she had never gotten to share in that wondrous experience of having Kara Danvers in her life. So could she really blame her for wanting to know more?

Lena sighed, but nodded, crossing her arms over her chest like she could make sure she wouldn’t fall apart just talking about Kara again. To think about her when it all seemed so far away.

“That’s…”

Other Lena looked at her with expectant yet guarded eyes, a white-knuckled grip on her bedsheets, and a clenched jaw, like she was setting herself up for disappointment, and Lena couldn’t blame her.

Finally, Lena nodded and made up her mind.

“I can’t share everything I know about Kara. It wouldn’t be fair to her,” she said quietly. “But I can – ”

“That’s not what I want to know,” Other Lena interrupted her.

“O-kay?”

“I want to know – ” Other Lena sighed in frustration and ran a hand through her dark hair. Lena noticed the roots were dark and glossy, and clearly recently redyed, which strangely elicited a pang of something in her heart. She didn’t let it affect her and waited patiently.

“I want to know about you two. Not – not the facts that I could just find in gossip magazines,” she clarified softly. “The stuff that you don’t immediately see. I want to know… I want to know what it was like.” Her eyes sparkled with something Lena couldn’t immediately identify. “I want to know what it was like. You and Supergirl. What it could’ve been like,” she continued softly. “How it felt. Being…”

“Not alone?” Lena guessed quietly.

Other Lena shot her a look, and Lena knew that she had hit home. She nodded to herself and walked closer to the glass.

“I can do that,” she said softly.

Other Lena’s head snapped up, eyes narrowed in suspicion and hesitant surprise.

“You can?” she asked, voice so skeptical like she was waiting – expecting – the other shoe to drop at any second.

“I can,” Lena whispered. “I can tell you what it was like, being her friend, if that’s what you’d like to know?”

Other Lena swallowed, and her hands came to rest on her lap, toying with the fabric of her pants. Determination and anticipation mixed in hopeful eyes, and Lena could feel something wash over her; the realization that what she was doing was right. That it was necessary. And that it would be okay.

“Very much so,” Other Lena said hoarsely.

Lena shot her a shaky smile.

“Okay,” she said softly. “Okay.”

Other Lena sat up a little straighter, leaning in with a hopefulness that seemed to stem from such longing that Lena couldn’t help but feel giddy with excitement herself.

“I won’t be able to be too exact with times and names,” she warned. “I don’t know how it could affect your life when you go back to your world. I don’t want to mess with any other timelines, especially considering how little we know of fifth-dimensional ones.”

“I don’t care,” Other Lena said quickly, impatiently. “Whatever you can share.”

Lena smiled. “Okay. How about…”

Other Lena’s hands folded in her lap, hanging onto Lena’s every word. And suddenly there were a hundred different images that popped into Lena’s head, about a hundred different times when she had felt Kara’s presence in her life the most, and knew she could never go back to living without her ever again. She felt warmer and more comfortable than she had since the moment she’d decided to come visit her Other Half that morning. The words came so easily to her now, and she didn’t think she could’ve stopped talking if she had wanted to. She put down her purse and felt herself get lost in memories of when her life felt so much lighter, despite the horrors she’d had to live through. Because she had someone. She had Kara.

“How about I tell you about the time I lost someone close to me, and I thought I’d be alone in my apartment, alone in my mourning and then… and then she was there?”

Other Lena didn’t even blink, just followed Lena’s every word like she would explain the future to her with an unmatched preciseness.

“I can tell you about that time when she was there and I… knew I wouldn’t be alone again. Ever,” she whispered, just as much to herself as to her Other Self. “I can tell you about that.”

And Lena didn’t stop talking for the rest of that afternoon.

 

 

Lena bumped into Kara on her way out of the D.E.O. The blonde looked much better in a soft pink sweater and comfy jeans, her hair in a loose ponytail on her back, and her trusty, leather bag filled to the brink with books again.

“Kara,” Lena smiled so brightly, she just knew that the hated wrinkles around her eyes that even obscenely-prized eye creams couldn’t remove were on prominent display again. “I was just about to call you!”

“Oh really?” Kara looked nervous but happy. Her cheeks turned a light, happy shade of pink at Lena’s words. “That’s so sweet. I… I wanted to talk to you too! To thank you for last night, I mean. For, ehm,” she shook her head, stumbling over her words so quickly that she brought her hand up to fiddle with the edge of her glasses like it would steady her again. “Bringing me home and all. That was really nice of you.”

“It was my pleasure,” Lena smiled.

Kara looked over Lena’s shoulder and suddenly looked puzzled.

“Did… did you just come from – ”

“Other Lena’s cell? I did.”

“Oh.”

The alarm on Kara’s face quickly drove Lena to explain herself.

“Don’t worry!” she promised. “It was all good! We just… talked?”

“You did?” Kara looked skeptical, but covertly so, like she wasn’t trying not to believe Lena, she just really had a hard time doing so, which Lena begrudgingly had to deem fair.

“Yeah,” Lena shook her head. “It was surprisingly… okay,” she decided. “We talked. No miracles were performed today, though,” she said with a soft, deprecating tilt of her head, “but I see what you mean by talking openly with her. She can be… an interesting conversation partner.”

Kara blurted out a loud, warm laugh then, quickly covering it up with her hand, and Lena couldn’t help but giggle along when Kara quickly looked around, hoping no one had overheard her.

“That’s,” she scraped her throat and nodded, pursing her lips. “Yep. Yep, that sounds like her.”

Lena laughed, and for a minute, it was just like old times. Standing close together in a crowd of people who were so confused to see the two of them giggling together like schoolgirls, not privy to any of their inside jokes. Just the way they liked it.

Lena only realized she had to stop smiling when her cheeks started hurting and she realized she was looking sillier and younger than she had wanted to that day. She shook her head trying to regain her bearings and watched as Kara’s smile dimmed a little too.

“Listen, I do actually have to run,” Lena started apologetically.

“Oh yeah, no, me too!” Kara said quickly. “Andrea only gave me an hour before the next meeting, and I kind of wanted to talk to… you know.” Her voice trailed off but Lena understood. Of course she did. She nodded and shot Kara a quick smile.

“So you’re doing it again then,” Lena said, not hiding how much she’d kept track of Kara’s last visits to her Other Self at all. Kara smiled shyly. “It’s okay, Kara,” Lena reassured her. “I’m glad.”

“Yeah, well,” Kara looked down, trying – and failing – to hide a budding smile. “It felt good again. Seeing her. I think… I think I might want to try again. At least once every week or so. Just…. I think it might be good for both of us.”

Lena smiled softly.

“Well, I’ll leave you to your book club then,” she teased. “But I’ll call you later? If… if that’s okay?”

The way Kara’s face lit up and she just beamed right in front of Lena’s eyes was almost enough to make Lena’s heart stop beating altogether. She looked so positively radiant, so ready to shimmer and float with happiness that Lena felt her mind go hazy for a bit.

“I’d love that,” Kara whispered honestly and Lena had to bite her lip to keep from grinning too broadly.

“Well, alright then,” she whispered back, matching Kara’s excited smile. “I’ll talk to you later then.”

She reached for Kara’s hand on instinct and squeezed it. Before she could even dare to overthink it, Kara squeezed back.

“I can’t wait.”

 

 

Kara awoke with a painful groan.

The world was dark, pulsing, and heavy around her. There was a ringing in her ears and a pounding in her head so painful, it made her regret ever becoming conscious again in the first place. She let out a low moan and felt her throat close up. Her tongue was so dry, and there was a disgusting, dusty taste in her mouth she couldn’t seem to get rid of, no matter how hard she tried to get her body to swallow what little saliva she could produce. Slowly, achingly slowly, sensations started coming back to her. She felt like she’d run a marathon carrying an entire spaceship on her shoulders. Her muscles were screaming, and her back felt so locked in place she didn’t even attempt to move. She was lying flat on the ground, her cheek pressed against something cold. She squeezed her eyelids closer together when the ringing started changing to a cacophony of more and more sounds, all pretty indistinguishable, but incredibly piercing to her ears.

“Kara?!”

That was her. That was her name. It felt vaguely familiar in the wave of sounds around her. Kara wanted to reassure the sound that she was fine, but she couldn’t move her limbs. Everything hurt too much, and it felt too difficult to find it in herself to remember what it was like to talk. To produce the words that would make the voice feel calmer. So Kara tried to block it out. Maybe if she pretended she wasn’t there she could go back to the darkness around her and black out again. Rao, the bliss of silence and darkness seemed so comforting, beckoning her back with warm open arms and Kara ached to go back. But then she heard it again.

“Kara!”

It was louder this time. Clearer. It stood out from the mess of loudening sounds around her and seemed to pull her from the darkness with tugs and jolts. Her own name felt too sharp, and Kara flinched on the cold, yet quietly comforting spot she was lying, trying to curl her body up as much as possible like it would protect her from the outside noises and the outside chaos that was pressing down on her.

“Kara? Oh my God, Kara!”

Finally, Kara couldn’t ignore the familiar sound of her name anymore. Not when the panicked voice sounded increasingly familiar and pulled something from Kara that made her feel like she had to react to it. A primordial urge to go and run towards the voice rather than hide away in the cold darkness around her.

Kara felt her fingers uncurl painfully, her nails scraping against a rough surface. She swallowed again, and though it felt sharp and uncomfortable, and allowed the dusty taste to spread even further through her body, her body felt more like her own again, as though she could slowly start to reclaim it for herself.

Kara let out a groan again and tried to lift her body off the ground. The pain that shot through her was excruciating, and it took everything inside of her to keep her weight off the ground, balancing precariously on her elbows.

“Oh my God, Kara!”

The voices skidded to a stop beside her, and Kara could feel someone sinking down beside her. She felt warm, leather-gloved hands on her back before her eyes could open and get acquainted with the daylight again. Kara blinked the dust out of her eyes, shying away from the bright beams of light that turned the world an eerie shade of pale yellow. She felt herself being lifted, her hands uselessly dangling around for something to hold onto when they bumped against a thick safety vest. The world went from light yellow to the warmest of browns, and Kara felt herself grow calmer despite the pain. It took a while for the world to come into focus, but ever so slowly, the dark brown became more defined, and paired with the soft pronunciation of her name, Kara finally recognized the worried face of her sister.

“Alex,” she muttered.

“Jesus Christ, Kara,” Alex’s hand cupped her cheek, staring deep into her twitching eyes with so much worry, Kara had to repress the urge to apologize. “Are you okay? How many fingers am I holding up?”

A hand was shoved in front of Kara’s face, and Kara moaned at the speed at which the world kept changing colors around her.

“Three?” she guessed.

Alex’s eyes narrowed, but she begrudgingly put her hand down, and Kara sighed in relief knowing she’d guessed right.

“Just so you know, that isn’t going to get you out of a head scan later.”

Kara made a sound that was halfway between a complaint and a groan, but lucky for her, Alex was more concerned than she was annoyed.

“Here, let me help,” she said softly, putting one arm behind Kara’s back and pulling her up against her front.

“What happened?” Kara asked, letting her head fall against Alex’s shoulder. “Everything was fine and then…”

She wanted to shake her head, but the headache pounding against her skull quickly talked her out of that.

“Kryptonite,” Alex said grimly. “It exploded after you’d cleared this place when we got word of an undefined threat.”

“Oh.”

Kara vaguely remembered that. It was standard procedure. They got the call at the D.E.O., and while Kara hadn’t been able to detect anything abnormal in the office building she’d been called to, procedure called for her to get everyone to safety while the D.E.O.’s teams could scan the neighboring buildings for anything suspicious. Kara remembered going back into the now-empty building and then – nothing.

“Did anyone else get hurt?” she asked.

Alex shook her head. “The bomb didn’t do much damage. It was clearly intended for you. Trace amounts of kryptonite were hidden under the floorboards within remote-controlled explosives.” Her hand glided down Kara’s face, and Kara could tell Alex had to clench her jaw to keep from tearing up. “You’re lucky those guys weren’t able to get their hands on much. There wasn’t nearly enough in there to kill you.”

“Just enough to properly knock me out I guess,” Kara mumbled, bringing her hand up to her forehead.

“And enough to suspend your powers,” Alex said, and Kara looked up with a start. “It might take you a couple of hours before you’ll be back to your superpowered self, but you’re fine,” Alex quickly reassured her. “Be happy it just drained your solar reserves instead of seriously injuring you. I mean, look around!”

Kara did. Apart from some demolished furniture and some blackened walls, the structure of the building seemed remarkably intact and well-preserved. If the employees really wanted to, they could get back to work in that space within a week. Kara frowned.

“So their mission was a complete bust?” she asked. “I’m fine?”

“My guess is they weren’t able to get their hands on much,” Alex said. “They must’ve gathered what they could and hoped for the best. But don’t worry,” her hand ran down Kara’s dusty curls. “Brainy’s already looking into it. We’ll know who tried to hurt you before long.”

Her dark tone made Kara believe those perpetrators were better off hiding away for the rest of their lives in the middle of a Kasnian forest than they would be after Alex was done with them. She shivered and Alex quickly noticed.

“Here,” she uneasily slid her jacket out from under her vest and draped it over Kara’s shoulders. “It’s cold out today,” she smiled a thin smile. “Glad you finally noticed too.”

“Ha ha,” Kara said dryly, her rough voice only adding to Alex’s bemusement. “Sure, make fun of the alien who’s finally cold on the different planet. Very funny.”

Alex laughed, but it wasn’t as heartily as it usually was. She looked ahead and Kara pulled the jacket tighter around herself. Alex took a deep breath, a serious expression hardening on her face, and Kara could immediately tell what was up.

“Look, Kara, about what happened – ”

“We don’t have to talk about it,” Kara interrupted. “Not yet.”

“But – ”

“Alex,” Kara put her hand on Alex’s and managed to cover up her grimace of pain with a small smile. “I know you’re on my side. I do. And we’ll talk about it. But not when I’m covered in dust and you’re feeling guilty because you were scared I might die.”

Alex actually looked sick when Kara used the word ‘die’ but she managed to nod and shot Kara a weak smile.

“Okay,” she whispered. “Okay, that’s… that’s fair.”

She looked at Kara for a beat and then leaned in to kiss the side of her head. Though it hurt, Kara leaned into her touch and relished in the contact.

“What a heartwarming sight. Truly, makes me nostalgic for family times of my own. You know, before we all started trying to kill each other, of course.”

The voice sent shivers down Kara’s spine, and she immediately tensed in Alex’s arms. Alex’s response was quicker. Kara was pushed behind her and her gun was drawn before Kara had even properly processed whose voice could so easily make her skin crawl with fear and disgust.

“Lex,” Alex’s voice was so cold, Kara herself almost buckled. “I should’ve known you’d be here.”

“Well of course,” Lex gestured around the space. He was clad in an expensive, dark, wool coat, and his leather shoes left careless imprints on the dusty floor. “Panic and disruption, a kryptonite explosion, and our favorite superhero temporarily out of commission.” He shook his head, the feigned concern on his face making Kara feel sick to her stomach. “It is my duty as commissioner of the D.E.O. to be here and insure that my employees are safe and cared for.”

He looked at Alex and tilted his head in mock-hurt. “Why you’ve got that gun pointed near my feet, director, I’ll never understand. I come with good intentions.”

“Sure you do, Lex,” Alex said lowly. “This gun is only to ensure that your good intentions stay that way.”

“Oh, director,” Lex shook his head. “Here! To prove I mean no harm.”

He opened the button of his coat, letting it fall open, before raising his palms.

“See?” he waved his hands and smiled. “No weapons. I wouldn’t dare hurt National City’s little Superhero. Especially not with all those cameras around.”

Kara nervously looked over her shoulder and saw that Lex was right. Reporters were already flooding the scene and were just barely kept at bay by the dozens of D.E.O. agents blocking their view.

“You should go change,” Alex said in a hushed tone. “We don’t need the public to know you’ve lost your powers. It’s too risky.”

Kara sighed but eventually nodded and tried to stand up. She let out a pained, little groan, and Alex was instantly there to help pull her up. Her hand was warm and steady on Kara’s ribs, and she allowed herself to let her weight rest on Alex for most of the walk to the back offices.

“I’m going to need a word with you when you’re done there, Supergirl,” Lex noted casually.

“You can talk to her when she has her powers back,” Alex shot back, a protective arm wrapped around Kara’s shoulders, guiding her away from him.

“I’ll just wait until you’re done changing,” Lex said, studying his phone with mild disinterest as if Alex had never said anything. “Take all the time you need. I’m in no hurry.”

Alex opened her mouth to fight back, but Kara put her hand over Alex’s and shook her head. It wasn’t worth it. Lex never was. Alex begrudgingly nodded and led Kara to the back of the office, where she could change in one of the remarkably intact cubicles without anyone’s eyes on her.

“Glasses?” Alex asked softly.

“Boot,” Kara mumbled.

Alex stepped aside so Kara could slip the glasses on her face. It took less than a second for Kara’s pale blue blouse and white skirt to materialize again, and Kara finished off the look with a hair tie Alex passed fairly quickly.

“All done,” Alex whispered.

“All human,” Kara said. “Literally, this time.”

“We should get you home. I’d like to avoid anything big for the next couple of days.”

“Agreed.”

“And no over-exerting yourself,” Alex said sternly. “It’ll only prolong the healing process, and it won’t do you any good. Promise?”

Kara rolled her eyes but nodded, and Alex shot her a small smile.

They both walked back into the main office space, watching as D.E.O. agents worked in teams to both assess the damage and retrieve evidence from the scene.

“Director?” They both turned their heads when one of the agents held out his hand for Alex to see. “We could use a hand here.”

Alex sighed and looked at Kara.

“Go,” Kara said. “I’ll wait.”

Alex nodded and walked off, quickly joining the other agents, becoming part of the mass of black uniforms herself. Kara could see an almost physical transformation in Alex when she joined her team like that. The way the kindness and concern on her face would fall and instantly make way for a steeliness that she only ever seemed to lack with Kara.

Kara watched for a beat, grateful that her body got some rest, some time to get used to the heaviness of the atmosphere without her powers. She watched as Alex crouched down, inspecting the remnants of the bomb. The kryptonite hadn’t survived the blast, so all Alex had to work with were the charred remains of the wood surrounding the explosives, where traces of the materials used to fabricate the bomb could potentially give her some leads. Kara watched as Alex’s brow furrowed, her eyes scanning the patches her agents had pointed out to her.

“You know, I think your sister is doing a terrific job at the D.E.O.”

Kara stiffened when she heard that horrific voice near her ear. She quickly turned and found Lex standing next to her, head tilted in mind fascination as he observed the D.E.O. team at work.

“No really,” he said, “even with the obvious nepotism that landed her the job – her being the sister of one of the greatest powers on earth, that is – she is doing a fine job of it. Don’t you think?”

“I’m not discussing my sister with you,” Kara whispered icily. “I have to answer to you at the D.E.O., but I am most definitely not obliged to engage in small talk.”

Lex shrugged. “As you wish. I just thought your sister was bad at handling criticism, so I thought she might have an easier time handling the review from her little sis. But after all, what do I know?”

Kara frowned and turned to look at him. He was standing there so unnervingly unbothered, calmly observing the bustle around them like it was just another business meeting.

“What criticism?” Kara asked slowly.

Lex pulled a face, and Kara could barely refrain from rolling her eyes at his theatrics. And if Alex weren’t the subject of their conversation, she very well might have. But this was Alex. And nothing good ever came from Lex Luthor putting one of her loved ones’ names in his mouth.

“I’ve just overheard the team saying that Director Danvers is checking the files of some anti-alien protesters, considering them to be prime subjects for this attack.

Kara’s eyes narrowed.

“And what of it?”

Lex shrugged again, a maddeningly neutral and contemplative expression on his face.

“Well in this modern day of our thriving D.E.O. agency, how many kryptonite attacks does one really still encounter? I mean not to brag,” – this time it was Kara who pulled the face – “but we have pretty much eradicated crimes against our Kryptonian superheroes by limiting the amount of kryptonite on earth. Some is at the fortress, I know,” he pointed out, “and a very small amount remains, safely stored away,” he looked at Kara, “at the D.E.O.”

Kara froze.

“What I mean to say here, Supergirl, is that I think it’s pretty strange your sister is so eagerly searching for assailants outside our little bubble, when in reality – ”

“It was you,” Kara realized. She took a step back as Lex shot her a surprised – and almost proud – smile, folding his hands together, patiently waiting for her to continue. “That’s what you’re saying, isn’t it?” Kara demanded. “It was stored away at the D.E.O. where only you had access to it.”

“Well, me, you and Director Danvers, but it does seem unlikely that she would be very eager to blow you up. Unless there is a recent dispute I’m not aware of?”

“Cut the crap!” Kara hissed. “Why would you do this? Why attack me like this? There wasn’t enough kryptonite in there to kill me, you would know that!”

“Why of course I would,” Lex smiled. “Out of pure scientific interest, of course.”

“Why did you do it?” Kara demanded. “So I would lose my powers? So I would be vulnerable? I won’t be powerless for long and you can’t hurt me out in the open.”

Kara nodded at the room around her, filled to the brink with reporters and agents alike. Lex wouldn’t be able to lift a single finger to her without the whole world knowing. And he knew that. And yet… he looked more content than he ever had in her presence, and Kara didn’t like it one bit. Her entire skin had broken out into goosebumps, and she could feel the growing, nagging feeling in the back of her head telling – screaming – that something was very, very wrong.

“Why?” Kara asked again, her voice no louder than a whisper. “You’ve got… there’s nothing you can do.”

Kara’s mind was racing, eyes frantically scanning the windows behind Lex as if a new danger could be lurking behind every brick and every agent. As soon as she had spoken, she knew she was wrong. This was Lex Luthor, and he always had a plan. He was always one step ahead. If he really wanted to kill her, she knew he could very well take a shot. She’d been living under the pretense that his legitimacy and function would at the very least keep him at bay, perhaps not as concerned with her death as he was gloating about the power he held over her. She only realized now how very stupid that idea was. How naïve it was to think that he would just leave her alone. She was fine because he had allowed her to be for so long. He had allowed her more days than she had appreciated, and she would pay for it now. He had had access to kryptonite for ages, she was lucky he only chose to use it now and not earlier. Which begged the question again; why use so little of the kryptonite he had, when he absolutely knew it wouldn’t kill her? Why would he purposefully fail his mission?

“Why?” she asked again, desperation tugging at her words.

She only vaguely registered Alex’s presence still in the room, only a couple of steps behind her. If she screamed before he pulled a hidden knife that even Alex hadn’t spotted, would it give Alex enough time to dash over and save her before Lex plunged it into her throat? Would the agents even turn on Lex if that happened? Or would he have a story ready and massacre her again in on-camera interviews? Kara felt the fear creeping up on her, every second feeling heavier than the last.

“Oh I never intended to hurt you, Supergirl,” Lex said as if the idea itself was too preposterous for him to even contemplate. “I merely needed some… time.”

“Time for what?”

Her words were no louder than a whimper in the loud bustling of the room, but the way in which the corner of Lex’s mouth lifted up told Kara that he had heard her loud and clear.

“I know that you have recently gotten attached to my sister… to my Other Sister if you will.”

Other Lena.

“The thing is, Miss Danvers, that I had high hopes for her. Really, really high hopes. The way she walked into this universe, commanding and powerful?” He clacked his tongue. “I have never seen my little sister own her power that way. Ever. Throughout her life, she’s always remained this mousy, little scaredy-cat, who could never reach her full potential.”

“Don’t talk about her like that,” Kara cut him off. “You’re wrong about her.”

“I don’t think I am. I don’t make mistakes. Lena is as Lena has always been; disappointing. Don’t get me wrong,” he said, “she’s smart. Capable. But you know,” he leaned in like he was expecting Kara to get on board with him. Like he was making sound arguments that Kara would believe. “She had never risen to our name’s potential.” He leaned back and shrugged. “It’s sad. Tragic, even, given what she could accomplish with her mind and our name combined. But ultimately, she has always fallen short.”

Kara was boiling. Her fingers were cramping up with the urge to punch Lex in his smug, self-satisfied face, and not even the knowledge that her bones and flesh were now vulnerable to injury were a very convincing argument to stop her. The witnesses around her were doing a better job of that.

“I guess that is why I was so hopeful when it came to the Other version of her, you know?” he asked, eyes drifting over the busy room.

“What?”

Kara could hold her anger back only because of the notion of Other Lena. Lex was dangling her in front of her as if she would singlehandedly drop to her knees and beg him if he wanted her to. And the worst part was that they both absolutely knew it to be true. Kara felt sick to her stomach just watching him talk about Lena – either version of her.

“Well, let’s be honest here, Supergirl,” he said, sounding surprised, like Kara’s question was so absurd, it had caught him off guard. “She has done nothing but sulk behind a glass wall. The fire that I thought I saw in her when she arrived? Nothing but pretense – a cover for her insecurity and indecisiveness. Tragically mediocre. I know I shouldn’t have hoped,” he said, putting his palms up with a regretful shake of his head, “but I did. I genuinely believed she would be the sister I could work with. A partner. But alas, she is nothing but a knock-off version of the real thing, I suppose. A broken one at that. Sewn together with… scrap metal,” he decided with a disgusted pull of his mouth.

Kara didn’t know what to do with the swelling of anger she felt growing inside of her, threatening to blow her up from the inside out. She couldn’t even begin to point out how wrong Lex was about her – how disgustingly blind he was to Other Lena’s wit, intelligence, and radiance. She was more than Lex could ever imagine, different from everyone else Kara had ever met in her life, and blatantly true to her values in a way that Kara could only admire, no matter how many times she disagreed with her. There was a light in Other Lena that not even years of torture and loneliness had been able to extinguish, and Kara idolized her for it. She was more than what anybody in this universe and the next had ever said about her, and Kara hated that she had to listen to Lex diminish her abilities and thoughts like that… Like he knew her. Like he would be able to comprehend even a fraction of the wondrous things Other Lena was in her being and could do herself despite the horrid world she had to live in. Kara was repulsed by him. And Lex could see it all too clearly written across her face.

“Yes, well, I figured you’d disagree,” he said. “That is why I needed to keep you occupied for a bit while I did some of the… shall we say, decluttering of the D.E.O.”

Kara froze.

“Decluttering?”

Lex sighed. “Miss Danvers, do you know the average cost of a prisoner in the D.E.O.? Let alone a prisoner who requires an entire hall to be at her disposal just because she can’t play well with others? It’s more than triple what you make writing your little puff pieces at CatCo, I can tell you that.”

The words seemed to be coming through a fog. Kara could hear them, but they were slow to enter her mind, to transform into meaningful sentences. Something was dangerously off, and her mind wasn’t ready to accept it yet. It was obscuring everything, just to protect her.

“What are you saying? You’re moving her?”

The second the words came out of her mouth, Kara realized how ridiculously, childishly naïve they sounded. As if Lex would just choose the most non-violent option when he had the ability to hurt her. To destroy her even further, without breaking a sweat.

His next words confirmed her biggest nightmares, and it was enough to make the whole world spin on its head. Everything came crashing down so fast, it felt like Kara had been hit by a bus. The air was knocked from her lungs and her head was spinning so fast, it almost seemed like it was all a bad, bad dream.

“No, Miss Danvers. I’m having her terminated.”

“No,” Kara’s whisper was too quiet, she wasn’t even sure it had really been spoken.

“She is nothing but a waste of money, time, and resources, not to mention a terrible threat to my main superhero and greatest asset, so the decision was easily made. Her death warrant was signed this morning at the financial discussion.”

“No."

Kara stumbled.

"No, no, no.”

“See, I thought you’d react a little bit like this. That is why I did us both the courtesy of removing your powers for a brief spell while my officers can safely execute our decisions.”

Those were the only words that managed to pierce through the cloud of despair in Kara’s head.

She turned to Lex with big, desperate eyes.

Her throat was bone dry when she spoke again.

“So it hasn’t happened yet?” she rasped. “They didn’t… they haven’t done it yet?”

Lex pursed his lips and glanced at his obnoxiously big watch.

“Should be any minute now. No point in delaying the inevitable. Don’t worry, Miss Danvers,” he added with a misplaced, falsely empathetic smile. “I assure you that there is nothing you can do to prevent it. They’re probably getting her out of her cell as we speak.”

“No, no,” Kara whimpered, taking several steps back, stumbling from the unfamiliar heaviness in her limbs. “No, not yet. Not yet.”
