She was begging him. Begging him with everything she had. She felt like a little girl, looking up at someone she hadn’t realized was so big and so powerful – so ready to pulverize every glimpse of happiness in the world. How had she been so naïve? How could she have let this happen?

“Miss Danvers.”

There was a greedy glint in Lex’s eyes, like he was feasting on the misery he’d uncovered in Kara and was watching her fall apart with great pleasure. But Kara wasn’t going to break down. She couldn’t. Not when she still had time.

She still had time.

She could vaguely hear her sister’s alarmed “Kara?” but didn’t – couldn’t – react to it. That part of her brain was shut off. The only thing she could do, the only thing she could allow herself to focus on, was Other Lena. She turned away from Lex, his sly grin nothing more than a hazy memory in the back of her mind as the door away from the room seemed to grow bigger in Kara’s eyes. Even with the world pulsating around her, voices and figures commanding her attention, Kara paid them no mind. She knew where she had to go.

Alex's jacket slipped off her shoulders and fell down somewhere in the room as Kara turned on her heel, and ran.

She ran past the agents at the entrance of the office building and through the crowd of reporters who angrily shouted at her when she pushed past them, oblivious to and uninterested in any of their mundane irritations. She had to get to Other Lena. Kara walked out into the bright afternoon sun shining down on the crowded streets of National City and her heart sank. She was seven blocks away from the D.E.O. Seven long, treacherous blocks filled to the brink with people coming home from work or doing their final shopping for the night.

Kara barely had time to accept what she was going to do. She had no choice. She pushed through. And she ran. She ran through the crowds of people heading in the opposite reaction, ignoring the insulted stares and angry remarks when she brushed against people or knocked bags to the ground.

What did it matter? What did it matter when Kara could see Other Lena so clearly, sitting on her bed, fists clenched, heart sinking when she realized what was going to come. And she would realize it. She would be smart enough to know what it meant when ten guards showed up at her door, expressionless faces as her last contact with humanity before she would be put to death. She wouldn’t show a thing, of course, lips pressed into a tight line and an unimpressed glare at whatever agent tried to guide her up the stairs by her arm. But Kara knew that inside she’d falter. She’d die a little bit, knowing she’d survived so much, come so far, had been the first human to cross fifth-dimensional worlds, and would lose out to her own brother. While Kara was panting for breath, heart hammering in her chest, she wondered whether Other Lena would look around, arching her neck, hoping to catch a final glimpse of Kara – of someone who would actually care if she died.

The thought was enough for Kara to push through the pain in her side and keep running. The people and buildings around her turned into a beige haze. People actually jumped out her way now, probably turning their heads to wonder what would drive a girl like her to run so madly through the afternoon traffic. There were tears in Kara’s eyes, but she didn’t know whether they were from the wind that blew into her open eyes, or from something more sentimental that she didn’t even want to think of.

She watched a cab flash his lights trying to get her to jump in, but she could already see traffic piling up near the traffic lights, and Kara knew she couldn’t stop. She couldn’t stop. She just kept on running. Her feet barely felt the pavement underneath her anymore, bouncing off of it as if she could still fly, faster than she thought she could push her body to be. Her blood was pumping loudly in her ears, drowning out every other noise from the crowd around her.  

She had to get to her.

Kara could see the grey D.E.O. building rise up in the distance, dark and gloomy, and oh so close. If she could just make it. If she could just hold on a little longer… She couldn’t feel her legs anymore, she was running on autopilot, like she would falter and die if she ever stopped. Like she could lose everything.

She was going so fast, and yet not fast enough. She barely felt the pain of running anymore. She wasn’t. She was soaring. Her skirt fluttered around her thighs in a feeling vaguely reminiscent of her early days of being Supergirl. Her feet barely touched the ground before they lifted up again and she was almost, almost there.

Kara ran past one house, two houses, the iron gate that sealed off the D.E.O.’s premises to outsiders, and then – then she sprinted through the door and down the stairway, counting every blessing she wasn’t stumbling over her own feet going down.

She raced past security guards in her civilian clothes, but no one tried to stop her. No one bothered. The thought that she might be too late couldn’t even cross her mind as she slipped over the tiles on her way to the cells. She couldn’t be too late. She couldn’t be.

She couldn’t have been too late twice.

A guy in a suit looked at her with great alarm when she dragged herself through the entrance hall.

“Can I help – ”

“Lena,” she managed to rasp. “Lena?”

The man’s eyebrows knitted together, and he opened his mouth to say anything, but the weirded-out expression on his face just confirmed to Kara that she would find out what she needed faster if she went out and looked for information herself. She pushed past him and didn’t even allow him to stop her. She had to keep moving.

Kara picked up her pace again and ran through the next hall, opening the door to the darkened staircase that would lead her… lead her to Other Lena. Kara didn’t pause to take a breath, just continued onwards. Kara rounded the corner and Rao the hall was so quiet and was it darker than it had been before? Had someone turned off the lights? Were all the cells empty?

Kara passed one cell, then another, and another. Her eyes remained trained on the empty glass cells on her left side, stumbling more than running as her body finally seemed to realize the distance she had run and was just waiting for that one unfocused moment to make her feel it all at once. One more cell, another. Another

Kara’s heart sank with every cell she passed. Why had she never counted them before? How did she not know where Other Lena was? Why did the hallway seem so endless? Her heart was racing, her breathing so shallow, she almost feared passing out before she could get to the final cell. She skidded past the last couple of cells, stumbling over her feet, heart racing, breaths shallow and terrified, and then –

“What’s got you in such a hurry, Supergirl? So eager to see me?”

Kara’s mouth fell open as Other Lena chuckled from her spot on the bed, perfectly cozy in her dark blue slacks and T-shirt, an open book on her lap.

Kara couldn’t react. Her lack of experience with powerless-exercise had finally caught up to her, and her lungs were screaming inside her chest. There was a horrifying, stinging ache in her side that had her leaning over, one hand clutching at her stomach to keep upright. But her eyes never left Other Lena. 

She was there. She was still there. She was okay. And Kara almost buckled on the spot.

Other Lena looked back up at Kara and her laugh slowly disappeared.

“Supergirl?” she asked, standing up. “What’s wrong?”

It was only then that Kara felt how red her eyes were, tears and dust having mixed on her face to end up in what she could only assume to be a horrifying look. She was still gasping for breath, the relief of seeing Other Lena alive and well not fully having settled in yet. There was just Other Lena standing there, looking so confused, while Kara could barely comprehend what was happening.

“Supergirl, breathe,” Other Lena said slowly. “What’s going on?”

“I thought – ” Kara had to stop when her own coughing interrupted her. “I thought you were dead.” Her voice broke midway – and she struggled to catch her breath again.

“Dead?” Other Lena smiled confusedly. “What makes you think that?”

Through wheezing sounds and coughs, Kara miraculously succeeded in piecing the story together, her hands trembling still when she finished her story. Other Lena’s expression had darkened significantly throughout her explanation, and the storm on her face spoke entirely for her as she remained eerily quiet.

Kara finished her story with another bout of coughing but finally managed to stand upright again, arms crossed over her chest to hold on.

“Supergirl,” Other Lena said. “The D.E.O. might be a clandestine, protective institution, it still wouldn’t go so far as to play judge, jury, and executioner so openly. Not when Lex has put it front and center in every media outlet in the country. I mean, he’s evil and all that, but he wouldn’t be so reckless as to just let the D.E.O. and his own company get bad press for unethical treatment of prisoners, let alone the murder of one.”

“That…”

“Supergirl, did any of the agents upstairs actually look like they were preparing for a mission to kill a prisoner without due process?” She could almost smile.

“I… I don’t think so? They were just… working, I guess.”

“See,” Other Lena threw her a little smile, “I don’t think they would quietly be contemplating executing a war crime, you know? I think you might’ve noticed if they were about to murder someone in cold blood.”

Kara didn’t know what to say to that.

That…. actually sounded very logical. Kara wanted to say something, put the pieces together, but she came up empty. The situation didn’t make any sense.

“But then…” she paused. “Then why would he do all this? He didn’t attack me. My powers won’t out for long and I’m in a secured base with people who know me… Why would…”

Other Lena’s smile dimmed, her brow creasing while a certain unease crept up on her.

“I don’t know. I don’t – ”

They both looked up when the door at the end of the hall opened again.

“Lena,” Kara sighed in relief. “What are you – ”

“Alex called.”

“So – ”

“You need to leave right now, Kara,” Lena warned, rushing towards them. “Right now!”

“But I just – ”

“Lex has a plan, he always does. Kara, you have to – ”

They were interrupted by two short beeps coming from the inside of Other Lena’s cell. Kara’s head turned, and she heard a slow hiss coming from Other Lena. Her hand came to clutch her chest, where a light was shining through the dark material of her top.

“Lena?” Kara asked shakily.

“My vest,” she murmured.

Kara’s eyes glanced down, and she saw the outline of something straight and bulky underneath Other Lena’s shirt.

“What is that?”

“It’s the compression vest that’s containing the kryptonite,” Lena said, coming to a stop just a couple of steps away from Kara. "It has a remote lock for... for safety issues," she faltered.

Kara could only shake her head. Nothing worked, nothing clicked, until she looked up into Other Lena’s eyes.

She was trembling, her hand pressing down on her chest in pain, and Kara could see a vague, green glow emanating from between her fingers. The glass was keeping Kara from feeling any of it, but just to see it again made Kara’s heart quicken up. Her eyes flickered between the green shine under Other Lena’s hand and Other Lena’s eyes, which seemed to hold a myriad of emotions. There was confusion, fear – and then there was something that Kara couldn’t understand. A coldness that Kara hadn’t seen in a while. Something that made the hairs on her arms stand up and made it hard to swallow. Her fingers twitched by her side and she suddenly felt very, very seen by Other Lena. She was caught in those green-blue eyes, and things finally seemed to click in place and made Kara’s heart fall in her chest. The world slowed down, Lena’s panicked sounds sounding further away than before, and Kara felt a sense of dread push down on her chest again?

She took a step back, shook her head.

“Lena,” she whispered. Sorrow was tugging on her words, but Other Lena merely clenched her jaw, a rigid iciness had replaced the warmth and mirth that had been there not too long ago.

“Kara, we have to leave now!”

Lena took hold of Kara’s hand, trying to pull her away from the cells. Her fingers digging into her hand so tightly, Kara almost flinched. But Kara’s eyes remained locked with Other Lena’s.

And Other Lena’s eyes burned.

“Lena – ”

Kara didn’t have any words, there was nothing she could find, nothing to say, nothing that could stop what was coming.

Then a second beeping sound rang through the hallway, a button on the edge of the cell lighting up. Kara stiffened, and Lena’s hand felt clammy in her own, holding on so tight until her fingers went white around her own. Kara heard her sharp intake of breath, and she knew it was too late. She just knew it.

And then Other Lena’s door clicked open.

Chapter 11

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Other Lena stepped out of the cell with careful, hesitant steps, almost as if she was expecting the door to still be shut when she walked through it. Like the loneliness of her stay at the D.E.O. cells had finally gotten to her, and had driven her insane. Had her seeing things that weren’t real at all. Her eyes narrowed as she watched the door, stepping through it. But it didn’t close. Kara knew it wouldn’t.

The second Other Lena had officially descended the slight step of her cell and stepped foot on the dark tiles in the hallway, Lena’s nails dug into Kara’s wrist. While Kara could feel the little half-moon creases slowly denting her skin, she was too numb to register any pain at all.

Other Lena was now right in front of her, with not one millimeter of glass between them.

“Lena,” Kara whispered. There was a hint of enchantment in her tone, one she didn’t know how to get rid of.

“Kara!”

Lena’s terrified voice came out as a low hiss and made Kara feel only more on edge. She wanted to reassure her, go with her, do anything to help her feel at ease again, but she couldn’t move. She just kept staring. Other Lena was there. She was right there. And Kara didn’t quite know how to run when everything inside her wanted to stay put – and stay with her.

Lena noticed. She was trembling and frantically looked from Kara to her Other Self. She had both hands clasped around Kara’s left one, trying to pull her away from Other Lena without success. In her heart, Kara knew that Lena had the only right reaction. She was in danger. Rationally, critically, she knew that. But Rao, did she not want to listen to that part of her brain.

“Don’t you hurt her,” Lena suddenly hissed. “Don’t you fucking touch her!”

Kara was taken aback by the adrenaline rush in Lena’s words, the way her fear gave way to anger so easily, even though they both knew they were on the losing side this time. There was no winning this.

Other Lena’s eyes fell on Lena for just one brief second – Lena’s fingers tightened around Kara’s wrist – before she seemed to deem her too unimportant and insignificant to spend even a fraction of her thoughts on, and her eyes snapped back to Kara.

She took another step forward and Lena yanked Kara back, while Kara stumbled on her feet. Her body hadn’t caught up to the reality that she needed to run away. Maybe it had, but it just didn’t want to, stubbornly planting her feet in the ground to catch just one more glimpse of Other Lena.

Lena’s eyes narrowed between the two of them, and a tension thick enough to smother Kara filled the air. Every semblance of a movement on Other Lena’s part made Lena tense up more beside her, and it seemed like she was stuck between running away and running towards her Other Self.

But it was pointless. Kara knew it. If they ran, Other Lena would just rip off the security strip around her chest and kill Kara before they had a chance to reach the door. But if they stayed, Lena would fight. Kara knew she would. She could feel it in every fingernail breaking her skin. And she would get hurt. It would be a struggle, absolutely, but there was no way the fight would end well, and Kara knew she couldn’t risk Lena’s safety. She was powerless, but she was still Supergirl. She could still tell that nothing good would come from fighting Other Lena with Lena so defensively by her side.

So she did the one thing she could do. The one thing, still in her power.

She waited until the very last second. She clenched her jaw, every hair on her body standing up straight. A cold shiver ran down her spine, but Kara didn’t let it show. She kept her eyes trained on Other Lena and refused to let that mixture of blue and green falter for even a second. She could see the tension in Other Lena’s limbs, the anticipation in the way her narrowed eyes didn’t blink. Like a predator waiting to pounce. But Kara was ready for it.

She was ready.

The second Kara could see a change in the way Other Lena’s muscles shifted under her skin, she reacted too. She ignored the way Other Lena finally advanced, and used the momentum she had to turn around. And with all the power she still had, before the fear and alarm had even hit Lena at all, Kara’s hands found Lena’s shoulders and pushed her away as hard as she could. She still managed to catch the surprise and betrayal in Lena’s eyes in the split second it took her to realize what was happening, before she was knocked backward, sliding away over the tiles, falling on the floor, far enough away from Kara for Other Lena to kill her before Lena had the time to intervene.

Somehow Kara knew that if Other Lena got the chance to hurt her, she wouldn’t bother with Lena anymore. She’d be calm then, she hoped. Lena would be sad, furious, even, but she would remain unharmed if only Other Lena got the chance to do what she had so desperately wanted for years. If only she could execute her mission, uninterrupted.

All those thoughts flooded Kara’s mind, and a bizarre sense of peace fell over her. As if in slow-motion, she could feel her head turning to see Other Lena getting closer. She felt the hands on her forearms where Lena’s had just been, so ironically protective, before. Kara closed her eyes briefly and felt those nails digging into her skin like claws, pushing her backward until her back hit the wall.

She could hear Lena’s piercing scream through the hallway and opened her eyes to see Other Lena staring right back at her. One hand released Kara’s arm and flew to her chest, ready to rip off the protective cover that would kill Kara in seconds now that she was so weak and vulnerable before her.

But for some weird reason that Kara herself couldn’t really conceive of, she wasn’t scared. Not at all. She felt a strange sort of calm wash over her, with Other Lena’s hand letting go of her arm in favor of pinning her against the wall with her arm locked against Kara’s chest. And Kara stayed so very still.

She could already feel it, the green poison that worked to penetrate her skin. She could feel an uncomfortable, burning heat on the exposed skin peeking out from above the V-neckline of her blouse. It clawed her way up her throat, and Kara had to swallow to avoid the urge to cough. She could tell that if she glanced down, she would already see green lines creeping up her veins. But Kara didn’t want to see. She didn’t care.

It would be over soon if Other Lena wanted. So she opted to look straight at her instead. To take in her features one last time, if this really was how Other Lena saw their story end. If this really was the way to go. If Alex and Lena, and everybody else who had ever warned her about this, would be proven right. If she’d really been so wrong. An accumulation of her worst decisions, staring back at her.

Other Lena’s arm pressed down on her chest and Kara flinched in discomfort. It was a laughably minor sense of discomfort. Pain that would be insignificant, even if she wasn’t confronted with hellish pains yet to come. It was nothing, absolutely nothing in the face of what was to happen. It was a dull ache that wouldn’t even leave a bruise. One she could ignore. Her flinching was entirely instinctive, her body reacting to the suddenness of it all more so than the weight pushed against her chest, and yet, her face had shown a reaction.

A brief spell of discomfort written across her face in only the blink of an eye. But one that hadn’t escaped Other Lena. Her eyes fluttered down to see what had elicited Kara’s reaction, and as if she’d suddenly realized she’d hugged a friend too tight, she looked up, and for just a brief second, Kara thought she could see an apology ready to go on those lips.

And then Other Lena hesitated.

Kara saw it in her eyes. The brief flash of panic, the sudden realization that what she was doing was not going the way she’d planned. There was something in Other Lena’s eyes that clouded the wariness and calculated tension from before.

Kara thought she could see something break.

Other Lena’s fingers clenched around the strip closing off the kryptonite on her chest. Her fingers were white and trembling. She was so ready. One quick pull and it would all be over. She would be done. She would have everything she ever wanted, everything she came to this world to do.

And yet she didn’t.

The arm on Kara’s chest didn’t back off, but it seemed to tense up even more like it wasn’t sure what was happening around them either. It pushed a little harder against Kara’s chest, the dull ache blossoming uncomfortably. A storm of emotions flashed in Other Lena’s eyes – anger, worry, and then… traces of doubt.

Kara could see all of it flickering in her eyes, and she could feel her heart break a little for her.

“Please don’t!”

Kara couldn’t see her, but the panic in Lena’s voice was enough to make her stomach drop. She could just tell that Lena had gotten up from where she’d been pushed on the floor before, wanting so badly to intervene, but also entirely synchronized with Kara’s thinking. One wrong move and Kara would be dead. The direct exposure to kryptonite would destroy the frail, sun-less cells of her body, and she’d hit the ground before Lena would be able to get a single punch in.

Kara didn’t want Lena to see this. She didn’t want her to realize that they’d failed. That their plan to reform Other Lena – their hope to humanize her, had been in vain. Lena would see her worst fears come to life, and Kara just knew she wouldn’t be able to live with the consequences.

Her throat felt sore when she tried to call out to her.

“Lena.”

“Please!” Lena’s name was drowned out by the desperation in Lena’s voice, and Kara wished she could look at her. Wished she could reassure her, or make it better, just one last time.

“Please don’t – I will give you anything – everything! You can have everything, just please don’t – ”

A sob so painful rang through the air, and though it seemed to have no effect on Other Lena, it made all of it so much harder on Kara.

Leave, she wished she could say. Turn around and run far, far away. Pretend you’ve never met me. Start over. Leave, leave, leave.

But Lena stayed. Unwaveringly loyal to a fault.

“This can’t be what you want, please!”

Kara shifted against the wall, the bones in Other Lena’s arm increasingly more unbearable against her chest, slowly pushing the air out of her lungs, and making it so much harder to fill them with air again. Her chest was starting to ache, and Kara felt an uncomfortable heat spread from her neck to her back, just itching to move away from the suffocating hold.

“It’s okay,” she murmured. She only got the words out on the second try, her throat raw and painful from the traces of kryptonite already permeating the air around her. She didn’t know who she was talking to at that moment, and wasn’t even quite sure they’d come out at all.

Other Lena’s jaw clenched. Her eyes bore into Kara’s with renewed fire, her fingers clenching even harder around the fabric on her chest. Kara felt a burst of more kryptonite hitting her as Other Lena’s hand tugging at the fabric invertedly released more of the substance into the air around her.

She closed her eyes in pain and placed her palms flat on the wall behind her. She took a few deep breaths, trying to manage the surge of fire in her veins that made it so unimaginably hard to breathe. She let out a quiet moan, trying to gain ground on the pain creeping up so easily through every cell of her body. One breath, two breaths, and Kara finally managed to contain the pain in her body, to not let her entire mind fall victim to it again. She allowed the constant of pain pulsing through her to find its place along her other rhythms and forced herself not to lose count of her breaths. In and out, through the pain.

Kara opened her eyes again and blinked tiredly at Other Lena. Her own were probably bloodshot from the lack of oxygen that the Kryptonite prevented from circulating in her blood. The conflicted expression in her eyes made Kara’s heart soften, and she felt herself go a little slacker under Other Lena’s arm. With great difficulty, almost wrangling a sob out of her chest as she strained, Kara lifted her arm slightly, and laid her hand on top of Other Lena’s.

Other Lena’s eyes flashed, immediately falling to their hands, like she was expecting to see Kara weakly trying to fight her off, to push her away – but nothing happened. Kara didn’t want to fight, and she was almost sad to know that Other Lena would expect Kara to attack at all. Like she hadn’t long ago lost all the will and energy to fight any version of Lena at all.

But Other Lena faltered when Kara’s hand didn’t do anything but rest on hers. Kara’s fingers moved once, as if to get comfortable on the surface of Other Lena’s skin, but it didn’t remotely resemble a squeeze. It was a flutter of a movement like she was reminding both herself and Other Lena that she was still there.

Kara could vaguely hear Lena in the background, but it faded when she found Other Lena’s eyes burning in her own again. Everything faded. The tip of her finger felt the vein under Other Lena’s skin, and traced it in a therapeutic, repetitive movement that she hoped would be calming for at least one of them.

Kara heard Other Lena’s breath hitch in her throat before she could actually see a change reflected in her eyes. Could feel the muscles in Other Lena’s arm tremble against her chest. Her jaw clenched, her lips were pulled so tight Kara could see their color draining away. Kara unconsciously held her breath as well, waiting as Other Lena’s jaw set. Her own eyes fluttered as something wild flashed in Other Lena’s and then –

“Fuck.”

Kara released a shuddering gasp as Other Lena’s warm breath hit her collar bones. Her flesh broke out in goosebumps when she saw how her head was lowered, forehead hovering at the height of her chin. Other Lena’s entire body was shaking, her arm trembling so badly against Kara’s chest that the pressure seemed laughable compared to the threat she had seemed to pose earlier. The scent of the sterile, citrusy D.E.O. issued shampoo felt strangely familiar and clouded her senses for just a second.

“Fuck,” Other Lena whispered again, a wild, confused sob accompanying her words in a way that made Kara jump a little.

They stayed like that for what felt like an eternity. They could’ve been frozen like that for hours. Kara’s world was nothing but her own heartbeat racing in her ears, the dull ache under her skin, and the scent of Other Lena’s D.E.O-issued shampoo in the air.

But when Kara felt Other Lena’s hair brushing against her skin, something clicked in her mind, something instinctive forcing her to let go of everything that kept her glued to the wall behind her, and she shuddered. Her body moved before she had decided what it should do, and without thinking – without an ounce of impulse control – Kara moved, uncaring and unbothered about what reactions she could provoke. Kara moved forward and in one fluid move, gently moved Other Lena’s arm on her chest, so that it didn’t keep pushing on the tender spot. Other Lena didn’t protest. Her muscles didn’t clench, her eyes didn’t flash. Instead, she only winced slightly, letting herself be moved, until Kara’s hand moved up towards her jaw, and calmly lifted her head, so Other Lena was facing her again. Other Lena trembled, but she slowly opened her eyes, a wet, defeated yet defiant shine casting a softer hue over her blue-green irises. 

“Lena,” Kara whispered, and it came out like a reverent prayer, like she was unable to hide the wonder in her own voice.

“Don’t,” Other Lena whispered, shaking her head slightly. “Don’t.”

“It’s okay – ”

“I said don’t!”

Kara winced and Other Lena immediately softened.

“Please,” she whispered. “I can’t… I don’t know. I don’t – ” She shook her head and Kara felt everything inside her soften for the woman before her once again. Like every word she uttered could elicit a physical reaction from Kara without trying.

“Lena,” Kara’s heart broke just whispering that name.

“Don’t,” Other Lena murmured. “Don’t. Don’t, don’t, don’t.”

Her voice finally broke amid her stream of words, and though Kara wanted nothing more than to reach out to her, she didn’t dare say anything. She was too afraid to even breathe wrong, breaking the fragile state of Other Lena’s reticence to attack her. As if one single, wrong glance could set her off again.

“I don’t know what to do now,” Other Lena whispered, and when she looked back at Kara, there was a silent plea in her eyes. “Tell me – I don’t know what to do. I don’t – ”

And it was like Kara just understood.

“Okay,” she whispered, “it’s okay.”

“No, it’s not!” Other Lena hissed through the wave of emotions on her face. “It’s not, you know it’s not! It’s not right, I don’t… I don’t know what to do.”

“It’s okay,” Kara said. “I don’t either.”

Other Lena actually seemed to calm down at that. Like the honesty in Kara’s words had halted the emotions bubbling up inside of her, and she was only left with mild surprise and genuine relief. As if Kara matching her inability to comprehend anything that was happening around them was a comforting reassurance that she wasn’t going insane, not knowing what to do. That she was still on the right track, despite not having any certainties to hold onto anymore.

Kara wasn’t dead. Her cell wasn’t holding her anymore. And she couldn’t seem to do the one thing she had crossed the universe for. She had nothing to cling to when she couldn’t bring herself to kill Kara.

“I don’t – ”

“I know,” Kara whispered before Other Lena had a chance to spiral even further than she already had.

And somehow she did know. She could see it so clearly; having that one goal, that one thing to keep you going, the one thing that would be powerful enough to have you bite your teeth and cross the unknown – to cross universes, worlds, and sometimes, in Kara’s case, even planets. And when all that fell away, Kara could understand so perfectly how the earth would seem so unsteady under her own feet.

“I know,” she whispered again, less steady this time, like her body had to hear the words to process them, to relive them. “I know.”

And when Other Lena’s eyes caught hers, there was a spark of understanding, and something softened in the other woman’s face. Like the fear, the disbelief, and the frustration with herself seemed to become less important, seeing something similar reflected in Kara’s eyes. Like it made everything else less important.

“I can’t stop,” Other Lena whispered earnestly.

“Why not?”

“This is what I have to do. This is what I came here to do.” Her teeth gritted with every new word. “This can’t all have been for nothing.”

“Maybe it wasn’t.”

“You don’t know that.”

Kara heard a whimper coming from further down the hall, and knew that Lena’s patience with the situation was wearing thin. She prayed she would remain quiet. Remain invisible, just this once. Anything could set Other Lena off, and Kara didn’t want Lena to be the trigger.

“I can’t stop you,” Kara said softly.

Other Lena let out a silent, dry sob, eyes clenching shut as an expression of absolute misery flashed over her features.

“Don’t,” she whispered. “Please don’t.”

“Lena – ”

“Why did you do it?” Other Lena hissed, tears now angrily clouding her eyes.

“Do what?”

“Those visits!” she demanded. “The books, the games, the… the – all of it! Why did you do it? Why did you try to get close to me, huh? Did you do it precisely for this? So that you could manipulate me into feeling sorry for you when the time came?”

“No,” Kara winced, fighting against the arm on her throat, fingers digging into Other Lena’s flesh to pry her off of her.

“Then why?” Other Lena’s eyes flashed. “Why did you do it?”

“Because I care about what happens to you,” Kara said hoarsely.

“Bullshit!” Other Lena hissed.

“It’s not!” Kara insisted – suddenly just as angry as Other Lena was. Just angry enough to ignore the pressure on her windpipe, and push into her attacker. “Do what you want, kill me, hurt me, I don’t care. But don’t you for one second dare to twist what I did for you into something dirty. It wasn’t, and you damn well know that! I care! I always have! You don’t get to just take that away to justify what you’re about to do! I won’t let you!”

The words were sharp, aimed like arrows at Other Lena’s skin, and Kara could almost see where they had landed. Other Lena faltered for just one second before she regained her footing. She shook her head. Her throat bobbed as she closed her eyes, one stray tear running over her face. Kara regretted everything instantly.

“Lena – I didn’t…”

But before Kara could say another word, Other Lena’s hands were gone from her body, and Other Lena’s weight was gone from her chest. Kara gasped, the surprise of the sudden departure of warmth and pain leaving her strangely cold, fingers twitching to grab a hold of that heat again.

Other Lena had twisted away from her. Kara couldn’t see her face, but she could see how she trembled, arms clutched around her body like she was trying to keep the pieces of her scarred chest together.

Kara’s fingers glided over her chest, but felt no wounds, no painful cuts, just the thrumming of her racing heart pounding against her chest. Slowly, ever so slowly, she pulled herself up a little straighter, and watched the trembling woman before her.

She took a hesitant step forward, all too aware of Lena’s restless, alarmed eyes, watching from just a few paces away. Kara could almost feel how badly she wanted to yell at Kara to get out, to grab the chance she had gotten by some miracle, and escape while she still could. While Other Lena was still conflicted. As if she thought Other Lena could still change her mind so very quickly.

But Kara paid no mind to her friend’s unspoken concerns, and slowly advanced to where Other Lena stood. Shaky, unsure, and upset.

Kara reached out a shaky hand.

“Lena?” she whispered.

Other Lena didn’t turn around.

Kara’s hand touched her shoulder, and Other Lena flinched, jerking her shoulder away until Kara’s hand dropped uselessly to swing by her side.

“Lena,” she tried again, softer.

“Don’t,” Other Lena hissed. “Don’t.”

Kara felt her heart grow heavy with the renewed coldness in Other Lena’s voice, but quickly felt it shatter when she spoke again.

“You did this to me,” she whispered, a hint of sad desperation clinging to her words. “You did this.”

Kara didn’t bother correcting her. Not anymore.

“You… You did this,” Other Lena whispered, and the roughness of her voice made Kara wonder whether she was swallowing down tears that yearned to spill. “But I can’t. I can’t…”

She took a faltering breath. Her head lowered.

“I can’t kill you,” she said. “And you did this. You – you…”

She couldn’t finish her sentence, and Kara wouldn’t let her. Instead, she took a step forward and allowed her hand to hover by Other Lena’s side.

“Lena,” she whispered, close enough to see how the breathy words caused the hairs in Other Lena’s neck to stand up.

Other Lena didn’t turn. She sniffled and turned her head inward like she was trying to hide further away from Kara, as if she could protect herself better that way.

“Please.”

Kara’s whisper felt more like a prayer.

“Please, Lena.”

Kara could see the muscles in Other Lena’s arm tense up. It remained tense for the longest time, trembling and resisting inward forces that Kara couldn’t comprehend.

But then her fist lowered by her side, and her fingers unclenched. They twitched in the space between Kara’s, searching, doubting, for the longest time. But just then, like they had a couple of times before, Other Lena’s fingers bumped against Kara’s. And like they had known each other in another lifetime, there was a spark of recognition, of electricity, running up Kara’s arm when they touched. It felt just as magical, just as forbidden and sacred as their touches through the hatch, when they’d exchanged books and games. That felt like centuries ago now.

She let out an audibly shaky breath.

And then, the searching stopped. Other Lena’s fingers touched Kara’s, and then quickly, deliberately, convincedly, intertwined with hers. And Other Lena squeezed their intertwined hands as tightly as she could, tight enough to hurt, tight enough to turn both their sets of fingers pale white.

And Kara had never felt more relieved.

Kara squeezed back, just as tightly, as if she wanted to apologize, fight, make up, and welcome Other Lena, all in that one squeeze of their hands. She stepped closer, until her chin hit Other Lena’s shoulder, and felt the soft cotton of her prison suit against her skin.

There was nothing Kara could say. Nothing that hadn’t been expressed by their hands already. But still, she felt the overwhelming urge to say something, to convince Other Lena to turn around.

“Lena?”

Other Lena sniffled.

“Lena,” Kara said, softer this time.

Other Lena pulled her shoulders up like she was trying to hide away from Kara’s voice.

“Please, Lena,” Kara whispered.

“I don’t know what to do.”

Other Lena’s voice was so quiet, it sounded more like a far-away whimper, and Kara wasn’t sure she’d even heard.

“I… I don’t know what to do now,” Other Lena whispered, only a fraction louder than before.

“That’s okay,” Kara said quickly, “we’ll figure something out, I promise.”

Slowly, Other Lena turned around, and the expression of utter defeat on her face made Kara’s heart sink. Her eyes were filled with unspilled tears, one hand pushing against the faint, green glow poking around the edges of her torn shirt. Her whole body seemed to tremble like she got hit with such a sudden, absolute tiredness, that if she were to fall down now, Kara wouldn’t be surprised. She’d never seen someone so terrifyingly strong, be so utterly weak before. It broke her heart.

“We’ll make something work,” she reiterated, her voice now just as faint as Other Lena’s.

Other Lena looked at Kara and gave her an imperceptible nod, but Kara wasn’t sure Other Lena really believed her.

“Okay,” she finally whispered.

“Okay,” Kara said, the immense relief she felt flooding over her almost enough to make her float right up. “Okay.”

Her eyes searched Other Lena’s face, and found that the other woman had a hard time even looking her in the eye.

Other Lena raised her hand to wipe her face clean, and Kara felt immeasurably sorry for her. She waited patiently until Other Lena brought her hand down, and only then realized she was still holding her other one. Other Lena didn’t seem to notice, so Kara didn’t let go. She was more focused on the red rim around Other Lena’s eyes. On the way her nose had also turned a darker shade of pink, along with her cheeks – though the rest of her face seemed even paler than before.

“So?” Other Lena asked hesitantly.

“Right,” Kara snapped out of her private reveries instantly, like she’d been caught red-handed. She quickly shook her nerves off and looked at the only person around who would know what to do next. She turned to Lena.

Lena was stiff and looked so disheveled compared to how Kara had seen her before. She may not have been crying, but her face was red from what Kara thought to be holding her breath, waiting to see how the scenario would play out. She was breathing too quickly, her chest rising and falling too fast to be normal, and Kara felt an instant gush of guilt knowing that she had left Lena to cope with the situation by herself, with no control over what would happen. How terrifying it had to have been, standing far enough away to know there was nothing she could do, yet close enough to observe how fragile the situation was, and how quickly it could go sideways, without her standing a single chance of reversing it. Kara swallowed and caught Lena’s slightly bewildered eyes.

Kara took a step toward Lena. Other Lena followed her a couple of steps but came to a tentative halt just a couple of meters away from her counterpart. Kara almost didn’t notice, until her arm went taut, holding Other Lena’s from afar. She looked back with a questioning glance in her eyes, but Other Lena seemed to understand and quickly let go, bringing the hand up to join her other one in protecting her vulnerable chest. 

Kara wanted to reach back, but she also desperately needed to move forward. Knowing that Other Lena was behind her, waiting, was enough for Kara to push through. She took one step, two steps, while Lena took her own steps closer too – and suddenly Kara was right before Lena again.

Lena looked her up and down, her body trembling with emotions that Kara couldn’t decipher. She was breathing loudly, clearly trying to hold back, if the bulging vein near her temple was any indication. She looked conflicted, fingers flexing into loose fists every few seconds.

Kara swallowed her nerves and felt oddly vulnerable under Lena’s searching eyes.

“I…”

“Are you alright?” Lena asked. Her voice was rough, shaky.

Kara nodded quickly. “Fine,” she whispered hoarsely. “I’m fine.”

Lena’s fingers were a cool and surprising sensation, lifting up her chin, and Kara jumped a little. But when her eyes passed Lena’s, she found herself being lifted up still, missing Lena’s gaze. Lena’s worried eyes didn’t stay on her face but lingered at the sight of her neck. Then, before Kara could register it, two of Lena’s fingers brushed up against her neck, just above her left collar bone. The touch was so sudden, so light, it made Kara falter. A shiver ran down her spine, and she couldn’t for the life of her tear her eyes away from Lena again.

“You’re hurt,” Lena murmured. Kara barely heard it.

“Huh?”

Lena blinked, and then looked at Kara.

“You’ve got bruises,” her fingers tip-toed along a horizontal line on her neck. “Right here. A whole necklace of them.”

“Oh,” Kara took a step back, gently taking Lena’s hand and bringing the reluctantly stiff fingers down. “It’s nothing. It doesn’t hurt.”

That was a lie. The pain thrummed a little, right around where Other Lena’s arm had pressed up against Kara’s chest and neck. But she could stand it. Besides, by Alex’s calculation, she didn’t have much time as a human left. They’d be gone before Kara would even have the time to see them in the mirror.

Kara caught Lena’s gaze and tried to get her to smile, by forcing a weak smile on her own face.

“See,” Kara shrugged. “All good.”

Lena’s lower lip quivered, and she shook her head in a barely noticeable move.

“Lena – oh!”

Kara’s words were cut off by Lena’s strong arms wrapping themselves around her shoulders, careful not to brush up against the painful bruising on her neck. Lena squeezed her tight, pulling her in close enough for Kara to almost feel slightly dazed by the scent of Lena’s delicate perfume. Lena’s fingers dug almost painfully through the fabric of Kara’s shirt, into the skin of her shoulder below. The pain was so, so welcome.

“Don’t,” Lena said sternly. “Don’t you ever put me through something like that again. Don’t you ever expect me to stand by again while you – fuck.”

Kara’s hand slowly, but almost of its own volition, came up to rest on Lena’s waist. Lena only whimpered, and pulled her closer.

“Not fucking ever, you hear me?”

“I, I do,” Kara said quickly. “I’m sorry.”

Lena sniffed.

“Yeah,” she said with the smallest voice. “You better.”

Kara couldn’t help but smile, and could feel Lena’s conflicted half-chuckle, half-sob against the side of her head.

“I’m alright,” Kara said softly. “We’re okay.”

She felt Lena nodding against her shoulder, and after holding on for just a few seconds longer, they both reluctantly separated. Lena was still sniffling, and her eyes were suspiciously red-rimmed, in an eerie reflection of her Other Version’s face just moments before, but when their eyes locked, she still managed to throw Kara a small smile.

Kara turned around and saw Other Lena staring at the ground with a small frown on her face. Uneasy and uncomfortable, she had folded her arms around herself, keeping her chest covered as best she could. When she felt Kara’s eyes on her though, she looked up, and her defenses seemed to drop at least a little bit. Her arms, while still crossed over her chest, went a little slacker, and her eyes softened considerably. Kara smiled and motioned her forward. Other Lena’s eyes went colder when she saw her counterpart, but she merely pursed her lips and stepped forwards, until she reached Kara’s side, which Kara counted as a major win.

Kara nervously looked from Lena to the Other Lena, but no one said a thing. The atmosphere, which had just turned from homicidal to slightly peaceful, grew colder just by having the two women standing so close to each other, and Kara instinctively wanted to push between them.

Maybe that was it, she mused. Maybe two versions of the same person just weren’t meant to exist in the same universe. Nothing good ever seemed to come of it. Even her own counterpart, split from her own soul, could not have handled a coexistent life, and maybe it was too much of Kara to expect more from her two Lenas. Maybe it was too much to expect from any sane human being.

But while her mind was racing, trying to come up with a theoretical foundation as to why the situation might still go sideways, something shifted in the dynamic. Kara held her breath as she watched Lena calmly – if not with a slightly clenched jaw – nod once in Other Lena’s direction. She could have gotten whiplash from how fast her neck snapped to see Other Lena’s reaction. But Other Lena merely raised her chin, facing her Other Half straight on. And eventually, to Kara’s surprise, Other Lena didn’t attempt to smirk or snark her way out of the situation. Instead, she nodded back, and then diverted her gaze.

Kara could feel the rush of relief enter her lungs like a breath of fresh air, and she could barely repress a nervous smile. Lena caught her eyes though and threw her the briefest and thinnest of smiles to reassure her.

Then the door opened, and everyone flinched.

Kara pushed in front of Other Lena the moment she recognized who it was.

“Alex, don’t!” Kara said, spreading her arms as wide as she could, cursing her body for its inability to do the one thing it was meant to do. Why now? Why now be weak when someone needed her so badly? When there was no one else to help?

“Don’t hurt her! She didn’t break out, I swear!”

Alex walked in, gun drawn, but put her other hand up in peace after she’d quickly scanned the room.

“Calm down,” she said curtly. “I know. Lena texted.”

Kara looked at Lena, eyes bulging with surprise. Lena looked annoyed, but little else, cheeks blushing just the tiniest bit.

“Well you didn’t really think I was going to do absolutely nothing right? I trust you, but I’m also not an idiot.”

Kara wanted to smile, wanted to thank her, wanted to talk to her – but that all required time and space she didn’t have, time she needed to redirect to Alex, eyeing Other Lena wearily, her gun still firmly grasped in her hand.

“Alex,” Kara just whispered.

“Lena said you were in trouble,” Alex said, before adding: “both of you.”

Kara nodded, speechless. Alex nodded too.

“The D.E.O. is crawling with agents. But I have a way of getting you out.”

“All of us?” Kara asked, unable to keep the surprise out of her voice.

“Lex did this,” Alex said. “Whether she is good or evil, she is a weapon in his hands.”

Other Lena stiffened beside Kara.

“So we can’t let her have him. If you and Lena trust her, then I’ve got your back.” She shot Kara a brief look, one that seemed to go way deeper than their current conversation. One that seemed to speak on many things, all at once, and Kara felt oddly vulnerable under Alex’s meaningful gaze. “I always do.”

Kara managed to shoot her a small smile, but she knew that if it were just her and Alex, she would’ve run to her. Would’ve wanted to drag her away to some booth in the corner of a little dive bar, where they could delve into their previous fight over onion rings, margaritas, and cheap beers, without the rest of the world getting any say in it. And if Kara could still read Alex right after all these years, that was exactly what Alex was thinking of too. Unfortunately, the situation at hand didn’t provide them with the luxury of such a conversation. Instead, they could only do this, exchange the tiny nods and meaningful gazes that would, for now, make things right.

“We do have to go, though,” Alex said, eyeing the door through which she had come. “The alarms were turned off, but that doesn’t mean someone won’t come looking down here.”

“So what do we do?” Kara asked.

Alex was already on the move.

“There’s another way up, one that doesn’t cross the great hall of the D.E.O.,” Alex said. “If we go through, we can get to my office, get Other Lena dressed in some D.E.O. clothes, and maybe, maybe, we can stand a chance of going out undetected,” she looked at Kara over her shoulder. “Then we can bring her to one of our apartments and continue our work in trying to get her home.”

A lump formed in Kara’s throat again at the mention of home. The horrible, cold hellscape that Other Lena came from. The place she helped create. Kara couldn’t think about that now.

“Okay,” she said hoarsely. Then again, a little stronger. She could feel Other Lena’s eyes on her.

Alex walked to the wall next to the entrance of the prison hall that lead to the staircase out. Instead of walking up though, she carefully tapped a single black tile which buzzed just once before splitting and revealed a numerical pad.

Alex entered a code, and the tiles retracted, revealing a narrow opening that led to a seemingly endless, dark hallway. Kara momentarily forgot about the alarming nature of their situation, and her mouth fell open.

“How long has that been here?” she asked.

“Since the D.E.O. opened,” Alex said calmly, retrieving something from her belt.

“And how did I not know about this?” Kara asked, a little affronted.

Alex shrugged. “You tell me. You’re the one with X-ray vision.”

“Yeah, well, I don’t randomly X-ray the D.E.O. all the time looking for secret pathways, Alex,” Kara spluttered. “You couldn’t have just told me?”

Alex sighed, and finally looked at Kara. “If I told you,” she said calmly, “I doubt it would’ve remained a secret pathway for long.”

Kara’s mouth fell open in disbelief and she glared at her sister, earning a small chuckle in return. Kara huffed and rolled her eyes.

Typical.

“Alright,” Alex said, stepping back. “Lena can lead the way – ”

“Lena knew?!”

Alex threw her a look and Kara quickly put up her hands. She caught Lena’s apologetic smile and just shook her head.

“Right,” Alex said. Alarm bells went off in her head when Kara saw the silvery rings that Alex had retrieved from her belt. Handcuffs. “You,” Alex said unkindly to the Other Lena, whose expression immediately darkened. She reminded Kara almost of a cat that had been caught off guard, hairs raised on its back with its ears flat.

“I have a name.”

“Walk over here, hands where I can see them,” Alex ignored her.

“Alex!”

“Couldn’t even last one minute without wanting to see me in chains, huh?” Other Lena muttered dryly, but she put up no fight. She tried to get in front of Kara, but Kara wouldn’t let her.

“You can’t be serious,” Kara spat.

“Let her go, Kara.”

“No, screw that!”

From the corner of her eye, Kara caught how Other Lena arched an eyebrow and Kara could just feel how badly she wanted to take a jab at Kara’s attempt at a dulled expletive.

“This is not a discussion.”

“You’re damn right it isn’t! She’s not doing anything wrong – she’s the one in danger right now! As soon as Lex finds out she didn’t do as he planned, he’ll try to get his hands on her! We can’t just treat her like a prisoner when she’s in just as much danger as the rest of us.”

“Forgive me if I don’t trust the woman who almost killed you, when Lex Luthor tries to use her to kill you again,” Alex said heatedly. “Now let her come here before we all get caught!”

Kara saw Other Lena shake her head, giving up.

“If she wanted to hurt me, she would’ve already!”

“Oh yeah?”

“Yes!”

Alex walked up to the both of them, and Kara immediately tensed up, trying to find even an ounce of the bravery she usually had in her day-to-day life. It felt much harder to fight when it was her sister standing before her, instead of just any other villain.

“What about that then?” Alex nodded at Kara.

“What?”

“Those bruises around your neck sure don’t look like hickeys to me,” she said dryly.

Kara suddenly became uncomfortably aware of the heated throbbing around her neck and chest, where Other Lena’s weight and weaponized heart had been just minutes before.

She hated that little self-satisfied glint in Alex’s eyes that told her she’d won, the way her smile tilted in one corner just the slightest bit in that smug, blood-curdling smirk.

Kara wanted to say something, retort back, but was held back by Other Lena’s hand squeezing her own. Her head whipped back to look at the other woman, and she found only a small smile on her face.

“It’s okay,” she shrugged, one hand still holding the green glow of her chest at bay. “I’ll play along if it makes her feel better. She’s got a point anyways.”

She shrugged it off, but Kara could see right through the nonchalant mask that Other Lena had put on. She was scared.

“No!” Kara said, blocking Other Lena’s path. “She helped us. She saved me! She could’ve just as easily killed me, but she didn’t! That means something to me, and it should mean something to you too!”

“Oh my God!” Alex threw her hands up and took one threatening step closer to the two of them. “I’m not going to stand here and argue with you over something that should be common sense to everyone who isn’t – ”

“We don’t have time for this!”

Everyone’s heads turned to Lena, whose surprising voice cut through their heated bickering with commanding clarity, raising the hairs on Kara’s neck.

Lena walked up to Alex, and all Kara could do was stare.

“I get that you don’t like this. I get that you don’t really like her. I’m not sure I do either. But I told you what happened. She stopped. She had every chance, and she stopped. Kara trusts her.” She swallowed, clenching her jaw, turning to Kara for only a second. When her eyes briefly met Kara’s, a spark ran over Kara’s spine with enough energy to light up an entire room.

“We can’t just – ”

“We have to go,” Lena stifled Alex’s protests. “We all have a shared interest in not letting my brother get what he wants, and she is with us on that. So let’s set aside our differences for just once, and let’s get the fuck out of here before Lex shows up.”

Everything in Alex seemed to clench up, and her face turned so sour that Kara believed she would hear about this for a long, long time. And while she stood tall and terrifying, almost towering over Lena, the latter’s glare was enough to make anyone lose their power in the blink of an eye. And Alex finally caved.

“Fine,” she mumbled. “But this is bullshit.”

“I’ll make a note of it,” Lena said tiredly. “Let’s just go.”

Alex glared at Other Lena, before begrudgingly sliding her handcuffs back on her utility belt. Kara felt herself deflate, and felt almost dizzy with relief flooding her body.

“Thank you,” Other Lena said, cordially polite.

“Don’t thank me. My sister believes in you,” Alex said curtly. “I don’t. Not even a little bit.”

“Alex.”

“No,” Alex didn’t look at Kara, and just kept her eyes on an unflinching Other Lena. “Nothing more than that. As for me, I generally don’t feel warm and fuzzy inside when a person halts their murder attempt on my sister halfway. I will get you out of this building, and then I will get you home. But don’t expect me to go around celebrating just because you did the bare minimum.”

“Understood,” Other Lena said calmly.

Kara sighed, shaking her head, but Alex ignored her.

“Now come on,” Alex said curtly, “Lex is not the type to sit around waiting. We need to go.”

She turned around and briskly walked back over to the uncovered doorway, Lena shooting Kara an apologetic look, before turning in her step and following Alex. Kara sighed, closing her eyes for a brief second. When she felt Other Lena hesitantly take two of her fingers in her hand, though, she turned her head, and their eyes locked. Other Lena looked unsure, yet steady. Nervous, but prepared. It calmed Kara down, though she didn’t know why. Maybe because it felt good to have someone equally lost and confused by her side, uncovering an unsure future together.

Other Lena squeezed her fingers twice, before shooting Kara a small smile, accompanied by a lifting eyebrow. Almost like she was daring Kara to follow. Kara couldn’t help but smile back. Their hands separated as quickly as they had linked up, and after taking a deep breath, Kara followed Other Lena to the doorway.

The four of them lined up to the dark entrance, with Alex leading the way, taking forceful, angry – and frankly childishly – large strides, getting swallowed up in the darkness quick enough to disappear from Kara’s sight entirely.

Lena took a deep breath and followed.

“Close the door behind you,” she said over her shoulder. “Red button, on the left.”

Kara and Other Lena awkwardly moved out of each other’s way to let the other go in.

“You go – ”
“After you – ”

They both chuckled nervously, and Kara footed out of the way, making a vague hand gesture for Other Lena to go in first.

Other Lena just breathed out and nodded, throwing Kara a small smile before going in. Kara herself took a deep breath, looked over her shoulder once to check out the empty hallway where so much drama had unfolded over the last few of her months on this earth, before shaking it off. She turned around, pressed the red button, and watched as the door slowly closed, sealing its entrance off to the people who would come looking for them. The darkness became absolute. There were no lightbulbs inside, no led-lamps, and no electrical wires that could even indicate that anything was linked to some light source. At least not until Alex turned on the flashlight on her phone, and provided the bare minimum of light necessary for them not to stumble over their own feet. Kara could only make out the Lenas' shapes in front of her, and Alex’s silhouette before them, drawn against the light.

Kara could feel her breathing get louder in her ears, and she tried to take deep, even breaths. She turned and allowed herself to be guided by the footsteps in front of her. She took one step after the other, and found the tiles below her feet to be even and steady, nothing scary or medieval like her mind had conjured up. She walked until she tripped over her own feet in the dark, and bumped into the person before her, who let out a muffled sound.

“Sorry,” Kara whispered. “Sorry!” She didn’t know why she was whispering.

“That’s alright,” Other Lena’s husky voice whispered back.

Kara let out an undistinguishable sound in the dark.

Other Lena’s hand reached out in the dark, looking for Kara’s. Once its searching fingers found them, she wrapped their hands together tightly, squeezing just once, to let her know she was there. By now, the touch felt familiar and oddly reassuring. Kara squeezed back. She took another step, and this time she was too close. Other Lena had only been able to take a small step forward, and Kara had, by the skin of her teeth, just managed not to fall against her. Instead, she felt the heat radiating from Other Lena’s body, close enough to touch hers. Other Lena’s long hair was just in reach, and if Kara had gotten any closer, it would’ve tickled her face.

“You okay back there?” Other Lena whispered. It hurdled Kara out of her own head, and she felt the heat rushing to her cheeks in a blush she was glad no one could see.

“Fine,” she whispered hoarsely.

Other Lena squeezed. Her hand felt clammy in Kara’s own. Kara didn’t mind. In fact, she wouldn’t mind holding Other Lena’s hand for as long as possible.

The hallway suddenly narrowed considerably into a bottleneck, and Kara unconsciously started holding her breath more, feeling the walls brush up against her shoulders. Before her, she could hear Lena groan, and Alex muttering under her breath that it wouldn’t be much longer. Kara tried not to focus on it too much. Instead, she tried to count her breaths, and tried to ignore the sounds around her. For the first time in a long time, she could no longer hear the outside noises. The people in National City’s bustling lives. The airplanes, crossing over their heads with the continuous, deafening droning of their motors. The emotions and heartbreaks that made people so much louder, loud enough to be heard over city lines and borders. A constant flux of chaotic, head-splitting noise – suddenly gone quiet. It felt nice, not to hear the creatures scurrying in the walls, nor the agents rushing through the D.E.O. over their heads. Instead, she could only hear her own breathing, calm and steady, echoing in her ears.

But then Kara caught wind of something else. Or someone else, rather. A different pattern of breathing, louder and more irregular than her own. Without noticing it, Other Lena’s hand had gotten clammier, her fingers stiff and uncomfortable in Kara’s. Other Lena’s breaths came at a quick pace, and Kara would bet her meager salary at CatCo that if she were to have her superhearing that time, she would have heard Other Lena’s heart hammering out of her chest.

She took a step closer, her thumb hesitantly brushing over the back of Other Lena’s hand.

“Lena?” she asked. “Are you okay?”

“Fine,” Other Lena whispered, but it sounded cold, forced through gritted teeth.

Kara went quiet. She heard Other Lena sigh, but couldn’t see her face in the dark.

“I don’t like small spaces. Hate them, to be truly honest.”

“Oh.”

Kara felt like an idiot for not realizing it. The way Other Lena had been so quiet, moving so slowly through the dark, unsure of every step she was taking. If there was any fear that Kara could understand better than anyone else, it was this one.

She nodded quietly to herself in the dark.

“Me neither.”

“You don’t like small spaces?”

Kara shook her head tightly before she realized Other Lena couldn’t see her move in the dark hallway.

“No,” she said. “I don’t.”

It went quiet for a bit, before Other Lena softly brushed Kara’s skin, swinging their conjoined hands a little bit, as if it would make both of them feel better.

“Knew we had more in common than a decent taste in literature.”

She looked back, and Kara could only catch a glimpse of a row of white teeth grinning at her, and she instinctively laughed back, feeling a small weight lift off her heart. The familiarity of Other Lena’s laugh brought on a whirlpool of emotions in Kara’s head, and she wondered, already melancholic, though Other Lena hadn’t left her side yet when she had gotten so completely addicted to the sound of her laugh. How much she would miss it when Other Lena was back in her own world.

Her hand came up to join her other one in holding Other Lena’s hand as if it had suddenly turned into a lifeline in the dark tunnel of the D.E.O. If it bothered Other Lena, she didn’t mention it, and instead squeezed Kara’s hands with her own, before turning back around, guiding Kara along with her, their hands tied.

 

 

What had only been a trip of mere minutes had seemed like an hour-long walk through the hidden depths of the D.E.O. When they finally managed to open the door to the end of the tunnel, everyone but Alex groaned at the sudden influx of a mixture of daylight and artificial lamps.

“Alex?”

Kelly’s voice made Kara’s head snap up, and after blinking against the light, slowly coming closer to the door, she realized the door had led to Kelly’s office. One by one, Alex, Lena, and her counterpart – albeit a little hesitantly – walked over the threshold and left the tunnel behind them.

She dropped Kara’s hand, and Kara wasn’t prepared for how cold and untethered she felt without it. She clenched and unclenched her fist by her side.

“I’m sorry, honey, I didn’t know you were even in today!”

Kara could see how close Alex was standing to Kelly, holding her hands tightly, blocking Other Lena’s view in an instinctively protective stance.

“That’s alright,” Kelly trailed off, “I was just – oh my God.”

Her eyes grew ten sizes just looking at Other Lena’s disheveled, unsure presence in her office. Kara could see Other Lena’s form go rigid, like an animal, driven in a corner, caught in the eyes of the people around her.

“Please don’t freak out, I’ve got it handled!” Alex said quickly. “I can explain!”

She took Kelly aside as best she could in the suddenly cramped office, while Kara, too, stepped out of the hallway. The door closed behind her automatically, before she even had a chance to catch a glimpse of the hallway they had walked through.

She could see Kelly listening to Alex’s attempt to fill her in, unabashedly eyeing Other Lena over Alex’s shoulder from time to time as she talked. Other Lena just looked at the floor. Kara noticed that one of her hands was still on her chest, holding the green glow at bay the best she could.

“Can I…?” she had to clear her throat, her voice was hoarse from having been so quiet during her walk through the tunnel. Other Lena turned her head to look at Kara. Kara pointed at her chest. “Do you need me to help with that?”

Other Lena looked down with an almost amusingly puzzled knitting of her eyebrows.

“Oh,” she whispered. “That.”

She shrugged and lifted her head to throw Kara a slight smile, but Kara could see a pained wince shining through.

“Lena,” she could feel the stress in her body giving way to an innate softness that the other woman always seemed so capable of pulling out of her.

“I know, I know,” Other Lena said, fiddling with the fabric above her heart. “But it’s no use. I looked at it.”

Kara came closer and guided Other Lena to a lone office chair in a corner of the room.

“It wasn’t just any old T-shirt that kept it close, see? It’s kind of like a bulletproof vest – if such a vest had a lock.”

Kara frowned and looked closer, but only saw what looked like a melted piece of plastic near Other Lena’s shoulder.

“But… the lock…”

“He burned it,” Other Lena said calmly. “It’s completely ruined. I checked. No way of repairing it.”

“He detonated it from afar.”

Kara looked up, but it wasn’t Other Lena who had spoken – even though it had been her voice. Kara looked over her shoulder and saw Lena, arms crossed.

“He must’ve had some emergency code that he used to fritz the system. A failsafe, as it were. It’s the only reason why we can’t protect you from…”

She didn’t need to point, and she didn’t need to finish her sentence. Other Lena’s carved expression said enough.

“I’ll just keep holding it,” she muttered. “It’s not a big deal.”

“It’s heavy,” Kara commented softly.

“I’ll manage.”

Kara paused for just an instant before she tried again.

“Can I maybe tie it up for you?” she asked hesitantly. “Just because it won’t be very practical, you know, having to run out of here while you have to clutch your chest every step of the way.”

Other Lena threw her a look.

“It wouldn’t be hard,” Kara said. “We just use something to bind the vest close to your body so you don’t risk it falling off.”

“I have a belt you can use,” Lena suggested, and Kara beamed at her.

“See?” she asked a slightly skeptical Other Lena. “Belt! And I have a scarf somewhere!” She looked at her bag. “Somewhere.”

“Kara,” Other Lena began softly, “you really don’t need to after what happened…”

“It’s not about having to do it,” Kara cut her off gently. “It’s about wanting to.”

Other Lena’s eyes softened, a glimpse of vulnerability mingling in with indecisiveness, but eventually, Kara’s insistent look convinced her, and she sighed, giving in.

Kara smiled triumphantly and beamed at Lena over her shoulder. Lena shot her a weak smile, and walked over, sliding the thin, black, leather belt from its loops and over its dark, pinstriped, satin pants. She seemed to want to pass it to her Other Self, but Other Lena’s hand remained on her chest, the other on her knee. She stared Lena down and raised a questioning eyebrow, and Lena sighed.

“Kara?”

“Right here.”

Kara’s hand shot up from her bag with a thin, crumpled-up, pink scarf, covered in a yellow flower pattern.

“Knew I had one in here,” she mumbled.

She held it up in front of Other Lena, who looked less sure about the situation the more she looked at the scarf.

“Come on,” Kara gently coaxed her. “It’s just a temporary solution. It’ll be fine!”

Other Lena sighed and looked away, but the faint wave of her hand seemed to indicate that Kara could proceed. Kara smiled and moved forward, first crouching down, before then sinking down to her knees so she could be at the same height as Other Lena’s heart. She took up her scarf and held it at a distance, just in front of Other Lena’s chest, as if she had to measure where it would fit. She twisted the fabric at its corners to get a good grip for a possible knot. She shuffled closer on her knees, her arm brushing up against Other Lena’s leg. The fabric of her blue pants was so thin, that she could feel the heat of her skin right against her arm.

Kara wondered how much softer the skin of Other Lena’s leg would be compared to the scratchy fabric of the D.E.O.

The thought was enough to send an electrical shock through her body, and she almost dropped the scarf. She made the mistake of looking up, and found Other Lena staring down at her, impossibly close. Her mouth was opened slightly, and there was an undecipherable look in her eyes that Kara instantly got addicted to. Kara’s fingers halted their work as she found herself completely captured in Other Lena’s eyes, yearning for something she had no definition for – something that pushed her to want to get even closer. For a split second, Kara thought she could see Other Lena bending forward slightly like she was urging Kara up, and herself down – like there was something inside her wanting to get closer too –

An uncomfortable cough behind her sent both of them reeling back.

Kara felt her cheeks heat up at the reminder of Lena’s presence right behind her. She quickly went back to folding the scarf. A quick glimpse up through her eyelashes showed an indifferent, absentminded look on Other Lena’s face, but from her position on the floor, Kara could see a pink flush creeping up on her neck.

The idea that Other Lena might not always feel as powerfully unaffected by such trivial things as embarrassment made Kara have to repress a smile.

She’d twisted the scarf quietly in a way that would cover Other Lena’s heart, but would be tight enough to be tied up behind her back. She reached out.

“May I?” she asked.

Other Lena nodded once, tightly.

Kara advanced, placing the scarf over her chest. It went over the vest with the broken lock but shifted a bit when she moved. Frustrated, Kara leaned in to smooth it out, but let out a surprised yelp before she’d even gotten close enough to touch.

All eyes were on her as she pulled her injured hand back to her chest.

“What? What happened?” Alex asked, running over.

“Nothing,” Kara said, biting her tongue to keep from crying out again. She was already fighting the sudden onset of tears that had appeared as soon as her hand had come close enough to Other Lena’s kryptonite core.

She looked up and found that Other Lena was staring at her with a mixture of disgust and horror, like she couldn’t believe what her body had done – how it had betrayed them both.

Kara wanted to say something to make it better, but Lena’s hand on her shoulder pulled her back.

“Let me see,” she urged her gently. “Please, Kara.”

Alex was behind her, and Kara didn’t want to alarm her, so she shook her head. Lena caught on quickly.

“Nothing,” Kara said – voice scratchy. “Dumb accident.”

“You okay?” Alex checked.

“Fine.”

“Alright. Be careful.”

Kara threw her a look.

“And hurry.” She threw a ball of clothes Kara’s way. “D.E.O. issued uniform. With some luck, we might get the Other Lena out of here without anyone noticing.”

Kara’s uninjured hand reached out to grab the clothes and pull them towards her.

“Almost done,” she croaked.

Alex threw her a confused look, but turned back to Kelly when she asked a question.

“Now will you let me look at it?” Lena asked gently.

Kara sighed, shooting Other Lena – who was looking more withdrawn with every passing second – an apologetic look and relaxed her arm enough to allow Lena to gently take her hand, and carefully uncurl her fingers.

Lena winced as Kara let out a pained whimper at the sight of her red, blistered hand. The skin looked raw, and so very tender, brittle enough to break and bleed with one wrong move. But instead of looking at her own injured hand, Kara looked up at Other Lena, who was fixated on it.

“It’ll pass,” Kara said quickly, despite herself. “It’ll heal in no time. Alex said my powers should be coming back any minute, right?”

Other Lena didn’t look at her but nodded.

“It’s fine,” Kara said again, coaxing the other woman to look into her eyes, all while Lena was still tending to her hand. “I promise,” she added softly.

Other Lena shook her head.

“Let’s just… try again,” Lena said, looking from Kara to Other Lena. 

“No,” Other Lena said roughly. “It’s fine, I don’t want to do more damage.”

“You won’t, I promise, just – ”

Kara took a deep breath and looked down. Her hand was still gleaming, the painful red skin just waiting to rip apart.

“You didn’t mean to,” Kara said softly. “And I didn’t look. I’ll be more careful this time, just…” She drew her shoulders in, shaking her head slightly as she looked back up into Other Lena’s eyes. “Just please let me do this for you.”

She could see the conflict in her eyes again. The way her throat bobbed like it was trying to swallow down something that would inevitably sound hurtful or rejecting.

“Okay,” she whispered. “Okay.”

“Okay,” Kara couldn’t contain a smile.

“Jesus,” Lena muttered.

“Just get it over with,” Other Lena murmured, and Kara obliged.

She carefully shuffled closer to the other woman again, still on her knees on the cold floor. Her white skirt was getting stained from the dirty floor, and her knees were starting to ache and get cold on the chilly tiles, but she didn’t care. She just inched closer, focusing only on the task at hand. She carefully investigated the scarf in her hands, before reaching out and wrapping it around Other Lena’s chest. She leaned in closer to connect it at her back, careful not to touch, but had trouble tying the knot. She fumbled with it for a couple of seconds, a frustrated little draw of her brow. A cool touch on her fingers made Kara look up, as Lena smiled tiredly at her, taking over the tying work.

“Thanks,” she whispered.

Lena just shook her head.

“Don’t mention it.”

Kara handed her the belt, and together, they managed to wrap Other Lena’s chest back up, keeping the kryptonite concealed.

“Good?” Kara asked, leaning back on her knees.

Other Lena carefully moved her shoulders, but the cloth didn’t move. The knot Lena had made held up, helped by her thin black belt, fastened tightly on her back.

“Good enough,” Other Lena said, mouth twisting in a tiny smile. Kara smiled back.

“Here,” Kara looked up and found Lena’s hand, her immaculately manicured fingers stretching out in a one-word invitation. Kara gratefully took it and allowed herself to be pulled upright.

“Thanks,” she said, a little out of breath. “For the…” she flapped with her hands, and Lena looked at her with a quietly bemused smile. “Well,” Kara finished awkwardly, “everything really.”

Lena chuckled and took a step closer to Kara.

“Don’t mention it,” she whispered, and Kara felt a spark running through her body, deregulating every function until she was effectively rendered speechless.

“Right,” Other Lena said, and Kara almost jumped at her voice. She’d taken the short time of Kara and Lena’s conversation to pick up the bundle of clothes on the floor and get dressed. She was clad in the same black uniform that every other agent on the base wore, but Kara still couldn’t conceive of how anyone would be fooled. Other Lena’s face stood out against everything – against anything. Her delicate features, her piercing eyes, and the way she seemed to walk through any space like she was in total control – how could anyone really think she was just any other agent? Just any regular person?

She looked a little unsure, and rubbed the bulky part of her chest, adequately covered under the dark D.E.O. long-sleeved jacket.

“You okay?” Lena asked.

“Oh great,” Other Lena said, pulling a face. “From one uniform to another. Love the squashing of any sense of individuality in this place.”

“Look at it from the bright sight,” Lena piped up, “at least this one doesn’t feature an inmate number.”

“Hilarious,” Other Lena muttered dryly, as Kara muffled a smile. Still, when Lena wasn’t looking, Kara caught Other Lena’s eye, and she swore she’d seen a wink sent her way.

“Alright,” Alex walked over. “Vasquez just texted. Most of the D.E.O. agents have been called to the site of the kryptonite bomb. No word yet on back-up by the others, so we’re on our own for this. The other agents have been called into training so if we want to leave unseen, we have to go now.”

Her eyes lingered on Other Lena when she said it, and Kara watched how the other woman rolled her eyes. Despite that, she threw Kara a look, and stood up straight, walking to the middle of the room, where everyone had gathered in the meantime.

Kara was pulled into a quick side hug from Kelly, who had, in the time that it had taken Kara and Lena to fix Other Lena’s vest, calmed down at least a little, though Kara could still catch her eyeing Other Lena with unbridled curiosity.

“We move through the D.E.O. in one group. I lead. No one deviates from the path, and no one talks. We go straight to my apartment – he’ll have scouts at Kara and Lena’s apartments.”

Other Lena groaned beside Kara.

“And here I thought I could catch a hot shower at my place.”

“Don’t worry,” Kara said gently. “You can still shower at Alex’s. I’m sure her shampoo’s a lot better than the one you’ll find here.”

“Oh yeah?” Other Lena threw her a look that made Kara’s stomach flutter. “Does she have a custom-designed rain shower showerhead with perfect temperature control and heated tiles?”

“No, but I think she has some purple shampoo for dyed hair somewhere in there?”

Other Lena laughed that heart-warming, teeth-baring smile of hers, and Kara melted just a little.

“Can the discussion on showers wait until after we’ve left this place?” Alex cut in. “This is serious. If Lex finds out – ”
