Ales sounded as in charge of the situation as she always did, her voice demanding and imposing the way it always did when she was giving out commands. But Kara could see the cracks in the façade. The nervous beads of sweat near her temple, the rigidness of her muscles. Alex was terrified. Kara wanted to help. Wanted to reassure her. But she found no words to comfort Alex. The buzzing in her stomach started again, and Kara could feel the adrenaline taking over.

“We get it,” Other Lena eventually interrupted. It was jarring in the space where only Alex’s voice really seemed to count. “Lex is out there,” she said calmly. “We have to move before he finds out that Kara isn’t as dead as he wants her to be.”

Alex’s face twitched in a way that made Kara worry she might pop a vein, and she nudged for Other Lena to stop. The woman looked at her, but Kara ignored her.

“Fine,” Alex said curtly. “Let’s go. Lena behind me, then Kelly, then the Other Lena, and Kara finishes the line. Single file. And you – ”

She glared at Other Lena, who raised an eyebrow.

“Keep. Your head. Down.”

Other Lena did a mock solute, and Kara silently bemoaned the entire situation.

“Ma’am, yes, ma’am,” Other Lena smirked, the huskiness of her voice making Kara feel all sorts of embarrassed and flushed, and she shook her head.

Alex looked like she wanted to have the final word, but she eventually relented and simply clenched her jaw, turned around, and marched out, the others right behind her.

“You know,” Other Lena said, right before she slipped out the door too, face suddenly extremely close to Kara’s, “I think your sister’s starting to take a liking to me.”

Kara smiled weakly.

“Your completely undeserved and unfounded confidence is inspiring,” she agreed, and Other Lena laughed. She squeezed Kara’s hand one final time before slipping out the door, leaving Kara’s fingers tingling and reaching out to nothing as she too left Kelly’s office, the door falling shut behind her.

Later, when she was alone at home, staring at her walls wondering how she’d gotten there, Kara would remember that laugh as the final, happy sound she’d heard before everything went totally, horrifically, impossibly wrong, and she would wonder why she hadn’t lingered on it more, remaining criminally unappreciative of its beauty – as she headed forward, unknowing.

 

 

For a short while, it looked like the plan was going to work. For a few minutes, they thought they had won.

They were walking through the D.E.O., and all of Alex’s concerns had seemed moot. The agents didn’t even look at them. Didn’t notice. Kara was tense for the entire walk down the stairs, and into the main hall of the D.E.O., but later relaxed when she noticed no one eyeing them with suspicion or concern. There were no alarms going off. No agents running to get more weapons. Alex only had to hold up her D.E.O. ID, without ever uttering a single word, and the agents let them pass through the various security measures without a hitch.

Everything was going perfectly.

Kara could already see the literal light at the end of the hall. She saw the hope reflected in Other Lena’s eyes as she tilted her head, privy to the National City’s rays of sun for the first time in a very long time. The light seemed to brighten her features and made her pale skin glow. She looked radiant. She turned her head a little to absorb a little more light, blinking against the brightness she had grown unaccustomed to in her months at the D.E.O., as they walked the final meters to the staircase leading up to the city. A gush of wind blew a strand of Other Lena’s dark hair across her face, and she had to shake her head to move it away, exposing the rare, carelessly happy dimple in her cheek. When her head turned, she opened one eye and caught Kara’s unabashed, wondrous gaze. She winked, and grinned again – in that free way of hers that showed off her perfect teeth, that showed the mischievous side of her so damn beautifully –

 

"I should’ve known that even you would fail.”

 

And then their moment was gone.

Kara felt ice run down her back as that jarring voice brought her tumbling back down to reality. Her heart started beating loudly in her ears, the blood rushing to her head in a way that made the world seem to pass by in slow-motion. She turned her head, praying and begging that her imagination was running wild, that she was going insane, that her mind was playing tricks on her, that goddamn all of this had been a dream. She’d rather lose the wins she’d gained with Other Lena today in a dream, than face the crushing hopelessness that his voice had stirred inside her chest like a heavy block of ice.

But there he was.

Just as she’d left him before.

His wool coat had been discarded, but he was still dressed in his impeccable, gray, three-piece suit, studying his nails, sounding as calm as he would discussing projected sales numbers for the following fiscal quarter.

“Lex,” Kara whispered, the defeat she felt dissipating her words before they could reach anyone.

Everyone before her had completely stiffened, and no one dared speak. It was like they had been collectively kicked in the gut, and all the air had been knocked from their lungs. The hope they’d felt shimmer just moments before, crushed by just one sentence.

Kara felt a lump in her throat, and for a moment, she thought she might drown in misery.

“We’re heading out,” Kelly said slowly. “You can’t – ”

“No,” Lex said calmly. “No, you won’t.”

From the corner of her eye, Kara saw Alex move, but before she could figure out what she was doing, Lex interrupted them again.

“I wouldn’t reach for that gun, director. Not unless you want to create a panic and alert everyone in the D.E.O. that their most prominent prisoner, who horrifically maimed several of their beloved, fellow agents, forcing them out of their duty, has escaped. How well did you train them, do you think?” he asked. “Will they confront her with restraint, or do you think their trigger-happy reflexes mingled with some innate sense of restitution and vengeance might take the upper hand?”

Alex froze, and Kara saw Other Lena flinch, bowing her head like she had to hide away. It made her feel infuriatingly useless. Kara saw Alex’s fingers clench around the gun’s grip. They were trembling with exertion, and Kara could see the resolve in Alex’s eyes wither and turn into defeat as she was forced to lower her gun. She shot Kara a helpless look, but Kara couldn’t do anything to reassure her but shake her head. She could feel the tears of frustration prick in her own eyes as the situation turned so horribly uncontrollable right in front of them.

But it held one advantage.

“Kara,” Alex said tersely. And Kara immediately understood.

She caught Other Lena’s gaze, and quickly passed her to stand behind Alex, but just in front of Other Lena. Just in case. She looked back over her shoulder, and Other Lena shot her a wry smile. Kara didn’t have it in her to smile back.

Lex observed her actions with a tight smile but didn’t comment on her actions.

Later, she would hate that she hadn’t vocally wondered why that was. Why he had just let her move? Why wasn’t she thinking?

Lex seemingly shrugged off the actions in the room and continued talking like he hadn’t been seconds away from having his head blown off. So confident and arrogantly empowered by his assured safety, he never even looked back at Alex.

“When you first came here, Lena,” he started, waving his hand carelessly in the direction of Other Lena without looking up at her, “I had hoped – I believed – that there was finally a great version of you, in my immediate presence. I believed that with the power you rightfully wielded over those who would wish you harm, you could do great things. Even if one of those people you meant harm was me.”

He touched his hand and shook his head, disappointed.

“I believed that at least the existence of a common enemy would lead you to make the rational, correct choice – the only choice, as far as I’m concerned. And yet…”

He clicked his tongue, and the sound was so jarring in the echoing hall of the D.E.O. that it sent a shiver down Kara’s spine.

From the corner of her eye, she could see the agents seeping out of the hall one by one, and the desperate isolating loneliness that overcame her made her physically ill. Her mouth fell open as she soundlessly gasped for breath, staring at the last disappearing backs of the people who could possibly come to their aid.

They were all alone, out in the open with a predator now.

Lex had caught Kara’s desperate, lingering gaze.

“Ah,” he said, “the agents. Yes. It seems the remaining agents have been called into extra training. On both my account and the director’s,” he nodded in Alex’s direction, “or so it seems.”

Alex looked crushed.

“My Lena,” Lex turned to Other Lena again. He sighed, linked his hands behind his back, and shook his head. “My little sister. My only sibling in this world. The one true Luthor still walking this earth.”

Other Lena stiffened.

“When I first saw Supergirl’s body on that stretcher, the first day you came here, well,” he smiled.

Kara’s heart sank.

“When I saw the burns on her body, and those bruises on her neck, right after you’d almost snuffed the life out of her, I have to say,” he smiled, eyes drifting off like he was thinking back to a fond summer vacation, rather than the mangled body of a torture victim. “It was… well it was sensational.”

He looked up at Other Lena, his eyes brimming with a manic passion that Kara hated to encounter.

“That was the first time I thought you had potential. Potential to succeed where my other, weaker sister had failed. Potential to thrive within the family. Potential to utilize the weapons you were given, to once and for all, put the Luthors back where they belong,” he exclaimed. “Back. On. Top.”

His last words were louder, accentuated by a mad glint in his eyes, and an uncontrolled step towards Other Lena, one that made him look more terrifying than before.

He paused, yet no one moved. No one dared speak. His words lingered in the air, making the room buzz with only his voice. Only his authority. Only his power.

He straightened back up, and Kara let out a breath she didn’t know she was holding. He seemed to calm down a little, seemed to want to regain some semblance of control over the thoughts and emotions he was sharing so freely.

“But alas,” he said, clenching his jaw. “It was not to be. I should’ve known. I had suspected it for some time, but I was… sentimental. I held out hope. Hope,” he looked at Other Lena, “that there was someone else on my level. Someone intelligent I could share my projects with. An equal. But just as I’ve always had to walk alone – ”

“You’ve never wanted an equal in your life,” Lena interrupted him. Kara almost wanted to scream when her voice pierced through Lex’s monologue. Her heart was beating fast enough to make her dizzy.

“You’re an asshole,” Other Lena agreed. “And we don’t need the self-pitying bullshit.”

“But you are right,” Lena said. Other Lena looked at her. “You have no equal,” she said. “I’ve long surpassed you. We both have.”

Lex’s jaw clenched, and his eyes flickered dangerously.

“Is that so?” he asked slowly. He turned to Lena. “Tough words from a woman who can’t even stand on her own two legs before crying out for me or her mother to help her make any worthwhile decision.”

Lena almost faltered, but she kept her head up, and Kara felt infinitely proud of her.

“And you,” he turned to Other Lena, who merely tilted her head, confronting him head-first. “You might not have done as I’d hoped, but I don’t see how you could possibly view that as something positive.”

She didn’t understand. Kara could see it in her eyes. But she refused to back down and give in.

“Had you done as I’d pushed you to do, you would have a clear path forward now. You would have a home. A place to stay. A family. What is the plan now, Lena, hm? Are you just going to follow the merry band of super aliens out into the world of sunshine and rainbows?”

He smirked, and Kara could see how something cracked in Other Lena’s façade. She wanted to reach out but didn’t know how. She felt so absolutely useless. She just took a step closer to Other Lena, but Lex’s eyes made her heart freeze in fear. But he looked right through her. Like she didn’t matter. Instead, he just turned back to Other Lena.

“I’ve heard some of the things you’ve done in your world, Lena. I was impressed. I didn’t think you had in you. Murder, torture, a police state? Very impressive, little Lena. Very on-brand for a Luthor.”

And if Kara had the power to hear a heart shatter, she thought that would’ve been the moment she would’ve drowned in the crushing sound.

“So much pain, so much irreversible damage you’ve done to your universe. Much worse than I have ever accomplished on this earth, I might jealously add.” He smirked, and Kara’s stomach turned. “And you want to go back and play the hero? Tell me, how does that work?”

He folded his arms across his chest.

“No really, Lena, tell me,” he insisted. “What does one have to do to completely expunge any bad deed one has ever committed?” His voice lowered until he sounded dangerously reasonable as he spoke. “How much can one friendship forgive and make up for? Do you have the absolute numbers? Or have all those lives you ruined no face for you? You were always so very able to have some minions do your dirty work for you.”

Other Lena’s breath faltered, and she turned her head, looking at the ground with an expression of pure misery on her face. Lex had found every button he could, and he had pushed on all of them with all his strength.

Kara’s heart broke, but the hurt was drowned out by the all-consuming hatred she felt for the man before her. she wished, she prayed that her anger was enough to fuel the adrenaline in her body and to reignite the powers she knew were still inside her. She wanted to destroy that man. She wanted to hurt him in ways so graphic, the images in her head should scare her. Instead, they only made her want it more. Made her want to hurt him more.

She wanted him gone.

She wanted to be the one to personally remove him from their planet, and she wanted to hear him suffer before she got to do so.

Her hands clenched into fists, and she felt something of a lingering heat behind her eyes, dull and far away, but clinging to her cells in an effort to get back to the surface. She could feel her anger throbbing and turning within her, fueling dormant reflexes and powers she couldn’t remember. If only they could come back faster – if she could just reach them… It felt like hundreds of fingers inside of her were reaching out to a flame but could feel nothing but some surrounding warmth on their skin. If she could just push them forward a little harder, a little faster –

“I will give you this,” Lex said, almost as an afterthought. “You keep me on my toes, Lena. You make me think and rethink all my plans, and you’ve forced me to always, always,” he paused, “have a backup plan.”

And while later, much, much later, her friends and family would all tell her she couldn’t have known, that if she’d had her powers, she would’ve seen and heard it coming, Kara knew she couldn’t blame her lack of powers. She’d been late. She’d been distracted.

There were signs.

The way Lex’s hand had been in the pocket of his tailored pants, one finger rhythmically tapping against a cornered outlined object in his pocket. The way his eyes – just once, in a blink of a moment – had seemed to linger over their shoulders when he’d been talking, breaking his eye contact with the rest of them for just a second. The way he hadn’t commented on the way Kara had come to stand between Alex and Other Lena. How his eyes gleamed for just one second –

But Kara hadn’t figured it out. Not in time.

Lex’s eyes fell on her now, after having perfectly ignored her for the duration of the talk; but right then and there, she was his only focus. Kara’s heart froze in her chest, feeling a foreboding tightness around her lungs.

She took a step forward – just one single, miraculously small step forward – which saved her life. A beat later, she was hurdled forward by the force of something incredibly sharp and fast racing past her, scorching her arm.

She heard a metallic crunch, followed by a deep exhale before she felt the burn.

Kara hissed, clutching her arm, seeing red droplets appear on the white sleeve of her blouse. She blinked in confusion. The red droplets quickly spread and connected in the blink of an eye to form a growing red, wet stain. The mystery grew with the sudden onset of pain, hot and glowing, and impossible to repress, but still, Kara couldn’t touch her reddening sleeve.

She heard her sister shouting for Kara and Kelly to get down. From the corner of her eye, through a sudden onset of smoke, she saw Lena’s terrified eyes, before she was pushed away by someone who looked like Alex, and hidden from Kara’s sight. She saw Alex drawing a gun. Then a splash of black – a legion of uniformed agents, rushing in from all corners of the room, passing by her without noticing.

She looked up, eyes puzzled – and then she caught Other Lena’s gaze.

And the world had gone quiet.

Kara felt it come to a stop, all at once. No sounds, no time, no anything. The world was passing by in a quiet, slow, steady motion.

Not steady enough.

Kara could hear her own heartbeat in her ears. Slow. Quickening. Steadily making her aware that something wasn’t right. But she still didn’t understand. Maybe she didn’t want to. Maybe her brain was doing everything in its power to prevent her from understanding it because fully comprehending the situation unfolding before her would send her into a mental whirlpool of misery. One she would never be able to get out of again.

But as it was, the puzzle pieces, drenched in red, hot, blood, mixed with green had to fit sometime. And if it wasn’t for the blood on the floor, or the green sparks escaping the dark makeshift cover on her chest, it would be the look in Other Lena’s eyes.

Her eyes were open so wide, that Kara could almost count the individual, minuscule, little veins running through them. There was shock. Surprise. Fear. And then… then Kara saw the pain. Other Lena’s mouth opened in a silent scream, her face started trembling… No. Not just her face. Her entire body seemed to shake. Her fingers hovered in front of her chest, shivering. Convulsing. And that’s when Kara understood how the red and green flashes in the corner of her eye connected. Where her mind connected the sound of the impact of a bullet with the red blood spatters on her arm, and on Other Lena’s clothes, and the poison leaking out of the hole in her chest.

And the world caught back up with time again.

Chapter 12

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

The noise rushed in at the precise moment that a harrowing scream mangled its way out of Kara’s body. No one could hear it over the sound of shouting – the sound of other screams. The sounds of agents rushing into the D.E.O. hall. The words shooter and gun were yelled by someone close to her, someone whose voice sounded familiar, but Kara couldn’t place it. Kara barely noticed any of it. She didn’t notice anyone other than her.

Other Lena, whose body was somehow stiff and trembling at the same time, eyes still wide open like she didn’t quite know what to believe. Like she could maybe deceive her injury by pretending it wasn’t there – as if she didn’t want to know. She was standing before Kara, skeleton hands reaching out to nothing, with only one brave enough to hover up to her chest, where a red stain started matching Kara’s own.

Where the bullet had embedded itself in her skin.

“No,” Kara whispered. “No.”

It was drowned out by everything around her, but she didn’t care.

A tile next to her feet was blown to smithereens by a bullet she hadn’t seen and hadn’t heard. Its remnants ricocheted against Kara’s ankle and made her stumble forward, but she didn’t care. Other Lena was still looking at her, mouth falling open, lips trembling.

She made no sound.

Kara fell forward, moving on instinct.

Nothing mattered. Not the voices around her, not the screams and the echoes of bullets racing through the large hall, none of it. She could see the wound in Other Lena’s chest. It was growing. It was there. Other Lena was right there. Kara couldn’t shake herself out of the state of disbelief, but forced her body forward, forced it to do what every reflex and instinct inside of her begged her to do. She moved towards Other Lena. Unsteady on her feet, but deliberate, she struggled to move, the pain in her arm flaring up when she walked.

Kara took two steps before she heard a whistling sound, and felt her hair being blown to the side by an object racing past her, close enough to almost graze her ear. She squeezed her eyes shut, pulling her fists in front of her face.

Then, two loud bangs and a loud grunt confirmed that Alex had quickly responded. She could vaguely hear familiar voices, both good and bad, yelling and shouting things that did not register in the slightest.

Kara didn’t care.

She stumbled forward, reaching Other Lena just when her knees started giving out. Kara blindly stretched out her hand, fingers curling around the only patch of wet fabric she could reach. Kara held her. Kara held onto her for just that one, brief moment.

For just one second, Kara had her. She’d clenched the fabric of Other Lena’s shirt between her fingers, her muscles tout, trying to keep Other Lena upright.

For just one moment, they were looking into each other’s eyes – Other Lena’s wide with shock, and Kara’s burning with furious concentration. Other Lena blinked, her mouth trembling with exhaustion, trying to say something that her weakened muscles didn’t allow her to.

A bullet exploded next to them, and Kara screamed, covering her head. She looked up the second another shot from their side was fired back, but the entire world had turned loud, confusing, and unstable. Kara took a wobbling step towards Other Lena, the shouting and screaming around her disorientating her just long enough to lose sight of her – for just that one second.

But then the smoke cleared, and Kara could blink through her clouded vision. Other Lena was staring at her, mouth opening just once. And then her knees buckled, and she fell down, taking Kara with her.

Kara yelped as Other Lena grabbed her injured arm, the pain soaring through her body like a lightning bolt. She had to bite her lower lip to keep from screaming, biting hard enough to taste blood. She fell to her knees on the painful tiles, Other Lena landing just a few inches away from her. Kara grabbed her own arm, covering the wound, leaning back and forth in an attempt to stifle the pain at least a little.

For a moment, Kara thought Other Lena had landed well, on her knees, just like Kara had. For a moment, she seemed fine, just tired from the long, long day. Then Other Lena moved her head, and Kara saw that her eyes were vague and unfocused, lips still trying to form words, though they didn’t seem to be aimed at anyone in particular. And then Other Lena’s body didn’t seem to be able to carry its own weight, her body swerving slightly. She raised her head once, before falling to her side.

“Lena!”

Kara immediately let go, allowing the pain to race through her body as she leaned forward, crawling towards Other Lena. Her arms almost gave way a couple of times, and she saw black spots dancing in front of her eyes when she put her weight on the injured arm – but Kara kept going. It wasn’t important. It didn’t matter. She ignored it, couldn’t feel it anymore. It was nothing. Nothing.

“Lena?”

She crawled closer, hand slipping in a small wet patch of blood that made Kara bite down on her teeth, pushing through the angry tears in her eyes, ignoring the way her knees knocked harshly against the cold tiles.

“Lena?”

She finally managed to get to her, and Kara instinctively pulled her body closer. She pushed her arm under Other Lena’s neck, while her other hand touched her stomach, hand instantly soaked in a warm, sticky patch of blood. Other Lena let out a painful, mewling sound, and Kara tried to move her hand, but the wet, squelching sound from the now useless scarf over Other Lena’s chest shocked her enough to make her hand freeze, so scared she would do more harm than good.

“Oh Rao.”

Kara’s voice was strangled in her throat. Other Lena’s face was so pale, like all the blood had drained from her cheeks and was dripping onto the floor.

“Lena?” Kara’s voice broke, and she cupped Other Lena’s cheek. “Lena, can you hear me?”

Other Lena blinked at her, her mouth half-opened. But just when Kara thought she might be trying to form words, trying to say something, trying to reach out – a pained husk of her former voice left Other Lena’s lips.

But Kara could see the spark of recognition in Other Lena’s eyes. She was still there. She could still hear Kara – recognize her.

“Lena, don’t worry, okay? It’s going to be alright. Okay?”

She didn’t know why she kept asking for reassurance when she knew Other Lena couldn’t give her any. But her heart was racing, and the panic inside her body felt like barbed wire around her heart, and she just had to. If not for Other Lena, then for herself.

“It’s going to be okay,” she whispered again.

She stroked Other Lena’s cheek, gently stroking across her temple, just because it always calmed her down when Alex would do it for her. Because it felt like someone cared. Kara ignored the fear in the pit of her stomach that warned her of what might possibly be to come, but all her efforts couldn’t quelch the need she felt deep inside of her to make Other Lena as comfortable as she could.

“No,” she whispered, almost to herself. “It’s going to be okay. I promise, Lena, I’ll get you out. We’ll get you out, okay?”

Something red bubbled up in the corner of Other Lena’s mouth, and Kara felt her stomach turning.

“Alex!” she screamed over her shoulder. “Alex, help!”

She didn’t wait for a reply, and immediately returned her attention to the woman in her lap. Her hair swept around, and only when Kara felt the ends of the wet strands hit her exposed shoulder and stick to it, she realized it had been coated in Other Lena’s blood. She released a shaky breath and pulled Other Lena closer.

“It’s going to be okay, Alex is coming,” she said determinately. “Just hold on, okay? Alex is coming. She’s coming.”

Kara knew she had to do something. She wouldn’t wait. Alex was coming, she was rushing, and that was all that counted. But she had to get a jumpstart.

She frantically started moving her hand over Other Lena’s chest, determined to make the best of it before Alex came. She removed the wet scarf from Other Lena’s chest, trying not to think about how heavy it felt compared to before. The second it had lifted from her chest, a renewed stream of blood immediately started bubbling from the wound, and Kara rushed to cover it with her hand. She let out a yelp when her bare hand touched a piece of Other Lena’s kryptonite core that had once been stable, but had now turned liquid, and was oozing in trace amounts from Other Lena’s chest. Kara groaned, pushing through the burning pain that felt like her skin was being peeled from her hand layer by layer. She couldn’t stop herself from crying out but forced her hand to revolt against her own instincts, and to keep it stuck to her chest.

For just a moment, overtaken by shock, she leaned over, her body trembling all over when the pain, which had just been a dull ache before, penetrated every single cell in her body as the kryptonite took over. She breathed heavily, trying to focus on taking in even gulps of air, even when that air felt hot and scorching, and Rao, so painful.

Kara breathed through her pain, ignoring it the best she could, and leaned back, but stilled when she suddenly felt Other Lena’s hand covering her own, right on her chest.

“Lena?”

She could see Other Lena’s arm trembling. She looked so brittle, Kara could scream. Other Lena squeezed Kara’s hand, so softly, and with so little power, that she’d barely even felt it. Her trembling lips and shaking body seemed to beg Kara for help, and Kara felt like her inability to do so would drive her insane. She squeezed back, harder than she should, and helplessly, angrily, desperately, called out for her sister again.

“Alex!”

Her voice was getting shrill, and more desperate with each passing second. She could vaguely hear Alex shouting something back, but whatever it was got lost in the ocean of sounds around them. A sudden thrum of doors being pushed open made Kara’s head turn quickly. She looked up and saw a dozen D.E.O. agents swarming the hall, dressed in full gear, holding their guns at the ready.

For one brief second, Kara felt a treacherous flicker of hope burning inside of her, and she let out a dry sob, straightening her back so they could see her better. She could raise her hand to wave them over, but no power in the world could’ve stopped her from holding onto Other Lena.

“Here!” she croaked, her throat dry as sandpaper, the words barely audible in her own ears over the marching sounds of the agents, and the shouting in the background. “We’re right here!”

She bent back over Lena when they got closer, squeezing her hand, lips hovering over her cheek. The pain got hotter as she did so, but Kara didn’t care.

“It’s going to be okay, Lena. See? They’re coming. Someone… someone’s coming.”

The pressure around her fingers indicated that Other Lena had heard her, using what little power she had left to squeeze Kara’s hand.

But just as the flow of agents finally reached them, it split into two groups of agents running around Kara and Other Lena like they were just an obstacle to avoid. Leaving them to get to the real assignment.

“No, no, no, no, no!’ Kara shouted, her voice breaking in panic. “What are you doing? We’re here! We’re right here, please!” A crack in her voice silenced the last of her words as the agents continued forward, not looking back. “Please come back. Please!”

Kara lowered her head in defeat, pulling Other Lena close.

“Please,” she whispered. “Please.”

She felt pressure around her fingers again. Then, a more insistent squeeze, which forced her to raise her chin and look at Other Lena.

She tried to say something, her lips quivering.

“It’s okay,” Kara said quickly, shaking off the defeat, instead focusing on the hand under Other Lena’s head, which started rhythmically – instinctively – stroking her hair. She couldn’t lose hope. Not yet. Other Lena needed her. “Don’t try to talk, you need to save your energy.”

She didn’t know whether or not what she was saying was even medically sound. At that point, she felt like she was just mechanically reciting every single thing Alex had ever said to her while she was the one in the medical ward.

She had to get Other Lena to the medical ward.

Kara again felt Other Lena squeezing her hand, a little harder, a little more insistent this time.

Kara looked at her, and felt a pang in her heart.

Through the pain, the blood, and the misery of the entire situation, Other Lena’s eyes had cleared. She was alert, taking in the situation with such clarity that Kara felt a lump in her throat at the sight. Their eyes met, and Kara felt like she could suddenly see every moment leading up to now.

Meeting Other Lena in the Other Universe.

“Then you will die screaming.”

Finding her again in her own. And the pain that went along with that.

She remembered the fights, the discussions, the endless anger on both of their ends. The frustration, the shouting, the constant need to cry in her pillow after every new death threat…

But then she remembered all the other things. The good things.

The playful fights over books and their not-so-politically-correct origins. The hair-dye that Other Lena had beamed at when Kara had smuggled it into her cell. The way in which Other Lena would arch an eyebrow when Kara would play an out-of-character card in card games, forcing Other Lena to reevaluate her strategy. The way she had seemed almost… proud. The spark when their hands touched. The way Other Lena had smiled over her shoulder when they’d almost reached the end of the D.E.O. How quiet and surprised she had been with the horribly outdated chess set. How her eyes would light up when Kara brought more books. How she’d felt pressed against Kara against the wall. How kind she could be. How intelligent. How resourceful, powerful, and persevering. How loudly she could laugh like they’d known each other for years. The way Kara’s dark jokes would elicit the strongest emotions within her. The way she’d sung along to Kara’s old songs on her iPod, blissfully innocent and unaware of anyone else’s eyes on her – least of all Kara’s. The way she’d trusted Kara, even when she had no reason to. How fragile she felt, holding Kara’s hand in the dark of the hallway. How she’d squeezed her hand –

“Ka-ra.”

The voice was just a husk of what it used to be, ghostly, feint, and still so, so beautifully mesmerizing.

Kara realized she was crying when she saw her tears mingling with the red dots around Other Lena’s mouth, running down to her neck like minuscule, stormy rivers. She wanted to wipe it away but didn’t dare move.

“Ka-ra,” she whispered again. Other Lena was trying to say something, but the room was too loud, and Other Lena was too weak. So, careful not to move her hand, and careful not to disturb her mangled body, Kara gently lifted Other Lena’s upper body, until her head was hovering only slightly above Other Lena’s, the woman’s lips close to her ear.

“Ka-ra.”

“I’m here,” Kara said quickly. “Alex is coming, just hold on, okay?”

“She won’t… come,” Other Lena’s voice broke, and when Kara realized Other Lena was crying, her heart shattered. “She… won’t.”

“She will! She – ” She turned around, and with all her might, screamed into the darkened hall. “Alex, please!”

“I’m coming!”

Kara turned back.

“She’s coming, Lena, she’s coming! We’re not leaving you, okay? We’re not – I’m not leaving. I swear, I’m right here, Lena, and I’m not going anywhere.”

Kara pulled her in even closer in some grotesque, bloody hug, pleading silently to every God in the universe to give her this one time that things could end well. This one save that would mean everything.

“Kara,” Other Lena whimpered. “Kara…”

“I’m here, I’m here,” Kara whispered.

Other Lena’s hand lifted off the ground and struggled to find a grip on the back of Kara’s blouse. But once she had, Kara thought Other Lena might never let go again. She held on so tight that Kara couldn’t have moved if she tried.

“Please,” she whimpered. “I don’t want to die, Kara. I don’t – I don’t, I don’t want to die here, please.”

And Kara couldn’t keep it in anymore. She cried in Other Lena’s hair as Other Lena cried into her shoulder – deep, heavy sobs that carried the sound of her rasping lungs, as her hot tears soaked through Kara’s blouse. Kara held her close enough to burn her own skin through her blouse, holding her close enough to choke.

“You won’t! I won’t let you! Someone’s coming, I swear. Just hold on, someone – ”

“I’m here, I’m here!”

Alex – sweet, sweet, precious, holy, doctor Alex – skidded to a stop beside them, instantly falling to her knees.

“Are you hurt? Are you okay?”

“No – no! I’m fine, I’m fine!”

Alex’s hands patted her down, eyes searching frantically for anything that could indicate otherwise.

“Lena!” Kara interrupted her, feeling like she would go insane if Alex talked for one more second. “They hit Lena!”

Kara lowered Other Lena to the floor, quickly apologizing when the other woman groaned in pain. She didn’t let go of Kara’s blouse, and Kara didn’t let go of her.

“It’s going to be okay, Alex is here now,” she reassured her.

The pang of hope, which had been so lost before, rekindled, and Kara almost laughed through her tears in some sort of manic relief.

“See? I told you – I told you Alex was coming!”

She looked at her sister through her tears, her hand trembling from the stress of not letting go, her body aching – and yet she’d never felt more alive, than when Alex crouched down next to them.

Other Lena let out a pained mewl, one that made Kara redirect her attention immediately. Alex would take care of her, she knew that. She just had to make sure she was alright. She could do that. She could do that.

From the corner of her eye, she could see Alex’s hands strategically roam over Other Lena’s blood-soaked torso, carefully removing the wet cloths – carcasses of the clothes they had been just an hour before.

“It’s going to be okay, Lena,” Kara whispered in her ear, pushing sticky strands of her hair behind Other Lena’s ear. “I got you. Alex is here now.”

Alex gently pushed Kara’s hand away, just a few millimeters, but Kara had to bite her tongue. It felt like parts of her skin were melting off. The metallic scent of blood, pungent and nauseating, got even stronger than before, and if that didn’t alarm Kara that Alex had exposed the open wound in Other Lena’s chest, it would be the painful mewling, accompanied by weak scratches on Kara’s skin.

“Don’t look, don’t look,” Kara whispered in Other Lena’s hair. She didn’t know whether she was talking to Other Lena or herself. “It’s going to be okay. It’s going to be fine, I promise. I got you.”

Alex removed layer after layer, the floral pattern of Kara’s scarf invisible through the thick coats of blood. Kara vaguely heard her call out for help, heard her displace several things, heard her curse and grunt, inspecting whatever she found, and Kara ignored everything, and just looked into Other Lena’s eyes.

“I’ve got you.”

She hoped she could convey it right. She hoped, with all her heart, that Other Lena got what she meant. That she was there. That she was close to her. That she was forever sticking to her – with her, by her – in whatever shape or form she was allowed to be. Kara would not let her go.

She wouldn’t.

“Kara.”

“I’ve got you.”

“Kara.”

“It’s going to be okay, Alex is going to fix you up.”

Her fingers ran alongside Other Lena’s face and ear, tracing her skin like it would somehow take her pain away. The way her eyes remained fixed on Kara’s face made her hope that it did. No matter what happened, no matter where Other Lena would go, Kara was with her.

“It’s going to be okay.”

She was going to stay. She would hold Other Lena’s hand for as long as she could. She would stay by her side. She would stay, she would stay. She would stay.

“Kara.”

Alex’s voice, heartbreakingly, unmistakably full of pity finally pushed its way through layers of Kara’s mind, forcing her to acknowledge her voice.

Kara was trembling, holding onto Other Lena, staring into those bloodshot eyes, tears trailing down its corners, running over her cheeks down to her neck. She looked so fragile, depending on others, waiting for someone to rescue her, with no power of her own. How she would hate that; how it would scare her.

Kara didn’t want to listen to Alex. She knew, from the very first time Alex had said her name, defeat, worry, and careful concern lacing the vowels of name, that something was wrong. Something was going to break, and Kara didn’t want to look at Alex and find out what that was. She would delay the inevitable if only she could keep looking into Other Lena’s eyes.

“Kara, please.”

Kara squeezed her eyes shut once – just for a second. When she opened them again, she could see renewed tears forming in Other Lena’s eyes. Like she knew. Like she was waiting for the news.

“I got you,” Kara whispered, and tears spilled from Other Lena’s eyes.

Kara looked up, and Alex was sitting back, her hairline drenched with sweat, her forehead glossy, blood spattered across her features. Her hands looked like they had been dipped in red paint, still covering Other Lena’s chest wound. Her arms, though, were slack, like all the strength had flowed out of her with Other Lena’s blood. But what struck Kara the most, what made her heart clench in a sharp, continuous, sinking pain, was the lost, exhausted expression on her face, paired with so much regret and pity that it made Kara want to crawl back and hide under her bed.

“No,” she said, shaking her head. She looked back down, refusing to look at either Alex or Other Lena’s face.

“Kara, I’m so sorry.”

“No. No.”

It wasn’t true, it wasn’t true. Kara refused, refused, to look up. To face a reality she didn’t want to think about.

“Kara…” Alex’s sympathetic tone felt abhorrent in Kara’s ears, and she wished Alex would just shut up. “Kara, please.”

Kara looked up when Alex grabbed her hand, her other one still covering Other Lena’s wound, but her arm was slacker than before.

Alex looked like she was trying not to cry, and the immense pity and regret in her eyes made Kara’s heart sink so fast she felt dizzy.

She refused.

“What do we do?” Kara asked, shaking her bloodied hair out of her face. “Come on. Tell me what I can do. How can we – what do we do to fix her? How – what are you going to do?”

“Kara,” Alex’s voice broke, and Kara shook her head.

“I tried to stop the bleeding, but she’s still bleeding, and, and, I think we just need to get her to the operating table, but maybe you have to find a more durable fix for the wound?” Kara babbled, the words rushing out of her like water. “Maybe then we can lift her and transport her, and then maybe you can operate, right?”

“Kar – ” Alex’s voice broke, and it made Kara falter, shaking her head as if it would somehow make Alex go away. She heard Alex take a deep breath, and Kara bowed over, letting her forehead rest on Other Lena’s stomach, her hand gripping the side of her soaked D.E.O. shirt like she would disappear right in front of her if she let go.

“Kara, there’s nothing to do,” Alex said, so careful, so small. Like the gentle fragility of her words would erase its cruel meaning. “There’s nothing I can do for her.”

Kara shook her head, looking into Other Lena’s eyes while her tears ran down her cheeks.

“No, please,” Kara whispered. “Please. It’s not fair! It’s not true!”

She turned to Alex, pleading, begging for her to try something – anything.

“Please, Alex, you have to help her!”

“I wish I could,” Alex said, eyes shiny too. “I really, really wish I could.”

“No,” Kara whimpered. “No, no, no, please.”

“Kara, she’s lost too much blood. The kryptonite core was the only thing that kept her body functioning, and now that that’s shot to pieces – ”

Kara flinched, and Alex broke off her sentence in a whisper, like she understood that every word she said made the whole situation so, so much worse.

Other Lena’s grip on Kara’s blouse tightened, and when Kara looked at her again, she looked paler and worse than before. Her eyes were so wide, bloodshot with exertion, haunting against the sickening color of her skin.

“There’s just nothing anyone can do for her anymore,” Alex finished softly.

Kara bit her lip to keep from screaming, bowing her head so Alex wouldn’t see the absolute burning pain wrecking her body. How could this have happened? How did Kara let it happen? How did she let her down twice? How could she let her go? She held on tighter to the woman struggling to breathe in her arms.

“Please, Lena,” Kara whispered. “Please don’t go.”

She felt herself pushing Alex’s hand away, covering the burning wound with her hand again, uncaring and unflinching, this time. The pain was good – anything to feel something other than the pain inside of her, burning her nerve endings, scorching her skin, and letting her blood run cold. A sob rang out through the hall, and it took Kara a while to understand that it had come from her own body. She couldn’t comprehend that the waves of tears falling to the floor were hers, mingling with Other Lena’s on the other woman’s cheeks.

“Please, Lena,” Kara whispered through her tears. “Please. I’ve got you. I’ve got you.”

Other Lena looked so utterly terrified, so devastated in Kara’s arms that Kara felt like screaming her lungs out. She wished the whole world would collapse, she wished the Kryptonite dripping from Other Lena’s wound would kill her, she wished the whole world would just rot away and die – and she wished she could turn back the clock, and undo everything she’d done up to that point, so Other Lena wouldn’t be here. Dying, as she lay in Kara’s arms.

Other Lena’s breaths were getting louder – wetter, like the blood was racing through her airways too, forcing her to use all her strength just to inhale. And though Kara could see that her mouth was moving, trying desperately to say something – (to beg Kara to save her? To beg for her life, though it wasn’t Kara’s to save?) – but no words came out.

Kara wanted to reassure her anyway. Wanted to appease that young version of Lena hiding behind the panic in her eyes. She looked so utterly petrified, and Kara had no way of taking that fear away from her.

“There has to be something,” Kara whispered, but her words were in vain. Her mind had already accepted what her heart could never.

“I’m so sorry, Kara.”

Kara didn’t listen anymore. Alex’s voice was just a gust of wind in her ears, and she would fade away just as easily. There was only one person who still counted, who had absorbed Kara’s entire universe and would take it with her when she went.

“Please,” Kara whispered into Other Lena’s skin, the scent of her blood so strong she could taste it. “Not you. Please not you too. Please.”

Other Lena’s hand came up to cover Kara’s on her chest, the trembling fingers seeking for Kara like she was the only lifeline she had left.

“Please.”

It was no more than a whisp of air coming from Other Lena’s lips, and it was a miracle Kara had even heard her.

“Please,” Other Lena whimpered again. “I don’t… want – ”

Her next words were lost in a cough of blood, and Kara’s fingers tried to wipe the blood away from her mouth, but it was no use. Blood kept bubbling up, and her tears made it next to impossible to keep Other Lena’s face dry. Kara pulled her even closer, the horribly broken shell of a woman clinging to her so weakly – with all the strength she still had left. Kara’s forehead rested against hers, her head supported by Kara’s arm, and eventually, as Kara’s hand slipped from the wound, merely covering it with most of her uninjured arm, she cupped Other Lena’s face as gently as she could.

I’m here, she hoped to convey. You’re not alone. I’m not going.

Other Lena whimpered in Kara’s neck, fingers clutching her blouse tight enough for her nails to dig into Kara’s back.

“I’ve got you, I got you, Lena, I got you,” Kara murmured.

Afterwards, Kara had liked to think that the words, unintelligible murmurs of a suffering, dying woman, had been; “I know.”

A rasping sound that reminded kara nauseatingly of glued pieces of wet cloth slowly being pulled apart, emanated from Other Lena’s lungs.

“Don’t go, Lena,” Kara whispered against Other Lena’s forehead. “Please don’t go. I’m so sorry, I’m sorry.”

Kara had once read that death was… peaceful, in a sense. That before one died, there would be a rush of hormones, easing the pain of death, comforting a person to the point where they actually longed to sleep forever. A moment of clarity. Like one had to come out of the womb suffering but was rewarded at the end of their life by some sort of long-forgotten peaceful warmth that would embrace them and release them from the agony of it all. It had comforted Kara, that thought. Knowing that if in the end she did fail a mission and would be on the brink of passing over the edge, there would be no pain or fear anymore. No loneliness.

But when Kaa looked into Other Lena’s terrified eyes, saw her clinging to life, fighting to live, her drowning lungs sputtering for breath as red splatters adorned her mouth and her tears turned pink, running over her cheeks as her mouth moved silently, begging, pleading to live… Kara realized all of it had to be a lie. There was no relief written across Other Lena’s features. No sense of calm. No peace. Just a desperate, doomed wish to live.

“Mxyzptlk –”

It came out as a hoarse whimper, though she had meant to yell it. Had meant to scream it so loud that it would rattle the fifth dimension and force him to come down. She had to try. She couldn’t think of anything else to do.

“Mxyzptlk! Mxy – ”

Another wet, rattling couch wrecked through Other Lena’s body, making her shudder in Kara’s arms, and it turned Kara’s whisper into a sob. There was no use. There was no hope. She couldn’t do anything but stay.

Over and over again, her thumb rubbed circles over Other Lena’s cheek. She pressed her lips to Other Lena’s hairline so many times, begging her to stay with her whole body. She kept whispering variations of the same few sentences. That she was sorry. That she was there for Other Lena. That she would hold on. That things would be okay. Time felt infinite, and yet dangerously short, and when it finally happened, Kara thought everything might have happened in the blink of only a moment.

She was halfway through another whispered: “I’m right here, I’m not going anywhere,” when she felt Other Lena’s hand softly let go of her blouse. Her hand, once the steadiest part of her body, gripping onto Kara as she held onto life itself, dropped to the floor, and her entire body went slack.

Kara trembled all over, blinking tears away as she let out a shuddering breath. For a moment, it felt like the entire world was holding its breath for Kara. The world had gone quiet, waiting to see what had happened. Kara squeezed her eyes shut one final time, before forcing herself to look, forcing herself to face her.

Other Lena’s eyes were open still. The horror was still etched in her features, mouth open, like she had met death, and had gone screaming. There was no life in her eyes anymore. The lively spark that had enthralled Kara time and time again, that had lured her into Other Lena’s presence so easily, so intoxicatingly sweetly… was gone. Her face was a ghastly shade of white, her lips a pale blue color, as if everything about her wanted to announce that every aspect of life had left her. Kara gently lowered her arm, and Other Lena’s head rolled against her arm, with no power of its own.

She was gone.

Kara thought she might scream, or cry – harder than she’d been crying before. The way she’d screamed her lungs out for her parents in that pod, the only sound in an otherwise silently indifferent universe. The way she’d cried for Mon-El when he left, and she was so sure she’d just sent him to die, alone. But to her surprise, no sound left her lips. Not even when her mouth fell open, eyes clenched shut like she never wanted to see the world again, her whole body shuddering with an inhuman feeling of such horror, that Kara didn’t think she’d ever find the words to describe.

Kara sank back, her whole body giving up, all of her efforts in vain.

Other Lena was dead, and Kara didn’t think she’d ever want to live again.

 

 

It was dark for a long time, but Kara could impossibly tell how long.

She was cold to the bone. Shivering. The only source of heat she felt was the gnawing pain of the kryptonite still dripping out of Other Lena’s chest. Her knees were bruised from sitting on the cold floor, her back stiff and tired. She was dimly aware of Alex, sitting back on her knees just beside Kara, unable to help, but refusing to leave Kara alone for just a second. Dreamer was there now. So were J’onn and Brainy. But they hadn’t come forward yet. If Kara had to guess, someone had told them enough to know that there was no way of reaching her yet.

In her surroundings, there were words. Loose phrases that barely penetrated her mind, though after hearing them often enough, connected enough parts for Kara to piece together what happened.

Lex had planned everything all along. He had his people hide within the D.E.O. as a backup plan. Just in case Other Lena didn’t do what he had expected her to. If Kara had the power to feel anything, she might’ve found it darkly amusing that Other Lena’s final act on her world had been to absolutely ruin Lex Luthor’s day – and to destroy any horribly mistaken image he had of her. He’d planned it out enough for most superheroes to be gone. Dreamer and her friends were at the site of the explosion, exploring what happened while Kara had run the lungs out of her body trying to get to Other Lena – running straight into his trap with a blind willingness to find her.

Those words made sense. They connected something in Kara’s mind that explained enough for her to understand. But as it was, Kara couldn’t even figure out how to move from her spot on the floor, let alone process anything further than that. She didn’t care to understand what had happened. Not really. The only thing that stuck out to her, was that someone had said that the bullet was meant for her.

That made sense.

It was supposed to be her.

It was meant to be her, lying on the floor.

 

 

“Kara?”

Kara didn’t react when Alex carefully tried to reach her. She didn’t know how to talk anymore. She wasn’t sure she even wanted to. Alex had called her name a couple of times now, but Kara hadn’t found the strength to respond. She’d heard several variations on why she had to go now. Why she had to let go. But the one time someone had tried to gently pull Kara away, she’d lashed out, and shielded Other Lena’s body with her own until the hand had finally relented, too afraid to further upset her.

Alex sighed.

“It’s no use. She won’t let go. I can’t get her to let go. But you know she has to.”

“Let me try.”

The familiar sound of that voice sent arrows piercing through Kara’s heart, as she felt a renewed flare of pain flash through her.

“Kara?”

Kara didn’t want to look. She hid her face, her chin still resting on Other Lena’s head.

“Kara, honey, can you look at me? Please?”

The heartbreak in Lena’s voice was enough to rile up the guilt already stewing inside of her, and Kara sniffled, her eyes turning glassy, against all of her expectations. She thought for sure that she was all cried out by then. How could one person contain that many tears?

“It’s okay, you don’t have to look at me,” the voice eventually whispered. “I’m sure I… I’m sure it’s hard.”

Kara let out a shaky breath, staring at the dark tiles on the floor as if they could possibly whisk her away from there. She wished she could take Other Lena far away, somewhere beautiful, and peaceful. Somewhere could let her go knowing she was in good hands. Still, she knew that even in the most beautiful of fields, in the most gorgeous of circumstances, she still would not be able to let her go.

“You don’t have to look at me,” Lena continued softly, “but can you listen?”

Though Kara felt like her body was stiff and frozen, a dark, deformed version of the statue of Maria holding her tortured son’s body – the alien and the murderer – she managed to nod once, the movement jerky and uncontrolled. But it was enough for Lena to let out a relieved sigh, and from the corner of her eye, she could tell that Alex had nodded at her. She could go on.

“I know you don’t want to let go.”

Kara made a sound – half protesting, half aggressive, but the lack of use of her vocal cords for the last couple of hours made it come out more like a hoarse, pitiful, little moan.

“I know,” Lena said quickly. “I understand.”

How could she possibly understand?

“Kara,” Lena said slowly – yet so, so gently. “You did everything you could for her. You did what you promised.”

Kara wanted to scream at her, she just didn’t have the strength or will to move forward. Lena’s voice came somewhere from behind her, next to her. Kara wished she would go, and yet, she wanted to beg her to stay with her forever because she didn’t think she could live if Lena would go away too.

“Your powers aren’t returning as long as you’re holding her, Kara. Do you understand?”

It wasn’t patronizing. It felt like Lena was not sure how much Kara was understanding of anything, sitting there, and Kara wasn’t sure either. The words held meaning, but she also cared so little to process their meanings, that she’d rather just discard them as useless anyway. But Lena’s words made sense. Her voice made sense. Comfortable and so agonizing at the same time.

“The kryptonite is keeping you from getting better. I know there’s not a lot… there, but it will get worse Kara. If you stay there long enough, it will make you sick. It’s a wonder it hasn’t killed you yet. But a slow death will be unavoidable. You can feel it already, can’t you?”

Kara didn’t want to listen, but she knew Lena was right. She was so cold. So, so cold. She was scared to move her fingers, scared they might break off, frozen stuck to Other Lena’s cold body. Her head was heavy, her entire body sick with something she couldn’t process, and wouldn’t process, as long as she was sitting there. The pain in her arm was still there, but it was no longer sharp and stinging. It had turned into a dull, throbbing ache, one she could manage. Even if it made her feel so weak. So… absent. She felt light enough to float away, anchored only by Other Lena’s body on her lap.

“I know you feel like you can’t let go, but you’ll have to eventually. You know you do.”

Kara didn’t show any signs that she’d heard her. Eventually, though, Lena shuffled closer. Her voice came closer. Close enough to send shivers down her spine.

“You did what you had to do, Kara,” she whispered. “You did everything you could. You can let go now.”

“No.”

It was the first word that Kara had spoken since Other Lena had died, and she felt like a ghost, haunting the space around her with her barely intelligible sounds. If it had surprised Lena and caught her off guard, she didn’t show it.

“Why not?” she asked gently.

Kara’s lips trembled. Tears burned into her eyes with renewed force as she let out a faltering breath.

“Because she needs me,” she said slowly, like no one around her would possibly understand. Like she had to make them understand.

“Does she need you like this?” Lena asked. “Are you helping her like this?”

Kara wanted to shout, but instead, she could only let tears glide over her sticky cheeks, and turn her head away, squeezing her eyes shut so tightly, she wished she could shut the world out as well.

“She needs me,” Kara repeated, shaking slightly, the body in her arms moving with her. “She didn’t want to be alone. She can’t be alone, I can’t leave her, I can’t – ”

A choking sob killed the words in her throat, and Kara squeezed Other Lena closer.

“But you didn’t leave her,” Lena said gently, crouching down beside Kara. “You didn’t leave her once. She wasn’t alone. She had you.”

“No,” Kara shook her head. “No, no. I let her die. I – I did. I let her die alone. I couldn’t – I didn’t do enough.”

It seemed like all the self-control Lena had gone right out the window when Kara had spoken, because Kara suddenly felt Lena’s warm hand – the first source of heat she’d felt in so long that Kara almost melted into it – on her shoulder, her face so close that Kara had to fight not to look.

“Kara?” Lena asked, her voice breaking. “Please look at me? Please?”

Kara swallowed. Slowly, with so, so much trouble, she turned her head slightly, and in one jerky moment, their eyes met. Kara saw Lena’s eyes – green and blue, mixed with concern and love, and something that Kara had never put her finger on, something that made her so distinctively different from Other Lena.

She didn’t know whether she had hoped to find the same eyes. The same look. The same mischievous spark, the same tilted head, and characteristic smirk that promised adventure, adrenaline, and so much excitement. But instead, she was met with a familiar, kinder look. One that Kara would recognize out of a thousand different versions of Lena. It was her Lena. Her friend. Her Lena. But not Other Lena. Unmistakenly, distinctly not Other Lena.

Kara felt a rush of guilt when she realized how much that made her want to cry.

Lena’s other hand came up to Kara’s face, gently wiping tears away, her thumb lingering on Kara’s cheekbone. She was crouched on the dirty floor in her pretty clothes, and Kara almost wanted to say that she shouldn’t be in the dirt with her. In the pool of caked blood. But she didn’t think Lena was thinking about that now.

“I was supposed to stay with her,” Kara whispered hoarsely, calm and frozen while her tears spilled over Lena’s fingers. “I promised I wouldn’t leave. I promised her – Lena, I – ”

“And you kept your promise,” Lena said strongly. “You did everything you were supposed to do! You kept her safe. You stayed with her – you did. She wasn’t alone. You made sure of that. She’s at peace now, Kara. She’s okay. You made sure of it.”

“No,” Kara wanted to shake her head, but Lena didn’t let go of her, and didn’t let her eyes stray away from her for just a second. “No, she’s – I have to stay.”

“Kara – ”

“She was not at peace! She was crying! She was scared she – oh God,” Kara couldn’t look, the pain tore through her like a hurricane, and she felt like dying all over again. “She was so scared, she was so scared – ”

“But you were there to guide her through it,” Lena insisted gently. “You didn’t leave her alone. You didn’t let her face it by herself. You did that for her.”

Kara shook her head, unwilling to hear anything more.

From the corner of her eye, she could see Alex sitting back, watching their discussion with worried eyes, like one wrong word on Lena’s end would send her spinning again.

“Kara,” Lena said, following Kara with her insistent eyes until Kara had to tearfully return her stare. “You stayed. You did everything you could for her. You fulfilled your promise. And she died after having done the right thing. You gave her the chance to do the right thing. You stayed with her, attesting to that change. I’m sure she felt that.”

Her voice got softer, more soothing. Her finger wiped more tears away as she tilted her head, looking at her like she was sure Kara might break into a thousand pieces if she looked away.

“I called Mxyzptlk,” Kara whispered hoarsely. “I called Alex.”

Lena listened calmly, nodding her head.

“But Mxy didn’t help. And Alex couldn’t save her.”

“No one could’ve helped her,” Lena said gently. “She was struck twice. But even then,” she shook her head. “She’d been artificially held together for a long time, Kara. My mother is smart, but she’s not a scientific genius. The core was fragile. There was nothing anyone could do to help her after it had been shot, sweetheart.”

Kara blinked tears away, looking at Lena like she wished she could’ve said anything else. Anything like Kara’s powers could’ve saved Lena. A more advanced knowledge of science and medicine could’ve stabilized the kryptonite core and Lena could’ve walked, with only a bullet to proudly attest to her brother’s failed attempt on her life. She would’ve sported it with a grin and would’ve shown it off at every opportunity, Kara could just see it. She bowed her head, squeezing the tears away.

“I don’t want to leave her,” she admitted, heart breaking all over again.

“I know,” Lena whispered softly. “But you didn’t. You’re not leaving her. You’re letting her be cared for. You’re letting her body go – not who she was.”

“What’s going to happen to her? If I were to let go?”

“I’ll make sure she’s brought to the medical wing,” Lena said slowly, gently, as if she were talking to a child instead of a broken superhero. “They’ll take care of her there. I’ll get her some of my clothes. We’ll be gentle with her, I promise.”

The thought of Other Lena on a metal tray in some mortuary made Kara’s stomach turn, but it seemed like Lena could read her mind.

“We won’t have to go to any scary place,” she reassured her. “We’ll get her dressed. We’ll clean her up. You will get to say goodbye.”

Kara looked up at Lena, who radiated so much love that Kara couldn’t help but trust her.

“You promise?”

“On everything I hold dear,” Lena whispered back.

Kara’s head fell and she opened her eyes one last time, pain coursing through her body, to look at Other Lena. Pale. Dead. Empty Other Lena.

Lena was right. She was no longer there. Kara had said goodbye to her long ago.

“You can let go now, Kara.”

Kara nodded. She leaned over and pressed one final kiss to Other Lena’s cold forehead. She was no longer there. But just in case she was still there, lingering at the D.E.O. somewhere until her body was laid to rest, Kara wanted to say goodbye. Just one last time.

“Okay,” she whispered, leaning back. “I can let go now.”

Lena nodded, hand rubbing Kara’s back so warmly, so comfortingly, that Kara felt something inside of her loosen. A sort of peace, a restfulness, knowing someone else would take care of her. That Kara wasn’t alone. That she could pass the burden to someone else, even just for a moment, and a weight, however small, lifted off her heart.

But just as Kara was moving her shoulders, preparing her cold hands to let go of the woman who had so dramatically altered her life in just a few short months, a blur of blue-purple smoke, accompanied by a gush of wind, appeared by their side. Kara had to shield her eyes from the light while Lena immediately covered her, protecting her like she hadn’t been able to that day.

“Woof. They have got to invent a more comfortable way of traveling between interdimensional realms, I tell you. This really isn’t the trip I’d – Woah, many guns!”

Kara blinked against the light to find Mxyzptlk in his true form, standing in the grand hall of the D.E.O., every single agent present pointing their gun his way, while J’onn, Dreamer, and Brainy had their hands up, ready to attack. Ready to defend her.

“Mxyzptlk,” Kara whispered.

Mxy turned almost comically on the spot to look at Kara, and his face instantly softened, though his smile disappeared quickly when he saw her.

What a sight she must’ve been. Still crying, covered in blood and grime, hugging a corpse on a dirty floor. Kara would think she’d landed in another hell world, had she encountered herself like that.

“Oh dear,” he whispered. “Oh dear, oh dear.”

“She – she came through the portal, but now – ”

Mxy quickly shook his head, and Kara fell silent. It was a good thing, she figured. She didn’t know how far she would get in the story before breaking out into tears once more. So instead, she just asked:

“Why didn’t you come? I called you.”

“I’m sorry, Kara,” he said. “Someone messed with the fifth-dimensional portals, and the transference has been beyond terrible. I’m afraid your message must’ve gotten lost. Whatever caused the disturbance suddenly disappeared, and I heard you call my name, and well,” he shrugged. “Your wish is, and will always be, my command.”

Other Lena. The disturbance that could’ve meant her salvation, ironically unavailable due to her very existence. Like the universe had personally intervened to make sure there was no way of saving her. Kara could cry all over again.

Kara thought she might get angry – might curse him out, attack him for all she was still worth, which couldn’t have been very much. But instead, she just looked at him through her unshed tears and nodded.

“There was nothing you could do anyway,” she said quietly, both to herself and Mxy. Because there wasn’t. Lena’s hand on her shoulder reminded her of that.

“Maybe not,” Mxy said, quickly hopping closer, crouching down to get to Kara’s level. “But maybe there is something you and I can do together?”

Kara looked at him through her wet lashes, confused.

“What?”

“Remember last time? When I said I owed you one for all the, shall we say, shenanigans I caused in your life?”

Kara still didn’t understand, but she could feel Lena getting agitated beside her, clearly unimpressed by Mxyzptlk. Kara didn’t blame her.

“Kara,” he turned serious, his bright eyes boring into hers, willing her to understand something he could not spell out for her. “I can’t tell you what to do, and I can’t change what happened here. But I can still give you the wish you were promised long ago, remember? You didn’t use it. Which means, by Imp law, I am still required to say: I owe you one.”

Kara looked at Lena and then back at Mxy. Something awakened in her mind, and her eyes widened. Mxy lit up with excitement, fists clenched by his sides.

“Your wish is my command,” he repeated. “You and I can do things that might spark changes all across the universe! Tell me, and I’ll do what I can. You know I will. You called me here. Make sure it’s for the right reason.”

Kara looked at the woman in her arms, unmoving. Blue eyelids, of eyes that would never open again. Blue lips that would never whisper another word. A woman whose life Kara had personally altered by making just one decision – one wish. If she could change the outcome of so many lives once…

“I wish,” Kara started, voice breaking from exhaustion.

Mxy nodded quickly, excitedly. Lena, meanwhile, looked concerned, looking at Kara like she trusted her, but was afraid to leave her side one more time. Kara looked at Lena, who shot her a tense, but reassuring smile.

“I wish,” Kara started again, stronger, this time, “that Other Lena would be sent back to her universe, to before I had interfered in her life – to before I had wished she had never met me – and that her life went on the way it should have, with me in it. The good and the bad. That’s my wish!”

Was it right? Would it help? Did she mess up and make things worse? Would that even be possible?

“Are you sure?” Mxy asked, hands at the ready.

Kara looked back at Mxy, eyes full of a fire that she thought she’d never feel again.

“I’m sure. That is my wish.”

“I do love it when you’re so confident,” Mxy grinned. “Very well. Your wish – ”

Sparks shot from his hand in a gust of blue and purple smoke, and Kara had to hide her face in Lena’s neck to shield her eyes. Lena’s arms wrapped around her body protectively, and together they endured the force of Mxy’s spell.

 

 

Kara’s pain instantly faded. It felt like a huge knife had been pulled from her chest, and had been replaced with the strongest painkiller known to man, relieving her of the pain so quickly, and with such quiet force, she could almost faint. She gasped for breath as the lack of pain left her drowsy for a split second, and left the world painfully vague and ill-defined. Kara’s chest rose and fell quickly, her heart hammering against her chest with renewed vigor, the blood coursing through her veins like it hadn’t had the chance to before. She felt a rush of heat return to her cheeks, and to the tips of her fingers, which gratefully budged, released from their painful hold.

Kara stared confused at the empty space below her. Her bloodied hands, which had just been holding the cold, dead body of another woman, were shaking uselessly before her. Her dry sobs didn’t cease, shaking and rattling her chest with every raspy breath, tears still falling on the floor below, where blood was already curling, turning into ugly brown rust stains around the traces of a person who wasn’t there. Kara couldn’t stop crying, even though confusion had long taken over. Through her tears and painful sobs, her eyebrows knitted together in confusion, as she swallowed the pain away with the salty tears. After a while, the confusion seemed more important than the fear before, and Kara felt the flow of tears slow as she blinked, slowly gaining a better grip on reality.

“Where – where did she go?” Kara asked between bewildered, dry gasps of air. The shakiness and instability of her irregular heart and lungs remained. There was just confusion.

Kara looked up. “Where’d she go?”

Alex was in front of her, having kept silent while Lena had talked. The pale, tear-stained face of her sister looked just as lost and confused as her own probably did, her hands, splattered with the blood of Other Lena still clenched into fists on her lap. Lena looked just as confused, still holding Kara with one arm, though there was no one she needed protection from at that moment. Kara guessed that maybe Lena needed to hold her just as much as Kara had needed to hold Other Lena, and that was enough for Kara to let her.

“What happened?” Kara asked again. “Where is she? Where’s Lena?”

When she turned around, Mxy stood aside with a small grin on his face, his pristine suit horrifically unblemished in the room of horror they’d found themselves in. The devilishly mischievous sparkle in his eyes was enough to make Alex tense up beside Kara, but she didn’t care. Not in the slightest. Because in his hand, holding it up to them like he was personally teasing Kara with a Golden Ticket, the item that Kara had never been more terrified and more exhilarated to see, was another one of Mxy’s tapes. He slowly waved it in his hands, but Kara could still make out the title clear as day.

Tilting his hand with his signature smirk, Mxy waved ‘The One where Kara saved Lena’ tape before her eyes. Kara trembled. No one said a word as Mxy just grinned, purposefully prolonging the horrific suspense in the room before finally opening his mouth, saying:

“Shall we find out?”

Chapter 13

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“Shall we find out?”

Mxyzptlk flicked his hand, and in an instant, the cold, bloody scene of before was transformed into a modern TV room, with blankets, chairs, and pillows comfortably strewn around the place. Kara felt herself being lifted up and placed in a velvet loveseat, Lena clinging on to her slightly tighter when she noticed the lack of control over their movements.

“Maybe this shouldn’t be a free for all,” Mxy decided – and all at once, her friends around her, even the agents who had responded to the chaos – all of them were pushed out of the room with a strong gust of air, accompanied by a few panicked yelps and looks, as a TV screen appeared before them.

Alex shot him a look so vitriolic, that before Mxy could even snap his fingers, he’d come to the conclusion that it would save him a lot of pain if he decided to back off then and there. Instead, he casually directed her to one of the velvet couches in the room, right next to Kara. Alex sat down beside her, and after narrowing her eyes one last time at Mxy, focused her attention solely on Kara.

She took Kara’s hand in her own and squeezed.

The remaining agents did not get such a careful treatment and were shut out of the room with a strong gust of wind, before the door shut closed with a quick move of Mxy’s hand. 

Any other day, Kara would’ve berated Mxy for his lack of finesse and care for other people’s bodily autonomy, but Kara didn’t say anything. She couldn’t remember why she hated the fact that he had popcorn in his hands, watching the dark screen attentively as his video slid into the player. She couldn’t remember why she felt so powerless, having other people witnessing the outcome of her wish like some sort of spectacle. Maybe she could, if there was still something of herself present inside of her. Some remnant of the Kara she had been before she’d watched that bullet go through Other Lena’s body.

But instead, Kara was empty. It felt like her entire being had been drained, and she wasn’t quite sure what remained in her shell of flesh, cells, and bones. If she’d still had the power to think further than what she could see before her, she might wonder whether she was still there at all. But then she felt Lena’s hand drift to her waist, pulling slightly to get Kara to turn her head. She did, with great difficulty. Her tired eyes found Lena’s, waiting so patiently for her.

“Hey,” she whispered.

Kara wanted to reply but didn’t know how to.

“Whatever we see. Whatever happens,” she stared so deeply into Kara’s eyes that Kara thought she might be searching for a sign of life that just wasn’t there anymore. “We know you tried everything, everything, okay?” Her words carried weight, an insistence on being understood, an insistence on being believed. “No matter what,” Lena said, “you gave it your all, you understand that, right?”

Kara blinked tiredly at her, before nodding, just once.

Lena squeezed Kara’s hand she’d pulled in her lap.

“You did everything you could. No matter what happens.”

Before Kara could give Lena anything in return, the screen before they flickered to life, and Kara felt her stomach drop, like she was about to fall from the sky, unsure whether she could still fly and quit her fall halfway. Unsure of whether she even wanted to. She felt Lena squeeze her hand.

Whatever happens… Kara wouldn’t be able to do a single thing. It would all be up to Other Lena now.

 

 

Lena woke up with a start, her heart pounding in her throat. She gasped for breath, clutching her chest like she could catch her heart right before it slipped right out of her open chest. There were black spots obscuring her vision, her ears were ringing, and she couldn’t remember the last time she’d felt such an anxious, painful knot in the middle of her lungs. She could hear her heartbeat in her ears, pumping blood faster than it ever should.

Her heart.

Something was so terribly wrong – something was out of place. But Lena couldn’t put her finger on it. She could only deal with the creeping feeling that something was not as it should be.

Lena blinked against the light until the dark spots dissipated, and she could take in the room around her. Her head was pounding, a vague cloud of an imminent feeling that she had to do something obscured memories that forcibly tried to push to the forefront. Her head was a mess. Lena shook her head and looked down.

She was at her desk. Her flawless, white desk, designed for her by a friend at Reflex Angelo. She blinked in confusion. She was so sure it had been destroyed a long time ago in the attack by her brother. She was sure of it, she thought. Hadn’t she had to replace it with an uglier, black one instead? After months of revalidation? And hadn’t she had to replace the chair with a more comfortable one after her multiple surgeries by her mother had left her disfigured and unable to stand the pain of sitting down for long periods of time? One with support of her lower back, where an iron bar held her bones together?

Lena froze.

Slowly, she dared raise her head and look around.

It was her office, bathed in sunlight. It was a gorgeous, sunny day outside. She couldn’t hear the traffic from all the way up in her office, but something about the air and the light made her think that it was a good day. A peaceful, late summer day. One of those last days in which people tried with all their might to enjoy the final rays of sunlight and absence of rain to sit outside and anticipate the coming fall.

She couldn’t remember when she’d last felt that careless feeling of untethered joy in her city. There didn’t seem to be much to celebrate after she’d mandated curfews, and had filled the air with her HOPE bots. But she didn’t hear their buzzing outside. She didn’t see their shadows hovering over her floor.

Lena twisted her head. Behind her, her balcony was intact, tidy, and open. Just as it had been when she’d first taken of LuthorCorp and had made it her own.

"No," she whispered. "No.”

But no matter how much she didn’t dare believe that it was true, no matter how much she doubted her own memory, Lena had to ascertain that this was, in fact, her office. Just not the office she remembered leaving months ago to travel to another dimension…

Lena gasped and clutched at her chest.

There.

The feeling she couldn’t place before. Something so right, so common, so normal, a long-lost feeling that her body had celebrated before her mind had been able to conjure up an explanation as to why it shouldn’t feel right.
