Countless nights she spent at Kara’s apartment, comforting her as she cried – or became impassive and empty. Lena stood by her until Kara could feel things again, patiently tending to her like it was her life’s purpose. Something she would’ve hated in another life, when she valued no pain but her own. But for Kara, she felt every ache so much deeper in her own heart. She wanted to make her happy. She wanted to see her smile. So she cooked, sent gifts, stayed the night over and over again, if it meant making even the tiniest change. Even when Alex wasn’t allowed to help her – which Lena still couldn’t help but feel a little smug about, the part that wanted to stress Alex out just a little bit never having gone away completely – Lena was there.

She had to be there, Kara wanted her there.

Even if it was just to watch Rom-Coms with her as Kara fell asleep with a tired, restless expression on her face. Even if it was to hold Kara as she softly nudged her forehead into Lena’s neck, and Lena had to carefully, hesitantly wrap her arms around Kara’s fragile form – so unnatural a move for someone who had had no one to embrace like that in almost a decade.

But seeing Kara get better so slowly, over time, seeing that sadness transform into weak smiles, and quiet laughs shared deep at night, under the cozy covers, gave Lena a rush of life – a rush of purpose. She was there for Kara, and she helped her get better, slowly but surely. And Kara invertedly, easily, did the same for her. They made each other better, in the most beautiful ways possible.

There were still times that she wanted to reject Kara’s presence in her life. Wanted to curse and scream and rage. Missed her counterpart in a way she could never express to anyone. But seeing Kara’s face was enough to silence those thoughts completely. There were no two versions of the same person. They were different, Lena came to find out. Two completely different people. The Other Kara became a friend from her past, one she could still miss so deeply. But this Kara… this Kara became everything she had never known in a person. She became a purpose. A calming presence.

She was everything.

They belonged irrevocably in each other’s lives, and Lena found herself dwelling less and less on her past, and more on her future, with Kara prominently in it.  

 

 

Lena remembered bits and pieces of the past she had studied through the Other Lena’s documents delivered to her cell, but it felt very different combatting it by herself. Knowing it was Kara, Supergirl, who was suffering beside her, but not being able to say or do anything to help her… it was torturous in some aspects, but a blessing on other occasions. They both had their secrets to keep, the parts of themselves they wanted to keep hidden from each other, and from the world.

Lena had told Kara once that she was not as perfect as Kara might think she was. That she held secrets that she couldn’t share with anyone. Kara had simply looked at her, more calculating, older and wiser than she had ever seemed, before whispering that she understood, and that she was ready to listen when Lena was ready to tell – and that she would listen openly. Without judgement.

Lena was not too sure of that.

She worried, often and constantly, about how ethical it was, knowing she’d already met a version of Kara in another universe, and never telling her. Then again, Kara was not too keen on sharing that she knew Lena as two different versions either, as both Supergirl, her protector and often her colleague, and as Kara, her friend. Lena hoped they were even, but she often doubted they were.

And Lena could live with that. Mostly. But it was only later after, when their professional and personal lives began to intertwine more, that Lena began to understand why her counterpart had suffered so in dealing with Kara’s silence.

She had nightmares sometimes, after seeing Kara on the news after a fight. Or seeing her on a table at the D.E.O., veins glowing green under her skin in a tauntingly familiar manner. It felt horrid sometimes, watching Kara be crushed by someone on TV one day, and having to see her the next, seeing her wince out of the corner of her eye, weaker than before. How Kara would feign smiles, though Lena could see the pain in her wooden movements, the way she sought out objects to lean on every chance she got. Lena invented one thing after another to help over the years, relentlessly trying to find ways to keep Kara safe from anything and everything. From her, if need be. But it wasn’t enough.

It got infinitely worse when Kara was suddenly not the assumed winner anymore. When another appeared, equally strong, twice as ruthless, and eager to strike Kara down. Reign. Their friend. When Kara became suspicious of everything and everyone around her, glaring down dark corridors and looking over her shoulder like everyone was out to get her. Like Lena was out to get her. But even through the anger, even through Kara’s erratic behavior that almost made Lena slip back into the weaponized sharp coldness she wielded so well, Lena stuck by Kara. Relentlessly. Angrily. Willfully. She didn’t allow Kara to slip away, not as Supergirl, and not as her friend.

“You may not like the fact that I fabricated Kryptonite, and you have a right to argue with me about it, but you do not get to drag my family’s name into this.”

“You swore to me – ”

“I swore to keep this city safe! And that is something that you do not seem to understand,” Lena had said sharply. “I am on your side, Supergirl. I have always been on your side. I will protect you from Reign, and everyone who comes after! That is what I swore; that is what I promised! You might not like my methods, but you sure do love my solutions. Don’t you dare eschew my reasons for helping.”

Their fights simmered out as Lena held on and Supergirl apologized, and Lena knew she had seen a glimmer of surprise in Supergirl’s eyes in the heat of their fight when Lena hadn’t backed down. Lena silently forgave her for pointing fingers so easily, though she couldn’t deny that it had hurt. But Supergirl at least seemed to understand, and if Kara was even kinder and sweeter than before, then Lena could see that she really was trying.

Lena didn’t know if what she’d done, what she’d said to Supergirl, was alright. But in the days after, they continued to work together, even if it was sometimes in a crabby, cold environment. But they celebrated at the end of it, when they won, and encountered their new challenges ahead together. With a new understanding and more trust, Lena found. And Kara remained her closest friend. She was seated next to her on every game night, was privy to all Kara’s worries, hopes, and dreams, despite eluding any Supergirl subjects, and was closer to her than everyone else in her life. Aside from Alex, maybe – whom Lena had grown oddly fond of despite her initial objections – she was Kara’s favorite person in the world, and remained so even after their short spat at the D.E.O. And for Lena, that was still more than enough.

Even after her brother came back, teaming up with her mother to work against them, Lena endured. With Supergirl’s protection and Kara’s unconditional love and support. Lena was thriving. While it became alienating, seeing friend after friend get closer to Kara and be introduced to the secret identity that Lena was kept from, she allowed the pain to be there only as a mild ache. She knew Kara. She had known Supergirl. And she knew that when the time was right, Kara would let her in completely. And though it became longer and lonelier with each passing day, Lena accepted it, and almost never lost her cool around Supergirl anymore. It was enough, being friends with both of them. It was enough, being Kara’s most trusted friend, aside from that critical part. And it was amusing, watching her scatter around excuses whenever an emergency Supergirl situation arose. It was cute, watching her scramble away whenever she thought no one was looking. But Lena was looking out for her. For both versions of her, her heart and body, her mind and soul.

Lena loved her completely.

 

 

It shouldn’t have surprised her as much as it had, then, when Kara finally did tell her. But it overfell her.

They were all gathered up in the lobby of one of the most prestigious halls in National City to celebrate Kara. Lena was asked to deliver the speech, of course. Lena hated speeches with a burning passion, but celebrating Kara with every cell she had was also one of her chief reasons of being, so she bit through it. Moaned and struggled over it for months in her office – up until Kara came to get her, telling her it was much too late to fret over something ‘so stupid.’ Lena disagreed immensely. But how could she put the magnitude of Kara’s love, talent and warmth into words?

She’d poured over it with everything she had, and in the end, she concluded that she had managed to come up with something half-decent, that would at least moderately cover a small bit of the impact Kara had on the world. Kara. Just Kara.

Lena was walking through the hallway above somewhere above the main stage, hidden comfortably away from the crowd buzzing with excitement and Kara’s loved ones. The pressure was insane. And she didn’t even care that she didn’t actively want to murder Alex in this universe, she was still always trying to get under her skin for some reason or other (despite their begrudging agreement that stemmed from a deep form of love for Kara). She would not give Alex the slightest chance to even mouth off once. Not one joke that wouldn’t land, not one awkward stumbling in her phrasing. She would not let Kara and her friends down – she just couldn’t.

So she walked across the venue, round and round, while she could hear the buzzing underneath her feet getting louder, the crowd gathering below. She tried to ignore it, focus on the blurry text in front of her, but two employees walked past her, excitedly chatting about how Cat Grant was rumored to have entered the building, and she felt the sandwich Kara had forced down her throat that morning climb back up her throat.

“Fuck.”

Lena read and re-read the text, muttering to herself while her clammy hands crumpled the paper with every word she got wrong. She felt something rip, and cursed herself when she noticed how she’d absentmindedly torn off a corner of one of the sheets. She sighed, and briefly closed her eyes.

What the fuck was she even doing.

Lena shook her head and opened her eyes, taking a breath to steady herself before taking the text back from the top.

“Lena?”

Lena’s words died a little in her throat as she turned around with a start, only to find the woman of the hour behind her.

“Kara,” the relief of finding her and not some evil nuisance that just couldn’t happen that night. “You scared me.”

She looked absolutely enchanting in her beautiful dress they’d picked out together – Lena’s treat, despite Kara’s objections. Her expression didn’t match her look, though.

Kara tried to smile, but it was barely believable. She looked like someone who had just lost everything, instead of someone who won the award of her dreams. She was wringing her hands, perhaps to hide her trembling fingers. She was glancing up through her bangs intermittently to find Lena, only to cast her eyes down right after.

“What, ehm, whatchodoin’?”

Lena held up her pathetic excuse for a speech.

“Practicing? Just a warning, I wouldn’t get too excited. We might be able to wrap this thing up in a good ten minutes if we try.”

Kara barely smiled at her joke. That was fine, it wasn’t one of her best anyway.

“Kara?” Lena put her speech down and took a step closer to Kara, growing worried when she saw that Kara was actively avoiding her gaze. “Are you alright?”

Kara rubbed at her bare arms, nodding once, before seemingly changing her mind and shaking her head.

And even after all the years together, Lena couldn’t say she had completely gotten rid of her base instincts to hurt. She could feel the familiar rush of pain, daggers in her fingers, excitement in her veins. The urge to find the one who had wronged her, and to make him suffer. To maim and strike, to hurt.

“Did someone say something? Is it that new jerk Andrea hired?”

Her blood boiled just thinking about him. That smug smile, the annoyance in Kara’s voice when she spoke about him. No way she would let that annoying, slug of a man try to even utter –

“No, no nothing like that. No one’s… no one bothered me.”

Lena paused, watching as Kara crawled more and more into her own skin, like she was trying to disappear in the backdrop of her life. Like she ever could. She stood out in the world, blue eyes, blue dress, blonde hair, dazzling being and all. Lena’s heart broke a little, seeing her like that.

“Kara,” she said seriously, taking another step closer, hurting more when Kara seemed to look even more ill, “if you want to ditch this thing… if you want to go, I’ll have us both out of the country in less time than it would take the people here to notice we’re gone.”

“Lena…”

“I’m serious,” Lena said, inching closer, taking Kara’s hand into her own. “If you don’t feel like this is the right thing to do then – ”

“Lena, I’m Supergirl.”

The words, so long awaited and expected, stunned Lena more than she would’ve ever expected. She’d figured out so many scenarios in which she could’ve reacted to those words, but none of those came to mind when she was looking back into Kara’s tear-filled eyes. She was just… stunned.

Most of what Kara said, admittedly, went right past Lena. She was just so… flabbergasted. Kara was crying. She could barely hold herself together, shaking with misery and sorrow. Her black glasses clutched in her hands, tight enough to break. Lena wanted to reach out and console her, instinctively reach out to take the glasses out of Kara’s hands and put her arms around her, but found that she couldn’t. She was utterly frozen, and felt like the world was trying to pass her by, without fully letting her in on the moment. Everything was just… spaced out.

“You’ve been hurt so many times and I… I convinced myself that I was protecting you.”

I was protecting you, Lena wanted to say. You don’t know how much I have to make up for. Enough to fill a hundred lifetimes, and even that wouldn’t be enough. I’m here to protect you. But nothing came out.

Kara’s breathing became more irregular, her cheeks turning more red, the panic growing on her face with each new phrase.

“I was selfish, and scared, and I… I didn’t want to lose you. I – ”

A short breathless gasp prevented her from saying more, and her hand fluttered to her chest as if to steady herself.

“I just didn’t want to lose you,” Kara whispered. “I know it’s selfish to say – especially now – but I need you. I couldn’t… I couldn’t not have you in my life, Lena, I am so, so, sorry. But I just couldn’t b – ”

Lena had nothing to say, the words didn’t want to come. So she did the only thing that felt intrinsically right to every cell in her body. The only thing that seemed to still the confusion in her head, and the turmoil in her heart at seeing Kara like that.

She leaned in, cupped Kara’s cheek, noticed a faint flash of surprise in those glossy blue eyes, and kissed her.

The world went quiet all at once.

Kara’s skin was inconceivably soft under Lena’s fingers, her lips deliciously caught off guard, opened slightly in frozen surprise. Kara made a tiny sound, coming from deep inside her throat, and for a split second, the spell was broken. Kara pulled herself away, Lena’s eyes shooting open in surprise. She’d barely noticed closing them in the first place.

“Kara – ”

Her name came out heady, gravelly low, both a curse and a wonder on her lips. That seemed to be enough because Kara’s eyes fluttered.

She seemed to nod, almost imperfectively so, to herself and leaned back in, one hand sloping over Lena’s shoulder while the other one reached for her waist. Before Lena knew it, they were both leaning forward, meeting in the middle in a soft mash of lips. Careful, at first, exploring the feel of how their lips fit into one loving puzzle, but then Lena couldn’t help herself anymore.

She whispered Kara’s name into her lips, and felt a fire ignite inside her bones when Kara echoed hers. She couldn’t remember who was kissing who, or who had done what to deserve a liftetime of pain and mistrust. All she knew was that she could feel Kara’s heat under her skin, and that Kara’s lips and tongue were touching her own, and how incredibly, deliriously lucky she was to be so devoutly kissed by her.

Kara’s hand moved up towards her face, and a part, buried deep inside of her, felt vaguely reminiscent of a similar move, ages ago. But Lena didn’t even think about it. She relished in the feel of Kara’s fingers around her ear, her palm on her cheek. Nothing had ever felt more right before. Her Kara, around her, against her, before her.

“Kara,” she whispered again.

Kara barely interrupted their kiss, letting Lena speak only to let her lips wander around Lena’s cheek, peppering kisses along her jaw, only to slide up to kiss her cheek, and rejoin her lips as if she was hungry for them. Lena automatically kissed her back, her hand sliding to the back of Kara’s head as if to pull her even closer. As if letting go would stop the kiss, and would make all of it go away. But it wouldn’t. Because she was right where she needed to be.

This was exactly where she was supposed to be.

 “Lena?”

Kara broke away from Lena with her eyes closed, still panting for breath, but in an entirely more delicious way. Her forehead rested against Lena, her eyelids fluttering.

“Yes?”

Lena was just as breathless, just as overwhelmed by the sheer intensity of a kiss she’d waited so long for – one she hadn’t expected, but one she realized she’d longed for since the day Kara had asked her if she needed a friend, right there in her office. So bold, so dangerous, so audacious. Lena had felt the first sparks then, but was too hurt to even realize it. The love she had for Kara had only grown since, with every book exchange, with every coffee date and sleepover. With every whispered secret and every warm hug.

Lena belonged here, right next to Kara.

“Aren’t you mad?” Kara asked, daring to look up from under her eyelashes. They were still wet, still clinging together. “I thought you would… Aren’t you angry?”

Lena had to swallow, before nodding, just once.

“Furious,” she whispered, “but we have all the time in the world to fight about it later. I just want to be here with you right now. I just want you to kiss me again.”

Kara let out a shaky breath before nodding, interlocking her fingers behind Lena’s neck and kissing her, again and again.

“I have so much more to explain,” she whispered in-between kisses.

“So do I,” Lena whispered back.

Kara pulled away just far enough to look into Lena’s eyes.

“You do?”

Lena was able to manage a sad smile on her face.

“I’ve got so much to tell you. And I won’t hate you if you run away by the end of it.”

“I won’t,” Kara said, a determined glance in her eyes. “Never.”

She kissed her again, and Lena felt a storm of feelings inside of her, electing to let them wash over her, if only to fall back into Kara’s sweet kisses again.

“Besides,” Kara whispered into the corner of her mouth, “what if you run away first? I… I’ve done things I’m not proud of. Things you might…”

“I’m not going anywhere,” Lena said, wrapping and arm around Kara’s waist. “I’m meant to be here with you. Through the good and the bad.”

“You believe that?”

“Wholeheartedly.”

Kara let out a shaky breath. She shot Lena a weak smile that made Lena’s knees buckle.

“Alright,” she whispered. “We’ll both come clean then?”

“We will.”

Kara let out a small laugh when Lena kissed the end of Kara’s jawline, dangerously close to her ear.

“But not right now?” she asked.

“No,” Lena whispered. “Now, I just want this.”

By the end of it all, when someone from the venue had to awkwardly cough to interrupt them to inform them the presentation had been scheduled to start fifteen minutes ago, Lena was unable to say how she could ever go back to a life in which she didn’t get to kiss Kara. Her Kara.

“Right.”

Kara blushed a beautiful, pink color, and almost hid within herself, shooting Lena a shy smile. Lena was barely able to keep her heart from jumping out of her chest at the sight. She cleared her throat and straightened her form, reaching up just a little over Kara in her six-inch heels. She shot Kara a knowing smile before allowing herself to slip back into her cool, uncaring mask. She held onto Kara’s hand and shot the man a dull look.

“We’ll be on our way shortly.”

And that was enough to have the man nodding before scrambling away, barely registering the quick: “thank you!” that Kara shot his way.

Kara shook her head, and when she looked at Lena, they both burst out laughing.

“Alright,” Lena kissed Kara on the temple of her beautiful head, “you ready to do this?”

Kara took a deep breath.

“You promise to be up on that stage with me?” she asked.

Lena smiled. “Nothing could keep me from it.”

Kara smiled and pulled Lena in for one last, deep kiss.

“Then I’m ready,” she beamed.

“Good,” Lena smiled, before confidently, happily, and proudly guiding Kara downstairs, excited to face everything to come with Kara beside her.

“Though if that offer of getting out of the country still stands…”

“I will push you onto that stage myself, Danvers, don’t test me.”

Kara laughed. Lena followed her, smiling wider than she had in years.

Chapter 14

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Nobody said a word.

Kara felt three pairs of eyes glued to her face, waiting for a reaction. But there was nothing to say.

The screen had turned black. That was it. The last bit of Other Lena that Kara would ever see. She was gone. Off to live her life as if she was just a character on a show Kara had grown attached to over the years. The last Kara would ever see of her. The last fragment – the last proof of her existence was now gone. Over. Now there was no going back. Nothing to hold onto anymore.

It was over now. And Kara was well and truly alone.

She’d let go. She’d done everything now. Everything there was to do. There was nothing left anymore.

Was this when the healing was supposed to start?

 

Other Lena was happy. She seemed happy? Through the flashes of years and events muddling together, she seemed not to have lost her edge at all, but she’d at least found a life. Friends. People who loved her.

She got the happy ending Kara had taken from her the day she’d stupidly made that wish. And wasn’t that all she could ever ask for? To get her the redemption and love she deserved?

The answer was all there, a resounding YES in her mind.

So why did she feel so fucking hollow inside?

Like someone had started gnawing at the inside of her body, but had run away before finishing the deed, so Kara had to hobble around, a critical piece of her body missing – doomed to live on with this half-body.

She stood up, startling the room. Everyone looked at her. Kara didn’t know how to look any of them in the eye. Instead, she tried to say something, but failed to find any words. Her mouth was half-open, her fingers trembling slightly as she raised her head to find Mxy.

“Thank you, Mxy,” she said hoarsely. “For… everything.”

“Don’t thank me,” he said softly as if he was more overwhelmed by what he had seen now than the horrid life-or-death scenarios he’d run through with her before. So uncharacteristically quiet for the first time since Kara had met him. “I told you I owed you one.”

Kara tried to smile, though it made her feel like throwing up.

“It sure was a big favor to give out,” she said, no louder than a whisper. “Thank you.”

With that, Kara turned around, shaking enough to wobble on her feet. She heard her sister and Lena get on their feet, eager to rush after her, but Kara didn’t give them the chance to. She heard her sister call out words like “prolonged exposure” and “necessary overnight stays at the med-bay,” but they didn’t register properly.

“I’m just gonna…” she didn’t finish her sentence, too dazed to make out her thoughts. Then again, she doubted her words had been loud enough for any of them to wonder what would come next.

Kara started walking. She passed the D.E.O. agents in the hall, the walls a grey blur in the corners of her eyes. Before long, she was out the door, quickening her step, before finally rushing out the door of the D.E.O., hailing a cab before anyone had gathered the courage to rush after her. She imagined Lena might’ve forcibly convinced Alex not to. Maybe she was the only one who saw that Kara had to mourn first.

 

 

Kara didn’t know how she’d gotten through those first few days. She truly didn’t.

Her sister called, at first. Something about her body being extremely vulnerable from the extreme kryptonite radiation. Kara cut off the call before Alex could say a lot more. Alex stopped calling, but when Kara walked finally made it out of her bedroom and into the living room, she noticed a bottle of solar-cell-amplifiers on her kitchen table. Kara hadn’t heard her come in or get out.

The pills were still there, after that first week, unopened.

Andrea called, at first. Leaving some extremely pissed-off voicemails. But those calls eventually stopped too. Kara figured Lena must’ve pulled a hell of a lot of strings to get that done. Either that or Kara had been fired and just hadn’t found out yet. Her phone battery had been dead for days anyway. No way to find out.

Kara didn’t care. She wished she cared. In fact, she wished fervently, silently that she’d start caring again about the silliest and dumbest of things, because if her life from this moment on would just be this horrid hollowness? This unfillable void of grief and nothingness? Then she didn’t think she’d be able to hold on for a lot longer.

It consumed her. She wanted to crawl under furniture, mute the entire world and just disappear. But she wasn’t allowed such luck. Instead, she stayed where she was, in her apartment. Watching as time passed on, while her grief stayed.

The days stretched on. Kara just lay in her bed or on the couch. She didn’t eat. The thought of eating made her more nauseous than she already was, and she found herself on the verge of throwing up whenever her mind started to wander too deeply into the cause of her grief.

When she thought about Other Lena, she always started to cry, but never fully let go. Like the tears burning in her eyes was better than letting herself feel those same tears running down her cheeks. They stayed in the miserable limbo of nothingness that Kara grew to know so deeply.

She didn’t have her powers back yet. She didn’t know how long that would take. It didn’t matter much. She bumped into things sometimes, furniture, corners of tables and the like. She found that her legs were starting to sport strings of bruises. She looked at them a lot, poking the angry spots whenever she felt too dull inside. When they faded too, after having turned an ugly yellow color, Kara’s mind drifted off, and she closed her eyes again.

She slept a lot. She slept through the days and woke up most evenings, feeling more depressed when she saw how dark it was out. It usually made her want to retreat back to her bedroom altogether. When she didn’t sleep, she put on Netflix, and stared with hooded eyes at the TV screen, lit up with bright colors, as the laughing track played over her silent apartment.

She ordered food, but never ate more than a few bites, and watched the boxes grow in number on her kitchen counter, and on the floor beside the couch.

A part of her wanted to feel horrified at the dust gathering on her kitchen table. She wanted to hate the cold food going bad before her eyes. She wanted to hate how she could smell herself on the T-shirt she’d been wearing for the last couple of days. How her sheets were twisted in a mess on her bed, the blinds drawn 24/7.

But the truth was that she felt absolutely nothing. Not a thing.

So Kara lay back down on the couch, pressed ‘yes, I’m still watching,’ and allowed the world to pass her by another day.

 

Only Lena didn’t let her.

She showed up to her apartment after a couple of days, though it was impossible for Kara to tell exactly how much time had passed. It was somewhere after she’d finished another season of Friends, right after she’d seen something fuzzy growing on the pizza, and had gone through the laborious effort of closing the box, so it was hidden from sight.

She knocked at her door. Once. Twice. Incessantly.

Kara was on the couch and barely lifted her head, groaning slightly when the loud knocking refused to stop. It woke her up from her nap, and though Kara slept through most of the day and large parts of the night, she still felt exhausted when she was pulled so roughly from her comfortable silence.

She wanted to ignore it. She tried really hard, in fact. She put one of the couch cushions over her ears – the blissful underwater feel of the noise around her fading away a welcomed attribute of her non-powered state. The knocking stopped after a while. Kara put the pillow down. And then it started again a moment later, like the person at the door had heard Kara move and was determined not to let Kara get off easy.

Kara groaned.

She looked at the ceiling and knew she wouldn’t feel peace again until she answered the door and told whoever was there that she had no interest in rejoining the rest of the world for a while.

Kara forced herself off the couch with a quiet moan, and trudged over the door. She felt lightheaded, the blood rushing to her head as she moved, and swayed on her feet at one point. The knocking didn’t subside. Kara turned the lock with a sigh – and her heart dropped when she opened the door.

Lena.

Not Lena.

Her universe’s Lena. Of course it was. It couldn’t have been Other Lena, of course it wasn’t. There was no way that seeing her would ever be possible again. But her heart skipped a beat anyway, and she couldn’t repress the hopeful flutter that settled so deceitfully in her stomach when she saw Lena’s face.

But the second she saw those green eyes widening before settling in that all-too-familiar pitiful, sad look, Kara’s heart sank. She hated herself for allowing that wave of hurt to soar through her, to look at Lena and feel a tiny piece of resentment and loss gnawing at her heart because she wasn’t Other Lena. She was gone.

It took Kara a while to notice she was taking shallow breaths, and that she hadn’t responded to Lena’s question.

She shook her head, a dazed lightness making her head fuzzy.

“Kara?”

“What?”

Lena took a deep, understanding breath.

“I asked you how you were, darling.”

“Oh.”

Kara blinked against the light coming from the big window in the hallway. It hurt her eyes. She held a shaky hand up to block the light and found Lena’s face looking even more concerned in the light.

“I’m okay,” Kara whispered hoarsely. “I’m just tired.”

Lena’s eyes scanned her face and body as if to see whether she was actually still as alive as she claimed to be, but something seemed to freeze as her eyes settled somewhere on her face. The expression of pity seemed to make way for horror and a deep unsettlement that Kara didn’t quite know what to make of.

“Sweetheart, you…”

Lena had to take a breath and covered her mouth with her fist. Kara didn’t understand why Lena looked away, or why she had a glistening in her eyes when she turned back.

“Sweetheart, you… you have a little…”

Kara looked at her. She was so tired. She didn’t understand.

Lena looked down before pursing her lips, trying to get a hold of herself.

“Honey, have you taken a shower yet? After… after everything?”

Kara didn’t understand. Was Lena just coming over to berate her for her lack of personal hygiene? She didn’t feel very self-conscious but found that she didn’t much like it either.

“Why, do I smell bad?”

“No, no, no, it’s not that, it’s…” She took a deep breath before taking a step closer to Kara. Kara swallowed her nerves as Lena’s trembling fingers seemed to reach out to her face, but paused mid-air as if they thought better of it. “Honey, you still have some… blood, right over here.”

Kara froze. Lena’s fingers finally moved, and touched her forehead, right at her hairline.

“Oh.”

Kara didn’t know what to say to that.

“I didn’t… I didn’t know.”

“It’s here, and by your ear and… it’s… it’s…”

Everywhere. She didn’t have to say it for Kara to understand. She hadn’t looked in a mirror yet, hadn’t bothered or cared to in the last couple of days, but Lena’s face spoke a million words.

Lena nodded, tears sparkling in her eyes. She bit her lip as hard as she could, but when Kara reached out and lifted her own tresses of hair to her eyes just to find that the ends of it were knotted in thick, dark, dried strands of caked-up blood, she broke.

“Oh honey, please, let me.”

She gently took Kara by her hand, and led her into her own apartment. Kara was still fixated on the strand of blood-clotted hair before her, too numb and dazed to protest. She let herself be walked into her apartment, let Lena take over.

Lena guided her to her couch and sat her down gently.

She wanted to sit down next to her but stood back up when she saw the greasy, plastic, take-out bags on the couch. Lena looked around the apartment, but Kara didn’t want to see the disgust on her face when she took it all in, so she looked down instead. She heard Lena gulp and wring her hands together.

“Right,” she heard her whisper.

But when Lena crouched on her knees to face her, Kara didn’t see a sign of disgust or repulsion on Lena’s face. Instead, all she saw was concern.

“Honey, has anybody checked up on you lately?”

Kara pulled her feet up on the couch, and watched her TV screen, still frozen on a scene from a sitcom she couldn’t name.

“Alex stopped by,” Kara mumbled. “I didn’t want her here.”

Lena paused for a bit.

“Andrea said you haven’t been at work for a while.”

Kara shrugged. Lena sighed deeply.

“Alright, let’s take this step by step.”

Lena shrugged off her dark coat, folded it and put it over the back of her couch. She sighed and crouched back down to Kara’s level. She raised two fingers to graze at Kara’s chin with just the slightest amount of power needed to lift her head towards herself. Kara looked at her, and felt a little ashamed, seeing how worried Lena looked, how concerned for someone who shouldn’t get concern. Least of all from Lena.

“Honey? You need to take a shower, okay? This isn’t good for you. There’s… there’s no getting better like this. No going forward.”

She whispered it so kindly, so gently, that Kara couldn’t help but nod. Even if the words didn’t really make sense to her.

What if she didn’t want to go forward? What if she couldn’t let go? What if she missed Other Lena so much her heart felt like it was beating in her throat and the pain left her feeling so fucking hollow?

Going forward, getting better. Those seemed like foreign, impossible concepts to her. How would she ever move on? In her head, she was still there, still on the floor, with Other Lena in her arms. But Other Lena had moved on. She’d gained a life. A world of her own. She had moved forward. But Kara still had her blood on her forehead. Could still feel Other Lena’s lungs sputtering and heaving for any oxygen she could find. She still hurt when she moved, cramped up from sitting on the cold floor, exposed to the kryptonite that still hadn’t left her body completely. She could still hear her begging Kara for peace, for her life. Things Kara couldn’t give her. She could still hear her crying that she didn’t want to die. Scared. So innocently terrified of something so very real. Something Kara hadn’t been able to keep her from.

And she had. She had died. Right there. Right on the floor. In Kara’s helpless, useless arms. And there was only Kara left to remember.

How could she move on when she could still smell the iron scent of Other Lena’s blood all around her. She didn’t think a shower could ever wash that smell away. Wasn’t sure she wanted it to either. She didn’t want to wash the last traces of Other Lena away.

“Okay,” Lena’s smile trembled with relief, Kara just didn’t know how to smile back. “Okay, let’s get you cleaned up.”

Lena took Kara’s hand in hers, and slowly, gently helped pull her up. It took Kara’s tired muscles a while to force her body into motion, but she got there eventually, guided by Lena’s patient hands.

Lena walked her to her tiny bathroom, barely big enough to fit the two of them without sticking close to one another. Lena didn’t let it bother her. She sat Kara down on the lid of the toilet while she walked over to Kara’s bath, crouched down, and struggled to open the water faucet.

Vaguely, Kara recalled having to warn Lena that it didn’t work very well, that it was rusted after years of use, and that her landlord had never gotten around to fix it, but she was too tired and simply looked on.

With a struggling grunt, followed by a victorious, little sound, Lena managed to open the faucet, and cold water started spluttering out. She adjusted the temperature and held her hand underneath the stream of water before deciding it was alright.

“Shower or bath?” she asked, turning her head. Her dark hair swept over her shoulder and exposed a glistening, pearly earring. “Kara?”

Kara looked up, her head a little more tired than before.

“Bath’s fine.”

Lena nodded.

“Alright,” she stood up. “I’ll leave you to it then?”

Kara nodded. Lena walked over to the door and hesitantly paused to put her hand on Kara’s shoulder.

She looked like she wanted to say something, but escaped out the door before she could. Maybe she didn’t have much left to say after all.

Kara sat there for a while, watching the tub slowly fill with water. Lena had put the temperature on high, and the steam soon started filling the room, clouding her mirror. Slowly, ever so slowly, Kara hooked her hands under the sweater she’d been wearing for days, and with slow, wooden movements, started undressing herself. It took her too long, and the bathroom was too cold, and Kara felt stiff and uncomfortable as she walked over the cold wet tiles, leaving her clothes in a pile on the floor. She put in one foot after the other, her body so cold that the water felt scalding, uncomfortably hot on her skin. She forced herself to sink in anyway, to embrace the discomfort, and sit down. She shut the faucet down with both hands and then wrapped her arms around herself.

The water made her more tired than before, and Kara couldn’t remember why she was in there in the first place. She felt so, so tired. She pulled her knees close to her chest, rippling the water, and leaned her head against them. She stayed like that until the water cooled down.

After a while, there was a knock on the door. The room had fogged up completely, a bit of the water was draining away drop by drop, her drainplug old and weathered, unable to hold the water for such a long time.

“Kara?” Lena’s muffled voice reached Kara from behind the door. “Are you done? Do you want me to get some food for us?”

When Kara didn’t reply, Lena knocked a second time. Then a third time, slower.

“Kara?” the voice was gentler now, more on guard. As if she’d forgotten about what kind of zombie Kara had turned into over the last couple of days. Like she was expecting the old Kara to reply, hungry, and eager for a girl’s night in.

“Kara, can I come in?”

Kara closed her eyes.

“Kara please.”

Lena sounded so defeated the final time she said Kara’s name, that Kara’s heart broke right in two.

“Yeah,” she said hoarsely, so quiet she wasn’t really convinced Lena could hear her. “You can come in.”

That was all it took.

Lena opened the door softly, the door creaking on its hinges. A waft of cold air blew through the room and Kara shivered, her arms breaking out into goosebumps.

“Sorry!” Lena quickly closed the door behind her, standing before it with her gaze cast down, a hand before her eyes.

An awkward silence fell over the room. Kara looked at Lena for a while, then back to her tub. It was starting to rust near the edges, and Kara found a tiny cobweb in the corner of her bathroom, right between the foot of her tub and the closet with towels and toiletries.

“Will you be alright?”

Her look was earnest enough to make Kara waver.

“I’m fine.”

“Did you… did you wipe it away? The blood, I mean.”

Kara faltered.

“I… I don’t know.”

“Sweetheart I…”

“I don’t know where it is. I haven’t… I haven’t looked in the mirror yet.”

At that, Lena’s shoulders dropped.

“Of course,” she whispered, her hand lowering a little, her eyes closed in silent exhaustion. “Of course.”

“You can look,” Kara whispered. “It feels worse like this. Like you can’t look at me because I’m dirty.”

It was surprisingly honest, and Kara hadn’t expected those words to roll out the way they did.

Lena’s hand faltered, and then she lowered it, her eyes blinking against the bright lights above Kara’s mirror. When they took in the sight of Kara, cold, arms wrapped tiredly around her own shivering frame, the ends of her hair swimming in the lukewarm water, they softened.

“Kara,” she whispered. “Do you need help?”

“I… I don’t know,” Kara whispered back.

Lena nodded in understanding. “Alright,” she said gently, a sad, little smile on her face. “May I help you?”

Kara paused for a second before agreeing with a single, tired nod. Lena let out a relieved sigh, and after taking a second to gather herself, walked over to Kara, taking a towel and washcloth with her. She sank to her knees on the fuzzy bathmat, and put both of them down beside her.

When their eyes met, Kara suddenly felt her nakedness as a blemish, an injury. How broken, ugly, and scarred she looked, nothing like the woman she was two weeks ago. She was weak, powerless, bruised, scabbed, and stained with someone else’s blood. She felt ugly and vulnerable in a way she hadn’t really experienced before, and vain as it was, it made Kara feel utterly defeated in a way. Not knowing how to care for herself now that she felt like this. Not being able to take a shower, wash her face, or pick out new clothes. She was nothing anymore, in that bathtub. She was no one. And Lena could see it now.

“Sweetheart, can I…”

Lena trailed off as if she felt just as uncomfortable as Kara. She squeezed her arms a little tighter around herself. That seemed to give Lena the push she needed. She tucked her dark hair behind her ears and nodded to herself.

“I’m just going to take this,” she held up the washcloth, “and clean your face. Is that alright?”

Kara nodded, just barely.

Lena swallowed a lump in her throat, but didn’t let that stop her. She inched closer to the bath on her knees and slowly, cautiously, brought the cloth to Kara’s face. She started wiping away at the edges of Kara’s hairline, before dipping it in the water, quickly, rinsing it, and repeating the motion. She did that a couple of times, until Kara fluttered her eyes closed, the water warm on her face. She automatically leaned back, so Lena had full access to her face, and Lena expanded her reach. From her hairline to around her eyes, tracing the delicate line of Kara’s chin and cheekbones. Lena cleaned every part thoroughly, gently, as if she was honoring Kara’s face, instead of ridding it of dirt and grime.

“Sweetheart?”

No matter how delicately she’d whispered it, it still broke Kara out of her trance, and she jumped a little, opening her eyes. She looked around, but found Lena’s eyes to be just as steady and kind as she remembered them. She waited.

“There’s… there’s still some left in your hair. Would it be okay if I washed it for you?”

This time, Kara’s nod wasn’t hesitant. Lena smiled a little.

“Okay,” she smiled softly.

Lena put the tap on again, linking it to the detachable showerhead. She grabbed Kara’s shampoo and conditioner, and put them down beside her.

“Lean back,” she ordered gently, and Kara did.

 Her hair dipped into the water, and when she tilted her head, Kara caught a flash of a light-pink stream of water running over her shoulder and arm into the water. She wanted to look more, but Lena tilted her head again, forcing her gently to look into her eyes.

“Close your eyes,” she commanded softly. “It’s okay.”

Kara believed her.

She closed her eyes as Lena put the showerhead with deliciously hot water over Kara’s head, careful to let it all run over her back. Though she couldn’t see it, Kara could almost feel the dirt and blood detaching itself from her head. Clinging on relentlessly, but forced to detach as Lena’s delicate fingers lifted Kara’s locks, and combed through her wet hair.

Kara let out a little sigh, and it only seemed to instigate Lena more. She stroked Kara’s hair long enough for Kara to feel guilty about taking up Lena’s time and energy, just because she’d forgotten how to get out of bed and live a normal life. She was useless, occupying Lena’s time that was so urgently needed elsewhere.

The water was starting to take on a pink shine, and Kara felt bile rise in her throat. She quickly moved her head back up, determined not to look down again. She felt a tear running down her cheek as she cast her eyes upward, watching the light blue ceiling of her bathroom. Her eyes followed a slight hairline crack that had been there since she first moved in seven years ago. She heard Lena wince behind her and felt Lena rub a little harder in her neck. Lena lowered the washcloth to dip it back in the water to clean it. But in moving past Kara, the metallic scent that had haunted her every waking moment became infinitely more real.

Kara drew her shoulders closer together, pulling her head away from the washcloth, scared she might throw up from the mere scent of it. That was a bad call, because the second she did so, she saw the washcloth hitting the water, the grey cloth stained with dark spots that turned dark pink in the water.

“Fuck!”

Kara squeezed her eyes shut as tight as she could, trying to breathe through it.

“Hey, hey,” Lena was on her in a heartbeat, her comforting hands on Kara’s shoulder and the back of her head, caring and helping like it was in her primal nature to do so.

“It’s alright,” Lena whispered, “it’s okay.”

“I don’t feel good.”

Kara’s stomach was turning, and her throat was closing up quickly.

“Breathe, Kara,” Lena said, her hand gliding over Kara’s wet hair. “You’re alright, I’m here.”

Kara pursed her lips together, feeling hot tears running down her cheeks, too embarrassed to say anything.

“You’re okay,” Lena whispered.

But Kara knew she wasn’t.

“Don’t go,” she choked out, too embarrassed to look at Lena, but too afraid of that reality not to say it. “Don’t leave.”

“I won’t,” Lena said softly. “I won’t.”

Kara nodded. The tears were still there, gliding down her hot cheeks down to her neck. She wanted to say more. That she didn’t deserve Lena’s help or compassion right now. That she was taking up space that she shouldn’t. That she was sorry. That she’d missed Lena. All those things that would fall short or seem meaningless now. So Kara said nothing more at all. She had to stay like that for a while. Breathing in and out, Lena’s steady hand on her head and shoulders. Lena’s calming presence beside her.

“You’re alright now,” Lena whispered occasionally. And Kara let her lie, because it felt more comforting to listen to a lie than face her own lonely truth.

After a while though, after more care for her hair, after Lena had added more hot water to the tub, and after she’d straightened out the last of Kara’s tangles, Kara could admit more. Felt easier, safer, muttering the things that burned in the back of her head out loud.

“I… tried,” Kara croaked.

Lena’s head shot up at the sound, and she quickly fixed her attention on Kara, who hugged her knees close to her chest.

"I tried,” she echoed. “I fought for her. I… I fought, and we lost here, but I won anyway. I fixed it, right?”

The words sounded mumbled and disjointed, and Kara didn’t know how to put her feelings and thoughts into words any better.

“It just feels… it just feels like I lost. I lost everything,” Kara whispered, staring ahead. “I tried so hard, and I know we got the best possible outcome we could’ve hoped for but…”

“But you had to lose someone to win,” Lena whispered for her.

Kara swallowed the lump that had been building in her throat. The tears pricked at her eyes again, but she willed them to disappear.

“I just don’t… I don’t know how to go on now. I mean,” she rubbed at her face, angrily wiping away the tears sticking to her cheeks. “I mean I know what to do, normally. I know how to grieve, you know? I’ve done it over and over again. But this… this feeling of knowing she’s out there, that she’s happy…” Kara’s heart broke just as her voice did. “I don’t know how to cope with a world that she’s not in, feeling like she died – and she did.”

“She did,” Lena agreed softly.

“Right,” Kara said, getting more frustrated, “but she’s not! She’s happy! She’s alive and she’s good, but she’s not here. And I don’t know what to do with that. I don’t know how to grieve someone who just doesn’t exist in my world anymore. I just… I feel so fucking empty and sad all the time. And it hurts,” she admitted, flattening a hand against her chest as if to keep her heart from bursting out. “It hurts more than I can take. I feel… horrified, disgusted, to have seen her die – to have let her die like… like…”

She couldn’t finish it.

“But at the same time, she’s alright. She’s fine. Alive. Thriving. I can’t… I can’t understand how to grieve someone who’s still alive, when I can still smell her blood on me, knowing that I let her…”

It was too horrid to say. Like the words, spoken out loud in her bathroom, would make everything infinitely worse. Kara bit her lip to stop her from saying more.

“I understand,” Lena said softly. “I do. But it wasn’t your fault. Just his. Always just his. You did everything you could for her. Everything and more.”

Kara fell quiet.

“I just feel so… empty. And,” she tried to blink her tears back but felt too defeated to do so. “I just miss her so much.”

Then it was Lena’s turn to fall quiet, though Kara could hear her breathing pattern change, could hear her swallowing something she couldn’t say.

“I’m so sorry, Kara,” she finally whispered. “I… if you want me to go?”

Kara’s head jerked up. “I told you,” she said, looking into Lena’s eyes. “I don’t want you to go.”

“I don’t want to make it all worse,” Lena said. “I don’t want – ”

“You’re not making anything worse,” Kara whispered, leaning her head back against Lena’s hand. “I promise.”

“Are you sure?”

Kara closed her eyes and breathed deeply, leaning into Lena’s touch.

“It’s probably the only thing I am sure of right now.”

 

 

Lena helped her out of the bath and wrapped her up in one of her towels. After, she took the time to massage hair oil and treatments into Kara’s hair before carefully taking the time to brush through her tangled hair. She struggled at times, pulling at knots that had been there for over a week. Kara felt embarrassed by just how bad she’d let everything get, but Lena never said a word about it. With every pained sound Kara let out when Lena had to pull at a knot, Lena apologized. As if she was the one who wreaked that havoc on Kara’s hair. As if she was to blame. After a good fifteen minutes of combing through the curls and tangles, Kara’s hair was somewhat decent, better looking than it had in days.

She put on a fresh set of cotton pajamas, and Lena put some of Kara’s moisturizing cream on her skin – as if it would make up for the days of sitting inside with the dirt, blood and grime of explosives still on her face. Still, Kara appreciated the feel of it. Her skin looked dull, the lack of sun, energy, and the pull of sadness taking away the glow she usually carried. She brushed her teeth under Lena’s watch. Lena let her look in the mirror, and Kara found that the person in the mirror, though harrowingly thin and unhealthy, with dark bags under her eyes and a deep expression of unease and loss still oozing from every cell in her body, looked at least more familiar than she felt. Like her old self was still there, lurking under the surface, just waiting for someone to pull her out.

“Right,” Lena said, putting away the last of Kara’s products and drying her hands on a towel, “shall I get us something to eat?”

“No that’s alright,” Kara said.

“A day where Kara Danvers declines an offer to get food,” Lena smiled softly. “I do believe that miracles still exist.”

And it sounded so silly after everything that had happened in the past couple of months that Kara couldn’t help but smile back, even if it felt unnatural to do so.

“Let’s just get you to bed then, darling. We’ll eat tomorrow.”

“Thank you,” Kara whispered, and Lena returned it with a warm smile.

Having Lena be in her room should feel foreign and strange, but somehow, Lena fit perfectly within the soft and warm earthy tones of Kara’s bedroom. She stationed Kara somewhere by the door, and Kara watched demurely as Lena walked over to her bed, and stripped it of the sheets she’d been wallowing in for days. She should feel at least a little self-conscious about the mess Lena was cleaning up, but Kara felt too dazed to really notice. She was more surprised by the efficiency of Lena’s movements. Kara didn’t know why she was surprised that Lena knew how to make beds in the first place. The sheets ended up in a pile by the foot of Kara’s bed, after which Lena made her way to Kara’s linen closet, and took out a fresh set of sheets. Kara wanted to help, but she was only allowed to do so after Lena had already done most of the work, and only to shake the duvet in place.

Kara had to admit, after all of Lena’s work, her room looked a lot more inviting than it had before. Calming. Not the suffocating atmosphere of before, just a quiet, restfulness. She felt herself grow more tired just looking at the bed before her.

“Are you leaving now?” Kara asked, shooting Lena a glance.

“Do you want me to?” Lena asked gently.

Kara shook her head.

“I want you to stay.”

Lena let out a shiver of a sigh, her shoulders lowering just the tiniest bit, as if she’d been afraid to hear any other answer.

“Okay,” Lena whispered. “I’d like that too.”

They shared a tiny smile, before Kara slowly stepped forward, heading to her bed. The sheets were cold, and her skin broke out in goosebumps at the touch. She shivered and pulled her legs up closer to her torso, drawing the sheets up to her chin. She felt watched. Exposed. It felt awkward, like Lena was observing her at a zoo somewhere. Lena seemed to notice that too, because she blushed, and quickly looked down.

“I’ll, eh,” she pointed at the door, “I’ll just be over there and then you can call once you wake up or – ”

“You can join me here too if you want,” Kara whispered. “I don’t mind.”

Lena looked up, the surprise on her features making her look younger than she was.

“Are you sure?”

“You’ve slept over before, right?” Kara shuffled her feet together under her sheets.

“Yeah, but that was…”

She hesitated.

Before.

Before a lot had happened. Before they’d fought. Before they’d ruined the friendship they had, and before Kara had met Other Lena. Before… Before a lot.

“You don’t have to if you don’t want to,” Kara whispered.

“I want to,” Lena whispered back.

Kara smiled then and turned to lie down on her side. She looked at the wall before her and waited. After just a second, she heard Lena breathe out, her nerves permeating the air around her. But Kara didn’t have to wait longer than that. She heard Lena slip off her shoes, and felt her crossing the room. The sheets rustled as she lifted them up, a cold draft forcing Kara’s shoulders to draw closer together.

“Sorry,” Lena mumbled, and quickly got in. The sheets fell over them once more, and Kara almost sighed in relief when the heat radiating off of Lena’s body warmed the space around her.

Lena tugged the blanket up a little, while Kara tried to get comfortable on her pillow. It was too hot, but when she turned, her wet hair got crumpled into her neck and she had to shake it loose. Lena’s leg bumped into hers, and she quickly pulled it back, apologizing as if she’d burned it. The uncomfortableness of being in one bed together, one they’d successfully shared before, seemed to overfall them both, as they each fell quiet and still in their own spots.

Kara swallowed, and tried to quietly stretch her legs, quickly pulling them back up when she felt how cold the rest of the bed was. She felt the magnetic pull of Lena’s body heat, but didn’t dare get closer. She felt perfectly cramped up in her own bed, miles away from the woman whose breaths she could feel on her shoulders.

“I can practically hear you thinking,” Lena murmured, sending a jolt through Kara’s body. “I thought you wanted to sleep.”

“You’re not sleeping,” Kara pointed out quietly.

“I can’t,” Lena said. “Not tired yet. I think I’ll just answer some emails before I fall asleep.”

“Oh.”

“But you can sleep,” Lena quickly insisted. “I don’t mind.”

But though Kara the exhaustion in her very bones, her tired muscles sinking into her mattress like they wanted to drown in it, her mind stubbornly refused to fall silent. Refused not to be aware of the woman beside her.

“Say something,” Kara said hoarsely.

“What?”

“Say something,” Kara whispered. “I can’t fall asleep like this.”

“Oh, and what, what I say puts you to sleep like that?” Lena teased. “Just what a girl likes to hear, thank you.”

Kara smiled into her pillow.

“That’s not what I meant,” she said. “But I’d like to think about something different. If I don’t I… well you know.”

And Lena did know. She became quiet.

“I like listening to you,” Kara whispered. “It… it helps.”

Lena seemed to understand.

“Alright,” she cleared her throat, “let me see.”

She thought for a second. Kara pulled the duvet over her chin, eyes scanning the dark room. It was not late enough for it to be pitch black out, and she could see the last shimmers of the setting sun peeking through the weavings of her curtains. It didn’t bother her, though. Lena’s even breathing helped to make it seem later than it was. Kara felt the comfortable lull of tiredness in their room, the droning of the traffic outside hypnotizingly calm and reassuring – more so than it had bothered Kara in the days and nights before.

“I talked to the DA.”

“Hmm?”

“Lex,” Lena clarified, and Kara’s heart sank. “I talked to the DA about Lex. I thought it might finally be time to… I don’t know. Find someone else to help. And maybe we do, maybe… Maybe we might not get him on murder charges, but the fact that he tried his shit in front of a dozen government workers has to – ”

“Not that,” Kara cut her off hoarsely, her chest a block of ice, like she’d been pulled back to that horrid afternoon in that suffocating hall. “Don’t talk about him, please.”

“I’m sorry,” Lena said quickly. “Sorry.”

“Something else,” Kara whispered. “Please?”

“Right, right, of course,” Lena let out a tired sigh. “I… I don’t have many interesting things to share with you at the moment I’m afraid.”

“Doesn’t matter,” Kara whispered. “I like listening to you talk about anything.”

She blushed a little at that.

“Almost anything.”

“Alright,” Lena said softly. “I ehm… I could talk about…Well. I was thinking I might stop… dyeing my hair?” her voice trailed off into a hesitant question.

Kara’s eyes widened.

“Really?”

“Hmm,” Lena agreed. “I haven’t decided or anything. I mean, it’s going to look like a mess for months, or I’d have to chop it all off, so don’t quote me on this just yet. Even though Andrea would kill to get me on the ‘worst hairstyles of National City’ page of CatCo.”

Kara giggled. She could hear the smile in Lena’s voice, and wanted to lean into the sound, relaxing her shoulders the slightest bit, and closing her eyes with a peaceful sigh.

“I’m sure she’d be absolutely scathing,” Kara murmured. “And have me write it just to spite me too,” she added, and Lena laughed.

“Right? Can’t let her have that, she’ll be way too powerful.”

Kara nodded in agreement.

“How long has it been?”

“What? How long since I had virgin hair?” Lena teased, and Kara was glad the pillow kept Lena from seeing the heat rushing to Kara’s cheeks.

“Hmm,” she agreed. “How long?”

Lena sighed, her elbow brushing against Kara’s shoulders as she brought her hand up to stroke through her hair, as if the feel of it would provide her with the answers.

“I don’t know. I think I started dyeing it when I was twelve, maybe thirteen years old?”

“Wow,” Kara said. “Eliza didn’t even let me think about dyeing mine until I was eighteen.”

Lena gasped. “And did you?” she asked.

“Bright pink ends,” Kara smiled. “They lasted one summer.”

Lena laughed.

“Rebellious,” she teased, and Kara could hear the smirk in her voice.

She shrugged. “You know me.”

Lena’s smile dimmed a little, her fingers touching the wet ends of Kara’s hair. “I sure do,” she murmured.

The quietness crept up on Kara, and she couldn’t take it. She had to fill it, that silence between them. As if she were a shark, and not moving, not going forward with the conversation, would kill her. She cleared her throat.

“Why did you dye it so early on?” she said, looking up through her lashes. “And what’s your natural hair color anyway?”

Lena hummed, mindlessly twisting the fingers of one hand through Kara’s hair, the wet curls wrapping around her finger easily.

“It’s more like my mother’s,” she said after a brief pause. “Darker than hers ever was, of course, but lighter than that of the Luthors.’”

“Warmer,” Kara murmured absentmindedly.

Kara could hear Lena shrug, the sheets rising a little.

“If you say so,” she whispered.

“But why dye it so early?” Kara asked again, turning her head a little to the side as if she was afraid Lena wouldn’t hear her.

“Did she… did she never tell you why she dyed her hair?”

Kara’s heart fell and she felt that overwhelming wave of grief crash over her again. It had never been far away of course – but Rao did it hurt, feeling that storm break her bones and fill her lungs with choking water.

It took everything in her not to break. Instead, she schooled her face, and swallowed the lump in her throat.

 “Something about… feeling powerful,” Kara whispered. “That’s all she ever said about it.”

“Oh.”

Kara couldn’t talk about it anymore. It felt like whatever was left of her heart was shriveling up inside her chest, leaving a cold, gaping hole in her chest.

“Sorry,” Lena whispered, inching closer, like her hand was trying to get to Kara’s body to apologize. “I didn’t – ”

“It’s okay,” Kara whispered back, but her eyes were painfully dry. “Just… continue, please?”

“Okay.”

Lena paused – an awkward pause, one in which she clearly didn’t know what approach to take anymore.

“I’ll tell you how I went about it,” she whispered carefully. “If you still want me to explain?”

“Please.”

“I guess…” Lena hesitated. “I guess I just wanted to look more like them. My family. I never… never felt like a Luthor. I was constantly reminded of that too, of course,” she added, a tone of bitterness in her voice making Kara cast her eyes down. “I didn’t fit in, no matter how much I tried. I remember… sticking out in the family photos. I looked too much like my mum.”

She went quiet. Kara wanted to reach out, but before she could, Lena had shaken off whatever remnant of heartache she still felt and continued.

“I did it on impulse, really. Some girl at boarding school had a bottle with her. I bought it off her, and did it myself, late at night, in the bathroom so no one would see me struggle with it.”

She let out a short self-deprecating laugh.

“I had the hardest time dyeing it. It took me hours, and I had dark spots all over my neck and shoulders from spilling it so much. I came home later that week,” she said. “Lillian took one look at me and told me I looked ridiculous. Still,” Lena brushed a strand of Kara’s hair between two fingers, “she took me to a hairdresser the next day and got it fixed. He dyed it a little darker to make up for the whole mess I made. She didn’t smile or anything,” Lena said after a beat, “but she told me she’d made a new appointment to get the roots done two weeks later. And then she made the next appointment and the next. She liked it,” Lena said simply. “Even if she didn’t say it. And I didn’t look so out of place anymore. So I kept going to the appointments. Kept them up through college and then… well,” she shrugged. “Life. It seemed easier to just stick to what I knew.”

“So why change it now?” Kara asked after a beat. She had to gather her efforts to even get the question out, just because she needed an answer. She wanted to know. She needed Lena to keep talking, every tidbit of information she hadn’t known before a golden opportunity to learn more about Lena. But the exhaustion from before was reignited by the soothing, low tones of Lena’s voice, and Kara had a hard time even keeping her eyes open.

Lena paused. Her fingers stilled in Kara’s hair, but Kara made a soft, complaining sound in the back of her throat which shook Lena out of her quiet reverie and made her chuckle dimly. She inched a little closer, Kara’s mattress squeaking in protest. Her fingers braided themselves into Kara’s hair, and busied themselves trying to find a place for each resistant lock of entangled hair. Kara's eyelids felt heavier than ever.

“It was you actually,” Lena said softly, her fingers darting down to the ends of Kara’s hair, to her lower back.

“Me?” Kara smiled a little, closing her eyes. “How?”

“You told me my natural color suited me,” Lena said simply. “And… and you told me it looked pretty.”

“It did look pretty. You did,” Kara clarified, before being interrupted by a yawn that made her shiver. “Really pretty,” she concluded tiredly.

Lena laughed. “Thank you,” Lena smiled.  “You’re sweet.”

“I mean it,” Kara said. “I mean, not that you don’t look great now! You always do! It’s just – ”

Lena cut her off with a quiet chuckle and a soft hand on her own.

“It’s fine, Kara, thank you. I understand.”

“Good,” her cheeks were burning. 

She was highly aware that Lena hadn’t moved her hand back yet. It was still covering her own, her arm resting on the sheets that covered Kara’s body. Almost an embrace, but not quite.

“If I were you,” Kara said, barely stifling a yawn that made her eyes feel heavier than before, “I wouldn’t even hesitate. You’d look amazing.”

“Well,” Lena said gently, after a beat. “I’ll keep that in mind. Thank you.”

“S’okay,” Kara mumbled, sinking into her pillows, eyes closed. 

“Are you tired yet?” Lena asked softly.

“Mmm,” Kara mumbled, a little frown between her eyebrows. “Not yet. You have to keep talking.”

“Kara, there’s only so much I can say about my hair, okay?”

“Then talk about something else,” Kara whispered. “Please?”

Lena sighed, but Kara could hear the smile in her voice when she continued. Like she was glad to be asked. Glad to be needed.

“Alright,” Lena whispered. “I might have something.”

Kara smiled a little, and snuggled deeper into the covers.

“I might have… an idea,” Lena said slowly. “A concept – not even that, I suppose – but an idea. Something I want to work on. I don’t know if I can and if I could ever pull it off, it sounds so wild, too wild, to be true.”

“What is it?”

“I can’t tell you yet,” Lena said. “I’m afraid I’ll jinx it.”

“Oh.”

“But I can tell you it might take me an eternity to construct it? To figure out whether or not it is even possible to… I don’t know,” she sighed, shaking her head. Her hair brushed against Kara’s body as she did so. “It might just be an impossibly stupid fantasy, and it’s just – ”

“You can do it,” Kara said gently. “You shouldn’t doubt yourself so much. You’re smarter than anyone I’ve ever met. More driven too. If this is a project you really want to take on, then you will. I believe in you.”

Lena got quiet. “You really think so?”

“Absolutely.”

She yawned.

“No doubt about it.”

Lena chuckled softly.

“You’re tired. Go to sleep, Kara,” she whispered.

And though Kara wanted to protest, her body didn’t find the strength within to even try.

She wanted to ask Lena again if she would stay. But in the end, she was too afraid of either of their reactions, and chose not to.

“Good night, Lena.”

“Sleep tight, Kara.”

 

 

Kara woke up that morning in a dull haze, watching through half-lidded eyes as Lena adjusted her black heels, balancing herself on one foot. It was still grey out, though it looked like Lena had been up for some time. Kara watched as she made her way over to a mirror above Kara’s dresser, and pushed an elegant, golden earring through her ear.

“You’re leaving?” Kara’s voice was rough and scratchy, but monotonous. As if she just needed the confirmation.

Lena jumped a little. She turned around to face Kara.

“Sorry,” she whispered, “didn’t mean to wake you up.”

Kara shrugged.

“To answer your question,” Lena walked over to a chair in Kara’s room, the armrest of which she’d covered with her jacket the night before. “I am. I have to get to work, and I need a shower and a dress change before that.”

“Oh.”

“I’ll be back tonight, though.”

That took Kara by surprise. “You will?”

“Yes,” Lena said, turning to Kara with an airy smile. “Of course.”

“Okay,” Kara whispered.

She didn’t know why, but the quiet calm that had preceded her morning seemed to fade away with the pushing aside of the curtain to her room. As if she didn’t quite believe Lena would come back that night, but felt too mellowed out inside to bring herself to protest.

As if Lena could read her mind, she stopped moving, just as impeccably dressed and put-together as she was last night. As if she hadn’t slept over, as if her presence that night had been nothing more than a vivid dream. Lena looked at her, something akin to pity and understanding passing over her face. Kara looked away to avoid that stare.

“I am coming back tonight. I’m making pasta.”

“You are?”

“Hmm. I have just about everything at home, but I’ll have to stop at the shops for some things after work. I’ll be here around eight if that’s okay with you?”

“I… sure?” Kara said hesitantly. 

“Perfect.” Lena stood up.

“Oh,” Kara tried to sit up, suddenly awkwardly aware of the etiquette of having guests over – like Eliza’s voice was right there in her ear, berating her for letting Lena leave without a proper goodbye and an ‘always welcome back, get home safe’ accompaniment out the door.

“Oh no, please,” Lena rushed to say, a hand held up as if she could physically stop Kara from getting up. Maybe she could in this state, Kara mused. It didn’t feel like there was any strength left in her bones. “It’s only 5:30. You should get some more sleep.”

The hour at least explained the pale grey light coming through her curtains.

“Alright,” Kara said.

Though she knew very well she wouldn’t sleep anymore. She already felt the simmering, sinking feeling of nothingness she associated with consciousness creeping back inside. Lena would go. Kara would stay home, watching the hours pass, and ponder on how she’d get through the next couple of hours. Lena seemed to notice that too.

“I ordered you breakfast,” she said. “It should be here in about fifteen minutes. Will you eat it? Please, for me?”

Kara nodded slowly, and Lena shot her a grateful smile, as if Kara was doing her a favor, and not the other way around. It was confusing.

As a matter of fact, the rest of the day went by in a confusing blur. The rest of the week, really.

Kara’s breakfast came. She ate it in slow bites, watching the weather change outside her window, the sun glowing brighter before dimming down again. She watched it in quiet suspicion as if she was waiting for a sign. Waiting on a text message Lena hadn’t sent yet. An “I’m-so-sorry-I-know-I-said-I-would-come-by-but-things-just-got-in-the-way-I’m-so-sorry-I-swear-I’ll-make-it-up-to-you-some-other-time,” kind of text. The inevitable text that would cut Lena out of her life again. In a way, Kara was hoping for it, because it would allow her to return to her life and habits of not doing anything. Of hiding. Of mourning. But another, more curious part of her, longed to have the strangeness that was Lena Luthor back in her life. Needed to know and discover how she fit into the puzzle of Kara’s life now – and what that could mean.

So Kara waited on the couch until the shadows in her apartment became longer, and the light faded away. Until the screen in her living room became painfully bright. That’s when there was a knock on the door.

Lena waited to be let in, though Kara suspected she had a key already. Not that she could’ve used it even if she’d wanted to; Lena was beaming at her from behind two heavy bags of fresh groceries she was carrying – the vegetables on top wobbling precariously as Lena shifted on her feet. Kara was so surprised she came back, she forgot to smile back.

It didn’t seem to bother Lena. She shot Kara a quick ‘hi’ before heading to the kitchen like she’d been cooking there for ages. Like it was her home. Kara could only gape over her shoulder, and close the door with a soft thud.

“Pasta carbonara,” Lena announced as she spread the groceries out over the kitchen island. “Simple, delicious, comfort food. Is that okay for you?”

“Eh, sure,” Kara said hesitantly. She felt a little shell-shocked. Dumbfounded. Like she was an extra in a film that people had forgotten to give her directions for. Taking up space in a foreign, hostile environment.

“Will you help me?” Lena asked gently, draping her coat over one of the chairs.

Kara nodded and made her way over to the kitchen. That whole night, she didn’t think Lena actually needed her help once. The only thing she was tasked to do was break eggs into a bowl, and grate some of the cheese Lena had brought. She did it slowly, mechanically, but Lena never commented on it. She talked her through the whole process while Kara could only look at her, look at the deft way her fingers held on to the guanciale as she cut it, how her sleeves were rolled up carefully so she wouldn’t risk staining her blouse. How effortlessly she seemed to control every aspect of the meal – while Kara could only imagine the chaos she would cause trying to keep one pot from boiling over, and trying not to burn the guanciale in the other pan. Lena whisked the eggs, the cheese, and some pasta water so quickly, it was almost hypnotizing to watch. Something about the muscles in Lena’s upper arm clenching –

“Kara?”

“Hm?” she looked up in a start.

“Dinner’s ready,” Lena smiled.

It seemed Kara had focused too much on Lena’s movements to notice she’d already put the pasta in her egg mixture alongside the now sizzling pieces of bacon. Despite having felt apathy towards the prospect of eating before, Kara’s mouth now started to water at the sight.

Lena took out some cutlery while Kara grabbed two deep plates and placed them before Lena.

“Thanks,” Lena smiled, like she hadn’t done all the work. Kara just nodded.

She watched as Lena elegantly swirled the spaghetti onto the plates, the crispy bites of bacon peeking through the absurdly good-looking golden heap on her plate.

They ate in silence before the TV, and when Lena stood up to clean their now empty plates – Kara had practically licked hers clean – she did too. Once they’d done the dishes, Lena started cleaning the island, so Kara started helping too. Then Lena moved onto the trash, so Kara mindlessly walked around the apartment, collecting empty takeout boxes, and plates with suspicious-smelling remnants of food on them. Little by little, her apartment started looking less like a maniac’s hide out, and more like the place she used to live in. With every task they finished, Lena would move on to something else, never asking for help, but always smiling at Kara as she joined in. By the end of the night, her apartment was cleaner than it had been in days, and Kara actually felt physically tired.

When Lena went to her bedroom, Kara followed slowly, hesitantly, as if she was the one entering someone else’s apartment. By the time Lena had guided Kara to her bed, Kara looked over her shoulder and watched Lena slip off her shoes. She caught her questioning eyes.

“Want me to go?”

Kara didn’t think she’d ever shaken her head faster. Lena crept back into bed with her, maintaining a safe distance, just like the night before.

After a while, Kara asked: “Did you mean to trick me into cleaning my apartment just now?”

Lena let out a husky laugh.

“Not at first,” she admitted. “But when I saw you would just not stop helping me… well.”

“Ingenious,” Kara muttered.

“I try,” Lena said.

Kara felt more tired than the night before.

“Will you come back tomorrow too?”

“If you want me to,” Lena whispered easily.

“Please.”

 

 

The days went by quicker that way. Each day, Kara tried to commit to one task, before sinking back into the couch, waiting for the one highlight of her day. Lena, knocking on her door. Each new day, Kara tried not to open the door too quickly, tried not to appear too desperate and eager to see Lena’s face again. Each day, Lena brought new ingredients, cooking up meals too fancy for Kara’s kitchen that had only ever seen failed baking experiments and microwavable supermarket meals. She made curries, dumplings made from scratch, soups, and lamb chops with gratin dauphinoise in a sauce so delicious, Kara wouldn’t be surprised if she’d have a hard time fitting into any of her pants again after. She didn’t mind so much.

The pills Alex had left were always waiting for her next to the meal. Kara took them without protest.

And every night, Lena would get into bed with her, staying an unspoken few inches away from Kara’s body, though Kara had found that when she woke up in the middle of the night, she could sometimes feel Lena’s hand on her side, her even breaths against her neck. She never said a word to Lena once they both woke up.

Every night, Kara would ask Lena questions, and Lena would talk until Kara felt too tired to think about anything else anymore. Until Other Lena was a little further away than during the day, though she was never too far from Kara’s mind.

One night, after an episode of The White Lotus and eggplant parmesan, Kara couldn’t help but voice the question that had been bugging her for over a week now.

“Why do you keep coming over?”

Lena stilled beside her, and Kara rolled over so she could look at Lena’s face. She hadn’t calibrated the size of her bed well, because she ended up almost nose to nose with Lena’s, whose surprise was written all over her soft features.

“I don’t know,” she answered softly. “I guess it’s because you haven’t asked me not to.”

“Oh.”

Kara blinked, and when she looked back up, she found Lena still looking at her. She was close enough to touch. Close enough so Kara could study each line on her face, the slight almost imperceptible fuzz on Lena’s cheeks, each hue of blue in her otherwise green eyes.

Lena let her, never saying a word. Kara had to close her eyes to focus again.

“Do you think you’ll ever stop coming along?”

Lena sighed. “I assume I will, yes.”

That wasn’t the answer Kara wanted to hear, though deep down she knew it was the right one. It still didn’t make her heart weigh any less in her chest.

“Soon?” Kara asked, her voice barely louder than a whisper.

“I don’t know,” Lena said honestly. “Do you want me to stop coming by?”

“No,” Kara said quickly, eyebrows knitted together in weak desperation. “No.”
