“Then it won’t be soon,” Lena said gently. “I’ll be here for as long as you need me to be,” she paused. “Or as long as you want me to be.”

That at least settled Kara’s worries a little for the time being. She had no trouble falling asleep after but was plagued by nightmares of kryptonite bodies falling apart around her, their powerful skin poisoning her as she screamed for help that never came. She woke up when Lena got ready, more exhausted than before she’d gone to bed.

The nightmare repeated itself a couple of nights in a row, until one night, Kara felt herself being lifted out of a dream by a worried, soft, familiar voice. She woke up in a sweat, Lena’s hands on her face, her eye scanning Kara’s face like she was violently ill and had to be checked for symptoms.

Once Kara had stuttered the nightmare out in bits and pieces, tears that weren’t tears staining her red cheeks, Lena pulled her close, and whispered things that barely filtered through Kara’s brain, but calmed her down just the same. She slept right through the night after, bundled up against Lena’s shoulder. From that night on, Lena didn’t sleep so far away anymore. They went to bed with some distance between them but never said a word if either of them crawled a little closer, or wrapped their arms around the other. It was their silent agreement, their unspoken wish. Though Kara still struggled through the days, the nights weren’t even half as awful as they were before.

 

 

Sometimes Kara wished she was brave enough to ask Lena. To ask whether she could ever foresee a future in which they had settled back into something normal. Something like how they used to be.

She was too afraid of the answer, though, and too realistic to hope for a positive one. So she didn’t ask that. Instead, in the depth of the night, once she’d woken up from a dream again, too restless to fall back asleep, she’d asked something else – something safe in the darkness in which she couldn’t make out Lena’s face.

“Lena?”

“Hmm?”

Kara heard her rustle behind her, adjusting her head on the pillow. Her eyes were probably already closed, though she’d admitted to not being tired just minutes ago. But Kara had noticed a trend in Lena claiming not to be tired, only to be lightly snoring behind her right after.

"What do you want to ask me this time?" Lena asked, a hint of amusement in her voice. “Another burning question about my hair routine again?”

“No,” Kara said, but she heard Lena chuckle anyway.

“I wanted to ask you why you’re here,” she tried softly. “With me?”

“You’ve asked me this before, no?” Lena replied. She didn’t sound worried.

“I know, I know,” Kara asked. “But… but you said that you were here because I wanted you here.”

“Don’t you?”

“Of course I do! But…”

“But what?” Lena smiled confusedly in the dark. “Are you kicking me out?”

“No, of course not. I just… I was thinking about you, and – ”

“And what revelations about my intentions did you come up with?”

She still sounded amused. Kara knew the more she’d push, the quicker that amusement would turn to ash. Sometimes she wondered whether getting thrown into too many walls and houses had impacted her mental decision-making skills, because she still felt that pull, that urge to press on. To know, even if it would make things worse.

“I guess I was just wondering if, for you, it was about settling things.”

“Settling things?”

“Getting even? Like atoning for… whatever.”

“Atoning?”

There was no denying the iciness in that word. Wrong word, Kara had guessed that the second it had come out of her mouth.

“That’s not… I’m saying it wrong.”

“I think you must be.”

“Lena, I’m just worried you’re here because you think you owe me something.”

“And why exactly, would I owe you anything?”

“I don’t know,” Kara said, getting just as agitated by the coldness in Lena’s voice, “for fighting me all these months? For trusting your brother over me? For hating me when I was just trying to keep you safe?”

“Oh, I’m sorry,” Lena said, so coolly Kara’s hair stood up on her arms, “like you’ve had the best track record this year? Or any year, since we’ve met, for that matter?”

“Lena – ”

“You have lied and cheated your way through my life – through our entire friendship, but somehow, when I react adversely to that, I’m the one who’s crazy?”

“That’s not what I was trying to say at all – ”

“Or how about the fact that you chose to get close to the one version of me you couldn’t chase away, huh? How do you think that felt?”

“I wasn’t trying to hurt you, Lena, I just wanted to help!”

“Well how convenient that you never actually mean to, but always end up hurting me in the process.”

Kara dug her fingers deep enough into her pillow to hear the fabric rip.

“You know what? Forget I even asked,” Kara said, pulling the blanket over her shoulders.

“Sure, why bother acting like I get an opinion on anything that concerns me.”

Kara turned around and sat up.

“I’m sorry, the last time I checked, you wanted to avoid talking to me at all costs. Remember that?”

Lena sat up too.

“I believe I had every reason to do that, don’t you think?” She ignored Kara’s flinching. “I think you agreed with that once upon a time.”

“Lena – ”

“You know what bothers me the most?” Lena asked. “It’s that fucking self-righteousness of yours. It’s that fucked up sense of control you need over everyone’s lives – the need to check on them with both personas just to get that full picture of their lives. Not that we get to know either side of you completely – you made sure of that. We are just assumed to put total faith in you, while you treat us like dirt the second we make a decision that doesn’t align with your views.”

“Well if that’s all you think of me, then why are you here, Lena? I can’t do this for you over and over again! I can’t have this fight with you over and over again! If that’s why you’re here – trying to hash this out with me whenever – ”

“I’m not here to fight with you!” Lena said. “I can’t believe you would still think I’m only here either to fight or to beg for your forgiveness. You brought this up! Do you really think that little of me that my motivations can all be reduced to such clinical, moral resolutions?”

“I don’t know, Lena!” Kara said, her voice shrill and tired. “I don’t know! That’s why I asked! I don’t know anything anymore, and it’s breaking my head just thinking and doubting everything. I don’t understand why you’re here when you’ve made it so clear in the past that you didn’t want me anywhere near you, and it feels like I’m just counting down – just waiting for you to…”

The next part hurt too much to say out loud, so Kara let her hand drop and her mouth close. She felt her shoulders drop, and felt lonelier than she had in a while, sharing the same bed with someone else.

“Forget it,” she whispered instead. She could feel Lena’s eyes on her.

“What?” Lena asked, softly this time. “What are you waiting for?”

“I don’t know.”

“For me to hurt you?”

“Of course not, Lena.”

They were both quiet after that.

“Do you think they fought?” Kara asked after a while. “We never actually got to see it.”

“About the secrets, you mean?”

Kara nodded. Lena sighed.

“I think so, yes. Just because we didn’t see it doesn’t mean it wasn’t there.”

“Mxy always tends to show just what he wants to see,” Kara murmured.

Lena turned her head to look at her. She contemplated her question for a brief few seconds.

“Did he really try to marry you?”

Kara failed to stifle a smile. “Oh yes. Dress, proposal, and everything. Right in front of Mon-El too. He wasn’t very happy.”

“No, I can’t imagine he would be.”

Kara thought she could hear a smudge of satisfaction in her words, but she wasn’t quite so sure, so she didn’t comment on it.

She giggled a little at the randomness of it all, and heard Lena join in as well. She felt really young, all of a sudden. Like a girl at a sleepover, telling secrets about boys, while they giggled at the absurdity of marriage. It felt familiar, though Kara had never really had any real sleepovers with friends when she was young. She took a deep breath, and felt her arm brush up against Lena’s. They were both sitting against the headboard of Kara’s bed now, bare arms in tanktops touching, their hands clasped in their laps.

Lena turned her head towards Kara in the dark, and the light coming through Kara’s flimsy curtains illuminated only a sliver of her face. Enough to showcase a worried eyebrow, the soft look in her eye, and hesitant lips.

“Do you really believe it is so crazy to think that I am here because I care for you?” Lena asked softly. “Is it so preposterous to think that I love you? That I want to be here for you? That seeing you in pain is the last thing I’d ever want?” Her voice lowered, a husky whisper in the dark. “Is it really so crazy to think that I care about you?”

“I don’t know,” Kara whispered. “You seemed pretty clear about how you felt that day in the fortress. Is that not just honoring your wishes? Respecting that you wanted me to stay away from you?”

“You didn’t respect her wishes,” Lena said. “She wanted to kill you, and you still didn’t leave her alone. So what’s the difference, Kara? Why her, and not me? Why was she worth helping and I… wasn’t?”

“It wasn’t about that,” Kara shook her head and looked at Lena. “I just… I couldn’t bear knowing I screwed up everything. I couldn’t cope thinking I’d… ruined both of you. I had to believe that there was still a chance. I needed you, Lena,” Kara whispered. “And I just… I needed to fix this one thing, and I thought – ” She had a hard time swallowing the lump painfully lodged in her throat. “I thought I could still fix things. I’m not so sure of that anymore.”

“I’m here,” Lena whispered hoarsely. “That’s got to count for something, right?”

“What do you mean?”

Their eyes met, and Kara felt a dizzying spark she couldn’t quite define run down her spine at the sight of Lena’s eyes burning so intensely in her own.

“If you only continued screwing up – if you had actually succeeded in ruining us… well, then I wouldn’t be here. Then I wouldn’t even be here to make up for my own mistakes. Yours would weigh that much more in the balance of life, you know?”

Kara’s cast her eyes down.

“I mean that in the best way, Kara,” Lena whispered, her fingers brushing over Kara’s hand to get her to look back up. “I’m here because you’ve made it impossible not to care. You’ve tried. Twice. Twice, you’ve tried to help me. You cared enough to try. And despite our differences and our fights, I still have all this love for you and I can’t bear to know you’re falling apart somewhere. God, Kara – ”

She shook her head and Kara felt her breath shutter in her throat.

“If you really wanted to know why I was here… there you go. I still care. A lot. I guess that’s why it upsets me when you try and twist it into something it’s not. I’m still here,” Lena said, eyebrows knitting together in frustration. “I’m not planning on going anytime soon, Kara. But you can’t just stop trying to fix it now. And you can’t expect me to forgive and forget. You just might have to accept that this… whatever we have now, will, for the time being, be this… mixed bag. Good and bad. But the good part is that we’re both still here.”

“We’re both still here,” Kara echoed quietly.

“Exactly,” Lena said, looking softer than she had all night. She squeezed Kara’s hand. “I’m staying. Because I want to.”  

“Because you care,” Kara whispered.

“Because I love you,” Lena said easily – almost like she was giving in to the room around her. “Leaving would do neither of us any good.”

Kara shook her head.

“Thank you,” she whispered. “For sticking with me.”

Lena shot her a ghost of a smile.

“In every universe, right?” she asked with a wry smile.

Kara closed her eyes and smiled, before nodding.

“It seems like it.”

“Guess it’s fate then.”

“No use in fighting it,” Kara whispered.

“Foolish to do so,” Lena agreed. “So we might as well stay here.”

“In bed?”

“God yes. And sleep. Please.”

Kara giggled and nodded.

“Alright,” she whispered. “I can take a hint.”

“Good,” Lena said, lowering herself down on her pillow and closing her eyes. “Because you missed the first ten signs, but I’m glad you got the insinuation.”

Kara smiled as she looked down on Lena’s smiling face, eyes closed, her hair a jet-black ink stain on Kara’s light pillows. She felt the tension from before seeping away with Lena’s even breaths, and actually grinned when Lena frowned and held the blanket up for Kara to hide under.

“Some of us still have work in the morning, Kara, so I suggest you crawl under these sheets now.”

“Got it, boss,” Kara whispered, and giggled as Lena swatted her hands in Kara’s direction.

She slipped under the covers and relished in the feeling of Lena curling closer to her, throwing her arm loosely over Kara’s waist.

“Sleep,” Lena whispered in her ear, and Kara did.

 

 

Alex came by more often in the following weeks, mainly to relieve Lena of her “Kara duties” when she had to go to work. Kara figured they’d agreed on some sort of schedule, but she didn’t care enough to comment on it. She actually appreciated Alex coming by, because while Lena’s presence was a godsend, her insistence on healthy cooking dramatically interfered with Kara’s frequent fast food cravings. And Lena could try and persuade her all she wanted with “lemon prawn pasta” and “grilled parmesan eggplant,” it was Alex coming by with pizza boxes that really made her stomach growl.

They were sitting on Kara’s couch one night, eating a dubious amount of greasy food that Lena would most definitely disapprove of, when Kara felt like Alex was itching to ask her something. She didn’t feel nosy enough to find our herself, though, and instead kept her eyes glued to the TV while Alex sporadically picked at her food. She felt Alex’s eyes flipping between her plate and Kara’s face, casting intermittent looks around the apartment, as if she were looking for anything that could start the conversation. Kara just wouldn’t do it for her.

Finally, Alex cleared her throat, and Kara almost had to repress a smile at how transparent Alex and her intentions had become in all the years Kara had known her. Every minor expression, every sound she made, all signs of bigger things that Kara could so easily see.

“So,” she said, awkwardly shifting on the couch, as if having this conversation was making her physically uncomfortable. “Lena’s been staying over, she said.”

“Yeah,” Kara said, eyes still on the TV. “She comes by after work and cooks and stuff. Tells me to clean up and do laundry.”

Alex frowned.

“She gives you jobs to do around the apartment? Why?”

Kara shrugged. “Because I think she believes that if she doesn’t, I won’t.”

“Is that true?”

Kara frowned a little. “It’s not that I don’t want to. It’s just that I… forget. Sometimes.”

Alex took a while to respond. Finally she nodded, and whispered: “I see.”

Kara snuggled deeper into the couch cushions.

On the TV, Kara watched as reruns of Modern Family depicted a Thanksgiving crisis. Though she’d seen the episode before, she couldn’t say any of the plot was sticking with her. She just watched as happy, stressed people ran in and out of houses, and wondered what Lena was doing in that moment.

“That’s not exactly what I meant, though,” Alex said carefully.

“What do you mean then?” Kara asked.

“I mean… she’s been… staying over quite a lot lately, hasn’t she?”

“I don’t know. What’s a lot?”

“Jesus, Kara.” Alex ran a hand through her hair. “I’m just trying to ask you a question.”

“Then ask it,” Kara said irritably, “I don’t know what you’re trying to get at.”

“I’m just saying!” Alex said. “She’s been over here a lot, no? Like… all day? She’s been sleeping over?”

“Yes, and?”

“Nothing! That’s great,” Alex said, her voice getting considerably higher in pitch. “It’s good, it’s great.”

“Great.”

“Fantastic!”

They were quiet for a while, an argument between a father and his daughter breaking out on screen. After a while Alex started fidgeting and threw Kara a look.

“She stays the night?” she asked conspiratorially.

“Jesus, Alex!”

“I’m sorry! Why are you being so weird about it, I’m not judging?”

“Judging what exactly?”

“Whatever,” Alex started waving her hands between Kara and the space before her, “is going on between you and Lena!”

“There’s nothing going on between me and Lena.”

“Oh please.”

“I’m serious, Alex,” Kara pulled herself further to the edge of the couch. “Lena and I are just friends.”

“Kara,” Alex seemed to force her voice down. “You can’t really believe that, can you?”

“There’s nothing to believe, I’m well aware of where Lena and I are standing.”

“Oh Kara.” Alex’s voice got considerably softer. The pity from before was gone, but Kara didn’t feel any better. The look in Alex’s eyes made her feel more vulnerable than she had all evening. She felt watched and analyzed like her thoughts had all of a sudden appeared on her face, legible for anyone who saw her.

“I don’t think you’ve ever known.”

 

 

“Do you ever think about what we saw?”

Kara’s voice interrupted the quiet but comforting lull she’d found herself in for the last hour and a half. Neither she nor Lena had had much to say since dinner. Lena was exhausted from work – the regular kind, and the personal project she wouldn’t talk much about anyway. Kara could tell the late nights were getting to Lena, but she always showed up with a pure – if not tired – smile at Kara’s door.

Today, Lena had grilled vegetables and made the nicest fish Kara had ever tasted before. She had said so, and Lena had smiled at her before thanking her. That was the last thing they’d both felt necessary to say. After eating, Kara had cleared the table and washed the dishes, while Lena tidied up the couch. They’d fallen into that comfortable rhythm, neither of them having to communicate, yet falling into step so easily, so quietly – neither of them had even noticed or cared to comment on it.

Lying on the couch in Lena’s arms, both of them enjoying the warm evening breeze coming through the open window, Kara felt comfortable enough to ask.

Behind her, Lena kept stroking Kara’s hair, tilting her head slightly. Kara felt she wanted to catch her gaze, but she diverted her own.

“In what way?” she asked gently. Her fingers trailed down Kara’s long hair, and brushed her lower back.

“The way – you know.” Kara blushed. “How we saw them…”

Lena waited.

“How we saw them… together together.”

“Oh.” Lena’s hand paused for just a second, before continuing her absentminded caresses, as if her sole purpose on that earth was personally warm up Kara’s soul. “I suppose I do, sometimes.”

“Oh,” Kara’s heart started beating faster, and she could feel the heat creeping from her cheeks to her neck. She wasn’t sure Lena had noticed. Was she disgusted? Grossed out? Intrigued? “So, ehm, what… have you given it some thought?”

“I have,” Lena said, almost amused at Kara’s obvious discomfort around the whole situation.

Her fingers threaded through one of Kara’s half-braids – the ones she absentmindedly twirled in her hair whenever something was bothering her or stressing her out. Lena undid all of them with slim, precise fingers, and it would almost feel relaxing enough to drift off to, if not for Kara’s anxious desire to know.

Kara cleared her throat. It didn’t prevent the croaky hoarseness of her next question.

“What did you think?” she asked.

Lena hummed, continuing her task of detangling Kara’s hair like she didn’t have another worry in the world. Kara factually knew that to not be true, but she allowed herself to recline in Lena’s capable hands, selfishly claiming all of Lena’s time for her own comfort.

“I suppose… well. I think she got what she wanted, in the end,” Lena mused. “My… Other Half.”

It still sounded bitter, but there was a mixture of… regret in those words. Like it pained Lena to speak of her, but she longed to talk and hear more about her against her own will.

“For better or for worse. I believe…” she sighed. “I believe, or I want to believe… that if… if she was allowed – if she was worth the love of her Kara… I don’t know,” Lena lowered her head, shook it, fingers slowing in Kara’s hair. “I believe it means something,” she muttered. “Something important.”

Kara turned in Lena’s arms, searching those soft, blue-green eyes. They looked more vulnerable, and yet so mature.

“Deserving?”

Lena sighed, her fingers slipping from Kara’s hair, their task forgotten.

“She tried, I think,” Lena muttered slowly, “to work on herself. She did it here, even if she didn’t believe that was what she was doing. She was improving. She cared for more than her own selfish goals – her own ambitions. She was starting to learn. You gave her that chance of starting over, and instead of wasting it… she fought to keep herself in the light. She didn’t allow her own frustrations and emotions to get the best of her. I of all people should know how difficult that must’ve been. Especially after carrying the burden of knowledge of her past life.”

Kara cast her eyes down to Lena’s dark blue pants. Such a soft fabric between her fingers. So steady against her own trembling fingers.

“She fought to work on herself. And she succeeded. Or,” Lena corrected herself, “she at least proved herself worthy enough in her Kara’s eyes. Proved that she was capable of doing good. Of being loved. Of loving, herself. If she earned that in her Kara’s eyes then… then I think that’s more than I ever could’ve hoped for.”

“You weren’t sure she was deserving of her Kara’s love?”

“Darling,” Lena smiled a sad smile. “I don’t think any of the Lenas in any of the infinite universes are.”

Kara paused for a second, studying the lines in Lena’s beautiful, self-deprecating face.

“That’s stupid,” she whispered. “I believe every Lena in every universe is deserving of love – especially mine. I’ve got…”

She stopped herself, but when she looked into Lena’s vulnerable eyes, she couldn’t remember why.

“I’ve got so much of it anyways,” Kara whispered. “Especially for you.”

Lena held her gaze, and Kara could almost hear her brain stop. She looked so quietly confused that in that one moment, Alex’s words from days before came back and hit Kara like a truck. She had so many feelings for Lena – so many soft, incomprehensible, abundant feelings that Kara had no idea what to do with. And when Lena looked at her like that, Kara almost knew. Her mouth fell open just the slightest bit, her eyes softening and falling down Lena’s face –

Then Lena diverted her gaze, and the spell was broken.

Kara looked back down.

 

 

Later that week, in bed, Kara asked again.

“Do you think about it?”

Lena put down her book.

“I assume this is about what I think it is,” she paused. “About our previously interrupted conversation.”

Kara nodded and Lena sighed.

“Sure,” she said after a beat. “Sometimes.”

“Sometimes?”

“Sometimes,” Lena whispered hoarsely.

“Then what do you think about?” Kara asked.

Lena put down her reading glasses – the most wonderful of discoveries Kara had made since Lena had started sleeping over. Tiny, black-rimmed reading glasses in a thin leather case, now a standard item on Kara’s nightstand.

“You really want to hear my theory on it?”

“You have a theory on it?”

Lena threw her a look. Kara sat up straighter in her bed. “I’m kidding, sorry, I do. I do want to know.”

Lena sighed again, and Kara failed to stifle a smile, which Lena begrudgingly returned.

“Please? What do you think about?”

“I think we are all just… possibilities, you know? You and I? We are… outcomes of choices and circumstances. So, in that world, she was never as hurt by your secret as I was, because she was always tied to down by her own secret. In the end, we might be the same people, but we have not lived the same experiences. Thus, every eventuality and probability amounted to a different situation.”

“One in which they loved each other?”

Lena smiled at her, combed a hand through her hair.

“I think that is just about inevitable in any universe, darling. But if you mean romantically? Then… yes. I suppose it’s one possible ending for them.”

And for us? Kara wanted to ask. But Lena looked caught up in her own thoughts, taken over by realities thousands of lightyears away from theirs. And Kara felt like maybe she didn’t want a definitive answer just yet. Maybe she didn't need one just yet. Maybe this, this quiet, solemn space they shared was enough for now.

Maybe she just didn’t want the assuredness of a no.

 

 

“You’re kidding,” Kara’s grin was infectious. “You’re kidding?”

Lena groaned.

“Just… keep it quiet, will you? I don’t need Alex or anyone else to find out about this.”

“Oh you just know what she would say.”

“How I’m the stereotype of an annoying rich kid?” Lena said, unamused. “Yes, I’ve got quite the idea.”

Kara laughed, her fingers failed to hide her grin.

“Oh my God,” she whispered.

Lena sighed. “Come on, it’s not a big deal. I’m not even that good.”

Kara shook her head.

“I don’t believe that, you excel at everything you do.”

“Well, that just might be the exemption to that rule.”

“So how long?”

Lena threw her a look.

“How long did you take classical dancing lessons?”

“For God’s sake, Kara!” Lena threw her head back against the couch. “It’s been years. I trusted you with my secret, and you use it against me.”

“Not in a bad way,” Kara clambered to her knees to face her. Lena threw her an unimpressed look. “I just want to know! Please?”

She tilted her head sideways in a way that she knew Lena couldn’t refuse. And just like she thought, Lena groaned and closed her eyes, bringing her half-empty glass of whiskey up to her forehead to lean against it.

“Eight years,” Lena muttered. “I took classical dancing classes from the age of ten to fifteen. When I was sixteen I quit under the guise of having to take on too many classes at once. It wasn’t completely untrue, of course, but it was very much a stretch as to my motivation to quit.”

“Why did you hate it so much?” Kara asked.

“Well, one, because my mother made me do it even though I sucked at it – at least in comparison to the wannabe ballerinas in my class,” she corrected herself after seeing Kara’s protesting frown. “And then…” she sighed, “well mostly because I never got to do what I wanted. It was always so strict, so… constrained.” She shook her head and shot Kara a dim smile. “I didn’t like feeling like a puppet.”

It went quiet for a while. Then –

“Do you still remember some of it?”

Lena’s eyes immediately narrowed in suspicion.

“Bits and pieces,” she said slowly. “Why?”

Kara grinned wider than she had in weeks, and Lena groaned.

“Kara, come on. No. No, I’m saying no.”

“You have to!” Kara exclaimed. “I won’t film, I won’t say anything to anyone, but I have to see it, please?”

Lena sighed and Kara’s head perked up with a victorious little bop.

“Fine,” she groaned as she pulled herself up from the couch, but once standing, extended her hand to a confused Kara.

“What? You thought I’d be the only one making a fool of myself tonight?”

“But I don’t know how to dance,” Kara said. “I never took those classes.”

“Don’t worry,” Lena tilted her head with a smile that made Kara’s heart flutter just the slightest bit. “I was always good at leading a dance.”

Kara was taken aback, but took Lena’s hand anyway – she thought to herself that even if Lena hadn’t reassured her, she would have taken that hand. In any situation, at any time. Lena’s hand was warm, smooth, steady, and fit perfectly in her own. The metal band of Lena’s ring didn’t dig into her skin, but rather seemed to fit in the grooves of her fingers, her bracelet completing Kara’s own wrist just by lying against it.

She allowed Lena to pull her to her feet, and felt her heartbeat quicken when she realized just how close they were standing to one another. She was even more surprised when she realized just how little she minded that closeness.

They were standing close enough for Lena’s breath to hit Kara’s warm cheeks. Her breath smelled like the whiskey she had earlier, smokey and sweet, somehow. Kara felt captivated by Lena’s hooded eyes. She felt Lena guide her hand up to Lena’s shoulder, and felt nervous about how clammy it started to feel, and how Lena would definitely feel it through the sheer fabric of her blouse.

As if she could tell, Lena shot her a reassuring smile, but Kara didn’t think the expression she pulled on her own face even slightly resembled anything like a smile back.

Then Lena’s hand dropped to her waist, and Kara felt a bolt of electricity shooting down her spine.

“Rao!” she almost stumbled over her own feet.

“Are you okay?” Lena quickly glanced down to check if they were still okay, before laughing, and looking back up. “Jesus, Kara, we haven’t even started yet.”

“I know,” Kara mumbled.

“I mean, this was your idea!”

“I know, I know,” Kara said, shaking her head. “Like I said, I don’t dance.”

Lena stifled a comment and smiled instead.

“Let me make this easier.”

She slipped her phone from the back pocket of her dress pants and connected it to Kara’s speaker. She scrolled down a list with a thoughtful look, before her face lit up.

The soft tones of Say My Name by Destiny’s Child started filling the space around them, and Kara laughed in disbelief.

“This can’t be the music you danced to in those classes.”

“No, but it’s the music I wanted to dance to.”

Kara laughed, and the tension dissipated when Lena joined in. That soft, low tinkling of laughter that felt so intimately familiar at this point.

“It’s fine. Just follow my lead.”

“But I – ”

“I’ve got you.”

Kara’s breath hitched in her throat, her eyes caught in Lena’s. The look on Lena’s face softened. In a soft, off-key, awkward mumbling, she started singing along to the song.

“Say my name, say my name,” she sang, pulling Kara along with her body.

Kara laughed and allowed herself to be pulled in the direction of Lena’s body. Lena looked so awkward, so pained singing along to a decade-old song just for Kara’s sake.

“If no one is around you, say baby I love you. If you ain’t running game, say my name, say my name.”

By the time Lena’s voice had quieted down, and the music had taken over – Kelly, Beyoncé and Michelle’s warm voices filling the apartment, Kara realized that without knowing it, Lena had pulled her into her dance. She was dancing. One careful step at a time, she was being led around the room, never bumping against anything – because Lena kept her from it. Lena protected her from it.

Kara’s hand crossed behind Lena’s head, and Lena pulled her a little closer, swirling her expertly around the kitchen island, each step meticulously planned, and yet smooth enough for Kara to feel like she was almost flying. Lena pushed and pulled, her strong hand guiding Kara as they danced to the rhythm of the song. Kara didn't know how Lena kept looking in her eyes as they moved about the space - almost as if Lena had Kara's entire apartment mapped out in her head. Either way, Kara felt safe - she even felt pretty, and elegant in Lena's arms. The song played on and Kara couldn't help but enjoy every second of it.

She chuckled to herself and looked down.

“What?” Lena asked with a smile. “I told you it was silly – what?”

“Nothing!” Kara said, “It’s just… I’m happy.”

Lena’s hand that had been holding Kara’s tightened a little.

“You are?” she asked softly.

They came to a stop right when the next song started playing.

“Yeah,” Kara said, a little self-conscious under Lena’s intense gaze. “You make me happy.”

Lena seemed to shrink at those words, her eyes widening as her shoulders dropped. Kara took a small step back.

“That surprise you so much?”

It took Lena a second too long to break out of her stupor and shake her head.

“No,” she whispered. Then again, stronger. “No. It’s just… I used to believe that. I just hadn’t… been too sure of it these last couple of months.”

“Oh.”

“Which isn’t your fault,” Lena rushed to say. “You just… you surprised me.”

“You’re surprised I like you?” Kara laughed self-depreciatingly. “I can’t be much of a best friend if I make you feel that underappreciated.”

“Kara – ”

“Lena, if it weren’t for you, I never even would have taken those solar pills. I’d still be in a pile of misery on my couch, waiting until the world caved in on me.”

“I’m sorry – ”

“But it’s more than that,” Kara insisted.

Lena looked taken aback.

“There is?”

“Yes. You mean more to me than just… patching me up when I’m all messed up,” Kara whispered, shaking her head. “I mean, you do, and I love you and can never thank you enough for that.”

She ignored the jolt that accompanied the fuzzy feeling she got in her stomach whenever she uttered the word “love” aloud in Lena’s company.

“But you’re more than that. You… you make me smile,” and Kara couldn’t help but smile while saying it. “You make everything… mean so much more. You make me laugh. You’re kind. You’re sweet. You make me happy in such an effortless way, I just… I love you for it. I’m so happy you’re here – that you choose to be here with me. That you chose to stick with me.”

She blushed, looking down. She’d said too much. She’d been too awkward. Kara wanted to shake her head, take it all back, apologize –

But Lena drew her closer. She wrapped her arms around Kara’s neck, and this time Kara was forced to hold on to Lena’s waist in utter surprise.

“Thank you,” Lena whispered. “That means a lot.”

“Lena.”

Kara felt herself being pulled closer, Lena’s arms so tight around her shoulders and neck, like she never wanted to let go again. Kara could feel her tremble against her, and she fell quiet. She let her hands glide up over Lena’s blouse and pulled her closer too.

Kara felt hyper aware of their proximity, their skin and bodies feeling closer than they had before, though she knew that couldn’t be true. They’d hugged before, they’d slept in the same bed before. But in that moment, Lena felt like an extension of Kara’s own body as if she was meant to stay in that hold for forever, intertwining with Lena to make a new, better person of herself. Lena’s heart beat fast against Kara’s own skin, until she wasn’t sure whose heartbeat it actually was. The tips of her fingers were digging into Kara’s shoulder through her hair. Her lips were hovering close to Kara’s ear, but she didn’t say anything. Kara didn’t think she needed her too.

For the first time, she thought she might finally alright.

 

 

They walked into Lena’s lab together, on a Friday afternoon.

Kara had written her second article since The Big Thing happened, and Andrea, either overjoyed by Kara’s resurgence at the office, or out of fear for Lena (Kara suspected the latter) hadn’t left a single note on it. She’d sent it down to the editors, and told Kara to keep up the good work. To celebrate her achievement, though Kara felt a little ashamed to have to call it an achievement, Lena had taken her out for coffee.

She’d felt stronger. Though she wasn’t using her powers yet, she could feel their presence. The last of the Kryptonite had left her body without a warning or a goodbye note. And though Kara didn’t try to take it too hard, the absence of pain was a stinging reminder that the last piece of Other Lena had left her now too. It had taken a week of crying to deal with that, but Lena had been there with her throughout it all. Had never called her stupid or ridiculous for feeling such a deep sadness over it. She’d just held her close while Kara broke down.

But things were slightly better now. Kara was out in the world again. Only a couple of times a week, and a few hours at most, but she was out there. That seemed to be the most important part. And Lena, sweet, steady, loving Lena, was right there with her. It felt stupid to celebrate with a coffee, when Lena was at her apartment each morning pouring her one, but it was nice to be out in the world again. At least with Lena there by her side. 

She had been quieter than usual that day. Nervous. She’d played with her flat white with a spoon until the foam had dissipated, and her coffee did not look like it was worth the price they’d paid before. Kara didn’t pry, but didn’t have to either. She kept it to small talk. Told Lena about ideas for the next article – on the Writer’s Guild of America’s strike which Lena asked pointed questions about. Still, Kara could see her heart wasn’t in it.

She was in the middle of explaining how she was planning on interviewing one of the Succession writers, when Lena interrupted her.

“Kara?” she asked.

Kara looked up.

“You know I want to make you happy, right?” She sounded so nervous, it broke Kara’s heart a little bit. “Like… happy happy? You know I would do anything I could to… You know?”

Kara almost had to smile at Lena’s nervousness. It was usually her who messed up sentences by running over them in a hurry to get her words out. But Lena was wringing her pale hands tightly together, and there were worrying circles under her eyes, so Kara didn’t laugh. Instead, she shot Lena a small smile, and nodded.

“Of course I do, Lena.”

Lena nodded, but she didn’t look too convinced by Kara’s answer.

“I need to… I need to show you something. Something I made for you.”

“Alright, show me,” Kara smiled.

“I don’t have it,” Lena wasn’t smiling anymore. “It’s in my lab. It’s, ehm, that project I told you about?”

“Your passion project?” Kara asked, tilting her head. “Lena? It’s done?” Lena nodded. “Lena! You didn’t tell me! Congratulations, you’ve been working on it for months!”

Lena shot her a smile that wobbled so much, Kara’s smile faded.

“It’s for me?”

Lena nodded.

“Can I show you?” she asked hoarsely.

Kara swallowed the nerves creeping up her throat, and nodded.

 

They walked through Lena’s lab, a place under LuthorCorp that Kara had only been in a handful of times. Still, she could tell it was so characteristically Lena from the small touches in the room. Lena’s sweater, loosely folded over a chair in the corner. A second pair of reading glasses perched on top of a large pile of handwritten notes and data. A photo of her and Jack in hazmat suits on her desk, next to a small succulent that Kara had bought her ages ago. Her leather bag with deodorant, more notebooks, and a computer was thrown over a desk, next to a pair of dangly earrings that Kara figured Lena had to have taken out in frustration while she was working – the earrings bothering her too much to focus.

“It’s over here.”

Kara was pulled out of her exploration by Lena’s voice coming from around the corner. Kara dutifully followed the sound of her voice until she arrived at what looked like a big, metal door.

She furrowed her brow in confusion. It didn’t look as sleek and shiny as Lena’s usual designs, and Lena looked more nervous than she ever had presenting her new technology. She was usually so proud, and had always worked such long hours to achieve anything that she would almost burst with excitement when she finally showed off her work. But now… she looked two feet smaller than she was, shoulders tense and uncomfortable, her wide eyes staring at Kara with an innate sadness that Kara herself couldn’t place.

“What am I looking at?” Kara asked carefully. “Don’t get me wrong, it looks super impressive, but just for those of us who haven’t spent the last ten years engineering – ”

“It’s a portal.”

It came out so hoarse, Kara almost wasn’t sure she’d heard it right.

“A portal to…where?”

Before she finished the sentence, the realization had sunken in. She could see it in Lena’s eyes. Her heart made a move so unfamiliar, somewhere between a somersault and an emergency break out of her chest.

Though they both knew it was superfluous, Lena said it anyway.

“It’s a fifth-dimensional portal. That’s what I’ve been working on these last few months.”

Kara opened her mouth but nothing came out.

“It started as our project to get her home, but then… then everything went down. I was ready to take it apart for scraps, but then… Then I saw how sad you were. How much you missed her. I just,” Lena shook her head, her hand covering her mouth once as if it took too much of her to go on. “I didn’t think it was fair, how she was taken from you. I thought that after everything you did, how hard you worked… you deserved to at least say goodbye.”

“You made this,” was everything Kara could muster.

“I did,” she sounded a little desperate now. “I know it doesn’t look like much, but that’s just because I didn’t want you to wait any longer! I promise it works, I ran the tests a hundred times. It works. I promise, it’s just – ”

Kara turned to face her.

“You made this for me?” she asked.

Lena stopped. She swallowed a lump in her throat, a slight haze pulling over her eyes.

“I did,” she croaked. “I wanted you to have a chance to say goodbye.”

Kara nodded. She felt so dizzy she thought she might faint, her blood rushing so loud through her head, it drowned out everything else around her.

A chance to see Other Lena again. One last time.

“What… what do I do?”

“Ehm,” Lena nervously tucked her hair behind her ear, shaking her head slightly to steady herself. “It’s... it’s not hard, it couldn’t be more simple, really,” she said, walking over to a console beside the metal door. “I’ve already programmed everything, it will get you to precisely where you need to go. You can take as long as you want theoretically, but just for safety’s sake, I would prefer you come back in the next twenty-four hours or so.” She glanced up at Kara. “Unless… unless you want to stay longer, then… then I won’t stop you, but, I just, you know, would be less sure – ”

“No,” Kara shook her head, and Lena looked up at her. “No, what do I do?” She sounded so small, so… confused. “Like… what do I say? What if… what if she doesn’t want to see me? What do I do?”

Lena’s face softened.

“Oh Kara,” she whispered, a shine of the woman Kara knew breaking through her nervousness. She looked older understanding. “You probably know her better than any of us, including me. I think the only person who’d know what to say is you.”

Kara’s lips trembled. She nodded, balling her fists by her side.

“Okay,” she whispered.

Lena smiled sadly at her.

“You’ll be okay, Kara,” she whispered. “Whatever happens is up to you. I just wanted to give you this chance to – ”

“Thank you,” Kara cut her off. “Thank you, Lena – I… I don’t know what to say.”

Lena’s smile wobbled.

“That’s okay. I… I just want to make you happy.”

“You make me happy, Lena. Every day.”

“But you need this,” Lena cut her off. She shot Kara a knowing, sad smile when Kara could only look back at her. “It’s okay. I want you to have this. I want you to get your chance to say goodbye.”

Kara looked at the door before her. So cold and intimidating – looming over her like it was warning her not to go down that path. What if there was only more sadness waiting for her? What if Other Lena didn’t want her there? What if the place was worse than what Mxy had shown her – not wanting to hurt her feelings?

What if she didn’t know what to say to her?

Kara looked at Lena, nervous tears in her eyes.

“I’m scared,” Kara admitted. “I… I don’t want it to hurt more.”

“I know,” Lena said softly. “But you deserve a chance to find out. You deserve a chance to at least speak to her and tell her… tell her whatever you want to tell her.”

Kara looked at the door again, and back at Lena.

“You’ll be here when I come back?”

“I won’t leave for a second,” she promised.

Kara took her hand in hers and Lena squeezed it.

“You’ll stay? Tonight too?”

The fear was close to overwhelming her, her body trembling with fear and bubbling tears.

Lena smiled, and Kara saw that her eyes were glossy with tears now too.

“I’ll even cook you dinner if you want.”

Kara laughed, wiping under her eyes with the back of her hand.

"Promise?"

"Nothing would make me happier."

“Okay,” Kara whispered. “Okay, then... then I’m ready.”

Butterflies were racing around in her stomach, her heart going faster than it probably should. Like the few seconds on the highest top of a rollercoaster, waiting for the world to drop out from underneath her. Kara let out a shaky sigh.

She was ready. 

She stepped back, spreading out her tense fingers by her sides. She took a deep breath, and Lena started the machine.

Hi!!

I hope you all enjoyed this latest installment of Evil! Sorry this chapter (again) took a while longer to write. And then also the usual work-life shit got in the way, because of course it did.
The final chapter is partially written now, so it (hopefully) won’t be long before it’s out! (Who even believes me at this point lol.) I’m just a little scared the same emotions might come back writing that too, so we’ll have to see.

It’s really scary and kind of emotional to know that this story is almost at its end! I’ve loved writing it so much. I’ve met some wonderful people because of this story, and your feedback and love has made me a better writer (I hope) and a truly happy human being.

Chapter 15

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Kara found herself where she had been so many times.

Bathed in sunlight, having to hold her hand up to the sun, which filtered in peach-colored light through her fingers. Her hair felt hot in her neck, the sun heating up every hungry cell of her body – and yet Kara felt cold sweats in her palms, cold sparks of electricity running down her spine. Because when she lowered her hand, slowly, trembling as if she could somehow prolong the moment before she actually had to live it, she found herself standing on Lena’s familiar L-Corp balcony.

No. Not her Lena’s balcony. That balcony was about a universe away.

Kara was standing on another L-Corp balcony, bathed in sunlight, the wind whistling in her ears, and just a few feet away, talking animatedly into the phone while working away on her laptop, was Other Lena.

Kara lowered her hand shakily, her whole body trembling.

Her heart was racing faster than she ever thought possible, her stomach fluttering around like it wanted to burst. She felt faint, overexcited, overwhelmed, and utterly terrified all at the same time. It was too much. She felt like turning around and running away, like calling Lena in a blur of tears to get her out, to get her back, to run, to hide, because it was just too much.

But catching just that glimpse of Other Lena – just that miracle of seeing Other Lena at her desk, her frown etched on her forehead as she rolled her eyes to whatever the man on the other end of the line was saying… it was enough to keep her glued to the ground.

She was right there.

Other Lena didn’t notice her. She was swaying in her seat, holding the phone to her ear as she toyed with a pen in her hand, twirling it across the page of a black notebook without actually writing anything down. It was clear she wasn’t listening to whoever was on the other end of the line. Her eyes were unfocused, her attention clearly elsewhere. She wasn’t saying much, just allowed the man on the other end to drone on, nothing but a flash of occasional annoyance in her ears to indicate she was still listening.

Kara’s breath hitched in her throat as Other Lena’s fingers dropped the pen, and started playing with a lock of hair in the back of her neck that had fought its way out of her neat bun. She was so inhumanly beautiful and elegant, and Rao, Kara had missed her. Tears already jumped in her eyes at the sight of her, and she wiped them away quickly with the back of her hand.

Lena.

As if the video Mxy had shown her was just a farce, a show to keep her from asking too many questions. Like they had all collectively decided that she wouldn’t have been able to cope with Other Lena’s death, and they had to keep up an illusion to keep Kara’s mind from imploding. Maybe Kara hadn’t actually dared to believe that it was real – too afraid it wasn’t. Forever locked in an ironic play of a Schrodinger experiment she had never wanted to take part in.

But seeing her like that… Just a few steps away, behind the glass window, the view of Other Lena was so close, so real…It was just enough to break and mend Kara’s heart all over again. Like she couldn’t believe the woman she’d felt wasting away in her arms was actually here. Alive. More than that; radiating energy and a liveliness that Kara herself hadn’t experienced since the day she lost her.

A lump lodged itself firmly in her throat at the sight of her. Kara felt her breathing get shallower, bringing her fist to stifle the sounds coming from somewhere deep inside, the surprise and pain melting together to ruin her all over again.

Rao, she was really there. Right there. Just as beautiful and wonderful as the day she left her. Other Lena.

The haze in Kara’s head finally got to her, and she almost lost her balance trying to take a step – forward or backward - she didn’t know yet. Kara thought she could see herself as if she was just a plaything in a movie, ready to be whisked away by the director who could deem all of this too much. The fear of losing Other Lena again strong enough to keep Kara from even wanting to blink. But how could she keep her here, in this one moment? In this one rupture in time and space where Kara got to see her?

Reality finally set in when Kara realized she had no plan.

She blinked against her surroundings and felt a sense of bewilderment set over her, unsure of what the next step was. What could she do? What was she supposed to do? What if she changed something again? What if she ruined everything again? What if Other Lena faded away again? What if she just disappeared before Kara could even… could even what?She had no idea what to do. She had jumped at the slightest opportunity to see Other Lena again, to hear her again, to listen to the sound of her laugh, to watch that twinkle of daring excitement in her eyes, to watch that mouth pull up in a perfect smirk… But she hadn’t thought of a single thing to say.

What would she say? What was there to say? Would Other Lena even want her to be here? She already got the life she wanted, what else was Kara but a rude reminder of all the pain she had suffered before? A reminder of the clutches of her past, made real?

Kara suddenly felt paralyzed with indecision, her heart pounding ruthlessly in her chest.

What would she say? What should she do?

What if Other Lena didn’t want her there?

Before panic could overtake her completely, Other Lena turned in her chair, eyes roaming the ceiling as she innocently, almost childishly, spun from left to right in her seat, talking over the other man with casual ease, borne out of hours of relentless meetings with men just like him. Her ankles were crossed, tapping against the heel of the chair every once in a while, to change the direction she spun in, but always remaining within the same 90° angle of the window.

She took Kara’s breath away.

She looked so beautiful. So mesmerizingly, otherworldly beautiful. Even with the obvious annoyance on her face, rolling her eyes absentmindedly from time to time… she was gorgeous. It struck Kara, that even through all the years, through the same experiences as her own Lena, Other Lena still looked… different. Her eyes, warm as they were, were a little steelier like they had seen more than her fair share of misery over the years. She looked sharper, more on edge, even if that edge had softened considerably compared to the last time Kara had seen her.

Other Lena was right there, everything Kara had begged and prayed for for months… and seeing her felt like she’d been knocked to the ground.

She’d never felt such a deep urge to do two such antithetical things at once. Mxy’s name was hovering over her lips – just tingling to be spoken into existence, to whisk her away, back to the safety of a reality in which she was far, far away from Other Lena.

The other part of her was screaming at Kara to move her legs – to run to Other Lena, break the glass to her office if she needed to. To stage a scene, to have music playing, a dramatic re-entry into her life, to do something so big and extravagant that it would wipe away all the pain that had been letting Kara’s body decay and rot for these last, unbearable months.

Anything to be near her again. Anything.

In the end, it didn’t really matter what Kara wanted. Her body betrayed her. Her knees trembled so much, they almost buckled. She took a stumbling step backward to steady herself, the wind whistling in her ears from up where she was standing. It wasn’t a huge step, but it was movement. Movement outside of Other Lena’s window.

And Other Lena was nothing if not vigilantly perceptive. Years of attacks on her life would do that to a person.

Other Lena looked up sharply, and Kara felt her insides freeze up.

She was looking directly at her.

Other Lena was looking at her.

Her green eyes were as sharp as they were the day they’d last seen each other. Dark, guarded, apprehensive, and so combative. Dangerous. And then all at once, the surprise set in. A gleam of recognition, a sparkle of something not even Kara could define.

Kara couldn’t breathe.

As if even the mere sound of an exhale would kill the moment and take Other Lena away from her. It felt like sound had left the world around her. It pulsed around her, just as breathless. Just as anxious. The world had been reduced to nothing but the steady beat of Kara’s own heart, the feeling of being pulled underwater. And Other Lena’s green eyes.

Other Lena stared – she stared for what felt like ages. Then it happened.

Her mouth fell open slightly, an expression of complete and utter disbelief etched onto her perfect features. Her heartbeat picked up so fast that Kara almost worried about her. Her breathing picked up, and her shoulders dropped. She stood up so fast her chair spun in its place, the phone still clenched in her hand, her fingers stark white against the black material of the receiver. Her other hand came up to her mouth, covering her dark red lips with trembling fingers balled into a brittle fist.

She looked at Kara like she was a ghost, a grim reaper, one she hadn’t expected so soon.

In that moment Kara almost hated that she’d come in the first place. That she’d caused that shock, that disbelief, that disheartening frozen expression of horror in Other Lena’s eyes. She wanted to shout, wanted to apologize, wanted to escape. Most of all, she wished she could change the expression in Other Lena’s eyes – change the way she was perceived by the woman she’d longed so long to see again.

Kara didn’t know if she could ever talk again, staring at Other Lena with so much shock, fear, and such pain, that she didn’t know how to make any of it better. She wished she could say something, anything to take away the shock on Other Lena’s face, but she couldn’t. Her mouth stayed open in an apologetic, tiny, wishful, oh.

Kara could hear the man prattling on on the other end of the phone, trying to break the spell she and Lena were both under, but Other Lena didn’t seem to care. Neither she nor Kara were even listening anymore. It didn’t fit into their tiny pocket of space and time. That was reserved just for the both of them.

“I have to go,” Other Lena interrupted the man in the middle of his sentence. “I’ll call you back.”

“But Miss Luthor,” the man spluttered, “you can’t just – ”

Other Lena ended the call before he ever got to say what she couldn’t do. The phone clattered from Other Lena’s hand to the white desk, the sound reverberating through her office.

Kara still couldn’t move. Only her trembling fingers twitched by her side, the rest of her body frozen in fear, stuck in a fight-or-flight instinct that just refused to kick in.

It didn’t matter.

Because Other Lena stepped forward blindly, eyes locked on Kara. She staggered towards the door, her eyes refusing to break away from Kara’s face. She almost fell against the glass door of her office, pushing forward, her one hand placed squarely on the glass, leaving an imprint of her elegant palm and fingers behind when she finally did manage to find the handle, pushing the door open with all her strength.

Kara’s breath hitched in her throat at the sight of Other Lena clawing her way forward, as if the simple ten steps towards her proved to be an impossible obstacle course. As if the road to Kara was endless.

After what felt like years, Other Lena was finally on her balcony. Kara was on the other end of it, just steps away from her. The railing felt cold against her back, digging into her flesh like it was trying to force her to lean forward. She couldn’t.

Kara’s feet were icicles frozen onto the stone tiles of Lena’s balcony.

But it seemed like Other Lena had lost her momentum too. She’d come to a halt outside of her open door. She was panting, her eyes so sharp, Kara could almost feel hunted, captured. Other Lena’s hand didn’t leave the door like she had to be ready to run back inside if the situation became hostile. If she had to flee.

Her bottom lip trembled.

Something Kara could only describe as fear or disbelief flashed in Other Lena’s eyes. As if all the years she’d waited still weren’t enough to prepare her for the sight of Kara. Like Kara was a vision from a nightmare she hadn’t ever been able to forget. Heartbreak and pain personified. Right there on her very own balcony, where she thought herself to be so safe.

Kara wanted to open her mouth, to say something, anything to explain herself. But of course, there was nothing. There was just Other Lena. And all Kara could get past her lips was her name. Soundless, her vocal cords blocked, Lena’s name just an exhale formed by her lips.

Other Lena stood up a little straighter, her bottom lip trembled a little as she pursed her lips into a straight line, trying not to betray her feelings. Trying not to give away anything Kara didn’t have a right to.

Perhaps she was angry.

It occurred to Kara. Maybe Other Lena hated her. Maybe the pain she’d caused her in other lifetimes surpassed the joy of her new life. Maybe Other Lena couldn’t stand the reminder that Kara personified, a reminder of pain, misfortune, and torture. Of imprisonment. Of death. Who could really blame her?

Who could tell her that Kara hadn’t done the very worst she could; hadn’t bestowed such debilitating pain onto someone?

Tears formed in her eyes as the thought crossed her head. What if she hated her? What if she hated her? What if she hated her?

Kara’s heart beat so fast. The fear wrapping around her heart was so sharp, it stung. A mixture of hopelessness and regret choked back the few words she could possibly offer.

Kara felt a chill run down her spine as Other Lena’s eyes betrayed nothing, holding Kara prisoner in her green-blue swirls of unfathomable emotions.

What if Other Lena didn’t want her here?

She had to apologize. Apologize for everything – for the D.E.O., for Lex, for her own shortcomings, for her reckless, fucked-up wishes, for her inability to save her twice. Kara had so much to apologize for, and yet now was the time her entire being protested. Her throat was bone-dry, her voice non-existent, the words in her head useless and lacking in depth – lacking in everything. There were so many things to say, and yet everything Kara thought of felt useless, meaningless, and trite in the grand scheme of things.

But she had to say something. She had to at least try. She had to…

“Lena.”

It was barely anything. A scratchy sound above the city, light enough to be whisked away by the wind around them. And yet for Other Lena, it seemed to be so deafeningly loud. Kara thought she could see her flinch. Thought she could hear the word reach her. Her own name, uttered by a voice she hadn’t heard in years. One she might’ve forgotten since they’d last seen each other. Other Lena’s throat bobbed, and tears shot in her eyes.

“Oh God,” Other Lena whispered – and then it all changed quicker than Kara could process it.

The steps that had seemed endlessly long before were crossed in a fraction of a second. In a whirl of dark hair, teary eyes, and a haze of perfume, Other Lena had crossed her spacious balcony, the clicks of her heels still echoing around them by the time she’d hit Kara, and wrapped her arms around her. Kara barely had time to steady herself before she caught the familiar warm, soft form of Lena Luthor in her arms.

Though Kara knew her powers had come back a while ago, she’d never felt weaker in her life. She was completely and utterly powerless against Lena Luthor. In this and every other universe. So completely overwhelmed by the scent, the feel, and the vision of Other Lena, Kara allowed herself to be weak. She allowed herself to be pushed against the railing by Other Lena’s body, her arms steadying Kara in her embrace. She wrapped Kara up so tight, it felt like her entire being had been engulfed by her. Muscles clenched around her, a warm breath in her neck, a trembling body under her own hands.

Lena.

“Supergirl,” Other Lena whispered, her breath hitting Kara’s neck, hot tears rolling down Kara’s collarbones. “Supergirl.”

Kara squeezed her eyes shut, a dry sob escaping her lips without her permission. Other Lena’s arms wrapped around her shoulders, while Kara could only force her trembling hands to move up. They finally found a hold of Other Lena’s waist, the warm fabric of her black skirt so soft, Kara didn’t dare to touch it. Her fingers fluttered around Other Lena’s waist like she was afraid Other Lena could go up in smoke if she held on too tight. Like she’d be cheated out of her presence forever if she only dared to hold on so tightly. Kara suddenly felt like she’d waited lifetimes to feel this – to feel her – so impossibly close to her, to be so lovingly wrapped up in Other Lena’s arms. And yet she felt so scared, she wanted to cry.

The scent of Other Lena’s perfume – different from her Lena, Kara stupidly realized – combined with the scent of just Other Lena, finally pushed Kara over the edge. Her fingers clutched the fabric of her shirt, Other Lena’s beating heart reverberating in her ears. Her strong, steady heart. Untouched, unbroken, and so alive. So alive. Tears welled up in her eyes as she buried her face in Other Lena’s shoulder.

“Lena,” Kara whispered, tears clinging to her words as they came out. “Lena.”

Other Lena’s hand traveled up between Kara’s shoulder blades, holding their shaking bodies as if her life depended on it. Her fingers dug into Kara’s skin when she called her name. For once, Kara wished she was powerless so she’d at least have the marks of Other Lena’s fingernails to remind her that she was real, that Kara was here with her.

“Supergirl,” Other Lena whispered, her voice husky, yet so unbelievably warm and so, utterly Other Lena. The surprise and joy just tangible in her words. “You found me.”

Kara had found her.

Kara got Other Lena back.

She got her back. She was right there.

It was only then that the wave of apologies came back to Kara, the words that had once seemed meaningless rushing from her mouth all at once. Muddled and spilling over one another like she was afraid she’d run out of time. The “sorry's” ran over the “if I could have's…” while her heart hammered against her chest as if it wanted to catch up with her words.

“Supergirl, Kara,” Other Lena whispered into her hair. “Please. Stop apologizing.”

“I can’t!” Kara wanted to say, “I have to. It’s all I have left.”

But instead, all she could utter was another: “Sorry.”

Kara sniffled and hid her face as Other Lena allowed one last apology to slip through the cracks. Kara wished she could get closer, wished she could bury herself in Other Lena and never, ever let go again. She already dreaded the moment they would have to let go, her heart already clenching, anticipating their breaking apart.

“I can’t believe you’re really here,” Other Lena confessed, her hand traveling up to hold the back of Kara’s head close as if she could keep Kara from escaping. As if Kara could ever stand to let go again. “I’ve waited so long.”

Kara was embarrassed she could think of nothing to say. All those nights she’d spent dreaming of what she would say to Other Lena – what kinds of fights, shouting matches, or discussions they would have once they met again, all the scenarios she’d run through in her head, over and over again – they all fell silent. There was nothing in her head. Just the recurring echo of Other Lena’s name as she allowed herself to be completely overtaken by her.

“Supergirl,” Other Lena hummed again and just hearing her say it made Kara feel so, so weak.

Why bother thinking about the eventuality that Other Lena still wanted revenge? That she still hated her? What did it matter, when there was no way in this universe or the next one that in that moment, she could do anything to stop an attack if it were coming? She was so weak that it wouldn’t take much to overpower her. If Other Lena turned around now, a wicked smile on her face, Kryptonian dagger ready to be dug into Kara’s chest, Kara didn’t think she could even stop her.  She wouldn’t see it happen, and frankly, didn’t really care to. Being there – just there – in Other Lena’s embrace was enough. She would happily allow any attack to rain down on her, would welcome whatever force wanted to strike her down, and would probably not even remember what to do if it were to happen. She was fine where she was, and she wouldn’t move for anything or anybody.

She wouldn’t look up, just trembled in Other Lena’s arms, soaking in her scent, her being, her everything.

“Don’t let go,” Kara whispered, and she hated how strangled it came out – how vulnerable she sounded. “Please,” tears pricked in her ears. “Don’t let go.”

She felt Other Lena pause, tilting her head away from Kara as if to study her. Then she pulled her closer again, her hand soft and steady around Kara’s neck.

“Never,” she promised. “We can stay like this however long you want. God,” her hand pulled Kara impossibly closer. “I can’t believe you’re really here.”

The lump in Kara’s throat turned to stone and soon kept her from breathing calmly altogether. She felt the dizziness get to her, her legs for once so unreliable and unsteady.

“Supergirl, are you alright?”

Other Lena shot her a worried look, but Kara had only just accepted that Other Lena was really there; and to see worry and concern mirrored in those eyes she’d mourned for months was just… too much.

“I'm sorry,” Kara faltered, “I'm sorry I... I don't know.”

“It's alright,” Other Lena said as if she had been preparing for this to happen for ages. “I understand. Come on, sit down with me.”

Kara allowed Other Lena's soft yet commanding words to guide her, and she slid down the railing of Other Lena's balcony until she sat down on the ground. Other Lena crouched down with her, concern etched into her features.

“There you go,” Other Lena whispered. “Are you okay?”

Kara blinked against the sunlight.

Other Lena's face stuck out against it like a beacon of rest and tranquility. Her eyes sharp, all-knowing, and deeply reassuring. The sunlight lightened up the shade of her eyes until it was much lighter, a glassy sort of green. How could Kara tell her how weak she felt, how vulnerable when Other Lena looked at her like that? The laugh wrinkles around her eyes and mouth, the few grey hairs, glittering in the sunlight amidst her dark tresses. Her red ‘work’ lipstick, two shades darker than the one her Lena always wore.

“It's really you,” Kara whispered. She couldn’t quite hide the tremor in her voice. The almost childlike urge to cry for no good reason.

Other Lena's face broke out into a smile. Warm, unwaveringly bright.

“And it’s really you,” she answered softly. “You found me.”

“I’m sorry,” Kara whispered, her head so cloudy she could almost pass out. That would be just like her; to get this chance and then pass out to miss most of it. “I’m sorry I just… I’m, I’m so dizzy.”

“It’s alright,” Other Lena whispered. “Take as long as you need.”

“I’m sorry,” Kara echoed. “I thought… I didn’t think I’d get here. And now…”

“I understand,” Other Lena said, and when Kara looked back up at her, heart racing, Other Lena was smiling.

She was smiling.

“I’ve waited so long for this,” Kara whispered, a hushed confession on the church of Other Lena’s balcony. “And now I’m messing it all up.”

A soft chuckle left Other Lena’s lips.

“You’re not messing up anything,” Other Lena promised.

Her hand moved up Kara’s arm, soothing and soft in a way Kara knew she didn’t deserve.

“Kara?”

Kara tried to wipe her tears away with her sleeve, looking up at Other Lena like she was expecting her to send her away any second now.

Other Lena tilted her head and shot Kara that familiar, teasing look, one that had promised nothing good before, but at that moment meant the world to Kara. It was only slightly softened by the pearly, happy tears in her eyes. She looked so different, crying like this than the last time Kara had seen her cry. So much older, so much happier.

“Took you long enough. You do know I hate to be kept waiting, Supergirl.”

Kara let out a disbelieving laugh, surprising herself. It made Other Lena chuckle too.

Kara shook her head.

“How did you know?” she asked hoarsely. “I mean, how could you tell?” she asked. “How can you tell? That it’s me and not... not you know?”

Other Lena laughed.

“Oh darling, I think I could pick you out of a room full of Kara’s. It’s that look you have,” she added, more gently, her eyes softening just the slightest bit. “It’s the way you look at me. It gives you away every time.”

Other Lena reached out, like she wanted to pull Kara closer, but then thought against it. As if the first time she'd pulled Kara into a hug, she'd had no control over it, no power to stop herself. But now, crouched on the floor next to her, it seemed a step too far. She hesitated.

Kara wished she wouldn’t.

“It only occurs to me now,” Other Lena murmured. “Silly perhaps, after all these years, but it only occurs to me now that that was the first time I held you like that. I'm sorry, I should have asked.”

Kara swallowed, shaking her head slightly.

“You're forgetting the time I caught you,” she whispered hoarsely. “Back in L-Corp. Don't you remember? I held you then. My sister was yelling at me… Lena was there… I think you were trying to kill me?”

Other Lena let out a surprised chuckle. The sound was enough to make Kara want to cry all over again.

“You're right,” she said, a hint of amusement in her voice. “That was so long ago. How could I forget? Your ingenious way of trapping supervillains.”

Kara smiled, shaking her head.

“You were never really a supervillain, Lena.”

Other Lena looked at her with a daring glint in her eyes, falling back into her own teasing pattern like it was as natural as breathing. Like no time had passed at all.

“Don't patronize me, Supergirl. I know my strengths. At least give me some credit.”

Kara laughed, casting her eyes down.

“Fine. Our first consensual hug,” Other Lena acquiesced. “And even then I didn't ask whether it was okay for me to – ”

“It was more than okay,” Kara cut her off. “It was...”

The painful lump in her throat prevented her from saying more, but Other Lena seemed to understand. This time when she reached out, she didn't stop. Her hand found Kara's cheek, her thumb tracing her cheekbone, wiping away a smudge of wetness from a tear Kara hadn't felt escape. She gently tilted Kara's chin up so she could look at her.

“Supergirl,” she whispered, amazement clouding her voice. “It's been so long,” Other Lena whispered. “Why did you only come now?”

Other Lena’s touch felt as foreign as it felt familiar. Kara leaned into it like it was the breath of oxygen that would save her, after having been pulled underwater for so long. Other Lena understood then, and pulled Kara closer, leaving no space between them to pull away. Kara leaned her head against Other Lena’s shoulder and allowed her entire body to sag against her. Other Lena wrapped one arm around Kara’s shoulders, a touch so warm and so loving, that Kara’s eyes almost fluttered shut in complete and utter acquiescence to Other Lena’s warmth.

“I’ve missed you,” Other Lena sighed.

Kara closed her eyes and allowed those words to fill her soul.

It was everything she’d ever longed to hear and more. Everything she’d wished for but hadn’t dared to hope for. A warm blanket of more than forgiveness.

“Lena,” Kara finally whispered. “Lena helped make a machine. A portal. I mean, she made it. Finalized it. The portal.”

She realized how clumsy her words were coming out as if just seeing Other Lena was enough to render her completely uncomprehensive. “She... she brought me here.”

Other Lena's gaze turned indecipherable for a moment.

“Really?” she asked. She nodded to herself. “So she found a way,” she said softly. “I thought... I thought you might've used a wish for it."

Kara shook her head. “I used my final wish for you.”

Other Lena seemed to break out of her brief spell.

“You did,” she whispered. “You did. Of course. I... I always suspected you might have.” She swallowed too, her jaw clenching slightly. Remembering. “I always guessed but… it’s nice to have that confirmed. That’s…”

Her eyes were unfocused, staring at something Kara couldn’t see. They seemed to traverse a thousand years, hundreds of miles in a blink of a moment, so far away from Kara. An array of emotions flashed over her face, hardening her features, and instilling a guardedness that hadn’t been there before.

Kara hesitantly squeezed Other Lena’s hand, the one that rested on her face. As if by magic, Other Lena snapped out of her reverie, her eyes finding Kara’s. The steely look in her eyes melted away after just a beat, recognizing the woman before her. Her features softened before Kara.

“That was so long ago,” Other Lena finally said. “Your wish.”

“Yes,” Kara whispered.

Other Lena nodded. She looked at Kara then, really looked at her.

“I don't think I could ever thank you enough for that,” she said. “Not in a million universes. I wish I could – ”

“Please don’t,” Kara shook her head. “Don't.”

“But – ”

“I barely remember wishing it,” Kara whispered, pleading. “I just remember... I remember the panic. You know?”

Kara closed her eyes, trying so hard to find the right words. Trying so hard not to think of what she had relived every night and day since Other Lena had died, and yet find a way to talk about it like she could.

“I thought I'd already lived the worst day of my life, you know?” Kara tried to smile but had to look away when Other Lena’s eyes filled with pity. She didn’t need it, didn’t deserve it after everything she’d done to her.

“I just… I really thought nothing could ever come close to losing my home. My family. Nothing. How could I even imagine that something could ever hurt me that much again?”

She faltered. Her voice broke.

“And then there you were. On the floor. You – ” Kara took a faltering breath. “And I could do nothing. And it happened all over again.”

“Supergirl – ”

“You don't have to thank me for that wish,” Kara whispered, staring into Other Lena's conflicted green eyes. “It was my wish. It was the only way I could take the pain away. I did it for you just as much as I did it for me.”

Other Lena nodded slowly.

“Alright,” she said softly. “I understand.”

Then:

“Then just... thank your Lena for me. For doing what I couldn't. For letting me see you again, even if it's just this once.”

Her hand didn't leave Kara's face, and Kara didn't let it either. Her hand reached up to cover Other Lena's as she leaned into the touch. How she could go from shying away from Other Lena’s touch through the hatchet in a cell to leaning in so desperately to feel her so close in the span of mere months was almost ironic, but Kara didn’t allow herself to question it. She was too happy to relish in the touch, however briefly she could.

“You tried?”

Other Lena threw her a sad smile.

“Of course I did,” she whispered. “I would've given anything just to talk to you again. To ask you why, to ask you,” she shook her head, “a million different things. I wanted to ask you how your day went. What music you were listening to. How you’d slept that night.”

Her voice grew hoarse, and Other Lena shook her head as if it could somehow fix it.

“I wanted to yell at you, to cry with you… I wanted to beg you to come with me because I was afraid I couldn't do this alone.”

“Of course you could,” Kara interrupted her. “Look at you! Lena!”

Other Lena let out a sad, little laugh.

“Lena, just look at the life you've built for yourself! You did that! You made all of this happen. I'm...” she faltered. “I am so proud of you,” she finally whispered, hoping her honesty shone through in her words enough to convince Other Lena. “I'm so sorry I missed it.”

“I couldn't have done it without you,” Other Lena said gently, a glimmer of regret in her eyes. “That's what I wanted to tell you. That's why I tried.”

She shook her head.

“I tried so often. But I had nothing to go on. No sign of you, no trace of your universe. It was all gone. It was useless. I want you to know that I tried, Kara. I just... I never really got the chance. And after a while, thinking about it just drove me crazy. So I stopped trying.”

“I didn't even know there was a way to see you again,” Kara said hoarsely. “Lena caught me off guard. She never stopped trying. For me, I think.”

Something unreadable passed over Other Lena's face but changed into a small smile before Kara could take note of it.

“Of course she didn't,” she said softly. “It must've killed her to see you so unhappy.”

Kara had to look away at that. The thought of Lena waiting for her back in the lab caused a rush of guilt to flood through her. Other Lena must have sensed it. She quietly tried to catch Kara’s eyes again.

“Either way,” Other Lena just smiled at Kara, in a way she had never quite done before. With such warmth and love, so reminiscent of her own Lena. “I'm just so happy you're here now.”

Kara closed her eyes, just for a second, to thank the universe, to thank Lena, for giving her this chance. If this was a dream, she never wanted to wake up again.

“Me too,” she whispered. “Me too.”

Other Lena's hand slipped down from Kara's cheek, and Kara instantly missed the feeling. Other Lena raised her hand to shield her eyes from the sun, eyes blinking to get a better look at Kara.

“There's so much I want to ask you, Kara.”

“There's so much I want to ask you,” Kara said.

“Perfect,” Other Lena grinned. “Then we have all the time in the world.”

Kara let out a disbelieving laugh.

“Don't you have like... the busiest job in the world? I came by unannounced; I couldn't impose...”

“Please,” Other Lena waved her worries away with a roll of her eyes – a hint of arrogance and glee in its movement, confirming so accurately that this was the Lena Kara had met before. So different from her Lena, and yet just as enticing to be around. “I'll have Jess clear my schedule. Nothing could be this important.”

Her eyes softened again. “I mean it. Nothing.”

Kara shot her a small smile, and Other Lena took her hand in hers.

“Let's go inside. I want to sit down someplace nice, somewhere private. Like we didn't get the chance to before. I want us to talk comfortably.”

Like equals. Like friends.

Something they hadn’t been before. The inequality and distance between them always underlined by the physical boundaries of Other Lena’s cell.

Kara's heart ached at the memories, but she forced herself to keep her tears at bay.

“That would be nice.”

Other Lena smiled back.

“Come on.”

She extended her hand, and Kara took it. 

 

 

“Water?”

Kara wasn’t actually thirsty, but she was growing weary waiting on Other Lena’s couch, her hands playing with the hem of her skirt so often, that she was afraid she’d rip it.
