“Please,” she answered, watching Other Lena pour a second glass.

“I texted Jess, she’ll send everyone on their way,” she said, coming over and handing Kara her glass. “Gave her the rest of the day off too, to compensate for all the no doubt heated phone calls that took.”

Kara smiled.

“I also…” she hesitated, and Kara watched as she seemed to grow self-conscious before her. Kara shot her a patient look.

“I’ve asked Kara – my Kara,” she clarified, even though there was no need to, “I’ve asked her to leave us be for the moment. I, ehm… I texted her to say you were here.”

“She knows I’m here?” Kara asked.

She instinctively looked over her shoulder to shoot a weary look outside, but there was no one in the sky.

“She does,” Other Lena agreed softly. “We’ve, erm… we’ve actually discussed this happening before. This scenario.”

Kara looked at her in surprise.

“You’re kidding. You knew this would happen?”

Other Lena shrugged, sitting down next to Kara.

“Not exactly,” she said. “I guessed that perhaps in the near or distant future, you would want to know what happened to me. You’re a true hero,” she said, tilting her head with a sad smile aimed Kara’s way. “I doubted you could stay away, not knowing. I thought… I thought you might have gotten yourself mixed up with some fifth-dimensional creature to find your way to me. I guess I just have my own twin to thank instead,” she said softly.

Kara nodded. A beat passed between them.

“Well,” Lena said, shaking off the tenseness between them. “I’m just happy it’s sooner rather than later. I’d hate for you to see me old, grey, and saggy,” she teased, bumping Kara’s shoulder with her own.

Kara blushed and looked down.

“You would still be beautiful then,” she said softly. “I’m sure of it.”

Other Lena wanted to smirk, but it softened into a small smile instead.

“Charmer,” she whispered, and Kara laughed.

After a beat, Kara tucked her hair behind her ear and shot Lena a look.

“So… she knows I’m here?”

“She does.”

“And she doesn’t mind?”

Other Lena’s smile softened as she shook her head.

“No, she doesn’t mind. She understands that I have a lot to thank you for. A past that she can’t access. She understands very well how much I’ve missed you over these last few years and understands we have things to catch up on.”

“Oh.”

“That surprises you?” Other Lena asked.

“No,” Kara said hastily. “I just… haven’t had the best experiences with doppelgängers. It feels weird to know that I can be in the same universe with my Other Self and not have to anticipate an attack, you know?”

Other Lena laughed.

“Yes, I imagine that’s quite the shock,” she teased.

Kara could barely smile back. Other Lena looked up at her, a sad frown drawing over her features as she tilted her head to look at Kara.

“You look pale, Supergirl. Have you been sleeping alright?”

Kara could only nod, still entranced by Other Lena sitting so close to her. She’d never been so close to her for so long. There was always something separating them. The cell, the D.E.O., Alex… and yet there they were, sharing a couch like they had never known any different.

The fluttering between pain and relief reminded Kara that they had.

“I can’t believe you’re really here,” she whispered.

“I should tell you the same,” Other Lena said, smiling sadly. “I’ve waited so long… I… I almost thought, maybe you didn’t really want to see me again.”

“I did,” Kara said fervently. “I swear, Lena – ”

“I believe you,” Other Lena said, quickly. “I do.”

Kara faltered, her shoulders dropping slightly.

“But you have to understand,” Other Lena threw her a self-deprecating smile. “Fear mixed with self-loathing is one powerful cocktail.”

That, Kara could understand.

“How much time has passed for you? How long has it been since… since the incident?”

Kara found it hard to look at Other Lena like this. When she was so inquisitive, so interested in Kara’s life, when all Kara had thought of these last couple of months was Other Lena, and how much she missed her. It was hard when Other Lena had built her life so meticulously, with so much diligence and an iron will to go forward, while all Kara had done was fall apart.

Kara looked out the window.

The sky had darkened just slightly, the sunlight allowing streaks of pink and orange skies to accentuate the stark skyscrapers scattered across the city. She shook her head and shot Other Lena a quick look, before casting her eyes back down to her fiddling hands.

“I… I don’t actually know,” Kara admitted. “A couple of months at least.”

“You haven’t been keeping track?”

Kara shrugged self-consciously. “I barely know what day we are,” she whispered. “Time kind of… blends together.”

Other Lena looked at her with a mixture of sadness and understanding.

“Yeah,” she whispered. “I get that.”

Kara looked away. The reminder of the time without her was just as much a reminder that Kara would have to leave her again. She wasn’t ready for that. Other Lena seemed to guess that too.

“Well, what I actually meant to say was just that I… I’ve waited a long time. A really long time,” she whispered. “I’m just so glad I finally… I finally get to see you.”

Her fingers squeezed Kara’s own. Kara looked back at her.

“To touch you,” she said hoarsely. “To know that you were real. That you were there… with me.”

“Lena,” Kara’s eyes fluttered with tears again, and she wished she could stop it. “Rao, I’m sorry.”

“Don’t be,” Other Lena interrupted her, inching closer so her hand could reach out to touch Kara’s face. Kara almost gasped in gratitude to feel her touch again. “At least these are good tears. I’ve spent so long dreaming of the last time I saw you in tears…”

They both flinched at the memory.

“I suppose I should thank you,” Other Lena smiled sadly. “For holding me like that. For not leaving me. I can’t imagine it was a pretty sight.”

She chuckled self-consciously.

“It’s not often you get to thank someone for attending your death.”

“You don’t have to – ”

“I’m just afraid that once I start thanking you, I’ll never stop. I’ve just got so much to thank you for.”

“There’s nothing to thank me for, Lena,” Kara shook her head. “Nothing. Without me, none of this would have even happened in the first place.”

Other Lena leaned in, searching for Kara’s stubborn eyes. Once she caught them, she smiled.

“Exactly,” she whispered.

There was a familiar, teasing glint in her eyes, and Kara couldn’t help but smile back through her tears. That voice. That sharp, amused edge that always kept Kara on her toes – that always made her feel so alive.

For one horribly relieved second, she couldn’t even imagine how she’d gone one day not hearing that proud, rebellious lilt in Other Lena’s voice. That there would have been a day in which she hadn’t enjoyed that confident smirk, the endless teasing – because how could she have when the familiarity of Other Lena’s expression and voice was enough to turn back all the clocks? Back to when it was just them in the most terrible of circumstances, but in the most sacred of moments.

Kara smiled as the tears rolled down her cheeks.

“Oh, hey,” Other Lena pulled her closer. “Sorry, I’m so sorry.”

“No, no,” Kara wanted to apologize for ruining the one visit she’d even gotten. The once chance she’d gotten to throw everything out in the open. “I’m sorry.”

“Don’t apologize,” Other Lena whispered, wrapping her arms around Kara. “Don’t you dare.”

Other Lena’s scent engulfed Kara like a warm, winter blanket. A cozy, safe nest to be tucked away in. She was just ashamed her tears smudged dark traces onto Other Lena’s blouse.

“It’s alright,” Other Lena echoed, and Kara squeezed her eyes shut, just once. Just to let the pain wash over her – let it have its moment so Kara could really feel it. Could feel Other Lena dying, leaving, crying, gone. Let herself grieve in the unique moment where she could still be with her ghost. Who could ever say they got that chance?

When she caught her breath again, her chest rattling from the pain of it all, she tried to pull away, tried to look at Other Lena like she had to. Like she could wake up any minute now, and forget Other Lena’s face. Forget the way she looked at her. She didn’t think she could bear it.

“I just… I’ve missed you so much,” Kara confessed shakily. “I miss you. And she, Lena, she’s there and she’s wonderful, but it’s not the same. You’re not…” she hesitated.

“Not the same?” Other Lena filled in softly, understanding.

Kara nodded, a flutter of a sigh of relief leaving her mouth when she heard Other Lena’s words.

“It’s alright, you can say it,” she smiled. “It’s true. Even now, having lived my life exactly the way she has, seeing and experiencing it the way she has seen and experienced life… I still don’t think we feel the same things, or even see everything the same way. Even now, knowing my body is the way it should be, that my heart is just… there instead of this clump of poison.”

She took Kara’s hand and placed it on her chest, so Kara could feel the soft thumping of her heartbeat. Kara’s cheeks flushed when she saw how dangerously close her palm was to the plunging neckline of Other Lena’s blouse, and it took everything in her not to rip her hand away like it had been burned.

Other Lena laughed softly. She gently took Kara’s hand and placed it on her lap, before gingerly touching Kara’s hot cheeks with just two fingers.

“At least one thing remains the same in every universe,” she murmured.

Kara had to look down at that, and a fluttering laugh left Other Lena’s lips.

“Oh Kara.”

A renewed wave of tears brimmed in Kara’s eyes. Even though she knew Other Lena wouldn’t just disappear again, she also knew she couldn’t stay forever. Her time with Other Lena would be cut short, just as it was always going to be.

“I’ve missed you so much,” Kara whispered. “You don’t – you can’t understand.”

She looked at Other Lena with wet, desperate eyes.

“Every day I just… I keep thinking of you, I keep reliving every single moment – and it’s just… this pain, it won’t go away. I miss you so much, Lena. I couldn’t… I couldn’t help you, and you’re gone and everything just hurts so fucking bad. And I see you…. Everywhere. Everywhere. Every bookshop I pass, every music store, every… Fuck!”

Kara had to wipe her tears away with a messy hand, her entire body trembling with all her unspilled words, everything she’d ever longed to express suddenly bursting from her mouth.

“I see you everywhere,” she whispered, staring into Other Lena’s eyes. “I feel like I’m going insane. I can’t… I can’t go anywhere anymore without being reminded... without seeing you in every crowd. It… It scares me so much, Lena,” she confessed. “I can’t let go. I can’t… I can’t let go.”

And there it was. The truth that had been gnawing at her heart like a parasite, so out in the open for the first time.

“I can’t forget. I don’t want to forget either,” she said, “but I can’t live like this. I can’t let go,” she shook her head. “I can’t let go, I can’t… I can’t let you go. I don’t know how to,” she confessed, tears falling soundlessly on her lap.

“And you think I don’t understand?” Other Lena interrupted her gently.

Kara’s brow furrowed up in confusion, wiping away her tears with a clumsy stroke of her hand.

“It’s taken me years, Kara. And I’m still not quite done with missing you. Do you know how hard those first few months were for me? Those first years?”

“But,” Kara frowned in confusion. “But you have everything? You have the happiness you wanted. The life you wanted, don’t you?” she asked hesitantly. “Is that not…”

“Of course I do,” Other Lena’s face softened. “I have everything I wished for and more. I assume… I’m going to assume that you saw?”

Kara nodded, a little embarrassed at how voyeuristic Mxy’s exploits could be. How willingly she’d joined him in those exploits.

“Then you know,” Other Lena filled in softly. “I have a home, a job that I actually like. Someone who loves me unconditionally…”

Other Lena cast her eyes down at that, perhaps ashamed too, that she had picked Kara’s own doppelgänger to be happy with, out of all the millions of people in National City.

Kara’s heart clenched painfully in her chest, and she was reminded of something she’d heard a long time ago. Back when she’d found Alex sitting in a bar, about 9 months after Maggie had left. Alex had been eyeing the last in a long line of empty beer bottles on her table, not looking up, even when Kara came in to sit next to her.

“Did you know?” she’d slurred. “That she’s got someone new? Bumped into one of her friends today. She told me. Says it someone from the police force,” she’d said, eyes empty. “Of course she does. She’s beautiful. Amazing. Who wouldn’t wanna date her, right?”

She hadn’t waited for a reply, her eyes red, staring off into the distance.

“Do you know there’s this saying? I think it goes something like; I hope you’re amazingly happy and content, that you get everything you want out of life,” Alex’s lips trembled, “and I hope to God I never have to hear about it.”

It was only then that Kara had seen the tears.

It came back to her, then. When her heart clenched in something between jealousy and pure, unforgiving sadness. Longing. A life Kara had never gotten to experience, a life she’d never gotten to witness. One irretrievably lost to her. Kara didn’t quite understand where that clenching pain came from, only that she’d felt it a couple of times before, in the months leading up to her seeing Other Lena. But Kara wanted to hear everything Other Lena had to say. Every single word of it. So she bit those feelings away and listened.

“I don’t think there’s any version of me out there who could’ve had such a wonderful ending, you know?” Other Lena said, smiling. “The amount of happiness out here… well, I have my doubts that it’s deserved.”

“Of course you deserve it,” Kara croaked. “I’d argue the universe has a lot to make up for when it comes to you. You deserve everything good that’s coming your way.”

Other Lena threw her this smile again, that sad, grateful smile – devoid of any edges or sharpness.

“What I’m saying is, I got the happiness. The happy ending. More than I probably deserve. But that doesn’t mean I don’t miss you either.”

“It doesn’t?”

“God, Kara,” Other Lena looked up through the glass balcony door at the sun, sinking slowly into the clouds above the skyline of National City. “Do you know how often I’ve felt guilty for thinking about you? For missing you? Do you know how scared I am to forget?”

She threw Kara a pained expression that took her off guard.

“Do you know how long five years are? Do you know how treacherous and human my mind is? Do you know how easy it is to lose details over the years? To forget whether your blouse was dark or light? What words you used to describe me? Do you know how easy it is to forget the sound of your laugh when I surprised you?”

Her eyes were shimmering with unshed tears now too.

“I’m so afraid that every day I lose things from you. That every day I don’t think about you, the details will slip away faster and faster. I’m so afraid that one day, I won’t remember any of it. And you won’t be here to remind me.”

The last words came out in a whimper. She turned away, and Kara’s heart broke, seeing her hand go up to touch the skin beneath her eyes. To wipe away the tears Kara wasn’t allowed to see.

“I get scared too, sometimes,” Kara whispered after a beat.

She heard Other Lena sniffle, but her head paused. She was listening.

“I get scared that… that it wasn’t real. I mean, I know it was. It was,” Kara whispered. “But sometimes… sometimes it feels like every part of you was ripped from my life, root and stem. Every piece that I should’ve been allowed to keep… gone. Like you never even…”

She couldn’t finish those words, it hurt too much.

“I keep looking for you in scraps, in memories, in bits and pieces, in places around me – but I can’t find you, Lena. You’re everywhere, and yet nowhere at the same time. It’s like the universe wants me to forget by erasing the parts of you in my life, and I’m so fucking scared I’ll forget. But then – then I can’t think or walk or sleep without… without remembering. Without thinking of you, over and over again,” she said, her jaw clenching in frustration. “I just… I just miss you so much, and I’m just so afraid that it will never stop.”

“And would that really be so bad?”

Kara looked up to find Other Lena staring at her with soft, glistening eyes.

“Yes,” Kara whispered, no doubt in her mind. “Yes because it hurts. It fucking hurts, Lena.”

“I know,” Other Lena said softly. “And if I hadn’t had my heart ripped out and replaced with alien scraps, then I would say it was the most painful ache I’ve ever felt in my life, living this life, missing you. But I’m going to say the Kryptonite heart wins here.”

Kara laughed in surprise through her tears, and Other Lena joined in softly.

“I know it hurts, Kara. It hurt me too. But the pain is a reminder. That’s how I see it anyways.”

“A reminder?”

Other Lena picked up Kara’s hand and put it in her lap. She leaned in closer to Kara, eyes searching for understanding in Kara’s own.

“It’s a reminder of how much love we had,” Other Lena implored softly.

Kara’s heart stopped.

“Love?”

Other Lena chuckled softly, though it didn’t diminish the seriousness in her words.

“Yes, Kara,” she said. “Love. Complicated as our relationship was… is,” she offered hesitantly, “I know there was love there. What other reason do you think you have for showing up every day to talk to me?”

Kara opened her mouth, but couldn’t think of anything to say.

“There was love, Supergirl,” Other Lena implored softly. “Love for each other, but also a love for the people around us. For the people we wanted to help. For the better versions of ourselves, we wanted to become.”

Kara trembled. Other Lena tucked a curl behind Kara’s ear.

“I’m happy, Kara. Actually, abundantly, exuberantly happy. A kind of happy that I didn’t think was possible for me before I got to know you,” she shook her head. “I’m in the extraordinarily privileged position to have seen what my life could’ve been like without you in it. And I can’t say how much better it has gotten from the second you showed up in my life,” she said earnestly. “You don’t know how much that means to me. How much I owe to you. How much this universe owes you. Without you, none of this would have ever been possible.”

“You always – ”

“Had the capacity for change?” Other Lena filled in for her. “Maybe. But it would never have grown if it wasn’t for your kindness. For your willingness to help me.”

“Lena – ”

“You don’t know how often I lived something and wished to the fucking bottom of my heart that you could’ve been there to see it,” Other Lena said. “How much it hurt to know that you would never see the things you helped create. The changes I made for you. And that’s where the missing will always be.”

She tried to smile, but Kara could see her heart break.

“But I just know, in every moment that I live that I have to thank you for, that it is because of you. And that it’s because of the love we shared, that the good things happen.”

She squeezed Kara’s hand tightly in her own.

“I know the hurt and the missing will persist for a while,” she said kindly, her sad eyes keeping Kara glued to her every word. “It will feel like your heart is being ripped out of your chest and trampled on in a million different ways.”

Kara chuckled, but there was no humor in it. That was exactly what it felt like.

“When it does, I hope you try to think of me with fondness. I hope you try and find something to keep you through it. But most of all,” she said, squeezing Kara’s hand in her lap, “I hope you will learn to see the beauty in the missing part. The changes we went through, because of and in thanks to each other. That’s how I choose to see it,” Other Lena finally whispered. “That’s how I got through it. Get through it,” she amended. “I found the missing to be a testament to how much we cared for each other. How we loved each other enough to change.”

Kara finally looked away, fresh tears rolling down her cheeks.

Good tears, she hoped, but she couldn’t deny that the pain was still there too. Mixed in a bubble of too many feelings for Kara to really understand in that moment. She didn’t know how she could ever tell Other Lena that she found no joy, no fondness in her memories; that every image she had of Other Lena was stained with pain, misery, and so much regret. Regret that made her double over in the mornings, that made her feel like she could throw up her insides on the floor, regret that made her want to crawl under her bed and hide from the universe. Regret that made her want to die, instead of living that pain over and over again.

Joy. Fondness. Kara didn’t think she would ever possess the ability to connect those to her memories of Other Lena ever again. And maybe that was the biggest loss of all. Maybe that was the thing that was so slowly killing her, the silent, slow, creeping cloud that took away the last remnant she had of Other Lena.

Kara wanted to say all that, red with shame, and more hurt than she could ever express, but she found herself speechless, leaning over slightly, her hand over her mouth, as she shook her head.

That was enough for Other Lena. Her expression crumbled, and Kara barely had to close her eyes to feel Other Lena again.

“Oh honey,” Other Lena pulled her closer, and Kara allowed her tears to spill onto Other Lena’s blouse, her trembling fingers holding on to her as if she were her lifeline. “I’m so sorry.”

She was sorry. Kara was sorry. It was her fault. Her fault, her fault.

Other Lena’s arms were warm, and so comforting. Kara felt herself melt away in the embrace, allowing her head to rest against Other Lena’s shoulder, sinking away completely. Other Lena let her.

“I don’t want to say goodbye yet,” Kara whispered after a while. “Please.”

“Good,” Other Lena whispered back into Kara’s hair. “Because I’m not letting you go just yet.”

Kara nodded, even though they both knew they were just prolonging the inevitable. That was alright, though, Kara thought. Everything was alright if she could just stay with Other Lena a little longer. Just a little while longer…

 

 

“So,” Other Lena started after a while, her nails tapping nervously against the glass in her hands. “You saw then, who… who I ended up with. You know.”

“I do.”

There was food on the table before them. Fruit, some cookies Other Lena kept in the drawer beside her desk for in-between meeting cravings. A collection of snacks Other Lena had been able to scavenge around the empty offices on her floor. And while Kara hadn’t been particularly hungry, it seemed that every Lena in every universe held the power to convince her to at least eat something, just so she could get that winning, approving Lena smile back in return.

They’d talked about so many things that Kara had completely lost track of time.

Other Lena’s work. Other Lena’s ambitions, her stories, her experiences, her thoughts, her dreams… Kara soaked up every laugh, every piece of Other Lena’s life that she wanted to share with Kara, every morsel of information out there for her to grasp. But when the laughter had faded a little, and the conversation had finally turned soft, swaying into the territory of safe, familiar subjects, that Other Lena’s pensive expression returned.

Kara had known that it wouldn’t take long for Other Lena’s thoughts to wander again. They had probably never strayed far away from the subject of Kara’s life. Her experiences. She’d just noticed how utterly petrified Kara had been, out of her depth in this other universe, and had wanted her to feel safe and sound before she’d broach the subject of her life. But Kara could tell that the thoughts had lingered. The questions had persisted. And after the laughs had turned to soft smiles, and the peels of fruit had been collected into a small bowl on Other Lena’s table, after they’d gotten comfortable on the couch, only their knees touching in the middle, Other Lena had finally asked.

“You saw who I ended up with.”

Other Lena nodded to herself.

“You know,” she said, matter-of-factly. “I thought you might.”

Her head moved sharply in Kara’s direction. “The fifth-dimensional creature?”

“He showed me, yes.”

Other Lena nodded again, straightening her fingers on her lap. Then she sighed, lowering her head. She’d already undone her tight bun before, having gathered her hair in a loose ponytail. To avoid a headache, she’d teased, weaving her fingers through her dark tresses, the smell of her shampoo rendering Kara unable to speak anyways. Now, her ponytail spilled over her shoulder as she leaned forward, making her look tired like Kara was asking too much of her.

“Does it… bother you?” Other Lena asked.

Kara hadn’t even thought about that. All that time, all those worried looks she’d intercepted between her sister and her friends, and yet no one had even thought to ask her that question. She hadn’t even bothered to ask herself that question.

“No,” she said, and found that she was being honest too. “I don’t think so. I guess I… I see it as a separate thing.”

“Separate?” Other Lena’s asked.

“Well, it has nothing to do with me, I think. She’s her own person, her own being.” Kara thought about it. “I’ve always found my doppelgangers and I didn’t share too many of the same ideals, the same dreams… I think that just results in the conclusion that we are very much separate beings. Just like you and Lena aren’t… the same. Ergo,” Kara made a lame motion with her hand. “It has nothing to do with me,” she concluded in a whisper.

Other Lena shot her a puzzled look.

“While I can’t speak to your murderous doppelgängers,” she said with a raised eyebrow, “I don’t think I quite agree.”

“You don’t?” Kara asked.

“Kara,” Other Lena’s face softened. “Why were you so determined to help me? Back when you first saw me in your universe? What made you reach out and come visit me so often, when you knew very well I wanted you dead?”

Kara felt confused. “Because… well because it was my fault. I put you in that situation. I changed your life by making a stupid wish. By being selfish. I did that… to you. I had to make it up to you?”

She hated the way her voice trailed off into a question. As if Other Lena had to confirm it for her.

“While I don’t question your motives,” Other Lena said, “I don’t believe that’s the sole reason you came to me. I believe there’s more at play there.”

“More?” Kara asked.

“Kara,” Other Lena leaned in. “While I don’t doubt that you have a huge heart and enough love to rehabilitate every horrible person on the planet, I don’t think your guilt was your only reason for reaching out. I believe that we… that we are destined to be tangled up in each other’s lives. We are entangled by a fate that I don’t understand, but I do respect. How else could your interference in my life have had such huge consequences? A situation like that tends to make you see the bigger picture, doesn't it?”

“Well…”

“Kara!” Other Lena let out a disbelieving laugh, shaking her head. “I believe we belong in each other’s lives. We have to be in each other’s lives for us to function. That’s why we keep finding each other in every universe. That’s why…”

She swallowed and shook her head a little.

“That’s why, when I was at my lowest, I found Kara. I wanted to stay away from her,” she almost pleaded to Kara to understand. “I tried so hard. I was rude. Cold. And yet… it hurt more to be alone with this life you’d given me, than when I was reminded of you. Meeting her, being around her… it felt like I’d earned a part of myself back. I don’t want you to misunderstand me,” she said, eyebrows drawn in worry, “she is not you. She was so different, and at first, it felt hard to meet someone I thought I knew and rediscover her through this lens of a new chance. But I did. And it was hard, but I am so eternally grateful that I did. Because she brought something back. Something I thought I’d lost. Something I’m still not sure how to define,” Other Lena whispered, a sheen of wetness over her eyes.

“Forgive me, I’m not trying to get all weepy and sentimental on you,” Other Lena laughed self-depreciatingly. “I’m just trying to explain to you that I think you saved me because you couldn’t stay away. Because we mean something to each other, in every universe. That connection, that… something drew me to my Kara, just as it drew me to you.”

She seemed to deflate a little. “I must sound like a rambling hippy to you, don’t I? Talking about ‘the universe’ and powers above us. God,” she sighed and leaned her head back on the couch, staring up at the ceiling. “I know. I sound insane.”

“You don’t,” Kara said quickly. “I just…” she paused. “You know, that’s not the first time I’ve heard that.”

Other Lena rolled her head over the back of the couch to look at her.

“It isn’t?”

“No,” Kara smiled softly. “My Lena said the exact same thing not too long ago.”

“In what context?”

Kara blushed and cast her eyes down.

“The same one,” she whispered. “She believed every Kara would find every Lena in every universe. That we were meant to meet.”

Other Lena cracked a smile, and it broke through the seriousness of before.

“So she’s not all stupid then,” Other Lena teased.

“Hey.”

Other Lena laughed while Kara shot her a defensive look. “She’s the smartest person I know.”

“I know, I know,” Other Lena held her hands up in self-defense. “I’m just messing with you. Haven’t you missed it?”

Kara threw her a look, which only made her laugh all over again, but they both knew she was right. Kara had missed it so much.

“Besides,” Other Lena said, a dimming smile still on her face. “She brought you here to me. That’s more than I ever could.”

Kara smiled, looking down at her folded hands.

“She didn’t know if she’d be able to,” Kara whispered. “She didn’t tell me until it was ready. I think she was scared to disappoint me.”

Other Lena looked at her.

“She must’ve really thought you needed this. This… visit,” she said, choosing her words so carefully. “She wouldn’t have gone through so much trouble otherwise.”

Kara could only look away in response.

“Is that your way of saying – ”

“Yes,” Other Lena said simply. “She’s scared of losing you. To the memory of her own ghost, no less. She needs you. She wants to be in your life in the best possible way. If this was the only way she thought she could, why wouldn’t she invest time and funds – why wouldn’t she try to change your perception?”

“Because she wants me happy?”

“Because she needs you happy. She’s drawn to you, just as I am to my Kara. There’s no version of either of us that can be deprived of the other’s existence in their life. My story, with all its suffering, at the very least proves that.”

Kara looked away.

“It’s funny,” she said, but there was no humor in her voice. “Sometimes it feels like the complete opposite. Like all I’ve ever succeeded at is making the life of every Lena I’ve encountered completely miserable. No matter how hard I try,” Kara’s eyebrows knitted together, “it always seems to work out badly.”

Other Lena looked at her with pity, but Kara didn’t look. Didn’t want to feel it.

“Is it less worthwhile if it takes longer than a minute to make one’s life better?” Other Lena asked softly. “That’s a strange thing to hear coming from you. Was the time it took you to get through to me unwisely spent?”

Kara threw her a look, but Other Lena just responded with a raised eyebrow. Kara sighed. She always gave in.

“Of course not. It was worth… everything.”

“See?” Other Lena said, but there was no smugness in her voice. Just a soft expression on her face.

“I’m not saying it’s always going to be smooth sailing, but I promise you it will always be worth it. In every universe.”

Kara looked at her and finally shook her head with a short, disbelieving smile.

“What?” Other Lena asked. “What is it – do I sound crazy? Is that it?”

“No,” Kara smiled. “No. You just sound a lot like my Lena, is all.”

An ugly frown graced Other Lena’s features and Kara laughed.

“Yeah yeah,” she said, before Other Lena could open her mouth. “I won’t tell her.”

Other Lena softened and shook her head before tilting it in Kara’s direction.

“You better not, Supergirl. You wouldn’t want to get on my bad side.”

Kara could only smile at that.

 

 

“It’s getting dark out,” Kara said, rising a little from where she was resting against Other Lena.

They hadn’t said anything in a while, but neither of them minded. They relished in the quiet comfort of a silence they hadn’t been able to share back in Kara’s world. Uninterrupted, unbothered. Touching.

Their reflections were looking back at them from the glass door of the balcony, separating them from the dark, warm night air. The sounds from outside, the cars, the traffic, the life below, had quieted a little, the world settling for the evening.

“Is it?”

“God,” Kara tried to find a clock on one of the walls. “How long have we been here?”

“I don’t know. It doesn’t feel that long.”

Kara had to agree with her on that. The minutes and hours had never been enough to say everything she wanted to say. Every sentence felt rushed as if they had to get through everything in time. As if they were trying to fit entire months of conversations into a single hour. And yet, time had flown by. Kara had arrived when the sun had still shone brightly down on her on Other Lena’s balcony. Now the only lights she could see outside came from a sliver of moon behind some phantom clouds and the scattered lights behind the windows of the skyscrapers in National City.

“I wonder if I’m taking just as long in my world too,” Kara whispered, and a pang of guilt wormed its way into her heart.

She could just picture her Lena sitting on a desk, eyeing that portal with red-rimmed eyes. Worried sick. Was she scared she’d made a mistake yet? Was she afraid something had gone wrong in that other universe? Was she looking up at the clock, her frown deepening with every minute that passed? Would she be biting her nails down to the rim until they became a bloody, painful mess that would take too long to heal again?

Kara looked down at her lap and felt the nauseating pressure of time weighing down on her. She knew she would have to go soon. She knew she would have to go back. Even if she’d been stretching the minutes and seconds in this universe to last her long enough to stop the pain from festering in her heart. Like it would heal the pain – or at least subdue it for a while, even though she knew the pain would come back down on her like a brick wall the second she crossed the border to her own universe. She was just prolonging the inevitable. Hiding away in this corner of another universe as if it could make the reality of her pain just a vague dream she couldn’t quite remember.

“I don’t know,” Other Lena said airily. “But I don’t think it matters much, do you? I mean, we haven’t been here that long. We’ve still got time.”

Kara didn’t quite know what to say. She tried to smile, but couldn’t deny that the image of Lena, cold, waiting, eyes red from staring at the portal unblinkingly, trying to catch any signs of Kara’s return was enough to make Kara feel cold inside. Like she had to be somewhere else. Like trying to leave a party, knowing someone was waiting up for her.

And Kara realized it was exactly like that.

She knew exactly what would happen if she went back to her universe. To the last, minor detail, she knew.

She would go through the door, and Lena would still be there, anxious and waiting. She wouldn’t push Kara to share too much, but she would hold her, she would wrap Kara up in a hug, and promise her that it would be alright, even if she had no idea what she would have to fix in Kara’s life. Even if Kara would fall apart right then and there.

She would hold her just long enough, and dry her tears with tissues she always carried in her bag. She would let Kara calm down, would talk to her until Kara could feel some semblance of peace again, and then she would try even harder, just to get Kara to smile again. And Kara would. She always would.

She would get her driver to drive them home quickly, squeezing Kara’s hand in the back of the car, letting the quiet hum of the car lull them both into a comfortable silence.  They would drive back to Kara’s apartment, climb the wobbly stairs of Kara’s apartment block, all the way up to the fourth floor, where they would enter the quiet apartment together. Kara would open the lock, and Lena would turn on all the lights, taking her and Kara’s coats to hang them on the hangers by the door. She would head into the kitchen to make them both a cup of tea while Kara would turn the bedside lamp in her bedroom on and would make the bed. They would drink the tea together by the kitchen island in comfortable silence, or she would make small talk before they would both get ready in the bedroom to go to bed. Lena would do her extensive skincare. Kara would watch while she brushed her teeth.

They would snuggle up together, and Lena would hold her.

They would both go home together.

Because Lena wasn’t leaving her, and Kara wouldn’t let her. Because she needed Lena. Because she loved Lena more than she had ever loved anybody. And somehow being here for so long, though it had been a gift, a way for Lena to gift Kara back the person she’d lost and mourned for weeks, Kara felt lonely without her there to share it with.

But she would get to explain all of it, once she got home. She would crawl into her bed next to Lena, and she would spill it all. The tears, the stories, her thoughts, her feelings, the good and the bad, and Lena would still be there. To listen. To understand – to try, at the very least.

The feeling that had lingered all throughout the time she’d spent with Other Lena felt stronger now. More pressing. It hurt in that familiar two-sided way Kara had gotten to know intimately by now. Because returning to Lena would mean saying goodbye to Other Lena, again. It would mean facing the fact that she was not of this reality, that she wasn’t meant to be in this one. That she and Other Lena weren’t meant to stay in the same world together.

But it also meant going home to Lena.

It meant going home to her Lena.

A loud noise and bright lights gliding through the room suddenly pulled them both from their reveries, instinctively turning their heads towards the window, where they saw a helicopter in the distance, aiming to land on another skyscraper close by.

They both stared at it, shoulders tensed up, moving in sync as they watched tersely how the helicopter moved away from their line of sight.

The noise dimmed as quickly as it had appeared, but it had successfully ripped them from the quiet refuge of their pocket of time they had been hiding in. They both looked at each other as the lights of the helicopter left the room, leaving it darker than it had seemed before, even with the few, sparse decorative lights in Other Lena’s office.

Kara shook her head while Other Lena took a sip of her glass of whiskey. Her hand was trembling only slightly. It seemed that all these years, even in a different universe, hadn’t taken that fear away. Even when she softly placed her glass back down on the glass coffee table, the noise felt too jarring in the previously peaceful, quiet room.

The spell was broken, and they both knew it.

Other Lena scraped her throat.

“The only street noise you do occasionally get bothered by up here,” she joked dryly.

Kara let out a quiet laugh.

“Beats the drunken yelling you get near my apartment.”

Other Lena smiled, casting her eyes down.

Kara knew it was time then. She couldn’t quite explain it, but she felt that she had overstayed her welcome in this dimension, even if she didn’t think she would ever be ready to leave. It felt lonely, knowing she would have to go. As if another universe would close its doors to her forever. She wondered if in any universe she would ever get used to that.

“I’m not ready to say goodbye,” Kara whispered. It was honest, but it still hurt to say out loud, knowing it was time.

“Then stay,” Other Lena implored, a sudden fierceness in her words. She took Kara’s hand in hers and pulled it close to her body. “You’re more than welcome to. Please. We haven’t had enough time to talk.”

The urgency in her voice sounded desperate, and Kara had to keep herself from falling for it, because she would. She always would. A part of her tried to pull at the strings and jump at Other Lena’s proposal, would kill to spend just one night more in this version of National City – just one night more to tell Other Lena all the things she’d never gotten to in her world. Because there was more. There would always be more.

Kara looked back up at Other Lena and threw her a teary smile.

“I’m not sure there will ever be enough time.”

“Then let’s try,” Other Lena said, her fiery tone strong enough to convince Kara ten times over. But she knew she couldn’t.

“Please, Kara,” Other Lena said. “My apartment’s big enough to house a football team. You can stay for however long you want. I could take time off, we could talk, we could…”

“I’d just be an anomaly in your life, Lena,” Kara whispered softly. “You know that better than I do.”

Other Lena shook her head furiously like she would personally defy the laws of physics and bend them to her will if it meant holding Kara for a moment longer.

“You wouldn’t,” she insisted. “I’ve missed you for years, Kara, one afternoon isn’t enough.”

“You know I have to go home, Lena,” Kara whispered softly. “As much as I want to stay, neither of us can live like this. No matter how much I might want to.”

Other Lena pursed her lips together angrily, a flash of venom and pain glimmering in her eyes. It didn’t scare Kara. Not really, because as quickly as it had appeared, so quickly did it die down, leaving just frustration, fear, and sadness behind.

“It’s not enough time,” Other Lena finally whispered.

“No,” Kara agreed. “I don’t think so either.”

“I don’t want you to go back.”

“I have to find Lena,” Kara whispered. “I need to see her again.”

“Can’t it wait?” Other Lena asked. “Just… just a couple of days, no longer than that, please!”

“No,” Kara whispered. “I don’t think it can. I… I promised her I would be careful. I… I promised her I’d come home to her.”

Something flickered in Other Lena’s eyes. A hint of hurt, and yet… so much understanding. Like it dawned on her all at once.

“You love her,” Other Lena said.

“Of course I do,” Kara said, a hint of confusion in her voice. “Isn’t that the reason we’re both here today? If I hadn’t loved Lena enough to want to make everything right then…”

“Right,” Other Lena said slowly, but Kara got the idea that they weren’t exactly on the same page. Like Kara wasn’t in on some joke that Other Lena had figured out a long time ago but wouldn’t bother explaining.

“Right,” Other Lena echoed, casting her eyes down.

“She’s waiting for me,” Kara whispered slowly. “I promised her.”

“And she can’t wait a little longer?” Other Lena asked. But the venom had gone. It was a petulant, almost childish attempt to keep Kara there longer, but they both knew it.

“Maybe,” Kara said, “but… but I’m not sure I can.”

Other Lena looked up at that, her eyes indecipherable.

“She’s waiting for you,” she just said, slowly.

“Yes,” Kara whispered. “She’s waiting for me to go home.”

“Home?”

“Oh, yeah,” Kara blushed. “It’s ehm… she’s staying with me for a while. Just for a while.”

“Staying with you,” Other Lena said slowly. “As in…”

“She was worried about me,” Kara said. “She thought I wasn’t taking good enough care of myself so – ”

“So she’s taking care of you and staying with you – oh that’s clever.”

“Clever?”

“Nothing,” Other Lena waved it away. “But you,” she said, eyes sharp, “you don’t mind that then? Her staying with you?”

“No,” Kara said, “no not at all. In fact…” she hesitated. “In fact I think it’s been the best thing to happen to me in a very long time.”

The warm feeling in her chest confirmed that. Made her feel lightheaded in the best way.

Other Lena’s eyes softened, her hold on Kara’s hand loosening just a little, but never letting go.

“I see.” She bowed her head. “It’s like we said, isn’t it?” she asked. “Drawn to each other in every universe?”

“Lena and I had been friends for a long time.”

“Yet last time I saw you two, she couldn’t stand the sight of you.”

It came out sharp, meant to hurt, meant to maim.

Kara was visibly taken aback and instinctively pulled her hand away.

“I’m sorry!” Other Lena’s apology came so quickly, Kara barely had time to process the hurt. “I’m sorry,” Other Lena echoed, sincere regret in her eyes, lips trembling like she’d been surprised by her own viciousness.

“I didn’t mean to say that,” Other Lena said, her hand gliding back over the couch towards Kara’s, stopping just shy of her touch. “I’m sorry. I’m sorry.”

“It’s okay,” Kara whispered.

“It’s not,” Other Lena said. “Forgive me, I’m just…”

Kara waited, apprehensive of what was to come.

Other Lena blew the air out of her mouth and leaned her head back, her hair rolling over her shoulders as she shook her head.

She couldn’t look at Kara.

“I’m just… I really didn’t think I would get to see you today,” Other Lena said, her voice cracking. “It was just… nowhere on my list of things that I predicted could happen today.”

Her jaw clenched as she bit her would-be tears away, and Kara felt her heart go soft again. She realized, not for the first time, that she could never be sure of where her limits were when it came to Other Lena. There seemed to be nothing she couldn’t forgive, nothing that Other Lena could say that would make Kara rethink her next move. Nothing.

“I’m sorry,” Kara said, lowering her head. “I didn’t think about it. I just… Lena gave me this chance and I… I jumped. I didn’t think about how it would be for you, how it would feel,” she struggled to get the words out, her fingers tangling nervously in her clothes. “I just…”

 She turned and looked at Other Lena.

“I just wanted to see you again,” she confessed.

“It’s alright,” Other Lena said. “It’s not your fault. It’s just… I’ve run through every scenario in my head, thinking about how this would go. I’ve… I’ve had the time to think this through you know,” she looked at Kara. “You and I.”

She pulled her trembling hands on her lap, and Kara instantly missed the weight of Other Lena’s hand on her own. She had a self-deprecating smile on her face, lips wobbling like she wanted to cry as much as she wanted to be in charge of the situation again. She didn’t let it happen though, casting her eyes down before Kara got the chance to tell her it was okay. When she looked back up, her eyes were still glassy, but her lips were drawn, her jaw clenched. Her eyes were only soft when they looked back at Kara.

“I was ready,” Other Lena said slowly. “I thought I was going to be able to explain my life to you and tell you everything was going to be okay. I thought… I thought I would be in control, you know? That I had years to discover all the different feelings I could have, and that I had learned to deal with everything. That I could tell you it would all be okay. And now here you are,” Other Lena whispered, looking at Kara. “And I can’t let you go.”

The last of her words was lost in a whisper.

A dismissive shake of her head followed as she shot Kara a weak, wobbly smile.

“Isn’t that just silly?”

“It’s not,” Kara whispered.

Other Lena looked at her, the searching look in her eyes only accentuating how desperately she wanted to believe Kara.

“So how do we do this?” Other Lena asked, her voice young and fragile, begging for an answer that neither of them had. “How do we end this?”

Kara shook her head.

“What if we don’t?”

“Say goodbye?”

“Make it our goodbye. What if it’s just a… temporary thing? What if it’s just a,” she hesitated. “A ‘see you later,’ kind of thing?”

Like friends who would meet again for coffee. The time unspecified, but the occasion certain.

“A delay of execution,” Other Lena said slowly. “Perfect, I like it.”

She shot up from the couch and wiped her skirt straight with both hands.

“Yes,” she almost nodded to herself, “yes, it’s perfect.”

She extended her hand to Kara and pulled her up from the couch until they faced each other. Other Lena’s faux-cheery red smile looked painted on her face. Kara could see the control in each muscle. The conviction to go along with Kara’s idea, even if it felt equally heartbreaking to part with a lie. They both knew it. And yet they both weren’t ready to admit that it was.

“Just,” her eyes seemed to crack a little, though her smile never wavered, “don’t make me wait another six years, okay?”

Kara nodded.

“I promise,” she whispered.

Other Lena nodded too, smiling, though Kara could see the heartbreak in her eyes. The shared realization that that wasn’t up to Kara to promise.

“Oh,” Other Lena whispered.

Her trembling hand reached out and slowly tucked Kara’s hair behind her ear. Kara’s ear felt like it was glowing when Other Lena’s hand brushed against it. Other Lena paused, looking at her. She made a small sound, her tongue clicking against her teeth. She looked at her own motion as if it were the first and last time she would ever be able to make that move. Her eyes glimmered with more emotions than she would ever be willing to share.

But Kara understood.

“Just…”

Other Lena took a step forward, her hand slipping from Kara’s ear to her shoulder. She pushed herself up, just a little, her other hand cupping Kara’s cheek as she leaned in. Kara’s breath hitched in her throat. The moment seemed to last longer than it did. Other Lena’s fingers were cool to the touch, yet Kara’s face felt like it was burning.

Then, Other Lena leaned in closer, moving her head up just a little, to softly, gently, press a kiss to Kara’s forehead. It was a short, sweet kiss. A mere memory of her lips on Kara’s face. Yet her touch lingered.

Other Lena let out a breath, and Kara felt it on her eyelids. Other Lena lowered herself down to her heels again but didn’t move away. Instead, she leaned closer, until their foreheads were touching.

They didn’t speak.

Kara could only feel Other Lena’s face against her own, Other Lena’s fingers on her cheek.

 Kara looked at Other Lena, her eyes closed, her whimpers a wet dark sheen under her eyes, and was overwhelmed by a wave of sadness that overfell her. A deep fear that she hadn’t said everything, that she hadn’t said enough, that everything around her was falling apart before she could even get a grip on it.

Her heartbeat picked up again, a sense of urgency making spurring her on.

“Lena,” she said, the panic already palpable in her voice.

Other Lena opened her eyes and looked at her, and instantly seemed to know.

“I know,” she whispered. “It’ll be alright, I promise.”

“What if it won’t,” Kara asked. “What if… what if this really is the last time I see you, what if we’ll never – ”

Her voice seemed strangled, her heart felt like it was twisting and turning in her chest. Her idea of a peaceful goodbye from a second ago nowhere to be found.

“Hey,” Other Lena’s hands slid down to take hold of Kara’s shoulders as if she could steady her. “It’s fine. It’s going to be fine.”

“I’m not ready,” Kara whispered. “I’m not ready to lose you again. I don’t… I don’t think I can take it again. The first time… the first time it nearly killed me, fuck.”

Kara’s knees almost buckled, closing her eyes to keep the world from spinning.

“I don’t want it to hurt again. I don’t… I don’t think I can take it.”

“Hey,” Other Lena’s voice dropped, eyes searching for Kara’s own. “It’s alright. It’s okay. This won’t be the last time we talk. You know why? Because you’ll talk to Lena. She’ll make sure you can use that portal again, right?”

Kara wished she didn’t have to say what she said next.

“But what if we’re better off not being in each other’s lives? I know what you’re gonna say,” Kara said as Other Lena’s face contracted in frustration. “But there is only supposed to be one Lena and one Kara in every universe. What if we’ll just… what if we’re just prolonging the hurt by intervening in each other’s lives, time and time again?”

Other Lena paused.

Kara could see she realized the truth in her words just as much as Kara felt them straining her own soul.

“I’m happy,” she decided after a difficult, long pause. “Happier than I ever thought I could be. I have someone I love, who loves me, despite…” she let out a desperate, short laugh, “despite all the reasons she shouldn’t. I have a home. I have a life… A life I know I wouldn’t have had without you. Without the days we spent just… talking. Listening.”

Other Lena shook her head.

“My life started because of you, even if that wasn’t how it should have gone. You might be right,” Other Lena said, eyes shimmering, “you probably are, in fact. But I’m just… not okay with that,” she decided. “I’m not resigning myself to a life in which I never get to speak to you again. I won’t. I waited five and a half years to see you again. I can wait a while longer.”

“Yeah?”

Kara hated how strangled with tears her voice became.

Other Lena let out a shaky breath and nodded.

“I’m grateful, Kara Danvers,” she murmured, “to have gotten the chance to cross universes to get to know you.”

Kara’s eyelashes fluttered against her skin. She’d bite her teeth if she could, but Other Lena’s words had drained the last of her strength from her.

“You are going to do great things, Supergirl. With or without me there to see it. I hope to hear all about it when I see you again.”

Kara let out a soundless whisper, hot tears threatening to spill from the corners of her eyes.

“You should go now,” Other Lena said, nodding her head, her forehead still stuck to Kara’s face. “Your Lena’s waiting for you.”

Kara nodded too, and though both their eyes were closed, she knew Other Lena felt it too.

“I’ll miss you so much.”

“Please,” Other Lena let out a wet chuckle. “You won’t be gone long enough to miss me, right?”

Kara let her tears run down to her neck, let herself feel everything all at once.

“I promise,” she whispered. “I promise.”

 

 

When she arrived back at the lab, she felt like she was coming out of a long, deep dream. From the bright colors of the other universe to the grey of Lena’s lab.

The first thing she saw was Lena.

She was sitting in one of the chairs at her lab table, leaning her head on her hand. When she saw Kara, though, she shot up, the chair spinning in its place.

Her face contorted into a mixture of sadness and pity, and Kara could only imagine why. She must’ve been some sight, with swollen, red eyes, and a puffy face, shaking like a leaf.

“Kara,” Lena whispered.

That was all it took.

Kara crumbled on the spot, holding a trembling hand to her mouth.

She closed her eyes, wondering if the world would disappear beneath her feet – and if she even cared at all if it did – but didn’t fall. She couldn’t. Because Lena was already there, holding her so close, Kara couldn’t even sway on her feet. When they sank down to the floor, it was only because Lena was guiding her there, lips to Kara’s hair, arms tight enough to keep all of Kara’s pieces from falling out, holding her as Kara cried.

And she kept her close.

Kara didn’t know if she cried for minutes or hours, but Lena stayed close. She never even dropped her arms down. She was just there. She kissed Kara’s hair and face, allowing Kara to fall apart completely, and Kara knew they would get out of this lab together.

And though it didn’t feel like it then, Kara knew, deep down, that things would be alright again. She would feel happy again. She would be able to go on. Because Lena would be there. Lena would come home with her. She would cook. They would talk. They would dance to stupid 2000 hits. They would snuggle together on the couch to watch reruns of old sitcoms. Lena would ask Kara’s input on every little thing, even if Kara didn’t know a thing about it. They would rush out to go to work in the mornings and be happy to see each other again at night. And Kara wanted it. She wanted those moments more than she could put into words. She wanted it so bad that it would make this moment worth it. Would make the pain worth it. Because she would be with Lena, and Lena would be with her.

And most importantly, they would stay.

And Kara knew they would both be okay.

 

 

In the end, their first kiss wasn’t a bombastic, grandiose, dramatic kiss like it had been for Other Lena and Other Kara. There was no big speech, no tension leading up to it, no huge, earth-shaking revelations.

It was just them. Magical in its simplicity. Like a sweet, added touch to their routine.

It came in the dark of the evening, the quiet safety of their now-shared bedroom.

Lena had part of her wardrobe in Kara’s clothing rack. Kara now separated laundry based on Lena’s silk blouses and her own cotton T-shirts. Lena now shared Pinterest boards of new recipes she could try for them during the slow times at work. She now paid half of Kara’s rent (though there had been a discussion as to why she wasn’t allowed to pay all of it.) Her yellow, woolen blanket hung over the back of Kara’s couch. Her electric toothbrush had found its place in Kara’s bathroom. Her shampoo next to Kara’s, her laptop charger neatly stacked in Kara’s drawer.

Their routine that night was the same as it had been for dozens of evenings before.

They talked about their day over Lena’s homemade gnocchi in a spicy tomato sauce. Kara laid the table and cleaned the dishes while Lena put on a new jazz album Kara had gotten for her the week before. They’d settled on the couch, their feet meeting in the middle under their blanket as they read a few chapters; Kara from River Sing Me Home and Lena from Hamnet. A colorful stack of their books served as a decorative side table against Kara’s wall, next to the TV.

When they’d gotten tired, their eyes had met over the covers of their respective books, and Lena had smiled softly, before quietly announcing she would make some tea. She always asked Kara if she wanted one too, even if Kara had never refused before. While Lena headed to the kitchen, Kara would fold the blankets back over the couch, and would fluff the pillows just the way Lena liked them. She would head into the kitchen where Lena would have a steaming cup of tea ready in one of Kara’s colorful mugs. Lena drank her mint tea out of the ‘World’s Best Sister’ mug Kara had gotten from Alex years ago. (She’d laughed so loud the first time she’d realized what mug she’d been drinking from. It had quickly become her favorite.) Kara drank her apple-cinnamon tea from a big mug with a pink ‘K’ on it.

Kara had talked about her book. What she liked. What she hoped would happen. Lena had listened and had talked about her own book, her own thoughts and feelings, and ideas. They went over what they would be doing the day after; Kara would continue writing a piece on a new artist who photographed his hometown using only his newest L-phone. Lena had an important presentation coming up, but she’d already practiced her part in front of an enthusiastic Kara, so she wasn’t stressed. Lena said she would make them soup the next day, and Kara would go to the bakery two blocks further to pick up some bread to go along with it. They talked until their teas were finished before Lena had gently taken their mugs and rinsed them out in the sink.

Kara had turned off the kitchen light, before leading the way into the bedroom. They’d each changed into their pajamas, Kara’s a light-blue cotton thing, Lena her creamy, silk pair, the one Kara always washed with the utmost care.

They’d brushed their teeth together, their eyes smiling as they met in the mirror.

The night had gone just as normal.

They’d slipped under the covers together, Kara getting in first, lifting the sheets for Lena to get in. They talked for a while. Lena answered a few emails on her phone while Kara read an old New York Times article on the Feminist Foreign Policy. After that, Kara asked to turn off the lights, which Lena did.

Despite that, the room didn’t darken completely. Kara’s curtains let through enough light for their faces and forms to be clearly distinguishable in the early hours of the night. They were close. Their shoulders brushed as Lena balanced on her arm, looking over at Kara.

“Good night, Lena.”

“Good night, Kara. Sweet dreams.”

Kara smiled. Lena’s ‘good nights’ were always so tender, so loving. Kara loved going to sleep to Lena’s soft-spoken words, to the warm touch of her arm against her own. She liked closing her eyes, sinking into the pillows, knowing that when she woke up, Lena would be there. Her hair a messy bun of dark hair, two cups of steaming coffee on a small wooden tray on their bed. That soft, make-up-less smile that always made Kara’s heart soar in her chest. A smile that promised a good day, even in the worst of circumstances. It could storm, Andrea could throw her fit, she could accidentally delete an entire article without saving it first, and the day would still go well because she woke up to Lena’s smile and her freshly made coffee.

And now that same smile accompanied her good night.

But that’s when things deviated from the normal run of their night. The one small change that disrupted their normal routine and kept Kara’s curious eyes fixed on Lena.

Because Lena hesitated. Her smile dimmed just slightly, her eyes stuck on Kara’s face, an indecipherable, yet soft expression on her face.

She paused. Instead of turning around to lie down, she kept hovering in that same position, just slightly above Kara. Her hair looked wavy and long. It tickled Kara’s neck. Lena tucked some hair behind her ear but didn’t stick, and swung right back into place, accentuating her jaw, and the sharp lines of her cheekbone. A beam of moonlight showed just the bottom half of her face, the string of freckles across her nose, her soft peach skin, and her full lips.

She looked so utterly enchanting.

Something clicked in Kara’s mind as her heart skipped a beat at the sight of her.

Lena looked so soft. So absolutely, wonderfully beautiful in her hesitation.

Her tongue went dry in her mouth at the sight. Though it struck her every day, knowing how lucky she was to have Lena this close to her in her life, it overfell her more in that moment.

Kara pushed herself up on her elbows while Lena remained where she was. She paused, just a few inches away from Lena. It felt like she was moving on instinct, her mind in a state of vague panic, as she didn’t know what she was doing. She just knew that she couldn’t stay one more second so far away from Lena.

It was too dark to deduce the look in Lena’s eyes, but Kara could see her lips. They opened only slightly, the minty scent of her toothpaste and the flowery scent of her night cream urging Kara closer.

Kara saw Lena swallow, her lips making a soft sound as they separated again.

Her heart raced against her chest. She was only slightly aware of how dangerous her next moves were, how quickly she could fuck up something so beautifully innocent, something Kara didn’t think she’d survive if she lost it. And yet she didn’t think she could refuse to fulfill her own wish right at that moment.

Something vaguely familiar came over Kara, like a muscle memory pushing her forward. She knew. She knew. Lena’s name ran through her mind in a musical loop. Lena’s uneven breaths matching her own. When Kara pushed herself even closer and Lena didn’t move even a hair, Kara let out a deep breath. It in turn made Lena’s breath hitch in her throat. Kara’s eyes met Lena’s, and up close she could see the flicker of anticipation in her eyes.

Kara was struck with fear for just a moment, hovering close enough to touch, yet still far enough that she could back away and laugh it off if she tried. She met Lena’s eyes, every question clear to read. Can I do this? Can I risk this?

Lena looked at her, biting down softly on her lip. Then she smiled at Kara. That warm, familiar smile. That smile that greeted her in the morning, and sent her off at night. That soft, promising, sweet smile that got Kara through everything.

Kara swallowed her nerves and smiled back, just for one beat. She didn’t wait. She pushed herself up with one last, tiny push, and their lips finally met. Lena made a sound, her hand coming up to touch Kara’s face, her ring cold against Kara’s cheek. Her lips smiled against Kara’s own, broader and wider than before. The tiniest pressure was enough for Lena to pull Kara closer as if she’d waited forever for Kara to be this close.

Lena pushed her down, their lips never separating as she tangled her thin fingers into Kara’s hair, and pressed deep, warm kisses against Kara’s lips. Over and over again.

All Kara could think was that. That was what she had been looking for.
